What makes a good teacher? What makes a good father? What makes a good child, all bound by duty?

xexnoncores

This work contains CWs for: mentions of suicide and implications of child abuse/neglect.

Happiness Can’t Come From Assignments by xexnoncores

⚠️ content warning

Two People In Love

By Chrysophilius Marshall

I’d like for you to choke me
With ruby clocks and golden heels
I’d like for you to kill me
With purses heavy enough to bleed

I’d like for you to cut me
So you can say “it’s always been like this”
I’d like for you to shoot me
Because I know the hatred in your heart

I know the hatred in your heart
The living room is always filled with it
I feel the hatred in your heart
My own pounds when you feign a smile to me

I see the hatred in your heart
There’s no good reason for me to be like this
I cause the hatred in your heart
Because the worst husband alive is me

The worst husband alive is me
Even on weekends you won’t catch my voice
The worst person alive is me
Nothing says like nothing does to a housewife

The worst artist alive is me
When will the sun go down on my sins?
The worst believer alive is me
I wish we had gotten divorced instead.

November 1st, 2013

“Chrysophilius Marshall?”

She hates doing this. Temperance hates doing this, no matter who it is. Twenty years as a teacher and she’s still not able to tolerate this uneasiness. It never refuses to not tie knots in her stomach like she’s tasting coal grit in the air.

Without a word, a small boy packs up his things and follows her out into the empty hall. He looks like a child perfectly built by this school, with his smooth blonde hair, peachy skin, and dark brown eyes. His black uniform suit fits him perfectly.

“Yes ma’am?” he asks in an accent that is almost old-fashioned. There was posh English, and then there was talking like you were the Queen in the 1940s posh English. “What do you need? I’m trying to study.”

“I’ll ask for you to be granted some extra study time tonight before lights out,” she replies calmly. As she always does, as she always has to. Her face drops a bit with worry, but she’s never seen a kid catch what that means.

“I’m here to ask about—”

She shuffles through a beige duffle bag and quickly pulls out a piece of paper. Her mind spins with dozens of possibilities, all separated and extrapolated from her own sense of control.

“A piece of poetry you submitted for a homework assignment.”

He cocks his head to the side until she hands it to him and his face blanks white.

“What’s wr-wrong with this?” he asks with a frazzled tone. Almost a smidge too loud.

Damnit, I gotta calm him down, Temperance thinks. “There’s nothing wrong with any form of creative expression, Mr. Marshall. I am simply here to ask you why you turned in a piece of work talking about…”

She never knew how to feel about the billionaire kids. Most of them were brats through and through—they learned well, but mouthed down to whoever they thought they could get away with as discreetly as was considered proper. Nobody at this school really liked that it was manners and schedules being the only thing that kept them at bay so much of the time.

Although she had never heard this about Chrysophilius, not while she was teaching here anyway. He was quieter than most boys his age at fourteen. And apparently a little bugger when he was younger, according to the whispers of the other chatty teachers.

“…Um, a husband wanting to…kill his wife.”

She hoped she got that right. This felt like more than that, like some kid’s plea for their parents to kill each other, for them to kill themselves, for them to all take each other out in a murder-suicide.

Chrysophilius is silent.

He looks at the paper, turning it over a few times. His eyes seem to scan a universe that Temperance did not find, because he folds it up neatly after a minute and stands up straight to address her.

“…That’s a pretty generous reading of this,” he finally says after what feels like hours.

“What is it then?” Temperance’s voice is very plain. As plain as a bleeding heart could be, anyway.

“…The assignment was to write about something we never experienced before in the style of Gertrude Stein,” he says back. “That American poet who lived in France.”

He speaks so curtly, as if he’s practiced this. As if he knows what she’s here for. When Chrysophilius gets passionate, his voice shakes. When asked about his dislikes, his cadence runs achingly flat.

“Correct,” Temperance responds without missing a beat. “My question is—why is this so vivid? The imagery here makes me feel like you’ve seen this before. Are your parents okay?”

She looks around to see if anyone is within earshot. These marble floors betray little when it comes to secrets, yet hide everything except the reflections of what one hated the most. When mawed by tall, oak ceilings that yawned with modernity and yet still required a king’s toll to rest under, it was hard to imagine despair. It was difficult to visualize heartsickness in anyone situated among them.

“…Do I look like I’m married?”

She blinks.

“What?”

Chrysophilius sighs and shakes his head. “I did exactly as the assignment told me. I wrote about something I’ve never experienced personally. I’m not married, am I?”

“I would hope not,” Temperance replies stolidly. “Still, I just wanted to ask why—”

“Why does it matter?”

“Don’t talk back to me, young man.”

Chrysophilius bites his lip in a way few other boys would at a female teacher. This was the other oddity her colleagues spoke about—if you wanted him to behave, you sent a woman after him. Girls occasionally raised their voices at him to get an easy reaction, but they all stopped after a while because one of them went missing. Nobody ever found her body, and her parents had trouble remembering she even existed.

“…I’m sorry,” Temperance sputters quickly, putting all of that out of her mind. (That wasn’t real. She had to have imagined that whole debacle.) She has to help him. “I’m just worried about if you’ve seen this before with someone else. This kind of thing disturbs me.”

Nothing. Chrysophilius stands stock-still, looking at her, but there is nothing behind his eyes.

“…Can I go back to studying, please?” His words curls like an acetone aroma. “I need to focus on preparing for my GSCEs. I got good feedback on that assignment, so I don’t understand why you’re here.”

His voice is like glass, but reinforced ever so slightly as the edges. Obviously some of that was growing pains—voice cracks from where his adult self was trying to break into his child’s body, but Temperance feels like that had already happened in too many ways already.

What else could she do here? She thought he would be cooperative. She thought he would say something to her, and she’d get to give him over to the counselor. The light at the end of the tunnel is that the parents would obviously come over and talk it out, look at what their son was writing, and fix themselves accordingly. Change themselves promptly, in time for their child’s maturity. To undo some of the damage before it was too late.

This was easier back in America. Back in Florida where tabs were kept on kids without reservation. It was easy to tell the parents about something concerning then, be it their child flashing gang signs, drawing genitalia in their notebooks, biting others when they weren’t getting their way. A lot of them didn’t listen, but a lot of them did, and that was what mattered the most. The kid could be put on the right path after a talking to.

All someone needed to do was notice and care.

Temperance bites her lip. She’s painfully aware of her own Tampa accent now as compared to his, painfully aware now of the fact his family members controlled some of the most important banks and museums in London. Hardly anyone at the school had seen his father or mother, but their donations were joked to fund half the budget sometimes, their relatives three quarters.

…Actually, was it just his father who donated? She didn’t remember the mother ever showing up here…

“…Alright, well,” she says kindly and with her teacher face on, “if you need anything, I’m always here. The counselors are too. Please make sure to visit them regularly if you’re experiencing any difficulties, okay?”

Chrysophilius rolls his eyes. Hard. Temperance winces, knowing it’s best not to snap at him, but she still can’t help but want to tell him again to stop. She worked her ass off to be here, to get out of that hellhole state she lived in, and she wasn’t going to spend her working years taking lip from brats with silver spoons up their behinds.

…Oh, what is she doing? Fuck, he’s just a kid, isn’t he? Why get so mad? You’re the adult here, not him. Be understanding, Temperance. Be understanding of how he’s not as mature as you are, not had the life experiences you’ve had, not had the chance to make the same mistakes as—

Ah. He’s gone back into the study hall.

One call.

Two calls.

Three, four, five, six.

Chrysophilius sits in his bed after his twenty minutes of extra allotted study time with his spare phone in hand. They ask everyone to put theirs in bins outside their doors before they sleep, which gets checked promptly before a symphony of *clicks* echo throughout the hallways.

This extra phone is for special purposes.

Another call. Seven. The lucky number fails him.

Quietly, he steps out of bed and rummages around with small hands. He’s looking for a silver box with a foxhound insignia on it. A box carved by fairies, he was told, over a hundred years ago.

Got it. He was told to hide this from everyone. Don’t let anyone else see this.

He has to push books about accounting and the principles of stock exchange out of the way, but that’s fine. He finds those books boring except when the numbers get really, really big.

Inside the box is a menagerie of sparkling items. A wand that makes wind into a hurricane, a potion to turn someone into a wyvern, a smoke bomb to summon kelpies.

What he wants is an ivory dragon scale. A large, flat teardrop shape the size of his hand that is harder than diamond and cooler than morning dew.

He drags it out of soft velvet and holds it to his chest. This is a naughty deed, a nuisance desire, but that teacher hasn’t gotten out of his head the entire day. Her words have been burrowing at his head like a worm, like he’s done something wrong. Touched a stove he shouldn’t have.

The scale glows faintly and his phone finally rings.

“Hi Dad,” he says softly.

Amos sputters on the other end of the line. “Chr-Chrysophilius—! What happened, are you okay?!”

“…Yes,” he lies. It’s only a lie in the sense he is never mentally well. But he is always physically fine. Should he be able to tell others that his heart hurts?

“Then why on earth did you call me using the—?! That’s only for emergencies! I’ve told you this before!”

“I got homesick again,” he squeaks.

There is a pause. Chrysophilius can hear the clamor of a party dripping through the white screen held up to his ear, bubbly like a soda water with citrus in it. Even then though, Amos’s sigh is louder.

“…Chrysophilius, could this not have waited until later…?”

“It’s lights out time,” he replies shakily. The longer this goes on, the heavier his chest becomes.

“Right—your sleep is important—um…”

Chrysophilius shoves the box back underneath his bed, but not without pulling out a small statue of a dog. He rolls it over in his hands, marveling at how it seems to faintly glow despite the dark.

Amos gave this to him last year for his birthday.

“Did…anything cause this?” That voice shivers uncertainly. “Do you need me to come over? I can’t do this weekend, it will have to be next—maybe, I don’t know, Percival set up four different auctions for me to host, so I’m nearly besides myself on time—”

“I want to attend an auction…!” Chrysophilius’s eyes light up thinking about all of the possibilities there. He covers his mouth quickly, realizing he’ll be caught if he’s any louder than this. “…I-I want to attend an auction. Iris gets to go all the t-time.”

Amos sighs. “Iris is…special. She has to go. Besides, she’s older than you, so she can take care of herself—”

“Please…”

He turns the dog over in his hands. It used to float in an hourglass, but a moon-shaped rock and a girl from a painting turned that inside out and made it metal instead. What a magical time, what a magical moment…

There’s more like that waiting for him, isn’t there?

Iris always talked about it…she was practically made of it. That wonder, that mystery. Chrysophilius kept getting told he needed to take it slow, that he had to keep reading about it, but he wanted it now! He wanted it now!

He wanted it now…

I want Dad to show me stuff like Iris’s father does with her…

He mentioned that once to Amos, and at such a notion, he went very pale. Said nothing with a frown as he hugged him close and pulled him onto his lap, taking out a little silicon ball from his pocket that he pressed a button to turn into a butterfly. A butterfly with golden wings and platinum joints, with little flecks of blue fire following its mechanical movements around. It hissed steam when it had to be put back into its original form.

Cool technology too…it was kind of like the new models of phones they were making now. The ones with touch screens, as opposed to the landlines with handles he saw when he was younger. Or those big clunky boxes he saw in old movies.

“…I don’t want you to get hurt,” Amos says again. Sternly, with a tone Chrysophilius hates, because it’s the only time he sounds like he’s really trying to be a dad.

He wants to cry, but he can’t. Boys don’t cry. He’ll be improper for doing so. His dad doesn’t cry, yeah—so he shouldn’t do that over wanting to see him. He’s just…stupid, right?

Stupid enough to let all of that show to the teacher…Chrysophilius didn’t think anyone would care about his family situation. Writing that poem felt like he was threading something he shouldn’t have, talking about something he could get away with like a child eating too many cookies from the jar. It was fun until someone notice, fun until now when he was realizing his school didn’t care enough to make Amos call him more.

“…Please,” he says again, and that’s all he can manage with his meager hope. It’s all he can do as he clutches that dog in his hands through a blanket. His voice breaks, but he fights back tears valiantly.

He can only think about that poem in his head. He can only think about how he wrote it in between watching anime from a special USB Iris had made for him. Forget just stuff from this universe—what about anime from the fifth dimension?

(He couldn’t understand what was happening besides there being hot starfish people.)

Nothing is said as Chrysophilius yawns and his heart sinks. It fizzes and sputters, like a tablet to the bottom of a champagne glass. The chatter of the party buzzes in his ears in the background of the call.

“…Next break,” Amos says. “That will give me enough time—though it may not be an auction. I don’t know my schedule. That’s what, two weeks?”

“Fall break starts on Monday,” Chrysophilius whispers flatly.

Amos hisses under his breath.

“Goddamnit, goddamnit—”

He forgot my schedule again, Chrysophilius thinks to himself.

“Goddamnit—”

His voice strains weakly, waxily and as sand is washed away by the waves. Chrysophilius deflates until that tenor voice perks back up again, full of annoyance.

“Fuck, okay, be ready by Monday. Please.”

Full of annoyance, but so full of promise. Lucky for him, Amos kept the few promises he made. (But why?)

“I need you to be ready as soon as I pick you up. We will be flying out to Johannesburg on our private jet, understand? Don’t worry about getting breakfast from school, you can have something on the plane. Sorbet for breakfast, as a treat.”

Sorbet for breakfast, as a treat. Chrysophilius smiles wide, nodding like Amos can hear him. Somehow, he gets the memo.

“Splendid. I have to go now—”

A woman’s voice chatters over the phone. She sounds properly peeved, as if she’s been waiting on something. Chrysophilius hangs up as soon as he hears breathy kissing, a shudder running down his spine.

Ew. Gross.

…But also he wouldn’t mind a girl doing that to him. Does he have to wait until marriage for that?

Was that why Amos was so busy? He was keeping that lady waiting?

…Well, as long as she was nice. Chrysophilius never minded the other women in Amos’s life so long as they smiled at him when they saw him. Derry, his favorite, even sent him Christmas cards.

That couldn’t be said for his mother…

But there was no need to think about her tonight. Not before bed, anyway. Best not to dwell on bad omens.

Chrysophilius shuts his phone off and puts the dog statue underneath his pillow. The dragon scale he used slowly dissipates as the world turns, as the night crawls on and those beady little silver eyes glow.

He doesn’t know what it is, but smiles as he thinks he’ll ask Iris about it. She’ll be so nice in telling him; she’s going to give that big fanged smile she always does. In that snappy black suit of hers as well, a suit he’ll get to wear soon! When he’s eighteen, he’ll get one too! Everything’s going to change when he becomes a grownup, everything’s going to get better, he’ll stop being sad, surely. Having a job seemed to keep all the adults around him so busy—

And he’d get to see his dad more too! No more school to get in the way.

No more school to get in the way…

He sighs and closes his eyes. Sleep is important, but he wants to be happy.

Location: Solar System, close orbit of Sol

Although there's no such thing as "day" or "night" in extraterrestrial terms, it was still — loosely — another regular day in the cosmos, as these things go. Sauelsuesor was peacefully orbiting the sun when something stirred her awake. She immediately snapped to attention, eyes widening in alarm, and thrust one of her sable arms directly at the threat hurtling inexorably through space.


But I'm sure it's nothing to worry about.


In the meantime, it was December 30th, and that's Mister Toasty's birthday! He decided to rent out Site-203 for his big day, so after setting loose all the D-class, anomalies, and staff that never get mentioned (it's fine), he went straight to the commissary, where a sign reading HAPY BIRTHDAY MRTOSTY [sic] was strewn. Since this was Site-203, that meant that Senior Researchers Reuben Bialowieski, Rashid Safir, and Moira Silverberg; D-50050, Researchers Levi Dennison, Zhishen Liang, Kimberly Silva, and Maureen Dunharrow; therapist Dr. Lucille Riverson, Senior Containment Specialist Conroy Shulen, Junior Researcher Adele Ampersand, Junior Containment Specialist Guillaume Humboldt, and Site Director Cecil Talbot were all forced to attend!

Forced to, I say!

"Wait, what's going on?" Ampersand said, certainly not the only one there perplexed. Mister Toasty waved at her.

"Today's my birthday, and I'm celebrating it here with everyone!"

"Oh," she said, still no less perplexed. She blinked and shook her head. "Okay. Who are you again?"

Mister Toasty sighed. He pointed to his name badge:

"SCP AUTHOR Mister_Toasty, MAXIMUM CLEARANCE"

"Oh, so it's a self-insert," said Dennison. "I know about those. It's like how Stan Lee used to put himself into all sorts of Marvel films and TV shows."

"More or less," Toasty said, "but I'm only doing it this one time."

"So you summoned us all here to celebrate your birthday?" said Director Talbot.

"Yeah, you and all the other anomalies and characters I've written about ever since I joined the Wiki."

"So basically," said Shulen, "you forced us to stop whatever important work we were doing and dragged us out here just so you could throw yourself a party — and because you don't have any friends in real life, you needed to resort to us."

"Harsh, Conrad," Silverberg hissed. He snorted.

"Am I mistaken?"

"Not really," Toasty shrugged.

"And on top of all that," Shulen resumed, "do you seriously expect anybody to know who any of us are? You just dropped a laundry list of names that, I can guarantee, nobody remembers or cares about."

"Hey," Dunharrow grumbled in offense. Shulen just snorted.

"I mean, someone would have to have read every single one of your articles to have any idea…"

"That's enough, Shulen," Talbot stated. He issued an icy glare to the other man. "It's his birthday. Let the man do what he wants. It's fine if no one knows who we are."

"Thank you, Cecil," Toasty said, then waved to the person reading this. Yep, that's you!

"Okay, this is getting too meta for me," said Silverberg, throwing her hands into the air as she walked off. "I'm out! Call me when you're serving cake."

But there was no door. Oh no. OH NO! The room didn't have any exit! There was no way to leave! They were all trapped in that room FOREVER AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa or at least until the story ended.

"Come on, it won't be so bad," Toasty assured her. "Just wait around until everyone else shows up. We'll have some food, maybe play a few games, and then you'll all go back to your regular jobs."

Silverberg scoffed, clearly frustrated.

"Please?" Toasty implored her. "Like Shulen said, I don't have any friends. Besides…"

He then told her the real reason he was having this party. A cautious smile crept onto her face, and Silverberg relented.

"All right, I guess I can tough it out a bit longer—but try and lay off the fourth wall humor."

"I'll do my best," Toasty assured her. Bialowieski raised his hand.

"You mentioned you invited 'all the characters and anomalies you've written about'. Since none of us are anomalous, can I assume that you're expecting more guests?"

"Oh yes, a whole truckload," Toasty answered. "Of course, since this is a party, I don't really expect any of them to show up until later, since only a total nerd arrives early to—"

Suddenly a duck-billed platypus fell out of thin air and onto Ampersand's head.

"Wak, wak," it said. Ampersand screamed.

"AAAAAAHHH IT'S IN MY HAIR AND IT'S GOT HORRIBLE FANGS AND A MILLION MOUTHS AND IT'S EATING MY EYEBALLS, GET IT OFF GET IT OFF GET IT OFF GET IT OFF GET IT OFF!"

She flailed around for a good while with the platypus clinging on for dear life. Eventually, Dr. Riverson reached over and plucked it up. She regarded it sternly.

"Since this thing spontaneously appeared, I can only assume…"

"Ah, hello, madam," said the platypus. "Can I interest you in a tax representative?"

Riverson's eyes twitched. Luckily, Toasty came along and rescued it before it could be thrown against the wall.

"Hey there, J.S.! Thanks for coming to the party!"

"Wak, I wouldn't miss it for the world!" exclaimed the platypus. "Of course, I had to arrive early. It's only good manners!"


There was a long, dense silence.


"Right," Toasty drawled. He set it down on a table and introduced it: Joriah Shenandoah Cuthbert, SCP-8042.

"A platypus?" Humboldt stated.

"Yeah!" Toasty exclaimed. "A tax platypus! He does taxes for anomalies."

"For anyone, really," Cuthbert added. He raised a paw, and if platypuses could smile, he would. "Hiya."

"I already don't like him," Ampersand grumbled. Cuthbert groaned.

"Waaaaaaaaak…"

"Come on, J.S. is cool," Toasty assured her.

"You don't think you're being a bit biased?" Silverberg remarked. Toasty stammered and decided to get Cuthbert something to eat. Naturally, there was an unlimited supply of shrimp and crawfish at the party, so they both dug in, and encouraged everyone else to do the same.

"Is shellfish the only thing you have?" Talbot wondered, cautiously picking something out. Toasty waved at him.

"No, of course not: I've got any kind of food you want. This is my party, after all."

"Ah." Satisfied, everyone began to eat whatever they wanted. Dr. Riverson pulled Toasty aside and asked his permission to leave so she could bring someone to the party. Knowing who she meant, Toasty temporarily let her exit the room. When Riverson came back a few minutes later, she was seen leading an adolescent girl by the hand. The girl was floating a few meters above her.

"Hey, Amanda," Toasty waved. She smiled and saluted.

"Yo! Oh, cool, flautas!" Her mother pulled her down so she could eat, and SCP-8663-A officially joined the party.

"So much for having any alcohol here," Shulen grumbled.

"It's a bit early in the day for that anyway," Silva remarked. Liang grinned.

"Not for me it's not!"

"I heard that," said Toasty, and they gave each other a high-five.

"Not to be the one bearing the logical burdens," Bialowieski said in-between bites, "but if there aren't any doorways here, how do you expect people to show up?" Toasty smiled as he tipped back a sarsaparilla.

"Oh, don't worry: I've got ways of circumventing that. J.S., for one, can teleport—"

As Toasty pointed at the platypus with his bottle, a cloud of smoke emitted in the center of the room. From its center stepped four people, all coughing and waving the plumes away.

"Oh, perfect timing!" Toasty exclaimed, and went over to shake their hands, introducing them one by one. "Good thing I wrote all this down," he said, checking the back of his hand. He squinted: "Let's see… This is acting Director for Site-278, Phillipe Offet; their previous Director, Lamerock Bouquet; and its chief of security, Iseult Bodmall."

"Ahem," said the one I had missed. Toasty lit up.

"Ah yes, and SCP-7632-A. I never actually refer to her by name, but it's Medea."

D-50050 spat out his drink.

"The Tyler Perry character?!"

"No, the one from Greek mythology," Toasty answered, "though in all honesty, 'that' Medea could very well be an anomaly on her own. How ya doin', lady?" Toasty went to hug Medea; she embraced him in return and politely kissed his cheek.

"(You didn't invite you-know-who, did you?)" she whispered.

"No, no," he assured her, "just my own original characters." She smiled and released him.

"Good. Well, this is turning out to be a festivity of some repute already! Hello, Phillipe."

She smiled cruelly at him. He shrank back.

"I never expected to see you again," he sighed.

"Hmm, yes, small world and such." She chuckled. "Oh, don't give me that look: I'm here for pleasure—but only for awhile. Joriah?"

"Hehnk?" The platypus looked up from his crawfish buffet. "Oh, hi, Medea! Fancy seeing you again! Thanks for letting me do your taxes. Heh, I'm starting to wonder if I should just move to Orcadia, I've got so many clients there now!"

"Could you assist me?" she said. "I need to retrieve the rest of Toasty's guests, and doing all the work myself is a bit taxing. No pun intended."

"No problem," he replied, wiping his bill clean. "I'll just grab the ones on my client list first, if that's okay." The platypus instantly phased out, leaving Medea to smile. Toasty waved at her, and she vanished in a flash of lightning. Bouquet sidled up to Offet, a mug of hot tea in hand.

"Acquaintance of yours?"

"You could say that," he grumbled, deflating in exhaustion. "Remember that assignment the O5s sent me on before you stepped down? We, ah, met there."

"Fancy that," he replied, taking a sip. "You met Medea of Colchis and I ran into the Questing Beast."

"Speaking of which, is that…ah, creature here, or…?"

"Ah, yes, she's here, though I doubt anyone else can see her." He pointed over to a corner, where Toasty was gesturing as if he was scratching something large. Obviously, he could see it, too.

"When Medea comes back, I'll ask her to make it visible for the party," he assured them. Right on cue, she returned, preceded by a stiff breeze and blazing fire.

"Does she always make those florid entrances?" Talbot grumbled.

"I'm afraid so," Offet sighed. "She has an acute flair for the dramatic. Comes with being a tragic Greek heroine, I suppose." This time, Medea was escorting three ghosts. Toasty put his session with SCP-8089 on hold, greeting one of the spirits warmly while raising his middle finger at the other two.

"Oi, don't give me that," snorted one of the ghosts. "I seem to recall you invitin' us. You could at least pass along our names."

"Fine, fine," Toasty sighed: "Everyone, this is — err, I mean, these were Llewellyn Eames and Maxim Veridas. You don't really have to be nice to either of them. The cool one was Anatol Sobolevsky, or SCP-6683 if you prefer."

Everyone crowded around Gospodin Chudo and welcomed him warmly. Only Talbot approached Eames.

"Ordinarily I'd say it's good to see a former member of Site-203 after their passing, but I'll withhold the tidings in this case."

"Bugger off, Cecil; you ain't exactly a saint yourself," the ghost of Eames snapped.

"Hey, Lew, cool it," Toasty said. "I invited you here because you're one of my characters and I want everyone to be here. If you can't behave yourself, I'll have someone throw you out. All right?"

Emaes snorted and contented himself with drinking some Diet Ghost. Meanwhile D-50050, Ampersand, and Dennison were using Veridas as a pinata.

"Ouch, ouch! Stop, stop! It hurts and stings!"

Everyone laughed, and made sure that Gospodin Chudo was having fun. They didn't care about Eames or Veridas, because they were mean and bad.

"Stop breaking the fourth wall!" Silverberg shouted.

Ugh, fine. Anyway, Medea made sure that SCP-8089 was visible for the party, then excused herself to go retrieve more guests. She sank into the floor, leaving a puddle of viscous black goo behind. Ampersand pushed Veridas into it, and he roared in pain as ghostly hands rose out of the puddle and ripped his soul apart. Everyone laughed again. What a wonderful party!

Cuthbert materialized shortly, bringing with him a number of people: Junior Researcher Natalia Yegorova, agent Dana Ebony, UIU Deputy Director Harold Dyne, UIU agent Benjamin Garland, and Captain Natalia Szabo.

"Oof," Riverson said as she was elbowed by Bouquet, "it's getting crowded in here!"

"At least you didn't have to wander through Dr. Wondertainment's funhouse with Mr. Quacks-and-Tax," Szabo grumbled. She was accidentally shoved into Riverson; their eyes met, the latter grinning awkwardly. "Uh, hey there. Natalia Szabo of the Castaways."

"Hi," Riverson said, a little flushed. They shook hands. "Lucille Riverson. This is my—" She looked up, spotting her daughter playfully teasing the Questing Beast. "My daughter Amanda. She floats."

"Not the weirdest thing I've ever seen. Hey, Sky Dolphin, put er' there!" Szabo reached up and the two shook hands; meanwhile the Questing Beast approached Cuthbert, growling softly.

"Yes, yes, it's all right," the platypus muttered. "Even for me, you're notoriously difficult to track down. Don't worry, I've got your papers." Cuthbert then ruffled through his fur and produced a folder, which he handed to the Beast. The creature looked over the document carefully before nodding in approval.

"You weren't joking when you said he'll do taxes for anybody," Bodmall remarked. Toasty nodded.

"You know, I wanted to write a follow-up Tale about him. I was going to explore his origins and have him audit the Scarlet King."

Bodmall whistled, impressed. "Seems like a tall order. What happened? Did you get too many projects or something?" Toasty hemmed, tepidly refusing to answer. He shuffled off to greet Yegorova, who had joined Szabo and Riverson. The two Russian women immediately struck a rapport and started talking in their native language; Bouquet had smuggled some whiskey in and was drinking with Zhishen, Shulen, and D-50050; Ampersand wriggled her way through the crowd, finally isolating herself. Toasty noticed and approached her; she was talking to an older brunette woman wearing glasses. Toasty smiled and hugged her.

"Hey, Hilde. Glad you could make it."

"Uh, yeah," she answered, stiffly returning his embrace. "Me too, honestly. It didn't look like I would for a minute there."

"Eh, no worries," he assured her. "So how'd you get here?"

Hildegard Kemper pointed her thumb over at the corner, where the bust of a middle-aged member of German nobility was situated. Surrounding it were a number of people, all bearing glasses of punch and plates of hors d'oeuvres. Toasty chortled stiffly and approached it.

"Pardon me, your excellency." The bust turned around, its stony face lighting up.

"Ah! Master Toasty! Deucedly wonderful party you've organized here, my good fellow — and such company as I've not seen in many a fortnight!"

"I'm glad you're enjoying it, Baron. Would you like to introduce everyone, or shall I?"

"You are the host, my friend," the bust replied modestly: "the honor is yours." Toasty called for everyone's attention and rounded off even more names: agent Raven Wesson, Rhonda Smith, Claire Douglas, Romia Biancospino, Liath Cairill, Maya Sarasvati, and the honorable Baron Hieronymus Karl Friedrich Freiherr von Münchhausen, SCP-7784.

"Wait, Dr. Sarasvati's here?!" Shulen blurted. He, Silverberg, Safir, and Bialowieski sprinted over to her, aghast to see her alive and well. Sarasvati just smiled shyly and waved.

"Uh, yes. Hello."

"My god!" Shulen gasped. "Maya! We all thought you were… I mean, after what Eames did to you… Are you okay?"

"Yes," she said, clearing her throat. "Sorry to leave off so ambiguously like that."

"But you were covered in boils the last any of us heard about you!" Silverberg breathlessly exclaimed. Sarasvati nodded.

"Yes. I got better."


There was a very long, very painful pause. Everyone glared at Toasty.


"Just couldn't help yourself, could you?" Szabo snapped. "You had to sneak in a Monty Python joke, didn't you?"

Toasty just shrugged, earning himself a dope-slap. The party went on.

"Well, we're glad you're in good health now," Bialowieski said. "What can we get you? He may be a mediocre writer, but our host didn't skimp on the food."

"I think I'll just settle for some fried tofu and a portabello sandwich." Sarasvati reached for the food, put it on a plate—then stopped herself and quickly nabbed something else. "Oh, and an almond cookie!"

"A woman after my own heart." D-50050 smiled at her and winked; she grinned in return.

"Hello, Duny. Good to see you're well, too."

"I haven't yet been ejected into outer space," he shrugged, munching on pieces of brie. Sarasvati's eyes widened.

"That's an oddly specific boast."

D-50050 nodded. "Toasty was going to feature me in my own article, you know. Send me to a strange dimension, make me indestructible, toss me into space, make friends with Sauelsuesor…"

"That sounds promising," Sarasvati pointed. "What happened?"

"No idea," D-50050 shrugged, popping broccoli in his mouth. "It was just one of those things he never got around to."

"I'm starting to notice a pattern," said Bialowieski. "He wanted to do a 001 proposal with me in the starring role. That never happened, either."

"Reuben," Silverberg said, her voice patient but stern, "I warned him about the fourth-wall jokes, and now I'm warning you. I didn't come here to get bogged down in metaphysical jargon; I just want to have a good time, stuff my face, and maybe get stone drunk."

"But I thought with Amanda here, there wouldn't be any…" He trailed off, noticing a group of people gathered around in a circle. Raven Wesson, Natalia Szabo, Baron Munchhausen, and Conrad Shulen were all chanting and cheering, each of them taking turns drinking from a keg.

"Chug! Chug! Chug! Chug!"

There was someone resembling a lumberjack at the hose; he held it to his mouth with one hand and flashed a thumbs-up with the other. After consuming what must have been the entire keg, the lumberjack finally pulled away, exclaiming as he wiped his mouth and laughed.

"Another keg, beermaster!"

Everyone clapped and cheered. Toasty grinned and waved at another guest. A man wearing a toga and sandals floated over, a winged cap nestled at a slant on his head. Despite carrying a large keg in both arms, he didn't seem burdened in the slightest.

"Ambrosia straight from Olympus!" he exclaimed. Everyone cheered again. Silverberg scoffed.

"You were saying, Reuben? Excuse me." She slithered her way through and requested a turn at the hose, which everyone eagerly granted. Toasty noticed Bialowieski's shock and explained.

"Oh, this is Paul Bunyan," he said, indicating the lumberjack, "and this is Hank Green. Oh, wait, you two know each other, right?"

"In a roundabout manner," Bialowieski said. He approached the two cautiously; Bunyan pulled him in for a crushing handshake while Green just tipped his winged cap.

"Glad to meet a native son of Poland!" Bunyan exclaimed. "Toasty's told me a lot about you! He says you're one of his favorite characters!"

"Good to know," Bialowieski winced. Bunyan released him; Hank just laughed and tapped the man's bruised hand.

"It's been awhile, Reuben. Sorry about the difficulty with Bes and Whiskey Jack. You know how us tricksters are."

"Through rather unfortunate first-hand experience," he muttered. Hank laughed and apologized, and the party continued. Riverson and Szabo continued to chat in the corner; Dana Ebony and Rhonda Smith glared daggers at each other; Cuthbert was going around offering to do everyone's taxes; Paul Bunyan chatted with Baron Munchhausen and Medea over their shared experiences as public domain characters; Talbot and Bouquet exchanged stories; Ampersand and Kemper stood by Toasty, somewhat perplexed.

"So this makes two nerdy dark-haired women with glasses he's written about," Ampersand indicated.

"Yeah," Kemper nodded, sipping a drink. "I guess he has a type."

"Well, that and redheads," Toasty corrected. "I'm absolutely crazy for redheads. But nerdy brunettes in glasses are a close second."

"Ah HUH," they remarked. Toasty chuckled.

"Don't worry, you two are too young for me, anyway. Silverberg or Riverson are more to my liking."

"Lucky us," Ampersand muttered. She suddenly pointed to Hilde: "Wait, isn't there someone else from your article? Where's Letty?"

Hilde frowned, glancing away ruefully. The subject was clearly a sore one, and not a wound she wanted opened anytime soon.

"Well," Toasty said, "I invited her, but she knows Hilde'll be here, too, so I don't know if she'll come."

The three of them silently drank, stewing in all the unspoken hurt. Medea had the very good sense to appear just then, with more guests.

"Well, that was exhausting," she huffed, slumping over wearily. A 17th-century Dutch man stepped up first, stricken and slack-jawed at his surroundings. He introduced himself as Hubert van der Miir, occultist and archivist.

"My predecessor," Offet said; the two shook hands, one looking considerably more distressed.

"The witch… Ah, I mean, the lady… I did not know that, ah, she could travel through time…"

"Which explains why you're not a ghost," Offet remarked. He glanced over at the three actual ghosts: Sobolevsky having a grand old time playing Pin the Javelin on the Bad Guy, while Veridas was getting run through with javelins and Eames was sulking.

"And the others you requested," Medea said, pushing two rather amorphous and esoteric entities forward. One of them was an indescribable amalgamation of flesh and inorganic material, the other a transdimensional macroorganism who appeared as a Wolf, a Black Shape with large sharp teeth, and a shadowy figure teetering on the edge of reality and imagination.

Basically, SCP-7832 and SCP-7359.

"Hey there," Toasty waved. SCP-7832 immediately began constructing, building, adding, shaping…

"Shouldn't you stop it?" Dunharrow said. Toasty dismissed her concerns.

"Nah, it's fine. Let it have some fun."

"But you remember what happened the last time it got loose, right?"

"It's fiiiiiiiiiiiine," Toasty repeated. Dunharrow sighed and went back to drinking beer and playing games. Meanwhile, the Wolf approached Toasty, who scratched its head.

"Been a long time, buddy. You doing okay?"

"Can't complain," it replied. "Is this everybody?"

"Almost," Toasty said, somewhat forlornly. "We're still missing one person."

Just then, the door that, I swear, could never be opened until the story ended, suddenly opened. A young Italian woman stepped through, carrying a paper bag.

"Sorry I'm late, everyone: I got lost driving around again. I went and picked up some burgers, I hope that's oh…kay…"

Everyone froze and stared at her. She stared back.

"What? Wrong place?"

Hildegard Kemper nervously stepped forward, her hands folded. The other woman seized up.

"Hey, Letty."

Francesca Briscoletti, SCP-9199, swallowed.

"Hi, Hilde."

The mother of all awkward silences fell between them.

"Um, Letty — listen, I —"

"Don't," she interrupted, freezing Hilde where she stood. The other woman trembled, her lip quivering in grief.

"I'm sorry," she whispered, hunching over. "That's all I can say. I wish I could do more…"

"Yeah," Letty said. She pointed her thumb at Toasty, who stood by with patient anxiety. "About that. Toasty told me that he had planned on writing a follow-up tale if my article ever got big enough. A resolution, I guess you could say."

Hilde said nothing. She looked up slightly, more curious than hopeful.

"He wanted to show how I'd cope with everything, but then an actual anomaly, something you all didn't fabricate, came in from out of nowhere and started attacking people. The Foundation…didn't really know what to do. I mean, they only had experience with maintaining the veil — for me, I mean — they had no idea how to deal with an actual threat. But I came out of my funk and took command. I guided our site to victory, and we defeated the anomaly."

Hilde swallowed. She stood tall again, still curious but also…

"Yeah? Then what?"

Letty wiped a tear from her eye and approached the other woman.

"Oh, you know: predictably mushy stuff. I realized that…you all were my family, and…this world was still my world, and I had to protect it. Things like that. Hackneyed nonsense that any middle-schooler could cook up."

She smiled and took Hilde into her arms.

"And I understood that, at the end of the day, we were still friends, no matter what."

Hilde wept, returning the embrace.

"He told you that?"

Letty smiled.

"He didn't need to."

"God," Hilde shuddered, unable to stop crying, "that's about as emotionally stock as you can get!"

"I know," Letty replied, sniffling. "But…honestly, so what? He isn't wrong."

Hilde couldn't bear it any more. She looked down, removed her glasses, wiping her eyes.

"Sounds like it would've made for a good Tale. Too bad he never…"

Letty just hugged her closer.

"It's fine."

Suddenly, Levi Dennison piped up:

"Kiss her!"

"Yeah!" Liang shouted. "Let's see some tonsil inspections here!"

"[REDACTED] you," Letty snorted, raising her middle finger. Hilde just giggled, and they released each other. The moment, unfortunately, had been ruined a little, but the ladies still felt better after their heart-to-heart.

"It's still pretty hot," Liang muttered.

"Hey," Guillaume said, "if it helps, I'll make out with Dennison. I mean, it's only fair, right? If two guys start smooching, we need two girls in on it to balance everything out."

"I'm game," Dennison shrugged. Hilde just rolled her eyes.

"Sorry, I'm genuinely not into Letty like that. Besides, this technically counts as an interspecies relationship, and 4chan this is not."

"Damn it, stop with the meta jokes!" Silverburg shouted. A lewd expression graced Hilde's face.

"But, uh…I won't stop you fellas from doing it, heh."

"Yeah, let's see some yaoi!" Dunharrow shouted. Silva shrugged.

"I have no objections."

"Me neither," Szabo leered. "I'm always up for a gay old time, no matter which locker room we're talking about!"

"Oh, dear," Riverson sighed, "all this in front of a child!"

"Mom, shush!" Amanda hissed. "I wanna see boys make out!"

Dennison and Guillaume shrugged, looked at each other, and totally did the thing went ice skating instead.

"Oh, boo!" Amanda growled. "Toasty, you jerk!" Szabo snickered.

"Still hot. Anyone else want popcorn?"

And so, with that, all of Toasty's guests had arrived, and the main event could commence. A long table was brought in (don't ask who did it, or how, or where it came from…)

"Just repeat to yourself," said Wesson: "it's just a Tale, I should really just relax."

And everyone took a place, with Toasty at the head. He cleared his throat and a pleasant silence fell.

"Friends, anomalies, fictional constructs, the time has come for me to reveal the true purpose behind this party. While I do enjoy meaningless frivolity, I'm afraid something much more serious was the motive behind all this. You see…I'm retiring from writing for the SCP wiki."

A soft murmur rippled through the crowd.

"Now, I'm not going to retire just yet — I still have a few things I'd like to wrap up — and I'll certainly be around to read, review, and offer insight for anyone in the Ideas and Drafts forums…"

He winked and shamelessly held up a sign that read "PLEASE CONTACT TOASTY (me) FOR ALL YOUR GREENLIGHTING AND CRITIQUING NEEDS! (offer void in Utah)"

"But this is basically my swan song. Some of you may feel a bit crestfallen at the news, while others may honestly not give half a rotten rat's rear end whether or not I'm still around. Regardless, I won't be doing this anymore. I can't. The SCP 9000 contest opened my eyes to some very grim truths. You see, I put everything I had into my entry, slowly shaping it and nurturing it over the course of a year and more. I passed it around to more critics and invested more time and love into it than any other project that had come before. While I certainly didn't expect it to actually win the contest, I had hoped it would at least surpass my SCP 8000 entry, either in upvotes or ranking. Unfortunately, despite all of my hopes and efforts, this was not the case, and as of the time of this writing, is still not.

"And then we have 'Sir Francis Bacon's Fightin' Genius Time Commandos', which I spent four months writing, researching, and shaping into what I had hoped would be a fun adventure involving time travel and the Mekhanites. Unfortunately, hardly anybody else saw it that way, and it tanked pretty terribly. Between that and the results of 9-kon, my mental and emotional health took a serious blow. I realized that no matter what I did, I would never really be good enough, or popular enough, and all of my best efforts would languish in mediocrity. I can't do that anymore. I can't invest months of my life into something only for it to pass and be forgotten — or worse, cratered into oblivion. Yeah, I wrote SCP-7832, and even contributed to the Murphy Law hub, but on the whole, I was just another statistic that honestly did more good in the forums than the sandboxes. So I'm giving up and moving on.

"Will I ever return? Maybe, if there's a contest or a group collaboration that interests me, but basically, I'm done. But that's only half the reason I asked you all to come here. The other half is because…I owe all of you an apology.

"I can't speak for anyone else, but personally, I think you're all great characters with lots of potential — and I wasted that. I had so many wonderful plans in store, and such high hopes for all of you, but in the end, I realized I'll never be able to do any of you justice. I'll never be able to give D-50050 his literal moment in the sun, or square off Cuthbert with the Scarlet King, or patch up Letty and Hilde's relationship. And you can forget about that 001 proposal with Bialowieski, and all the other possible articles and tales that I could have written. I'm not good enough for that, and you all deserve so much better than what I can give you. I'm sorry for letting you down like that.

"That's it. That's all I have to say. Here's to all of you."

Toasty raised his glass, drank, and set it down. Then he walked away.

"I'd like to propose my own toast," said Talbot, standing as he raised a glass. He stared firmly at Toasty. "If you don't mind."

Toasty just sighed. "Go ahead."

"I'd like to toast the man who saw fit to make me the Director of Site-203."

He thank drank and politely wiped his mouth.

"And I'd like to toast the man who turned a loser like me into a pretty decent guy." Wesson stood next, raising his glass and drinking it.

"I'll toast him for bringing my daughter and I closer together," said Riverson.

"I'll toast him for giving me a pretty happy ending," said Medea.

"Speak for yourself," muttered Biancospino. She shrugged and raised her glass. "Ah, well. Here's to recycling me from another story and making me into a pretty cool villain."

"Here's to the man who gave me three lives, and my freedom," said Jay Doe.

"Here's to the man who had some of his articles translated for the Chinese and Vietnamese wikis," said Sobolevsky.

"To the man who used me to come to terms with his father's passing," said Bouquet.

"And who made me an Overseer on my very first day," Ampersand chimed in.

"To the one who believed in me, and cherished me, even when nobody else did," said Letty. She looked over at Hilde and smiled.

"And to the man who gave me a best friend when I was least expecting it," she added.

"To the man who gave me life," said Dunharrow.

"And me," said Silva.

"And me," said Liang.

"And me," said Dennison, "as well as a second chance at childhood."

"To the people he entertained with me," said Cuthbert.

SCP-7832 raised a tower of glasses it had constructed. Influence. Massive! Congratulations.

"To the friends he made with me," said Paul Bunyan.

"And to the ones who started it all," said Bialowieski.

Eventually everyone chimed in, raising a toast to their creator. He could do nothing but sit back down, sniffle, and smile in awe.

"Thanks, everyone," he whispered. "I don't deserve it."

In unison, they raised their glasses one more time, proclaiming, "HAPPY BIRTHDAY, TOASTY!"

Toasty wiped his eyes and blew his nose. He limply raised his glass again and set it down. Bialowieski and Talbot approached him, both of them carrying a wrapped box.

"We actually have a present for you. I think it's something you've wanted."

Toasty smiled and thanked them humbly. He carefully opened both boxes, finding a sawed-off shotgun in one and a chainsaw in the other. He grinned and wept again as he reverently took them out, one in each hand.

"Go on," Ampersand said, grinning as she nudged him. "Say the line."

Toasty sniffled and quickly wiped his eyes. His face glowed as he whirled the shotgun and slung it into a holster on his back, the camera slowly panning in on him. He held the chainsaw before him and whispered in a low growl:

"GROOVY!"





The party was beginning to die down a little. People were eating less, playing fewer games, and evidently hooking up with each other (because what's a party without an awkward drunken love exchange?). Levi and Guillaume were still ice-skating, Riverson and Szabo were finding more excuses to "be alone" with each other, Bouquet and Bodmall were invested in some serious "co-op" games, and even D-50050 looked like he had made a new friend as he gravitated to Letty. Toasty just watched, happy for everyone. Medea sidled up to him.

"You're not going to hook up with anybody?"

"Are you kidding?" he scoffed. "Even in my own ego-boosting story, I don't have any luck. Besides, who would I hook up with? Riverson's flirting with Szabo, Silverberg doesn't want anything to do with my fourth-wall humor, and everyone else is either too old, too young, or not even remotely human."

She smiled pitifully at him. Then she scooted closer.

"And what about dangerously unstable wild women with a tragic past and the wisdom of eons?" She smirked at him, and he got the hint.

"Seriously? You think I have a chance?"

"Should I dye my hair red, or wear glasses?" Toasty chuckled at her.

"No, you're perfect just the way you are."

She scooted even closer, until they were hip-to-hip.

"I'm glad to hear you say that. Truly. It's not often I'm around anyone so sincere…"

"Hey, is this seat taken?" Liath Cairill of the Chaos Insurgency staggered over and plopped herself down, draping an arm over Toasty's shoulder. She pointed to him, her one good eye leering. "I heard you like redheads. Do you fancy unpredictable women, too?"

"Um, well," he stammered, "Medea here is already sort if into me, I think…"

"Oh, don't mind me," she said, waving dismissively. "Liath and I are acquainted, remember?" She winked at the other woman, who stared dully until sobriety took over.

"Oh. Yeah, I remember. So you're really the witch Medea, huh? Big fan. We could use someone like you on our side."

"Emphasis on 'use'," Medea purred playfully. Liath blushed; Toasty's eyes widened.

"Uh…is this happening? Am I actually… I mean, both of you?"

"I'm game," Liath shrugged, "though I hope you're into scars and muscles."

"Yes!" Toasty croaked. "Yes I am!"

"And deranged mass-murderers with a heart of gold?" Medea added. Toasty grinned.

"Ladies, please! I know it's my birthday and all, but…"

They laughed and totally sprawled all over him, going in for a steamy three-way makeout sess—

PLOP!

A key lime pie splattered all over Medea's face.

"Got her!" shouted Henry Green. Medea angrily cleaned herself off.

"Hermes, you filthy Cretin! Why, I oughta…"

Medea picked up a nearby pecan pie and tossed it at him. Hank ducked down at the last second; the pie landed square on Phillipe Offet. Medea panicked.

"Whoops! Sorry, Phillipe!"

Offet angrily wiped his face clean. He reached over and plucked up a lemon meringue.

"PIIIIIIIIIE FIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIGHT!!!!!!!!"

He threw the pie at Liath, hitting her square in the back of her head. Toasty reached for a blueberry pie.

"Hey! That's my future girlfriend!" He threw it and hit Dennison, who had just gotten back from ice-skating. Dennison snarled.

"Oh, a wise guy, eh?" He reached over and hucked a rhubarb, accidentally hitting Ampersand. She screamed and returned fire, hitting Schulen. Everyone soon made a rush for the dessert table, picking up pies and throwing them at each other, until the air was saturated with sugary missiles. A pie landed square on Zhishen Liang's face; he wiped it off only for another pie to hit him; he squealed angrily, wiped it off, and got hit again. As he cleaned himself off, Anatol Sobolevsky approached him with a custard pie. Liang ducked down, chuckling impertinently, but Anatol ducked down with him, smacking him with a pie.

"Don't worry, sir!" Bodmall shouted, shielding Bouquet with her body. Several pies had already found their mark on her, while the former director was still clean. "I'll keep them off you! Just find a safe place!"

"Hey, Iseult?" She turned around, only for him to smile and throw a pumpkin pie on her face. She angrily wiped it off and reached for a blueberry. "Wait!" he cried, "I'm a victim of circumstance!"

She threw it at him anyway. He patiently cleaned himself off, and they laughed at each other.

"Here, Dolphin!" Szabo tossed Amanda a pie, which she launched with deadly accuracy from her perch. More pies were tossed her way; she downed Paul Bunyan and Baron Munchhausen before hitting one more person. Lucille Riverson angrily approached the two, smothered in peaches.

"Amanda! We need to have a talk!"

"Sorry, mom," she giggled. Szabo snickered.

"She's totally not sorry. Mmm, but you look good covered in pie crust and fruit filling!" Szabo curled up to her, tracing a finger over Riverson's neck. The other woman blushed furiously, but before anything could happen, a salvo of coconut cream pies fell on Szabo. Amanda floated overhead, giggling.

"Nailed her!"

The two women glared at each other, nodded in unison, and reached for a catapult with an oversized novelty cherry pie on it. Amanda panicked and tried floating away…

"FIRE!!!!"

The enormous pie hurled through the air, narrowly missing its target by a hair. It landed squarely on Veridas, burying him. Then he exploded. Everyone applauded.

"Now that," Szabo pointed, "is what I call a damn good cherry pie!"

The pie fight continued as more desserts were tossed willy-nilly. SCP-7832 wasn't used to throwing away perfectly good building material, but soon got the gist of the game, and tossed twisted and bizarre amalgamations of pie at anyone it saw. Claire got nailed in the head as she tried running for cover; Talbot got creamed…with, uh…cream…Letty and Hilde stood back-to-back as they fired off, and someone threw a pie directly at the camera, causing everything to temporarily go black.














(The lights come back on, showing a large American flag in the background. A reveille with trumpets plays as a figure marches up, wearing the uniform of a five-star General. He is resplendent with decorations and medals. He carries a riding crop in one hand, and salutes proudly with the other. The figure is revealed to be Joriah Cuthbert.)



Cuthbert: Be seated, wak.

(The sound of various people taking their seats is heard. Cuthbert puts his paws behind his back, pacing back and forth on the stage.)

Cuthbert: Now, I want you all to remember, that nobody ever won a war by getting hit in the face with an apple pie. They won it by making the other poor dumb schmuck get hit in the face with an apple pie! Friends, all this stuff you've heard about me not wanting to fight, about staying out of the pie toss, is a lot of horse dung! Platypuses traditionally love to throw pies! All real platypuses love the sting of bat—

(Suddenly, the pie fight breaks through the outer wall, spilling into the auditorium. Several people run towards Cuthbert, armed with pies.)

Cuthbert: Waaaak! Not in the bill! Not in the bill!

(Suddenly, a hand yanks Cuthbert up, dislodging some medals. Cuthbert is briefly relieved until he looks into the face of his savior.)

Cuthbert: Waak! It's you!

(Senior Containment Specialist Anatole Levye grins at him cruelly.)

Levye: Yes, it's me! Toasty didn't invite me to his party (along with probably like five other people he forgot about), so I decided to crash it! Now I shall have my revenge!

(Levye points a lingonberry pie at Cuthbert as the crowd surrounds him.)

Levye: Back off! Back off, I said, or the platypus gets it!

(The crowd stops.)

D-50050: (reading woodenly from a script) Oh no will not someone. Stop him and save that poor. Platypus. The poor thing.

Ampersand: Do it!

(Levye grins maniacally, wide-eyed and delirious. Suddenly, a drawer launches at him, knocking him over.)

Toasty: Whoa, what the Sam Scratch?

(More drawers are launched into the room, breaking down the wall. A group of elderly pirates swing in, armed with fan blades and pointed check spindles.)

Letty: Oh, no! It's the Crimson Permanent Assurance!

Liath: Not again!

Szabo: You and your Monty Python jokes!

(She is immediately leveled by another drawer.)

(The elderly pirates storm the room, mixing in with the pie fight.)

Toasty: Oh, jeez. I apologize for this, folks. Things seem to have gotten out of hand with my birthday. I really don't see any way out of this.

(Visuals cut to outer space, Sauelsuesor still pointing as an object soars through the cosmos. It is revealed to be a killer meteor wearing a ten-gallon Stetson hat.)

Meteor: WOOOOOOOOOOOO-HOOOOOOOO-HOOOOOOOOOO! WHEEEEEEEEEEEE-HAAAAAAAA! YEEEEEEEEAAAAAAAAAAAAAHOOOOOOOOO! WOOOOOOO-WHEEEEEEE-HAAAAAAHAAAAAAAHAHAHAAAA! WHAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA—

(Sauelsuesor continues to point as the killer meteor impacts the planet Earth, exploding it forever. She watches in dismay and disbelief for a moment before smacking herself in the face with her hand.)









Later…

At camp…


"And that was how I saved Switzerland!"

Mister Toasty stood before a campfire, smiling at a group of anxious-looking children. Due to the amount of distress clearly showing on their faces, it was highly likely that Toasty coerced all of them to be there under rather unscrupulous terms.

"Now," he exclaimed, "who wants frosty chocolate milkshakes?"

Before anything could happen, a clap of thunder and a blast of lightning ignited the sky. Time and space were torn asunder as a blue 1968 Volkswagon van erupted from thin air, barreling down the grass and skidding to a loud halt. Toasty stared at it in amazement as plumes of icy smoke wafted and curled around it, and the driver-side door hurled open, issuing a crazed man.

"Hey! Get in, nerd! We're going on an adventure!"

"Traveler!" Toasty exclaimed. A man waved at him casually from the passenger-side door. "Passenger! It can't be! I thought I sent you two back to the Ghost of Christmas Future!"

"You did, Kemosabe," Traveler said, his eyes livid and wild. "You did! But we're back! We're back from the Ghost of Christmas Future!"

Toasty stood in awe and bewilderment, hardly able to stand.

"Great Scott!"

The side door slid open. Toasty rubbed his hands together enthusiastically.

"Okay! Let's do this!" He eagerly hopped in, noticing a third man opposite him. It was the only other person he hadn't invited to his party, Foundation Agent Dana Allen.

"Hey there, Toasty! Welcome to the party!"

"Hey, Allen," he replied, the enthusiasm gone from his voice. An Alan Silvestri score stirred to life as all the doors closed and Traveler hopped back into the driver's seat.

"Wait a minute, man," said Passenger. "We didn't bring any toads with us. How are we going to get a psychedelic high without them?"

"Toads?" Traveler said, stone-cold sober as he flipped his shades on. "Where we're going, we don't need to lick…toads!"

The Silvestri score flourished to a crescendo as the van roared to life, engines firing, wheels burning, Toasty grinning with excitement as Traveler slammed his foot on the gas…


And it sputtered. The score came to a dead stop. Everything froze.


"Huh," Traveler grunted, "that's never happened before." He churned the key in the ignition again, pumping the brakes impatiently. The van kept stalling.

"Come on, man, give it some gas," Passenger said.

"Shut up! I know what I'm doing! Any minute now, the old girl will…"

The engine grumbled stubbornly. The van shook with Traveler's efforts but continued to lay dormant. He cursed and pleaded, but nothing happened. Toasty sighed.

"Have you tried jiggling something?"

"Check under the hood, I'll bet the toads got stuck there," Passenger advised.

"Is it the battery?" Allen said. "Did you remember to gas it up?"

"Everyone in the peanut gallery be quiet!" Traveler barked. "That's not how this baby works! I just gotta…find…the sweet spot…"

He kept turning the key and pumping the gas. The engine continued to grumble. The van was lifeless.

"Does anybody know a good towing service?" Passenger sighed. He took out a cell phone, but Traveler snatched it away.

"Wait! Hold on! I know just the guy to call for moments like these!" Traveler muttered to himself as he dialed the number, then continued to mutter while simultaneously jamming a cigarette in his mouth. "Come on, pick up," he whispered, tapping the wheel impatiently with his free hand.



FADE IN:

INT. MURPHY LAW'S OFFICE, NOON

A thick cloud of smoke billows into view, and at its center sits a man, surrounded by a half-filled glass of whiskey, the bottle it came from, an ashtray with four spent cigarettes, and small stacks of papers, two of which are currently nestled in his hands. He is casually flipping between the pages, seemingly paying no attention to their contents, throwing some into a nearby wastebasket while adding others to a pile.

NARRATOR

For anybody out there who thinks that a private detective's life is nothing but glamor, guns, gin, and girls, I've got a coupla bitter pills for them to swallow. Most of my work's done in the office, making love to some worn-out old typewriter, or shoving a beaten-up pen full of dry ink around on a scratch of paper. Today was no different, or at least it woulda been, if it weren't for…

A telephone rings. The man stops what he is doing, drops the papers on his desk, and picks up the receiver with disdain. He is MURPHY LAW: hard, handsome, his voice a harsh growl, and he is about to give the unfortunate soul on the other end a bit of the business.

MURPHY

Murphy Law detective agency.

TRAVELER

Hi! Mr. Law! I… Shut up, I'm on the phone! Yes, he picked up! Yes, it's really Murphy Law!

MURPHY

Hey, pal, or whoever this is, I hope for your sake that this isn't a prank call. I'm a bit tied up at the moment and not in the mood for any funny business.

TRAVELER

Oh! Oh no, Mr. Law, this is strictly professional! You see, our van broke down and — shut up, I'm telling him! Will you be… Ahem! Yes, err, our van broke down, and we were sort of hoping that since you're the expert on solving problems when everything that could go wrong, HAS…

MURPHY sighs with the weariness of a man beleaguered beyond the capacity for description.

MURPHY

Listen, Mister, uh…

TRAVELER

I am a traveler of the cosmos, on an eternal journey of insight, elucidation, and transcendental illumination!

There is a slight pause. MURPHY pinches the bridge of his nose.

MURPHY

Right. Mr. Traveler. I can solve a lot of problems, but vehicular issues aren't one of them. Maybe you should consider a mechanic, or a towing service…

TRAVELER

But you're our only hope, Mr. Law! The van! She won't! BUDGE! We're giving it all we've got!

MURPHY sighs.

MURPHY

Have you tried jiggling something?

A voice calls out in the background.

TOASTY

That's what I suggested!

The voices become an intermingled melange of noise. MURPHY growls softly and hangs up the phone, then takes another swig from his glass.

MURPHY

I'm getting too old for this.

FADE OUT.



"Well?" Passenger pressed. "What did Same Spade say?"

Traveler frowned as he handed the cell phone back. "I'm afraid we're on our own, boys. Not to worry, I think I almost have it this time. Maybe if I turn the ignition and pump the brakes and gas in a certain pattern…"

Traveler continued to try and revive the van, while Passenger yawned. Toasty and Allen just looked at each other.

"Never thought I'd end my stint as an SCP writer by being stuck here," Toasty said. Allen smiled sympathetically.

"Yeah. Still, Happy Birthday, Adam."

"Thanks, Dana."

Toasty sighed, rolled down a window, and looked out at the stars as the last of the sun's light faded on the horizon. Then, slowly, he closed his eyes.

SCP-621-EX

And Mister_Toasty…








It's a me-a







With special guests: various members of the O5 Council, SCP-179, SCP-208, SCP-423, SCP-682, SCP-1111, SCP-2747, SCP-3143, SCP-3456, SCP-3700, Placeholder McDoctorate, and Dr. Wondertainment.

And of course, extra special thanks to everyone who ever had anything to do with any of my articles.

Live long and prosper.

So long, space cowboy.

Goonies never say die.

And as always…

Keep circulating the tapes!













Toasty opened his eyes again. Traveler was still trying to coax the van to life, but it kept on stalling.

"Well," said Dana Allen, "at least this isn't the worst birthday you've ever had."

Everyone else looked up at each other, then glared at him and screamed:

"SHUT UP, ALLEN!!!!"





THE END

happy-birthday-mister-toasty.raw_source: [[>]] [[include :scp-wiki:info:start]] "Happy Birthday, Mister Toasty!" by  [[*user (Mister_Toasty)]] @@ @@ [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/mister-toasty| My author page]]] [[include :scp-wiki:info:end]] [[/>]] @@ @@ __Location__:  Solar System, close orbit of Sol @@ @@ Although there's no such thing as "day" or "night" in extraterrestrial terms, it was still -- loosely -- another regular day in the cosmos, as these things go.  [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-179|Sauelsuesor]]] was peacefully orbiting the sun when something stirred her awake.  She immediately snapped to attention, eyes widening in alarm, and thrust one of her sable arms directly at the threat hurtling inexorably through space. @@ @@ @@ @@ But I'm sure it's nothing to worry about. @@ @@ @@ @@ In the meantime, it was December 30th, and that's Mister Toasty's birthday!
