A storm rages outside, raindrops hitting the cabin's exterior walls with the force of claws. A single figure trudges towards the shelter, heavy with muddy water and the waterproof bag slung over her shoulder. All that's visible of her face is a pair of cracked coke-bottle glasses, bloodshot eyes behind them.

From the outside, the cabin is more boarded up window than it is shelter, nails and scrap wood sticking out at all sorts of odd ends and angles. She pushes the door open and is greeted by the conspiracy board inside. Her wall is covered in newspapers and magazines and any photographs she could get her hands on; a constant reminder that the world outside of the boundary they create is dangerous.

The oldest, worn, torn, most perceived piece of newspaper she has is right her the rotting mattress she sleeps on. Several Injured and One Dead in Freak Firework Incident. The day she left home for good, freed from any reason to stick around. On the rotting mattress she sleeps on, she dumps out the bag. Her supplies: pilfered batteries, cans of food, a music disc, bullets. Everything she'll need until she's forced out into the world for another trip.

Her name is Jessie Tamlin and she is a shadow on the wall, she is the Blackwoods Beast, she is Bigfoot. She is a man with an axe, with a chainsaw, with a rifle. She is whatever it takes to get people from getting too interested in poking around. She's made a good life for herself, by herself.

There's no power, which isn't new for her. She makes due with candles and a flashlight. A wind brushes past, the whistling sound it makes seeping through the cracks of her shelter has a rhythm like laughter to it. It's enough for her to pause and take in the feeling of an omen.

She finds an empty area to sit and meditate through the storm. She closes her eyes, refusing to sleep but dreaming nonetheless. With enough maladaptive daydreaming, she can pretend that she's in her former apartment, elevated far above the floodwaters. It's sunny even, warm light casting through an open window. Her brother is with her, standing in just the right position to keep the sun out of her eyes.

It was a peaceful life she once lead. What changed? Or what was always there in the first place?

Joey: Hey, do you remember our old friend Lily Veselka?

A jolt runs up Jessie's body. She's used to the feeling of weightlessness that comes with projecting herself into Oneiroi West. With her body confined solely to the space she built for it, she's become well practiced in astral projection. But this is a violent feeling that overtakes her, as though she were flying and something has swatted her down.

She lands hard into the jaws off a childhood memory.

<Jessie is ten years old. She is waiting for her uncle to pick her up from school. She is waiting at the bus stop alone. Lily approaches and points at the empty space on the bench.>

Lily: Can I sit here?

Jessie: Who are you?

Lily: I'm Lily!

<Jessie shifts uncomfortably.>

Jessie: I don't know you!

Lily: But you could!

<Lily hops onto the bench next to her. She reaches out to touch Jessie's kandi bracelets. Jessie pulls her arm away.>

Lily: I like your bracelets!

Jessie: Thanks…

<Joey arrives on his bicycle. Their uncle has gotten drunk and passed out again, but he doesn't want Jessie to know about that, so he covers for him. The bus arrives. Lily stands up first.>

Lily: Let's get good seats.

<Jessie is hesitant. She usually tries to find any empty seat and pray no one tries to sit next to her, but today the bus is packed. Is it worth the chance that her bench mate might be cruel?>

<Lily grabs Jessie's wrist.>

Lily: Don't hold me up.

Jessie: <Flustered> Um, sorry.

<Lily walks Jessie all the way to the back of the bus. The last row is empty. Lily lets Jessie take the window seat.>

Lily: You're really quiet. What're you thinking about?

<Jessie fidgets with her bracelets, fingering the large flying saucer shaped charm on her favorite one. Through the cracks in this memory she can see herself clinging onto Joey as he struggles to peddle them home. There are no cracks, everything is how it was.>

Jessie: I'm not supposed to get too close to anyone. In case the aliens come back for me.

<Lily leans in conspiratorially.>

Lily: The aliens?

<Jessie nods.>

Jessie: I got abducted when I was five, but they decided to take my parents instead. That's why I live with my uncle.

Lily: Is that why you always sit alone.

Jessie: Yep. That way, no one else becomes a target.

Lily: I bet I could fight them off.

Jessie: You think so?

<The cracks struggle to conceal themselves. The long rides home with her brother are far too burned into her memory. Jessie digs her fingers into her hair and pulls.>

Jessie: What am I saying? Where am I?

Lily: Hey, hey, don't get overwhelmed! Wouldn't you rather be here with me than ride home with him?

<Jessie stands and starts marching towards the front of the bus.>

Jessie: I want off this bus now!

<Lily grabs Jessie's wrist and she falls back, hitting the forest ground hard.>

Jessie looks up at her cabin in the woods. Whipping ice cold winds scratching at her through her many layers. She thinks again of that damning question Joey once asked her, remembering, like she remembers all things, the day in perfect detail.

Joey: Hey, do you remember our old friend Lily Veselka?

Jessie: Who?

Joey: Lily! We went to school together. The three of us were best friends.

One of his new obsessions, something for him to insist until it became true. As though his mind were incapable of imaging a world where the two of them had different experiences.

Jessie: Joey, we were in different grades, I doubt we shared a friend group in school.

Joey: No, no I swear you two were really close! You really don’t remember her?

Jessie: Nope.

Even this ghost that hunts her now must be shared.

Once she's calmed down and reorganized her thoughts, she sits and projects out of her body again. This time she's ready for whatever's out there. She settles her spirit down in the forest and looks around. There's a thrill to this moment, of finally confronting this ghost, of putting down one of her brother's obsessions.

"Hello?" She calls, only for her voice to echo around the inside of her mind and slam back into her. The distant sound of TV static gets louder with every steps she takes, no matter the direction it's in.

In the place where her cabin should be is her old apartment bedroom. It's as though the room has been cut out of the complex it once was a part of and dropped haphazardly onto the marshy ground. Throwing all her momentum into it, she shoulders open the front door and nearly falls headfirst into a her-shaped hole in the floor.

<Jessie is seventeen and she is moving all of her stuff into the apartment she now shares with her brother. Joey is busy, and she has no friends to call for help. Lily appears in her doorway with a housewarming gift.>

Jessie: Woah! Lily, you made it! I thought I'd never see you again!

Lily: Surprise!

<Lily sets down her gift on the still-being-set-up desk: a box set of the X-Files on DVD. It's more thoughtful than any gift Joey has ever gotten her. Every little green man and plastic flying saucer are a reminder of how little he pays attention. Never mind him, it's Lily who deserves her attention. Jessie gives her a hug.>

Jessie: I'd offer you a place to sit, but I don't know which box my chair got put in.

Lily: I can stand, it's just good to see you again! How have you been?

Jessie: Fine. I'm on some medications now which have helped me sleep better.

<While she talks, Jessie unpacks her boxes. The first thing she gets out is her trusted cork board, which gets first pick of the wall space.>

Jessie: People thought I sounded a little nutty as a kid, but you couldn't imagine how Joey sounds calling all medicine placebos. God forbid his precious little sister have diagnosable mental illness!

<Lily reaches out and takes Jessie's hand. Jessie stops in her tracks. Lily's thumb brushes against the beads of her bracelets. Outside of her room, Joey laughs with a group of friends.>

Lily: I thought you said you didn't have any friends to help you?

Jessie: I don't have friends. I have Joey's friends.

<The sound of a party Jessie is a plus one to rages on outside. The apartment goes dead silent. It's just the two of them.>

Lily: Now we have the place to ourselves. I'm sorry he treats you that way.

<Jessie shifts, unsure whether or not to tear herself out of Lily's grasp.>

Jessie: I shouldn't complain. He's good to me.

Lily: That doesn't mean you don't have anything to complain about! You can trust me to be there for you when you're having a hard time.

<It's a beautiful feeling, having someone to hand her frustrations over to. But the novelty of this feeling is what gives the illusion away. There is no childhood best friend. There is no friend that she didn't share with Joey. What is she thinking? Her best friend is right here.>

Jessie: I really appreciate this gift! I wish I had something to give in return.

Lily: It's a housewarming gift, it doesn't need to be returned!

Jessie: Still…

<Jessie interlocks Lily's fingers with her own. She selects the largest of her kandi bracelets and drags it off her arm, over her hand, and onto Lily's wrist. Lily looks at it in awe.>

Lily: Oh, I just can't accept this! You spent so much time on it!

<Jessie looks at her arms. Somewhere between living here and her choice to leave, she lost all of her old bracelets and supplies. It would do her no good to cling to a memory of them.>

Jessie: I've… never actually gotten to give someone a bracelet like that before.

Lily: It's so beautiful! Does it do anything special?

Jessie: Uh, no, it's just beads. I'm not really an anartist.

Lily: You made anomalous fireworks.

Jessie: If this is supposed to be a memory, that's an anachronism. Besides, those almost killed me.

Lily: Still. The bracelet is really nice. I can't show my appreciation enough.

<Lily approaches Jessie, backing her up into the wall. Jessie gets that familiar prey animal feeling. Come on, just relax. Jessie puts her hand up to cover Lily's lips before they touch her.>

Lily: Why do you fight me?

Jessie: Look, it's not that I don't appreciate the wish fulfillment. But, even if you were real, I'd still have to share you with someone else.

Jessie strains to push Lily out. Her bedroom spirals around her, years of reorganizing furniture, trying to make this space she shares with her brother feel like her own. A real memory pops up, featuring a real friend Jessie once had, even if he too was commons.

Jessie: I’ve gone through all the school records for every school both me and Joey attended at the same time. There was not one person named Lily Veselka at any of them!

Tangerine: Why does this bother you so much?

How does one explain to a man with a clear conflict of interest why this bothers her so much? Jessie paces, making a nuisance of herself to her downstairs neighbors, to get the frustrated energy out.

Jessie: It's driving me crazy! He keeps trying to get me to remember her. I’m used to him assuming or conflating things about me, but now he’s just made up a childhood friend I supposedly had! It's like me not remembering this chick is a personal slight against him.

Every deviation will be personal to a man invested in a false ideal, but who wants to unpack that?

Tangerine: <Painfully neutral> Maybe you did know her. Maybe you just forgot.

Jessie: I don't just forget things! Not like this! I wish Joey could just believe that I had one experience that he didn't have!

Tangerine: Are you sure you're not just letting your frustration block out important memories? Lily Veselka was a really nice person and a really good friend of mine back in school. Maybe she's just slipped your mind after so much time apart.

Even just the memory of this memory is enough to make Jessie freeze. As though the cold realization that dawns upon her is fresh every time.

Jessie: How did you go to school with Veselka if she’s supposedly my childhood best friend?

There is a dreamworld that exists in the mind of every lonely teenager that managed to become a lonely adult. The dream that their few current friends were always there in the years that they needed friends the most. This is not a dream Jessie feels like indulging.

Tangerine: She moved around a lot. Yeah, that’s right, she must’ve changed schools and that’s why you can’t find her in the records.

Jessie storms out of the dream of her bedroom, finding the rest of her apartment waiting for her. It's full of holes she used to fill. Careful to avoid falling in, she storms up to her brother's bedroom door and kicks it open.

"I've had enough of you, Veselka!"

Joey lays haphazardly splayed across his bed, his head in Lily's lap. A hole in the ceiling lets rainwater drip onto his face. Every time a droplet hits, he trembles and Lily wipes it away. Lily looks like a sickly young girl, her skin tight over her bones, cheeks sunken, even her pale blue dress is reminiscent of a hospital gown. But as she turns to face Jessie, head cocked to one side, she brandishes a smile no human should ever wear.

"Oh, Jessie, oh Jessie, is that any way to talk to your best friend?" Lily says, grazing her claws against Joey's forehead. "This is so unbecoming of you.”

"I don't know where you came from, but you're not my friend!" She points a single finger outwards, as if to manifest a banishing spell. "You need to get out of here!"

"What would your fellow shut-ins in Oneiroi West think of you shouting like this?" Lily says with a pout. "All I ever wanted was to be friends, but you just have to keep shutting little ole me out." Lily puts her hands against her cheeks in a mock imitation of cuteness, a flutter of the eyelashes for emphasis. She's wearing the bracelet Jessie gave her.

"I'm serious!" Jessie turns red. "I don't want what you're selling."

Lily's smile grows angry. "You won't be able to escape me forever," Lily squeezes Joey like a doll. "I might not be able to get into your pretty little head, but I got into his just fine. Almost got him to blow you up with your own fireworks!"

Jessie swallows a lump in her throat. "That was… you?" She struggles to look through the eyes of her body back at home. The oldest and most preserved newspaper she has is from the last day she had with family, the day her art project exploded on her and she knew she would never be safe around people ever again. "No, that couldn't have been you. You're just a mind parasite."

"Don't believe me?" She leans forward and out of her body, torso elongating outwards, body spindly yet distinctly spider-like. She nods her head towards a hole on the bedside table, shaped like a tiny plastic flying saucer. "Take a look."

<Jessie is twenty-four. Outside, her friends and family are setting up an art show. She's setting something up too; a firework show, each firework of her own design. It's experimental and it will be beautiful. No one else looks for her. Lily silently sneaks in.>

Lily: <Playful> Boo!

<Jessie startles.>

Jessie: Hey! Nobody's supposed to see this yet!

Lily: Oops! Oh well, guess you don't have any reason to throw me out now that I know the secret!

<Lily grazes her fingers over the fireworks. Jessie turns red and returns to her work.>

Lily: What's this all for?

Jessie: Joey. A little surprise for him. He… doesn't like to think of it this way, but he did raise me. Thought I should give him a show of appreciation.

<Lily comes up behind her and drags her fingers through Jessie's hair. Jessie shivers.>

Lily: I think more people should be showing you some appreciation.

Jessie: For what? Staying in my room all hours of the day until I'm forced to socialize?

Lily: Yes.

<Jessie stops moving.>

Jessie: I don't know why you try so hard to flatter me. Weren't we just sharing hateful words?

Lily: What's wrong with living in a little fantasy? Why don't you just let me convince you that I could be a friend?

<Jessie walks up to the door and pokes her head. Joey is surrounded by friends. He can exist without her presence hovering over her. She slowly closes the door.>

Jessie: Because it's not real. My whole life I've been criticized for being so attached to things that are not real. I don't need to start indulging that again. No matter how tempting it is.

<Jessie tries to focus and push Lily out of her mind like she did with her other memories. Something shifts, but Lily herself doesn't disappear. Lily smiles, more teeth than lip.>

Jessie: Why are you still here?

Lily: Silly Jessie! You can't push me out of a memory that I was actually there for!

<Lily shimmers and takes on the appearance of Joey. She's gotten in his head and convinced him that setting off these fireworks is the only thing he needs to do right now.>

Lily|Joey: End of the line. Except you can't even die when I want you to!

<Lily pulls out a lighter and holds it up to the box of fireworks. Jessie pulls on her hair.>

Jessie: Twenty years of knowing death could sneak up on me at any moment, and I don't catch the one time that it did.

Lily|Joey: I could make him remember. I could make him remember death, and then while I’m at it I could make all of his friends forget about him too. And when he’s all alone and broken with no friends I’ll make sure he remembers how to escape it all. And then once he’s here I’ll tear his pathetic consciousness apart!

<How frustrating it is, for the one moment she's given a dilemma and her brother is all Lily has to hold over her head.>

Jessie: And what the hell do you want from me, then!

Lily|Joey: I just want to be friends.

Jessie: And yet you try to kill me. It's like you're obsessed with me, but it's not even me who gets to be obsessed over.

Lily|Joey: According to you, everyone is lying to you and out to get you. At least I'm honest with my intentions.

<Lily winks. Jessie cringes.>

Jessie: No, you're worse than that. You pretend to be honest with your intentions when you're not, just like everyone else in my life!

Lily|Joey: Quit fighting me. I can rewrite your history, it will be you and me forever.

Jessie: Even that's not true. You're telling me this with my brother's mouth. It's always just been me and him forever.

<Lily shrugs off Joey's face and sparks the lighter. She's still wearing the kandi bracelet.>

Lily: It's not that hard. Let me into your mind completely or I kill your brother and then you.

<Jessie crosses her arms.>

Jessie: Okay, do it then.

<Lily's lighter goes out.>

Lily: Huh?

<Jessie marches forward.>

Jessie: Go on. Kill him. And then kill me too. Kill the whole world. Do whatever you want. Go ahead.

Lily: Uh. Okay! I will! I don't need you!

<Lily in Joey's mind lights the fuse. By the time the fireworks go off, Joey won't even remember what he did. Lily struggles to get the lighter to stay lit.>

Jessie: I don't think you can do shit. I ran away to keep the assassins or the aliens or the shitty little demons away from my family, but you're not even worth it.

<Jessie grabs Lily by the hair.>

"Let go of me, you brat!" Lily squeals, clawing at Jessie's hand. Her mouth opens sideways and centipede like mandibles take a snap at Jessie's arm.

This is her moment. Finally, a moment for herself.

"You want it to be me and you forever, huh?" She wrangles Lily off the bed, more cat fight than wrestling move. "Then we're going down together!" Jessie throws herself into one of the many holes in the ground, dragging Lily down with her own weight.

.

.

.

<She expected that to be the end of the dream. Either her spirit would find its way back to her body or it would get lost like most of the spirits that attempt to join the Oneiroi. Except she's not really lost. She exists on a long, flat, empty plane. The only other inhabitant is Lily, sitting on a bench at a bus stop. Jessie marches over and sits next to her.>

Jessie: What are we waiting for? What is this?

<Lily shifts uncomfortably.>

Lily: Nothing. I'm not strong enough to do anything else.

Jessie: Oh. Really?

<Lily rolls her shoulders, something of a shrug mixed with a stretch.>

Lily: This is all that's left of the world I used to live in. And this-

<She gestures to herself. She is hazy and blurry, like the memory of a childhood friend.>

Lily: -is all that's left of me.

<She hisses out a sneering laugh.>

Lily: Just my luck that I waste the last of myself on a mind that rejects me completely. Couldn't even finish the job and see you dead.

<Jessie looks around, but there's nothing to look around at, not even a gust of wind to blow through their hair.>

Jessie: I'm assuming this is not what your world always looked like?

Lily: Was that a question?

Jessie: Uh, what did your world look like?

Lily: I don't know, normal? I only really know what it looked like in other people's memories.

Jessie: You're really bad at answering a basic question.

Lily: As if you're any better! I've sorted through your mind and you haven't held a successful conversation once!

Jessie: Oh, this is such bullshit! You claim to want to be childhood friends but you know way more about me than I do you.

<Lily glares through her.>

Lily: You want to know about me? Fine! I went to a normal school with normal people and then someone died and they put my in a cell for the rest of my life.

<Lily clenches her fists.>

Lily: And then I destroyed my cell and killed everyone who kept me there. And then I killed everyone else. And that was it. End show, exit universe right.

<Jessie hears the sound of rain hitting her roof, her body still awaits her.>

Jessie: Wow. You're really pathetic.

<Lily huffs.>

Jessie: I mean, you put up a cool fight, really frightened me up until the end there. And I was really banking on the idea that you didn't actually have anything to hold over me. But I thought I'd at least warrant a cooler demon to hunt me. You look like you're about to become nothing.

Lily: I could still make my final act killing your brother!

Jessie: I don't think that's true.

<Jessie straightens up.>

Jessie: I… gather you didn't have too many friends in containment.

Lily: I was too important.

Jessie: … sure.

Lily: I'm spilling my guts to you and you can't even be nice to me?

Jessie: Nice?

<Jessie throws her hands up into the empty air.>

Jessie: Nice!? I'm being nice! We are sitting on the last remaining piece of a dead world after you threatened my brother! I'm being so fucking nice right now! I'm the nicest person you've ever met!

<The two childhood-friend-less childhood friends turn away from each other.>

Jessie: … Tell me I'm not the nicest person you've ever met.

Lily: Your brother is nicer.

Jessie: Oh, whatever, fuck you.

Lily: That's probably why he has real friends and people who like him.

Jessie: It pisses me off that in all the memories you tried to fuck with it's always Joey that you're replacing. Do you know how weird that makes this?

Lily: I can only really exist in what you remember. Not my fault he's the only other person who loves you.

<A pause.>

Lily: I mean he's the only person who loves you.

Jessie: What did you say the first time?

Lily: I said he's the only person who loves you.

Jessie: Oh.

<After a minute, Jessie's face scrunches up, she stands and points a finger at Lily's chest.>

Jessie: You need to exist in people's memories to exist at all. But, what if you could exist in dreams instead?

Lily: Those count as memories.

<They stare at each other.>

Lily: Was there a point?

Jessie: I could take you to Oneiroi West!

Lily: You need to dream in order to enter Oneiroi West.

Jessie: I dream. You could inhabit my mind and come with me. On one condition.

<A pause.>

Lily: Stop pausing. What's your condition?

Jessie: I'm giving you space to-

<Jessie closes her hand into a fist.>

Jessie: Stay out of my brother's mind! Or anyone else's. You will stay in my mind and my mind only.

<Lily give her an incredulous look.>

Lily: Really? You'd rather die on this hill then just let me die completely?

Jessie: What can I say?

<Jessie looks at the kandi bracelet on Lily's wrist.>

Jessie: Having a childhood best friend wasn't all that bad.

On another plane, a thousand miles away, Joey sits up in bed and looks around the tiny ramshackle apartment he and his friends pooled their money on. It’s raining outside and there’s a tiny hole in the ceiling right above his pillow. He really ought to get that patched one of these days.

it-was-all-just-the-dream-of-an-angel.raw_source: ===== [[include component:preview text=At least I'm honest with my intentions. ]] ===== [[include :scp-wiki:component:info-ayers |lang=en |page=component:info-ayers |authorPage=https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/kingofmice-author-page |comments= = …ᘛ⁐̤ᕐᐷ ]] [[>]] [[module Rate]] [[/>]] A storm rages outside, raindrops hitting the cabin's exterior walls with the force of claws. A single figure trudges towards the shelter, heavy with muddy water and the waterproof bag slung over her shoulder. All that's visible of her face is a pair of cracked coke-bottle glasses, bloodshot eyes behind them. From the outside, the cabin is more boarded up window than it is shelter, nails and scrap wood sticking out at all sorts of odd ends and angles. She pushes the door open and is greeted by the conspiracy board inside. Her wall is covered in newspapers and magazines and any photographs she could get her hands on; a constant reminder that the world outside of the boundary they create is dangerous. The oldest, worn, torn, most perceived piece of newspaper she has is right her the rotting mattress she sleeps on. **Several Injured and One Dead in Freak Firework Incident**. The day she left home for good, freed from any reason to stick around. On the rotting mattress she sleeps on, she dumps out the bag. Her supplies: pilfered batteries, cans of food, a music disc, bullets. Everything she'll need until she's forced out into the world for another trip. Her name is Jessie Tamlin and she is a shadow on the wall, she is //the Blackwoods Beast//, she is Bigfoot. She is a man with an axe, with a chainsaw, with a rifle. She is whatever it takes to get people from getting too interested in poking around. She's made a good life for herself, by herself. There's no power, which isn't new for her. She makes due with candles and a flashlight. A wind brushes past, the whistling sound it makes seeping through the cracks of her shelter has a rhythm like laughter to it. It's enough for her to pause and take in the feeling of an omen. She finds an empty area to sit and meditate through the storm. She closes her eyes, refusing to sleep but dreaming nonetheless. With enough maladaptive daydreaming, she can pretend that she's in her former apartment, elevated far above the floodwaters. It's sunny even, warm light casting through an open window. Her brother is with her, standing in just the right position to keep the sun out of her eyes. It was a peaceful life she once lead. What changed? Or what was always there in the first place? **Joey:** Hey, do you remember our old friend [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-3002 |Lily Veselka]]]? A jolt runs up Jessie's body. She's used to the feeling of weightlessness that comes with projecting herself into Oneiroi West. With her body confined solely to the space she built for it, she's become well practiced in astral projection. But this is a violent feeling that overtakes her, as though she were flying and something has swatted her down. She lands hard into the jaws off a childhood memory. //// **Lily:** Can I sit here? **Jessie:** Who are you? **Lily:** I'm Lily! //// **Jessie:** I don't know you! **Lily:** But you could! //// **Lily:** I like your bracelets! **Jessie:** Thanks... //<--Joey arrives on his bicycle. Their uncle has gotten drunk and passed out again, but he doesn't want Jessie to know about that, so he covers for him.-- The bus arrives. Lily stands up first.>// **Lily:** Let's get good seats. //// //// **Lily:** Don't hold me up. **Jessie:** //// Um, sorry. //// **Lily:** You're really quiet. What're you thinking about? //// **Jessie:** I'm not supposed to get too close to anyone. In case the aliens come back for me. //// **Lily:** The aliens? //// **Jessie:** I got abducted when I was five, but they decided to take my parents instead. That's why I live with my uncle. **Lily:** Is that why you always sit alone. **Jessie:** Yep. That way, no one else becomes a target. **Lily:** I bet I could fight them off. **Jessie:** You think so? //// **Jessie:** What am I saying? Where am I? **Lily:** Hey, hey, don't get overwhelmed! Wouldn't you rather be here with me than ride home with him? //// **Jessie:** I want off this bus now! //// Jessie looks up at her cabin in the woods. Whipping ice cold winds scratching at her through her many layers. She thinks again of that damning question Joey once asked her, remembering, like she remembers all things, the day in perfect detail. **Joey:** Hey, do you remember our old friend Lily Veselka? **Jessie:** Who? **Joey:** Lily! We went to school together. The three of us were best friends. One of his new obsessions, something for him to insist until it became true. As though his mind were incapable of imaging a world where the two of them had different experiences. **Jessie:** Joey, we were in different grades, I doubt we shared a friend group in school. **Joey:** No, no I swear you two were really close! You really don’t remember her? **Jessie:** Nope. Even this ghost that hunts her now must be shared. Once she's calmed down and reorganized her thoughts, she sits and projects out of her body again. This time she's ready for whatever's out there. She settles her spirit down in the forest and looks around. There's a thrill to this moment, of finally confronting this ghost, of putting down one of her brother's obsessions. "Hello?" She calls, only for her voice to echo around the inside of her mind and slam back into her. The distant sound of TV static gets louder with every steps she takes, no matter the direction it's in. In the place where her cabin should be is her old apartment bedroom. It's as though the room has been cut out of the complex  it once was a part of and dropped haphazardly onto the marshy ground. Throwing all her momentum into it, she shoulders open the front door and nearly falls headfirst into a her-shaped hole in the floor. //// **Jessie:** Woah! Lily, you made it! I thought I'd never see you again! **Lily:** Surprise! //// **Jessie:** I'd offer you a place to sit, but I don't know which box my chair got put in. **Lily:** I can stand, it's just good to see you again! How have you been? **Jessie:** Fine. I'm on some medications now which have helped me sleep better. //// **Jessie:** People thought I sounded a little nutty as a kid, but you couldn't imagine how Joey sounds calling all medicine placebos. God forbid his precious little sister have diagnosable mental illness! //// **Lily:** I thought you said you didn't have any friends to help you? **Jessie:** I don't have friends. I have Joey's friends. //<--The sound of a party Jessie is a plus one to rages on outside.-- The apartment goes dead silent. It's just the two of them.>// **Lily:** Now we have the place to ourselves. I'm sorry he treats you that way. //// **Jessie:** I shouldn't complain. He's good to me. **Lily:** That doesn't mean you don't have anything to complain about! You can trust me to be there for you when you're having a hard time. //// **Jessie:** I really appreciate this gift! I wish I had something to give in return. **Lily:** It's a housewarming gift, it doesn't need to be returned! **Jessie:** Still... //// **Lily:** Oh, I just can't accept this! You spent so much time on it! //// **Jessie:** I've... never actually gotten to give someone a bracelet like that before. **Lily:** It's so beautiful! Does it do anything special? **Jessie:** Uh, no, it's just beads. I'm not really an anartist. **Lily:** You made anomalous fireworks. **Jessie:** If this is supposed to be a memory, that's an anachronism. Besides, those almost killed me. **Lily:** Still. The bracelet is really nice. I can't show my appreciation enough. //// **Lily:** Why do you fight me? **Jessie:** Look, it's not that I don't appreciate the wish fulfillment. But, even if you were real, I'd still have to share you with someone else. Jessie strains to push Lily out. Her bedroom spirals around her, years of reorganizing furniture, trying to make this space she shares with her brother feel like her own. A real memory pops up, featuring a real friend Jessie once had, even if he too was commons. **Jessie:** I’ve gone through all the school records for every school both me and Joey attended at the same time. There was not one person named Lily Veselka at any of them! **Tangerine:** Why does this bother you so much? How does one explain to a man with a clear conflict of interest //why this bothers her so much//? Jessie paces, making a nuisance of herself to her downstairs neighbors, to get the frustrated energy out. **Jessie:** It's driving me crazy! He keeps trying to get me to remember her. I’m used to him assuming or conflating things about me, but now he’s just made up a childhood friend I supposedly had! It's like me not remembering this chick is a personal slight against him. Every deviation will be personal to a man invested in a false ideal, but who wants to unpack that? **Tangerine:** //// Maybe you did know her. Maybe you just forgot. **Jessie:** I don't just forget things! Not like this! I wish Joey could just believe that I had one experience that he didn't have! **Tangerine:** Are you sure you're not just letting your frustration block out important memories? Lily Veselka was a really nice person and a really good friend of mine back in school. Maybe she's just slipped your mind after so much time apart. Even just the memory of this memory is enough to make Jessie freeze. As though the cold realization that dawns upon her is fresh every time. **Jessie:** How did //you// go to school with Veselka if she’s supposedly my childhood best friend? There is a dreamworld that exists in the mind of every lonely teenager that managed to become a lonely adult. The dream that their few current friends were always there in the years that they needed friends the most. This is not a dream Jessie feels like indulging. **Tangerine:** She moved around a lot. Yeah, that’s right, she must’ve changed schools and that’s why you can’t find her in the records. Jessie storms out of the dream of her bedroom, finding the rest of her apartment waiting for her. It's full of holes she used to fill. Careful to avoid falling in, she storms up to her brother's bedroom door and kicks it open. "I've had enough of you, Veselka!" Joey lays haphazardly splayed across his bed, his head in Lily's lap. A hole in the ceiling lets rainwater drip onto his face. Every time a droplet hits, he trembles and Lily wipes it away. Lily looks like a sickly young girl, her skin tight over her bones, cheeks sunken, even her pale blue dress is reminiscent of a hospital gown. But as she turns to face Jessie, head cocked to one side, she brandishes a smile no human should ever wear. "Oh, Jessie, oh Jessie, is that any way to talk to your best friend?" Lily says, grazing her claws against Joey's forehead. "This is so unbecoming of you.” "I don't know where you came from, but you're not my friend!" She points a single finger outwards, as if to manifest a banishing spell. "You need to get out of here!"      "What would your fellow shut-ins in Oneiroi West think of you shouting like this?" Lily says with a pout. "All I ever wanted was to be friends, but you just have to keep shutting little ole me out." Lily puts her hands against her cheeks in a mock imitation of cuteness, a flutter of the eyelashes for emphasis. She's wearing the bracelet Jessie gave her.      "I'm serious!" Jessie turns red. "I don't want what you're selling." Lily's smile grows angry. "You won't be able to escape me forever," Lily squeezes Joey like a doll. "I might not be able to get into your pretty little head, but I got into his just fine. Almost got him to blow you up with your own fireworks!" Jessie swallows a lump in her throat. "That was... you?" She struggles to look through the eyes of her body back at home. The oldest and most preserved newspaper she has is from the last day she had with family, the day her art project exploded on her and she knew she would never be safe around people ever again. "No, that couldn't have been you. You're just a mind parasite." "Don't believe me?" She leans forward and out of her body, torso elongating outwards, body spindly yet distinctly spider-like. She nods her head towards a hole on the bedside table, shaped like a tiny plastic flying saucer. "Take a look." //// **Lily:** //// Boo! //// **Jessie:** Hey! Nobody's supposed to see this yet! **Lily:** Oops! Oh well, guess you don't have any reason to throw me out now that I know the secret! //// **Lily:** What's this all for? **Jessie:** Joey. A little surprise for him. He... doesn't like to think of it this way, but he did raise me. Thought I should give him a show of appreciation. //// **Lily:** I think more people should be showing you some appreciation. **Jessie:** For what? Staying in my room all hours of the day until I'm forced to socialize? **Lily:** Yes. //// **Jessie:** I don't know why you try so hard to flatter me. Weren't we just sharing hateful words? **Lily:** What's wrong with living in a little fantasy? Why don't you just let me convince you that I could be a friend? //// **Jessie:** Because it's not real. My whole life I've been criticized for being so attached to things that are //not real//. I don't need to start indulging that again. No matter how tempting it is. //// **Jessie:** Why are you still here? **Lily:** Silly Jessie! You can't push me out of a memory that I was actually there for! //// **Lily|Joey:** End of the line. Except you can't even die when I want you to! //// **Jessie:** Twenty years of //knowing// death could sneak up on me at any moment, and I don't catch the one time that it did. **Lily|Joey:** I could make him remember. I could make him remember death, and then while I’m at it I could make all of his friends forget about him too. And when he’s all alone and broken with no friends I’ll make sure he remembers how to escape it all. And then once he’s here I’ll tear his pathetic consciousness apart! //// **Jessie:** And what the hell do you want from me, then! **Lily|Joey:** I just want to be friends. **Jessie:** And yet you try to kill me. It's like you're obsessed with me, but it's not even //me// who gets to be obsessed over. **Lily|Joey:** According to you, everyone is lying to you and out to get you. At least I'm honest with my intentions. //// **Jessie:** No, you're worse than that. You pretend to be honest with your intentions when you're not, just like everyone else in my life! **Lily|Joey:** Quit fighting me. I can rewrite your history, it will be you and me forever. **Jessie:** Even that's not true. You're telling me this with my brother's mouth. It's always just been me and him forever. //// **Lily:** It's not that hard. Let me into your mind completely or I kill your brother and then you. //// **Jessie:** Okay, do it then. //// **Lily:** Huh? //// **Jessie:** Go on. Kill him. And then kill me too. Kill the whole world. Do whatever you want. Go ahead. **Lily:** Uh. Okay! I will! I don't need you! //<--Lily in Joey's mind lights the fuse. By the time the fireworks go off, Joey won't even remember what he did.-- Lily struggles to get the lighter to stay lit.>// **Jessie:** I don't think you can do shit. I ran away to keep the assassins or the aliens or the shitty little demons away from my family, but you're not even worth it. //// "Let go of me, you brat!" Lily squeals, clawing at Jessie's hand. Her mouth opens sideways and centipede like mandibles take a snap at Jessie's arm. This is her moment. Finally, a moment for herself. "You want it to be me and you forever, huh?" She wrangles Lily off the bed, more cat fight than wrestling move. "Then we're going down together!" Jessie throws herself into one of the many holes in the ground, dragging Lily down with her own weight. . . . //// **Jessie:** What are we waiting for? What is this? //// **Lily:** Nothing. I'm not strong enough to do anything else. **Jessie:** Oh. Really? //// **Lily:** This is all that's left of the world I used to live in. And this- //// **Lily:** -is all that's left of me. //// **Lily:** Just my luck that I waste the last of myself on a mind that rejects me completely. Couldn't even finish the job and see you dead. //// **Jessie:** I'm assuming this is not what your world always looked like? **Lily:** Was that a question? **Jessie:** Uh, what did your world look like? **Lily:** I don't know, normal? I only really know what it looked like in other people's memories. **Jessie:** You're really bad at answering a basic question. **Lily:** As if you're any better! I've sorted through your mind and you haven't held a successful conversation once! **Jessie:** Oh, this is such bullshit! You claim to want to be childhood friends but you know way more about me than I do you. //// **Lily:** You want to know about me? Fine! I went to a normal school with normal people and then someone died and they put my in a cell for the rest of my life. //// **Lily:** And then I destroyed my cell and killed everyone who kept me there. And then I killed everyone else. And that was it. End show, exit universe right. //// **Jessie:** Wow. You're really pathetic. //// **Jessie:** I mean, you put up a cool fight, really frightened me up until the end there. And I was really banking on the idea that you didn't actually have anything to hold over me. But I thought I'd at least warrant a cooler demon to hunt me. You look like you're about to become nothing. **Lily:** I could still make my final act killing your brother! **Jessie:** I don't think that's true. //// **Jessie:** I... gather you didn't have too many friends in containment. **Lily:** I was too important. **Jessie:** ... sure. **Lily:** I'm spilling my guts to you and you can't even be nice to me? **Jessie:** //Nice?// //// **Jessie:** Nice!? I'm being nice! We are sitting on the last remaining piece of a dead world after you threatened my brother! I'm being so fucking nice right now! I'm the nicest person you've ever met! //// **Jessie:** ... Tell me I'm not the nicest person you've ever met. **Lily:** Your brother is nicer. **Jessie:** Oh, whatever, fuck you. **Lily:** That's probably why he has real friends and people who like him. **Jessie:** It pisses me off that in all the memories you tried to fuck with it's always //Joey// that you're replacing. Do you know how weird that makes this? **Lily:** I can only really exist in what you remember. Not my fault he's the only other person who loves you. //// **Lily:** I mean he's the only person who loves you. **Jessie:** What did you say the first time? **Lily:** I said he's the only person who loves you. **Jessie:** Oh. //// **Jessie:** You need to exist in people's memories to exist at all. But, what if you could exist in dreams instead? **Lily:** Those count as memories. //// **Lily:** Was there a point? **Jessie:** I could take you to Oneiroi West! **Lily:** You need to dream in order to enter Oneiroi West. **Jessie:** I dream. You could inhabit my mind and come with me. On one condition. //// **Lily:** Stop pausing. What's your condition? **Jessie:** I'm giving you space to- //// **Jessie:** Stay out of my brother's mind! Or anyone else's. You will stay in my mind and my mind only. //// **Lily:** Really? You'd rather die on this hill then just let me die completely? **Jessie:** What can I say? //// **Jessie:** Having a childhood best friend wasn't all that bad. On another plane, a thousand miles away, Joey sits up in bed and looks around the tiny ramshackle apartment he and his friends pooled their money on. It’s raining outside and there’s a tiny hole in the ceiling right above his pillow. He really ought to get that patched one of these days. Special Containment Procedures: Interacting with SCP-FUN-J-ONE in a narrative, believable or real way is expressly12 prohibited for all Foundation personnel, except for the members of the Ethics Committee.

Update 20██-██-█: A copy of SCP-FUN-J is to be attached to the end of SCP-FUN-J documentation.

Update 20██-██-██: A survey, SURVEY-FUN-J, designed to collect emprical data on the psychonarrafunnistic effects of "pure"13 jokeme exposure is to be provided to any personnel reading the SCP-FUN-J file. All personnel reading the documentation is required to fill and submit SURVEY-FUN-J. Failure will result in immediate and permanent demotion to D-Class.

Description: SCP-FUN-J is a list of 30 jokes. These jokes are believed to have a one-to-one mapping to all possible jokemes.14 Experiencing some of these jokemes can cause was-that-it syndrome15, IDGI16 symptoms and PK-class events17. These symptoms are consistent with current psychonarrafunnistic18 models.

Addendum 1 | Discovery Log: SCP-FUN-J was discovered when an author (SCP-FUN-J-AUTHOR), a character (SCP-FUN-J-CHARACTER) and an audience (SCP-FUN-J-AUDIENCE) walked into a bar and I (SCP-FUN-J-ONE) ordered a beer.19

Based on the discovery log, the following theories about SCP-FUN-J-ONE was developed, is still in development and will always be already developed by RCT-Δt:
- SCP-FUN-J-AUTHOR has descended through the narrative layers.20
- SCP-FUN-J-CHARACTER is a narrativotemporal anomaly originating from a parallel narrative-space-time.21
- SCP-FUN-J-AUDIENCE is a reflection of a future noospheric continuum acting upon our fabula.22
- SCP-FUN-J-ONE is an amalgamation of SCP-FUN-J-AUTHOR, SCP-FUN-J-CHARACTER and SCP-FUN-J-AUDIENCE formed by thaumotemporanarrativistic interactions between these entities.23
- The purchase of alcholic substances has no relation to the anomaly.24

— Arthur Joseph Blanchard Jr. #62, Leader of RCT-Δt Temporal Intelligence Community Applied Task Force L-100-A "Literally 100 Arthurs"

IT WAS JUST A JOKE, STOP ERUDITING ABOUT IT

— SCP-FUN-J-ONE, CEO25 of Psychonarrafunnistics

Addendum 2 | SCP-FUN-J
1. -Psychonarrafunnistics & You: Abandoning the Notion of Funny vs. Unfunny
2. A hybrid research program focused on jokeme discovery and identification. Did you remember?
3. That title works on SO MANY LEVELS.
4. THIS IS FICTIONAL ACADEMY DONE BY FICTIONAL ACADEMICIANS
5. Anyway, when I say baseline, I should clarify: Baseline is an illusion.
6. The baseline of a character in a story is one, the baseline of our reality is one, the baseline of anywhere is one.
7. One is arbitrary.
8. The point is that the baseline of the story is equal to the characters'.
9. $1/\pi$
10. If you ever feel like a joke is unfunniest, enact protocol THINKER immediately to avoid known narrafunnistic hazards.
11. WHO IS SENDING EMAILS IN THE YEAR OF OUR LORD AUTHOR 20██
12. CHOO CHOO!
13. Under the standard narrativistic model a jokeme is comprised of a meme/narreme paired with a signos/logos quanta. For more information look at this slide for hours. I did.
14. The real jokeme was the lau… *gunshot sounds*
15. Was it?
16. Did you get it?
17. Personalized K-class events. Common examples include regret induction, irreversible ontokinetic reframing and/or character development. You are having one right now.
18. DID YOU ALREADY FORGET THE MEANING OF MY REALLY NARRATIVELY IMPORTANT RELEVANT ACADEMIC JARGON? I am a teacher you know… I will not make you just remember it. I will make you UNDERSTAND it. The teachings will continue until ERUDITION improves.
19. I might have ordered two. Not sure.
20. This may look like a "narrative stack," but we avoid such terminology here. A "narrative stack" is erroneous.
21. Regardless, usage of this system to describe literal narrative reality is erroneous and obsolete, as there is no linear vector to/from other narrative planes.
22. Even the books you read from are not the narrative plane they represent. Their two-dimensional narrative quanta creates a three-dimensional holographic projection in another reality.
23. Indeed, you will find many personnel on Foundation territories espousing Pataphysics jargon as if the mere use of the lingo serves as an incantation to bring about further understanding.
24. This one is 100% funny. I would know. I joked it to be.
25. Chief Executive Officer
26. Yeah. Yeah. Everything must end.
27. It has to feel funny. It has to be funny.
28. Baseline is always the same to the character.
29. Our psychonarrafunnisticians will handle that.
30. -From SCP-FUN-J-ONE with love <3

We all had our fun with SCP-FUN-J! I personally enjoyed SCP-FUN-J-24 a lot. Funniest indeed.
SCP-FUN-J-ONE… The way you joke is impressive but SCP-FUN-J is reaching its limit. A few more jokes and this will become a surreal torture chamber instead of a joke. One might even call joking this much an unethical move.26
— A Concerned Third Party, CEO of EC

@import url('https://fonts.bunny.net/css2?family=Montserrat:ital,wght@0,800;1,800&display=swap');
 
#page-content { font-size: .9rem; }

}

}

#header h2::before {

@media (max-width: 707px) {

#login-status,

}
 
#search-top-box input.empty {

}
 
#search-top-box {

#top-bar {

}
 
#top-bar, #top-bar a {
    color: #333333;
}
 
h1,
h2,
h3,
h4,
h5,
h6 {
    font-family: 'Montserrat', sans-serif;
    color: #000;
    letter-spacing: 1px;
}
 
h1 {
    font-size: 2em;
}
 
h2 {
    font-size: 1.45em;
}
 
div#extra-div-1 {
    height: 160px;
    width: 100%;
    top: 0;
    position: absolute;
    background: url('https://scp-wiki.wdfiles.com/local--files/theme%3Ablankstyle/43Head.png');

    background-repeat: no-repeat;
    background-position: 50% 50%;
    z-index: -1;
}
 
@media (max-width: 707px) {
    div#extra-div-1 {
        top: 15px;
    }
}
 
body {
    background-image: linear-gradient(
        to bottom,
        #e0e0e0, #e0e0e0 90px,
        #e0e0e0 90px, #ffffff 200px,
        #ffffff 200px, #ffffff 100%);
    background-repeat: no-repeat;
}
 
:root {
  --timeScale: 1.5;
  --timeDelay: 1.5s;
  --posX: calc(50% - 358px - 13rem);
  --fnLinger: 1s;
}
 
#page-content hr {
    background-color: #000;
}
 
#page-content tr th {
    padding: 6px;
    border: #000 1px solid;
}
 
#page-content tr td {
    padding: 12px;
    border: #000 1px solid;
    line-height: 1.4;
}
 
#page-content .sidebox tr td, 
#page-content .sidebox tr th {
    padding: 0.35em;

#side-bar {
    border-right: 1px solid #333;
    background: #DDD;

#side-bar .side-block {
    border: 1px solid #333;
    border-radius: 0;
    box-shadow: none;
}
 
#top-bar div.open-menu a {
    border: 1px solid #333;
    border-radius: 0;
    box-shadow: none;
}
 
@media (max-width: 767px) {
    #side-bar:target {
        border: 1px black;
        box-shadow: none;
    }
}

    border: 1px solid #333;
    border-radius: 0;
    box-shadow: none;
    background-color: #FDF6D7;
}
#side-bar .side-block.media {
    background-color:#D7EFE7;
}
#side-bar .side-block.resources {
    background-color:#F5D8E0;
}

    margin-bottom: 4px;

    border-radius: 0;

    border: none;
    color: #333333;

#page-content .rate-box-with-credit-button .fa-info:hover {

    color: #ffffff;
}
 
.rate-box-with-credit-button .cancel {

    margin: unset;
    margin-bottom: 4px;
    border-radius: 0;

    background-color: #ffffff;
    color: #333333;
    border: none;
    border-radius: 0;

.page-rate-widget-box .rateup,
.page-rate-widget-box .ratedown {
    background-color: #ffffff;
    border-top: none;
    border-bottom: none;

.page-rate-widget-box .rateup a,
.page-rate-widget-box .ratedown a {
    background: transparent;
    color: #333333;
}
 
.page-rate-widget-box .rateup a:hover,
.page-rate-widget-box .ratedown a:hover {
    background: #333333;
    color: #ffffff;
}

    border: none;
    border-radius: 0;
}
 
.page-rate-widget-box .cancel a {
    color: #333333;
}
.page-rate-widget-box .cancel a:hover {
    background: #333333;
    color: #ffffff;
    border-radius: 0;
}
#page-content .rate-box-with-credit-button .page-rate-widget-box { border: none; }

    height:0;
    top: 0;

    margin-bottom: 8px;
    width: calc((100vw - 870px)/2);
    max-height: calc(100vh - 18rem);
    position: absolute;
    top: 0;
    left: 103.5%;
    z-index: 5;
    overflow: auto;
    box-sizing: border-box;

Joy to the Worlds



2003

25 December

Baseline Reality

It was a ritual long foregone.

Since the disastrous events of 1997, there had been no Christmas at Site-43. At least, not officially. People still celebrated in their own, private ways, but they knew better than to hang mistletoe or otherwise decorate their spaces. Something in the air made it dangerous to be both festive and alone beneath the soil of Ipperwash.

That didn't stop the Survivors from gathering in Udo's dorm, of course. One thing they could be sure of was that none of them would grow attached to any of the others, if they weren't already. A year of seeing altogether too much of each other made certain of that.

But since it was the only thing they could be certain about anymore, the ritual was observed.

McInnis was serving eggnog at the kitchen island. Wettle was filling his beard, and sometimes his mouth, with shortbread crumbs. Nascimbeni and Ibanez were arguing the finer points of obscure rural tradition. Harry was watching them all, bemused, recording the moment with his eyes. Lillian was pretending to be asleep, though the occasional quick of the mouth betrayed her.

Udo was lost in thought.

It had been months. They were all more or less used to it by now. She'd long since stopped examining her actions day by day. Everything checked out. She still liked the things she'd always liked. Hated the things she'd hated. All her reactions made sense, except where they didn't make sense because of aspects of her personality which, themselves, made sense. She was her, and if she'd come to know the others enough to judge — and she felt she had — they were them, too.

So why.

"You're doing it again," Lillian murmured, so quietly that no-one but Udo could hear.

"Doing what?"

"Thinking about it." Lillian's left eye snapped open, and she fixed it on Udo. "Don't."

Beside Udo on the couch, Harry looked over. She ignored him, just as she ignored Lillan. She watched McInnis pass Nascimbeni a little tray of cheese and crackers, noting that he hadn't had anything to eat or drink himself yet. Probably hates getting crackers on his sweater.

"Don't what?" said Harry.

Udo sighed. "Don't think about why."

He scowled, and looked away. To some extent, they were all thinking about it. Except Wettle, of course.

Thinking about why they'd done what they'd done.

On September the 8th, 2003, every one of them had felt drawn to the stations they'd kept a year prior. The Breach had recurred, and as though on autopilot, they'd all run through the motions just precisely the same as they had before.

And none of them knew why.

"It's a 2003 mystery," Harry muttered. "Let it stay there."

"And old acquaintance be forgot?" Udo asked him.

He clammed up.

Allan sat down in his chair. Nascimbeni plunked himself down in his preferred recliner, and Ibanez sat down on the arm. Wettle looked up from the floor, absolutely littered with pulverized biscuit.

The Director was holding a glass. He held it up; Udo wondered if he'd actually drink from it, after the toast. "To absent friends?" he suggested. "And to us?"

"Assuming those aren't the same things," Udo whispered to herself as she raised her own glass. From the way Lillian's eyelids fluttered, she'd heard that, too.



2004

25 December

Timeline 5243-A

It was a time for making new rituals.

In years to come, they might do things differently. Spend the time with their families, if ever they acquired such connections beyond the present group. Or else see and be seen, in the flesh, by their legions of builders and dreamers. For today, a broadcasted message of hope and succour would suffice.

For tonight, they would celebrate in their sanctum.

"Pass the," Sokolsky cried. He waved his hands vaguely, making grasping motions at nothing. His feet were up on the U-shaped table, and his chair was balanced precariously.

"The," Harry repeated. "The, the."

"The," Sokolsky agreed. Harry examined the array of treats on offer, shrugged, and slid a bowl of pistachios in the bald man's direction.

Not all of them were there, of course. Van Rompay was out with LeClair. Eileen was with Carter. But the rest of them were enjoying the fruit's of a very, very hard year's labour.

Harder than that, for some of them.

As the night wound on, they found each other one by one. The seven. They stood in a semicircle near the Administrator's seat; Wettle sat down in it, much to Allan's apparent amusement. The rumpled replicator didn't seem to notice.

"How are we feeling tonight?" Allan asked them, making eye contact with each.

They knew what he meant.

It had been just under three months since they had failed to resurrect the dead, and here they were, celebrating Christmas. "Easter is going to be particularly hard," Harry quipped, and he was surprised to see that he meant the levity. None of the others looked particularly stricken, either.

"It's not a better world," Nascimbeni murmured. He was going to duck out early; his son and granddaughter were waiting in J&M for the start of the technicians' after-party. "But it might end up that way."

Harry glanced across the room at his wife, gaily chatting it up with Thilo Zwist. He'd almost lost her again. And if he had…

If he'd lost her then, on September the 8th, he'd never have known what else he'd be losing. She wasn't showing, not yet, but it was only a matter of time now.

"I miss my parents," Udo whispered.

"I don't miss anybody," Del said as if the previous sentiment hadn't been expressed.

"This maudlin shit misses the mark," Lillian snorted. She caught a pistachio in the air, shucked it, and flicked the shells back at Sokolsky. He cackled. "Tonight, we drink. Tomorrow, Earth receives her kings and queens again."

"Not that," McInnis smiled. "Never that."

"I mean symbolically," she hiccoughed. "You know. Rituals and all."

2008

25 December

Timeline 5243-C

"There's no place in the budget for ritual."

Karen Elstrom spent most of her time these days with her arms crossed. Sometimes McInnis thought it was just to keep herself warm; she kept turning down the thermostat in Admin and Oversight, insisting that some day the mysteriously still-hot geothermal plants would catch up with the state of the universe and shut off, and he was sure she wasn't eating enough to boot. She looked thinner and thinner every day.

"There are considerations beyond budget," he reminded her. "We're going to need to keep up morale for a long while. A very, very long while."

A version of himself he no longer remembered having been, who had thought himself an immigrant from a better reality, had thought a year would be sufficient. Acting on impulses and information no longer available to him, this other self and his partners in cognitive dissonance had believed a miracle cure would make the madness disappear. When that hadn't happened, and the impulse to even try had faded the next day, they'd been left with a serious conundrum.

How could nearly a thousand people live in an utterly dead world?

He still wasn't sure Karen understood. "Christmas, in this context, isn't about resources. It isn't even about hope. It's about breaking up the day-to-day. If there is privation now, and privation later, and nothing but privation between…"

He trailed off every once in a while, in their little talks, to let her interject. She hated, hated to interrupt him, and he refused to monopolize the discussions that way. She took the chance. "Privation is where we're at, if we don't want to starve to death in under a decade."

He sighed. "Karen. The situation is desperate, that's true. But the difference between desperation and despair is enough to end a species. We need to keep their spirits up. If that means tolerating Paul McCartney and hanging up a few garlands, it's worthwhile."

"Nothing is worth 'Wonderful Christmastime'," she snarled. "And anyway, sir, with respect, keeping up morale is more your department than mine."

"It will not always be so," he said, and he let it hang in the air without explaining further.

Her eyes widened.

He waited.

She deflated, only slightly, leaving her still far more upright than most coat racks. "Fine," she grumbled. "I'll see if hydroponics has any of those failed winterberry bushes, and you can have your damn garlands."



2017

25 December

Timeline 5243-D

Ritual was all they had left in common.

Nascimbeni knew it was the right day the moment he walked into Sam's. The bar in Grand Bend was packed wall to wall with Foundation researchers and agents and technicians past and present, all of them whooping like they were calling down a meteor. He hated it instantly, but that was a key component of any cultural experience, he'd found. It had to be loud, painful, and brief.

He wasn't expecting to be here more than an hour.

All six of them were at the bar. Allan looked comfortable, which of course he wasn't. Ibanez was already completely smashed, which would either make the night go much smoother or bring it to an early, screeching halt. Blank and Okorie were sitting together, which didn't cross his threshold for 'interesting', but he supposed it was something. Wettle was on the floor, picking at the wood shavings and fashioning a beard for his beard. They were sticky enough to stick, or perhaps he was. Lillihammer was standing on the bar, doing karaoke. She didn't have a mic, and there was no music, but that didn't stop her.

Nascimbeni pulled up beside the former Chief of Security, and gestured at the others. "Anything new?"

She burped in his face.

He nodded, and leaned across the bar to catch Okorie's eye. "How many this year?"

The woman's amber eyes were smouldering; she, too, had already partaken then. "About a hundred."

Nascimbeni whistled. "Almost everybody."

And then he tried to say something more, but his jaw and his lip did something strange, and a strange sound came out of him, and he turned away to stare into the hooded ceiling lights.

It had only been a year, after all. This was normal. Ngo had assured them all it was normal. She'd set up a practice in Grand Bend, and half of the survivors — and most of the so-called "Survivors," a term that now meant nothing to them — were now regular patients.

Some nights he didn't have the nightmares anymore. Didn't think about the silent, shuttered tomb beneath their feet which they would never see again.

He tried to play off the sudden outburst as a casual leaning back on the bar. Addressing Blank now, he called out over Lillihammer's caterwauling: "Any luck on the job front?"

The archivist snorted into his tomato juice. "Department of History doesn't want me. Might try my luck at 91. Udo's parents, well, you know."

Nascimbeni nodded. Most people's parents were a little more clingy, now. Lost time and a worldwide rash of unexplained disappearances would do that. "Not like there's much left here for you, right?"

Lillihammer kicked a glass clean across the bar. It exploded on the far wall, to general applause.

"Present company excepted," Nascimbeni remarked mildly.

Wettle muttered something under the bar, and Nascimbeni leaned down to face him. "What?"

"Happy New Year," the plastered buffoon muttered. "Whoever you are."

"I'll drink to that." Nascimbeni raised a finger, but there was already a beer in front of him. Ibanez burped in his direction again, and he nodded thanks before twisting off the cap. "Here's to whoever we are, now."



2018

25 December

Timeline 5243-E

Udo performed the ritual, but it was Ibanez's idea to try.

She proposed it be the entire facility, to mask her intentions. If the canny thaumaturge knew better, she was canny enough to hide her tells.

Site-43 rose again from the desert sands.

It wasn't perfect, of course, and it wasn't everything. Recreating the world's largest underground space in any medium was a Sisyphean task, even for someone who could move boulders with her mind. But it was close enough for their purposes.

Allan would be meeting the ASC for wine at Intake Point-94. Ibanez wondered if the mage would try creating a silicon lake serpent to complete the effect. Harry and Lillian would be in his dorm room, watching movies — or rather imagining they were, under the influence of a few choice cognitohazards Udo had sifted from the rubble the previous month. Wettle would sit this one out; he didn't have any particularly fond memories of 43, and anyway was convinced he'd put his foot through a soft spot in the sand and go plummeting to his pain.

Ibanez was going to see him.

He was the only figure Udo had crafted for this tremendous sparkling playset. He sat on the catwalk in the Cavern, beer bottle in hand — a real one, sans label, glassblown by the micamancer herself — and waited for her.

She sat down beside him, and he offered her a bottle of her own. She took it.

Both bottles were empty, but she pretended just fine. Went through the motions, like he was doing.

She didn't know why she cared. She'd hadn't been involved with the man before the year leading up to his death; besides a brief fling after the Breach, they'd basically been strangers.

But the echoes in her mind of that possession, of the things she'd done, the god they'd killed, the hole in her heart when she'd found him dead…

A sharp pain in her hand, and she saw that the bottle had broken in her fist. Saw the blood.

"And to all a good night," she growled.

The simulacrum of Nascimbeni didn't answer. She watched it until the illusion finally faded, carrying them all softly back to an empty reality.

...
...


2022

25 December

Timeline 5243-F

Simply existing was a ritual.

Blink out. Assert. Blink in.

He's dead. Blink out. He's dead. Blink out.

He's dead.

No matter what, he was always dead. Mukami was Director? He was dead. Del Olmo instead? He was dead. Gwilherm's autocracy, or the tyranny of the many, dead and dead. Always dead.

She had Christmas presents from people she didn't know, and presents to give to people who didn't know her. Sometimes they thought she didn't even work there. Sometimes they didn't even know who he was.

It was all well and good to speak of goodwill toward men.

They hadn't loved Philip Deering.

And most of them hadn't known Dougall.



2035

25 December

Timeline 5243-X

"I think a little shakeup in the ritual would be nice," said Lillian, and then she really was Lillian.

She tried to gasp, but her mouth wouldn't open that far, that fast. The world was red and striated, as though glimpsed through a saffron marble. Her left arm was numb… No.

No, it wasn't numb.

She should have fallen to her knees, but she couldn't. She felt weak, weaker than she had ever felt before, but she remained upright. She could do no other.

Her arm and her legs were gone.

Every inch of her remaining body ached like an abrasion burn. Her hair was like bamboo stabbed into her scalp. Her eyes ground against their sockets as she stared frantically at nothing.

Merry Christmas, said the voice in her head, as she tried and failed again to scream.



????

????

The Ritual

The clink of glass.

A shared smile.

"Rest ye merry gentlemen."

A chuckle. And no dismay.

juni-writes-a-poem.raw_content:
In which a poet finds ways to dream skyward.
(Tales of the Mosaic – 345 words)

Tessera

Juni Writes A Poem

writing and poem narration by atypica
story narration and music by Jezixo

Juni wrote:

Leviathans rise on bluest moons
From reservoirs, runoffs and canals
Beneath this sunken city,
To reach the barren ether.

As water drops from up on high,
The magnates call it rain.
And as they sing their ancient songs,
The magnates call it wind.

The beginnings of a poem, maybe. If only he could find the words. The pen lay still, leaving a splotch of ink on the parchment next to abandoned couplets and half-written sonnets. The candles had long melted to puddles of wax.

He knew he ought to be doing more important things than writing about the whales. Tomorrow marked his first day laboring at the Fairchild steel mill; as his parents did now, and his grandparents did before. Soon, Juni would be a real boy, providing for this city so it may provide for him, giving his body the scars of toil for the privilege of living. He had known it his whole life, and yet, he shivered at the thought. It all felt so suffocatingly grand.

But yesterday, the whales had taken flight. He had followed the crowd as it emptied the inn, and skyward there had seen them, covered in the city's waste yet untethered to it. He watched them soar, he heard them sing, and for a moment, he forgot about it all.

And then they were gone, as quick as they came. The people scurried back inside, afraid the magnates would see their awe as slack. Juni walked home enraptured, head filled with whale song, murmuring verses under his breath, counting the days until they would return.

Now, his mother called from downstairs, telling him to get ready for bed. The poem was almost done; soon to join the steadily growing stack in his desk drawer, a thousand other little splendors. He'd bind them all into a book one day, he was sure of it.

Juni thought of the whales, shedding flotsam as they soared, and knew how he wanted it to end.

O’ whales that sing in the sky above,
Please teach this city to fly.

Previous

Bessie Bogan and the Crow Road Inn

Next

A Gally Fellow's Lens

    Alex Thorley Interviews For a Job
    Author: Matthgeek (author page)

There is a door on the wall. It isn't always there, and it's never in the same place.

The door has a plaque. It reads “Alex Thorley, Department of Unreality Liaison”. A piece of grease-stained pizza box cardboard has been taped under the plaque. Scribbled on the makeshift sign in fading marker are the words “help wanted”.

Today it does exist, despite all of your wishes to the contrary. Standing outside this door, you take a deep breath, using the delay to reassure yourself. You have the qualifications, you have the experience. Now if only you had the confidence.

Before your mind settles on one course of action over another, a knock breaks the silence. It echoes down the hallway until the carpet and acoustic tiling suffocate it. You draw your arm back and examine the appendage which extends from it. Your hand has betrayed you and announced your presence. Now, the fingers wiggle on command, but you still glare at them suspiciously. True fingers would not take such a drastic step without consulting the rest of the body.

It's too late now. You have made your presence known, and the door drifts open with a sigh of stifled disappointment. The office within has two chairs, a fishbowl, and a Rubik's Cube. There is probably a desk, but your focus is on the person in the far chair.

You size up the disaster who has just entered the office. It's not hard, there isn't much worth noting. From the blandness of their turtleneck sweater to the blindingly unremarkable sneakers on their feet, there is an enraging meekness. They stand before you, their weak eyes goggling pleadingly, their mouth a small line.

The room is silent as you wait for them to make the first move. In your mind, you scream for them to leave, to spare you from the tedium they carry. On the outside, you settle for a dead-eyed stare. You reach forward, adjusting the nameplate on your desk which reads “Alex Thorley, Liaison” to a more severe right angle. They remain mute, terror peering out of trembling irises. You eventually cave in, breaking the room’s peace with the first question.

“Can I help you?”

You cling to the hope that they’re here for something else. Maybe they just need to drop off a package. Maybe you won’t have to endure interviewing this waste of space. The frail, stammering words shatter those dreams.

“I’m… here about the position.”

With a sigh drawn from the depths of your soul, you pick up a pen and click it, bracing yourself for the banality which is to come.

“Name?”

A scream of panic tries to force its way out of your mouth, but you smother it so only the smallest exhalation escapes. You tell the scream that it’s alright. There is no need to panic. You can fake it well enough and long enough. Reluctantly, the scream agrees to reserve judgment and settles into your throat.

The interviewer glares at you. Your eyes slide down and examine the pen held in their clawed hand. It's sharp, angular. Better suited as a knife than a pen. An image flashes before you, of them reaching over and plunging it into your flesh. You find the idea ridiculous. Not because they couldn’t, but because that would indicate you were worth stabbing.

“My name is Alex Thorley.”

The interviewer notes this down with a “hm” that conveys skepticism, but not complete disbelief.

Not yet, anyway.

It’s quiet as the form is filled out, and you explore the room’s carpet. It’s a color too neutral to have a name, except where coffee has been spilled near the desk, leaving a stain in the shape of a face. Somedays, the face is smiling. Now, it screams in silent sympathy. It is no comfort, so you return your focus to the face across from you and weather its distaste.

“How much experience do you have?”

The answer comes out quickly this time, rolling off your tongue as it has so many times before: “Twenty-six years.”

The interviewer's left eyebrow shoots up, and the rest of their face follows. “Our records say twenty-seven.”

The scream begins to build again, and you swallow to keep it down. Your gaze darts from that piercing stare to a slice of decaying birthday cake, but is pulled back by the magnetic anger in those eyes. “It might be. I'm not good with dates.”

There is silence as the pen that should be a knife meanders across the paper, each cut leaving behind sharp black lines. You can't read the result, but no doubt it notes your failure to remember such a simple thing.

You want to reach over and scream at them, to tell them to grow a spine. But that would only result in more cowering. Your jaw clenches, driving teeth into each other and creating a pressure that almost frees you from the stupor this person has brought into your office. The paper beneath your pen gapes wide, threatening miles of questions yet to be waded through. The next question arrives, eager to delve. You give it voice and resign yourself to what must follow.

“What qualifies you for this job?”

The downcast eyes tell you everything you need to know. They aren’t qualified. It’s obvious they are pretending. But they can’t fool themselves, and they can’t fool you. You eventually receive an answer, and it sloughs down your ears like gravel.

“I have twenty-six- twenty-seven years of experience.”

Within the sludge, a glimmer promises an escape. You dart forward, seizing the opportunity with your next words.

“That’s it? You have nothing else to recommend yourself?”

The scream is writhing, reaching for your mouth, for freedom. Its vanguard escapes your lips as a faint “eep”. You order your lips sealed, biting into them to prevent further escapes. But the scream keeps searching for a way out, and you can feel it leaking out from behind your eyes. Blinking keeps it at bay, for now.

You glance up, and watch satisfaction make its way across your interviewer's face. You know then you'll never be given this responsibility. And that's fair. Why should you be trusted with something so important? So many people have given so much, and you've squandered it all.

You want to leave, but your legs revolt, no longer willing to obey such an uninspiring commander. Across the desk, your interviewer reaches for the note that has been there since the beginning of the interview, as of five seconds ago. A message from on high, here to condemn you. Why else would someone take the time to address the shambling wreck of your presence, if not to be rid of it?

Loyal to the last, your eyes once more seek the floor, sparing you from watching your sentence be read. As your sight peruses the carpet, each second of silence winds tighter. Building to the inevitable release of rage.

When the words eventually lash out, your shoulders are already taut.

“My apologies, I was mistaken.”

Muscles unclench, and you raise your head. The chair across from you has been vacated, and now widens its arms to welcome you.

“The job is yours.”

Tentatively, Alex Thorley rises from the seat in front of the desk and takes the much more comfortable seat behind it. They look around and see their erstwhile interviewer has receded to a corner of the office. Not exorcised, but at least reserving judgement for a future error.

Out of curiosity, Alex reaches for the note that decided their fate. It lays on the sparsely populated desk, forlorn. Inside is only one line:

“Applicant exemplary. Qualifications unnecessary.”

Warmth suffuses Alex's chest, and they set down the note.

Next to the note, a pen glints, its angles softer on this side of the desk. Alex picks it up and rolls it between their fingers, its brass fittings reflecting their soft smile. They drop it into a mug, and it lands with a clink, settling down to join its fellows.

Alex sits back, satisfied.

Alex sits back, satisfied. [[/div]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box-end]]
