Framed in glass, or polished stones or metal, the surface reflects the world of the viewer, projecting a space that feels familiar, but also incredibly alien; a copy of a copy, reality just out of reach. Your mirror is almost always completely covered with a spare sheet from the bedding provided to you by the university, which was never comfortable compared to your usual moss. It stands like a stone obelisk in the corner, drab grey among the half-domesticated grotto you reside in during your months off the island. It's easy to ignore, and although the occasional gust sometimes reveals a corner, drawing your eyes to the shimmer for just a moment, your curiosity turns morbid the moment you realize only [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|It##[[/span]] waits for you, just under the surface. In your youth, you learned that mirrors, reflections, were a gateway to deception, to allowing in not just thoughts, but oftentimes vengeful spirits or monsters that weren't really there. You felt, almost, as if you were not meant to perceive yourself to the extent you did; your distant relatives, deer, would see their reflection in the water momentarily during a quick drink, but from your conversations, they did not seem to process that it was, in fact, themselves looking back. In your own experience with water, you found  there was nothing you could do to stop the wavy reflection from looking back, regardless of one's mastery over the element. On most days, you could choose to ignore this, either through obstruction or by tracing grout lines on the bathroom tile with your eyes. But today is not most days, as were most days since your unfortunate experience at [[[to-serve-deer|dinner]]]. After a particularly rejuvenating bath, you wrap yourself immediately and tightly in a robe, not even allowing yourself the chance of a hint of your reflection on the water's surface. You wring your hair into the bath, allowing the damp bundle to rest over your left shoulder, and grab a small, glass jar filled with a clear, jelly-like substance. The mirror waits for you, as it always does. You call upon nature, call upon the vines in the earth to lift up the sheet. A soft glow emanating from you illuminates your dim enclosure, and slowly but surely the mirror is half-uncovered. You open just enough of your robe to reveal the scar, and dip your fingers in the jar, closing your eyes as you apply the ointment.   When you open them, you find two clawed hands sitting snugly on your waist. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//"Hello, child. Taking care of your **reminder**?"//##[[/span]] the discordant voice shrills at you. In your panicked state, you stumble backwards, tripping on a root you're not quite sure you called to be there. You look in horror at the mirror, and that's when you see [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|It##[[/span]]: your [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Shadow##[[/span]]. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Its##[[/span]] form, your form, contorts and twists as [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|It##[[/span]] slowly melts through the sheet of crystal, like yolk meshing with egg white, until the [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|infernal afterbirth##[[/span]] leans over you on all fours. You attempt to close your eyes, but you feel one of [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Its##[[/span]] clawed fingers gently lifting your chin, causing a sound between a whimper and cry to leave you. "G-go away. You should not be here, I did everything right!" You open your eyes to the toothy grin of your [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Shadow##[[/span]], and your ears droop as the sound of [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Its##[[/span]] laughter, like rock scraping rock, fills the space. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//"I deserve to be here, just as much as you, **whelp**. You were thinking of me, and I have **just** the perfect gift for you."//##[[/span]] As much as you don't want to believe it, your [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Shadow##[[/span]] was correct. Most times, you knew your place and your limits, the difference between right and wrong. You were able to suppress your more… harrowing thoughts, instead choosing to fill your mind of the many volumes found in the Wanderers' Library, or in the epics Hana would recount to you over your evening meals. But everything changed when you stepped hoof into that restaurant and Hana was in danger. The experience left you wounded, sure, but you felt powerful standing to defend her from harm. For a brief moment, it felt as if all the fear in your body had melted away and was replaced with something else entirely. It was a feeling you missed, and one you almost yearned for as the horrors of everyday life, of living as //you// are, slowly began to return to your mind. "And why should I trust what you are saying? Last time I listened to you, we almost died! Hana can barely look me in the eyes now." Much to your surprise, the [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Shadow##[[/span]]'s expression softens. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//"You are juvenile in your understanding of us, child, and mistake our intentions. You allowed us control, and now we know exactly what you desire."//##[[/span]] The [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Shadow##[[/span]] places a hand on your bare skin. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Its##[[/span]] touch is cold, and you feel a chill course through your body, following the fractal-like mycelial branches that burrowed themselves under your skin. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//"You want control over your form, but your fear blinds you to inaction. If you continue to live as you are now, you will tear yourself and the world apart with your repression. We simply offer you freedom."//##[[/span]] You pause for a moment to weigh the [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Shadow##[[/span]]'s words. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|It##[[/span]] feels almost… sincere in [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Its##[[/span]] offering; finally there was something that understood exactly how you felt. After all, was the form before you not also you? Although [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Its##[[/span]] hair and nails were overgrown and filled with mud and brambles, [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Its##[[/span]] teeth dagger-like, and eyes glowing with [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|crimson##[[/span]], your eyes could trace each of the [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Creature##[[/span]]'s ribs, a reminder of a struggled upbringing, and the patchwork pattern of short and long strands of fur that dotted your upper legs. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|It##[[/span]] wears [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Its##[[/span]] nudeness with an almost confident air, while you hide from reflections every time you change your shirt or step out of the bath. "H-how do I know that this is not a trap?" you ask through shortening breaths. Your mind races with the possibilities, but a muddled mixture of fear and doubt wants to believe that [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Its##[[/span]] offer is simply too good to be true. The [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Creature##[[/span]] stands up and grins at you; [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|It##[[/span]] knows that you've been won over. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//"If you truly believed this were a trap, you would have fought to get rid of me by now."//##[[/span]] [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|It##[[/span]] holds out a hand to you. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//"Consider this an apology. Turning over a new leaf in our relationship. I can assure you, you will not regret it."//##[[/span]] You hesitate for a moment before extending your hand upwards. The [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Creature##[[/span]] pulls you off the ground at a speed to nearly whiplash you, before [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|It##[[/span]] disappears with a sound half-cackle and howl. You watch as the vines pull the remainder of the sheet off the mirror, and you feel compelled to take a look at yourself. Your eyes glow a [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|crimson red##[[/span]] that doesn't seem to fade away after a repeated series of blinks. You slowly bring your hands to your face, allowing your fingers to touch your cheeks. Normal. You feel normal, at least physically. Your mind feels heavier than before, though, and you hear as another voice joins your monologue. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//Finally, everything is back to where it belongs. Does this wholeness not give you comfort? Enough, perhaps, to walk this treacherous path?//##[[/span]] "What would you have me do?" you respond, to the empty room. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//There is something waiting for you in the Library to retrieve. After you do, send for our **knight**.//##[[/span]] You feel your heart drop. "What does Hana have to do with this? Why does she have to get involved?" [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//Our knight possesses something that we do not. All will be explained after you visit the Library.//##[[/span]] You attempt to detect any shred of deceit in the [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Shadow##[[/span]]'s voice, but none comes through. Hopeful, you begin to think that, maybe, the [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Shadow##[[/span]] is telling you the truth. You throw a shawl around your shoulders and, taking one last look at your apartment, head towards your impromptu objective. ----- [[div class="text-container-wrap"]] +++ Hana 📷💙 [[div class="text-container"]] [[div class="sent"]] [[span class="text"]]Hello, Hana? Are you available tonight? I need your help with something.[[/span]] [[/div]] [[div class="recv"]] [[span class="text"]]Uhhhhh we should be finishing up with rehearsal soon[[/span]] [[span class="text"]]I can leave now if it's urgent though[[/span]] [[span class="text"]]What's up?[[/span]] [[/div]] [[div class="sent"]] [[span class="text"]]Oh, it is nothing urgent. When you are finished, if you would meet me at my apartment, that would be wonderful. The door will be open for when you arrive.[[/span]] [[span class="text"]]If it is not too much to ask, can you bring your paints and brushes over as well? I require them for a sort of project that I am doing.[[/span]] [[/div]] [[div class="recv"]] [[span class="text"]]Yeah sure sounds good[[/span]] [[span class="text"]]Love you see you soon[[/span]] [[span class="text"]]💙[[/span]] [[/div]] [[div class="sent"]] [[span class="text"]]I love you too.[[/span]] [[span class="text"]]❤️[[/span]] [[/div]] [[/div]] [[/div]] ----- You shiver as you pace around your apartment, thumbing through the fading pages of the large tome you were promised held all the answers. It wasn't quite what you were expecting; you had encountered texts belonging to the Nälkä before, but fleshcrafting was something you were wary of. There was something terrifying to you about permanence, and you often stood on the ledge of change, sure in your ability to make a decision, but lacking the willpower to take the leap. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//You do not need to jump. If you truly allowed me to assist you, all it would take is a little push.//##[[/span]] You try your best to ignore the urge, and instead return your attention to the book. This text was somewhat unlike fleshcrafting, though, and while the processes it talked about were still permanent in nature, there would be enough time for you to step away if you found your decision getting ahead of you. The author called for intricate spirals and complex runes and a multitude of open eyes to be painted across one's body. For once, the [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Shadow##[[/span]] was telling the truth; there would be no way to do this without Hana. "How do we know this will work? What will the Foundation say about the changes during my examination? They will know I changed something about myself." [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//You cannot let your jailers prevent you from living the life you so desperately dream to live. They certainly have not stopped our knight from doing so.//##[[/span]] You pause to think for a moment before the [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Creature##[[/span]] speaks again. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//You continue to doubt my true intentions?//##[[/span]] "Last time I let you take control, we almost killed someone. She saw me turn into a monster and nearly rip someone apart. I am afraid that will happen again." [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//You let me in because you were too weak and afraid to protect her on your own. I gave you the freedom to seize your own strength. What you did with that freedom was your responsibility. Do you not think that our knight would have done the same for you? Our… guardian does not fear killing as you do.//##[[/span]] "D-do you think she sees me as a monster?" [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//I know that you are not a monster. However, she cannot see you if you do not make yourself known; your true self, that lies within. Only then will you know what our knight thinks of you.//##[[/span]] ----- Hana Thompson walks with a hurried strides across campus, breathlessly whistling along to the repeating melodies from band practice. For a Tuesday night in April, it was quite nice out; the weather was warming, and although Hana likened herself to a space heater during the particularly cold times of year, the breeze brought about a comfortable equilibrium. On any other night, she would probably take her time walking, wait for the luminous orbs adjacent to the pathway to light up, or even return with her camera to snap some pictures for a friend back on site. Tonight, she hardly noticed the scenery around her. Tonight, Hana was almost entirely lost in thought. The person known as Hana Thompson was a combination of many different things, and she always prided herself with being able to offer or learn something new in a situation. But most importantly, she was an incredibly guilt-ridden person. She stops to catch her breath at a sidewalk, watching as an assortment of different colored birds scramble away from the scattered remains of fries and a burger as a toddler approaches. //Meri would have told me the name of all of those.// Hana curses herself; she had made herself quite scarce around her lover in recent times, both because of the demanding schedule of her band and school and the random assignments that would require her to meet Adams or some other agent to receive her mission. In the free time she had, though, Hana didn't know how to reach out. Usually, Hana would select an activity, venue, or even just a time to meet, and the pair would enjoy the presence of one another. But Hana hadn't invited Meri out since the massive fuck up that was meant to be their anniversary. The robotic //wait// of the crossing light disappears and Hana resumes her trek to Meri's dorm. It was a path Hana knew intimately; two lights, past the toothpaste barber pole and recently repainted restaurant seating to the large white apartment building on the left. She could do it with her eyes closed at this point, but instead, her eyes catch a glimpse of the fire-colored horizon. //Red.// When Hana did come to visit Meri, to check on her wounds or to just awkwardly exist behind the façade she had been putting up, she's reminded of the color and stench of blood. Blood that should have been on Hana's hands, not Meri's. //I promised her that I would protect her. She only turned into that... [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Creature##[[/span]] because I failed.// She stops before the entrance of the building, hyping herself up for whatever came next. All Hana could hope for was Meri's forgiveness. Although Meri had specifically asked for her help tonight, a small, nagging part of Hana's mind worries that this would be Meri calling things off, the last straw that would break their relationship. She carefully opens the door to the dim, bioluminescently-lit apartment, opening it just enough for her to pass through before carefully closing it behind her. Hana quietly places down her guitar case and removes her shoes; //certainly she can't be sleeping by now? Maybe she forgot I was coming? No, she wouldn't do that.// She steps deeper into the apartment, ready to sheepishly call out her partner's name, only to find Meri nervously pacing, clad only in a soft robe. Hana's face begins to burn as the fawn regards her. ----- "Hello, Hana. Apologies for not leaving the lights on for you, I was just… thinking." You watch pink blush blooms across Hana's cheeks as she freezes for a moment in the vestibule. Even in the low light, she casts quite a distinctive silhouette compared to the space around her: on her back is the guitar case you helped embroider flowers and insects onto, which she sets down near the entrance. She wears her familiar baby blue jacket, as well as an unbuttoned shirt with a stringy tank top beneath it, and a pair of cargo shorts. You notice a mismatch of paints and brushes in a bag in her hand, though she grips it away from her body, as if it were of some danger to either of you. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//Perhaps//##[[/span]], [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|It##[[/span]] says in your mind, [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//your judgement is clouded by your own anxieties. Unless-- does the princess believe that our knight has reason to be fearful of you?//##[[/span]] "I-it's alright, don't worry. I didn't mean to walk in on you changing. I can step out for a sec if you want?" //Does she think I am disgusting? Maybe this is too much for her. I made a mistake.// [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//Your only mistake would be inaction. It almost killed you last time. Will you make the same mistake **again**, child?//##[[/span]] You see her take a small step back, and you shrink somewhat. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Something##[[/span]] compels you to speak-- but the voice is your own. "No please, stay. There is… something I need your help with." Hana pauses, and looks at you inquisitively. "Is something wrong, Meri? Are you alright?" You can hear a tinge worry weaving through her words. She hasn't approached you yet, a fact you are both thankful for and troubled by all the same. You take hold of the tome next to you, and with what little courage you can scrape up, open it gently to a bookmarked page. "Earlier today I was at the Library for... a project, and I stumbled across this volume." You soften your voice slightly. "It is a book on low-level body transformations through the use of thaumaturgically-altered designs." Hana steps closer, and you carefully hand the book to her. She skims through the text before tracing her fingers over the sketched eye, the intricate curves and spirals that cover much of the next few pages. Hana hands the book back to you, and you place it on a chair. "I've dabbled in basic thaumaturgy before, but this doesn't seem too difficult. To get the effects the book is talking about, though, you need a rather large focus. What do you intend to use for this?" You begin to blush and look towards the floor. Your face burns slightly as you reach for Hana's hands; they're soft but tense as she matches your grip. You nearly have to choke the words out. "H-Hana. I need you to paint those designs on my body." "I-I-- " You watch as Hana's face turns pinker than a camellia. "A-are you sure? Just a little bit ago you were cautious about holding hands and this-- is a big step from that. I just want to make sure you're comfortable." She begins to rub her thumbs over your fingers. For a moment, you find yourself once more on the edge of words. There's something so primal within you, telling you that it's time to run and hide, to tell Hana you changed your mind and allow yourself to be alone once more. In the approaching darkness, in the [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Shadow##[[/span]], however, you see the smallest fleck of hope. For a moment, you spot the small flickering of something new, a sense, maybe something that can build to the fires of new feelings. Something that, despite the fear of your birth, and the repression of all the feelings of love that get shrouded by self-hatred, you think you can make your own. You don't want to miss this chance, not while you still have her. "I have been thinking-- I did not know how to tell you, and I was so close to losing you." You sniffle. "I am learning that there is so much I can be, but I do not know how to get there."   [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//It is by your blood and your hands that you will be recreated. Our knight will only be here to look upon what she has unleashed.//##[[/span]] "I understand, don't worry. I am so proud of how far you've come." She opens her arms to you. "Will-- will you let me help you be brave?" You whisper out, "Please." You quickly nod your head before nestling it in the crook of Hana's neck, careful not to poke her with your antlers, as tears begin to well in your eyes. The faded smell of her pomegranate perfume and dried sweat overwhelms you, and you lose yourself in her. "I am so scared of what I am, Hana. I do not want to hide from my reflection anymore. I do not want to view myself as a monster." Tears slowly begin to flow from your eyes, and you feel a hand cautiously begin to slowly run across your hair. A calming //shhhhhhhhh// leaves Hana, almost like a soft breeze, and your worry starts to melt away. After a moment, you pull away, noticing the dark patch on Hana's jacketed shoulder. She smiles at you, and takes a deep breath. "Alright, if we're going to do this, I'm going to need a second to get ready. I just need to check to make sure my paints aren't going to irritate your skin, but after that we can begin, yeah?" "Thank you, Hana." "It's not a problem at all, Meri. Thank you for letting me be part of this experience." She steps away, and you watch as she begins to check the labels on her tubes of paint and run the brushes across her skin. You turn towards the mirror, seeing yourself wearing a slight smile in the reflection. //How fortunate am I to have someone like her.// [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//We are fortunate indeed.//##[[/span]] ----- Hana directs you to sit on a stool in the center of your space, clearing the immediate area around you of any obstructions and tripping hazards. You sit in near-perfect stillness as you watch her work diligently, at one point stopping to wipe the sweat from her forehead. She brings the bag of paints over to you, opening it and offering you to select one. "Your book didn't say anything specifically about a color, so I thought you would be interested in choosing one." You look down at the mismatched selection of pigments, imagining what it would be like for you to wear one; oceanic blues and verdant greens, royal purples and soft pinks, daffodil yellows. Your eyes, and by consequence the hand not quite in your control, are drawn towards a deep red, reminiscent of the tenebrous flowing of wine. "I think that color would look nice on you." You survey Hana's face as she speaks, trying to search for any notes of discordance or any sign that this wouldn't have been the color the artist chose. A [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Voice##[[/span]] within you rumbles with laughter, before [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Its##[[/span]] graining speech fills your mind. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//Even our knight sees your true nature, the one you deny yourself. Have you considered that, perhaps, we are both trying to help you? That she too will push you towards the same path you are so fearful of?//##[[/span]] You watch as she pockets the paint and a brush in her shorts before walking towards your mirror. She removes her jacket and button-down shirt and hoists them across your mirror, allowing them to lazily oscillate before coming to a complete stop. You take note of the subtle flex of the muscles on her back, and how her tank top hugs her body in a way you feel would take centuries for you to be comfortable replicating. Hana smiles as she approaches you, her lithe, athletic form almost cat-like in its movement. You stare at her calves, the smooth muscles flexing as you wonder what they would feel like. Your earlier fears of physical contact seem to have been replaced with another sensation; a foreign one, a warmth in your stomach, a desire. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//You yearn to explore her body, and for her to do the same in kind.//##[[/span]] You deny the [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Shade##[[/span]], as your cheeks match [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Its crimson##[[/span]] stare. //I-- I do not understand the feeling which you refer to. I am simply appreciating her form.// The feeling of doubt bubbles into your mind. //Right?// Hana kneels down, gently flicking the blue streak of her parted hair from in front of her soft, brown eyes. "Alright, I think I'm ready to begin if you are?" //I love her. If she asked me to create a world for just the two of us, I would shape the earth and the water and the sky to whichever form would bring us the most peace.// [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//What if she wanted to leave your 'paradise'? Would you destroy the world if she asked?//##[[/span]] "Meri?" You feel the weight of a hand atop yours as she pulls you back to reality. She tilts her head, giving you a look that combines both understanding and worry. "Apologies. I-I think I am ready to begin." Hana nods and leans back, sitting on her heels. "Alright, cool." Hana pauses long enough for discomfort to appear. "I-- uh, how did you want to do this?" "The painting? You seem to have all the materials and the text to begin. Is something missing? "No I mean... your robe. Did you want me to remove it, or would you be more comfortable if you did?" "Oh. I-I can do it. One moment." "Right right. No worries, take all the time you need." You slowly and less-than-gracefully allow the robe to loose from your shoulders. It slides down your arms and then your side before stopping at the seat, your hips, level with the one scrap of cloth remaining on your body, protecting Hana from the sight of your nakedness. Almost instinctively, you wrap your arms around your chest, but feel only the small protrusions of your ribs. You know nothing is there, a reminder of the body you were born with, but this innate reaction was always enough for you to imagine there was. You're reminded of seeds, likening yourself to a bud that would blossom into a woman from the currently flat and barren ground. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//One must tend a garden if they wish to reap the rewards.//##[[/span]] Hana places a hand atop one of yours, her warm fingers brushing the ridges of bones and veins on the back of your hand.  At the feeling, you close your eyes and turn your head away. You're almost certain she can hear your heartbeat, convinced she can feel them too from how hard it pounds against your chest. You wonder what it might be like if her hand was on your chest directly; would touch alone cause rhythmic order to run into chaos, or would the pressure alone slow the pace down to something more manageable. Yes, you hope it to be the latter. The imagined pressure eases your panic, though when you open your eyes, you realize it was never there to begin with, only the fleeting remnants of desire buried in Hana's eyes. "Hey, it's alright. There's nothing to worry about. It's just me here." Hana laughs. "I can take my clothes off too, if that would help you be more comfortable. I was an art class model once because a friend needed a favor." You feel a heat rising to your face as you imagine Hana as you are now, sitting on a stool, demure, with only a loose robe draped over her. She had taken you to a great deal of museums in the short time you knew her, and you had always had a certain reverence around the many portraited nudes of masters past. Always a student, you listened intently to each and every word Hana spoke, followed the directions she gave you without question, until she deemed you ready to bring your learning to the practical. //Just put a little paint on your finger and run it along wherever you're comfortable starting.// was what she told you. She almost shivered as you began your work, watching you diligently as you slowly traced from her shoulder to her wrist, from her thigh to her ankle. You noticed her breathing grow more ragged as your finger slowly glided just on the surface of her skin. You weren't quite sure what to say, though you felt compelled to try to say something romantic in the moment. "You have, uh, very nice legs, Hana." Hana giggles. "Why thank you, babe." 'Babe', you learned, was a term of endearment in romantic relationships. Not wanting to seem ungrateful, you decide to continue. "You also have very pretty eyes-- babe." "I see I've taken your words tonight, dear. Is something //else// taking your attention?" She tilts her head and leans forward, causing you to freeze up slightly. "I-uh, sorry. I do not know why I am so--" "Nervous." She hangs onto that last 's' for a moment longer. "I think it's cute to see you like this, all flustered." Hana moves her head next to your ear before whispering to you. "Are you ready to be brave, Meri?" You swallow hard before nodding. "Y-yes. I am ready." Hana takes the tube of paint from you and takes your hand. She places a modest helping of paint in your palm before spreading the paint around with the brush. Hana leans back in the chair. "Touch me, Meri." You freeze, lost in the cobalt reflection of your hand. "W-where?" "Put your hand on my chest. Feel my heartbeat." The room goes still, you feel like time has stopped around you. Your heart beats louder and louder, palms sweat, part of you feels like you want to throw up. The [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Shadow##[[/span]] says something to you, but you hear nothing; you feel as though [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|It##[[/span]] can recognize that as well. You close your eyes, allowing yourself to relax, allowing yourself to focus on the amazing feeling of the kiss and the new ache you felt for connection. It feels as though space expands in contracts around you, a soft light entering your view, and then everything stops. You touch something, and you feel the erratic //thump thump thumping// from your outstretched hand. You open your eyes, and in a moment, Hana's body is pressed against yours; you know what to do now. Your hands press against her chest, cup her neck and her arms. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Something##[[/span]] coaxes your hands downwards, towards Hana's hips, drawing a giggle from her in the short, staccato moments between your kisses. She follows your lead, breaking away for a moment to kiss your neck. You imagine following suit, wondering [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|how it would feel to run your canines along her jugular##[[/span]]. Her hands travel downwards, finding their way to a particularly sensitive spot just above your tail that causes your body to tense. You let out a noise you're not quite sure you've made before, a mix between a bleat and a whimper, as you find yourself pressing your body into your partner. Hana begins to laugh, and you bury your head in the crook of her neck, planting kisses there in an attempt to salvage the moment. "That was cute. I wonder what other noises you can make." Your brain short-circuits as Hana keeps up the pace-- [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|guttural panting and primal moans rising to the surface##[[/span]]. You find yourself not so slowly beginning to fall behind, your breath getting more and more labored as her hands and lips continue to work. In a brief pause, a momentary respite from the flurry, your eyes find the mirror, find your eyes returned to their normal, cosmic hue, and find the [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Shadow##[[/span]] staring back at you. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//Take what you deserve. Submit yourself to her. Let your bond become whole.//##[[/span]] A feeling of dread overtakes you, one that you're unsure was hiding or simply suppressed by the presence of your [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|other##[[/span]]. It feels almost like waking up from intoxication, the moment of clarity that makes you want to curse yourself for everything that happened before. //I-I cannot do this anymore. Wait! I need your strength! I am afraid. Plea--// You feel Hana's hands at your waistline, and you freeze. She pulls back for a moment, just an inch from your face. Her expression is almost pleading, questioning, her eyes waiting for your response. You can see the tension in her shoulders, about to explode, to flee; [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|you wonder if she will replace you with another##[[/span]]. Your legs fold from under you, causing you to crumple into a ball on the floor. You close your eyes, and the world goes dark. ----- [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//Perhaps this was but a fool's spring. It matters not, time marches ever onwards and you cannot avoid the thaw forever.//##[[/span]] ----- When you finally open your eyes again, you find Hana sitting cross-legged on the ground next to you, slowly petting your hair. You try not to meet eyes with her, and instead pull yourself into more of a ball. She goes to run her hand along your head one last time, before placing it in her lap. "Hey." She says. Her voice is quiet, almost wavering. "Hey." You answer back. You're a whirlwind of emotions under a sky of exhaustion. You wish no more than the flora you're laying on to overtake you and bury you to spare you from the embarrassment. "I'm sorry for-- I'm sorry for moving so fast. I-I got lost in the moment, and I should have checked to make sure you were alright." She shifts. "God, I'm such a fucking idiot." [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|//This is **your** fault, not hers//##[[/span]]. [[span style="text-shadow: 1px 1px 1px #BC3030;"]]##red|Its##[[/span]] words echo in your mind, but you push them out. "H-Hana?" "Meri?" You turn, still hiding your eyes from Hana's, but just enough for her to enter your view. She's thrown her jacket over her, but you can see the red and blue smudges of paint on her skin from your time together tonight. The rest of her appearance bears reminders as well: her tousled hair, her still-elevated breath, a collection of small, bruise-like splotches on her shoulder. Looking up a little further, you see lines of make-up cut by fallen tears. //Do not cry for me, my Iris. We still have so much time.// "Can you hold me?" Hana sniffles, wiping her eyes, and nods. She stares at your legs, at your hips a moment before she lays on her side behind you, cautiously draping her arms over you, pulling you close, but not too close. She gives you a soft kiss on your shoulder, hoping that it would stoke the fading embers of the night, but you're entirely afraid of what continuing would look like. You let the fire die. But... it's comforting; the weight, the warmth. As you welcome sleep, you smile, wishing simply that you were brave enough to have this all along. one-side-of-an-interview-with-a-containe.raw_content:
Interviewee: The only family that really matters is the one you pick for yourself.

Content warning for depictions of transphobia.

Interviewee: Hey doc.

Interviewee: Yeah, I’m doing alright.

Interviewee: No, I have not gone to the group sessions. You know why. I’m not ready for that yet.

Interviewee: I can’t feel comfortable if everything feels like I’m slowly getting pinpricked in the back over and over again.

Interviewee: Why are you still trying to force me to like any of this? No matter how soft the bedsheets are, a prison is still a prison.

Interviewee: I know.

Interviewee: But it’s hard to get used to it. How can I? This isn’t my life anymore. This isn’t any life to live.

…

Interviewee: At least this isn’t 17. But let’s be real here, anything is better than 17.

Interviewee: As if.

Interviewee: I know the people here aren’t just cold-blooded bootlickers. They go out partying, they have lives and dreams of their own, they care about each other and others like them. They’re human.

Interviewee: But guess what, doc. So are we.

Interviewee: I’d rather not switch subjects. I know this is about me, but it’s more important that we talk about you. The Foundation you, I mean.

Interviewee: Must be really topical, if your clients have this conversation with you all the time.

Interviewee: Circles and circles, huh?

Interviewee: Yep, you do the best with what you have. But there needs to be more done.

Interviewee: I don’t know, I just want to do something for the world, you get me? I’m tired of wasting away in this cell. I’m tired of watching the world burn around me. I’m tired.

Interviewee: Wish I could’ve done some activism, or something. Anything.

…

Interviewee: Look, when you’re moved from one shitty environment to another, less shitty environment, you might think it’s something, right? At least a change.

Interviewee: But I still have that empty feeling inside. Because it’s over. Everything that I looked forward to in my life is gone. The second I was finally able to just be myself for once without having to pass as someone I’m not, your people came, and now I’m here.

Interviewee: I know that you care. I know you’re trying. It’s nice that I can get therapy, and walk around out of my cell and stretch my legs. But I still feel that heavy weight under my pillow. I still have to see concrete walls every day when I wake up in the morning.

Interviewee: And I’ll always know that instead of getting out there and living my life the way I see fit, I’ll just be here. Talking with you once a week, and then back to my cell.

Interviewee: You gotta know how that feels, right?

Interviewee: Yeah, you can’t really change anything. I get it. But you have to let me go.

Interviewee: I don’t care if that means you lose your job, it’s not like your job is a moral one. You need to let me go.

Interviewee: But you won’t. And that’s fine. It’s fine.

Interviewee: I can still live in spite of it all.

…

Interviewee: Can I tell you something?

Interviewee: Great, thanks.

Interviewee: I’m better off here than back home. Only by a bit, though.

Interviewee: Yeah, I’ll tell you why. It’s why I’m here, right?

Interviewee: Haven’t exactly had the best home life. Mom left my dad and the house when I was three. Just walked right out, and never came back. Didn’t even know her face.

Interviewee: Only thing I learned about her after the fact was how much she drank. 10 cans of beer a day. It’s wild, I know.

Interviewee: My brothers were a rowdy bunch, but they cared a lot about me. We always spent the time wrestling and fooling around, or dunking on each other while playing Mario Kart in the living room. They always supported me when no one else would, and I’ll forever be grateful for that. I hope they’re doing well. I miss them.

Interviewee: But my dad, well.

Interviewee: He just didn’t get it. I tried to explain it to him, but he couldn’t get it. I don’t blame him. He grew up in a different time. People like me were hit with bricks, called slurs, killed. That’s still around now, but it was so much worse back then.

Interviewee: You know how I like to cross my legs, right? I do it because I want to. Not for any other reason. But my dad looked at me doing it once and told me I would look too much like a woman if I kept crossing my legs like that.

Interviewee: Yeah.

Interviewee: It’s okay, I’m better now.

Interviewee: I was never going to be the son that he wanted. I’m my own thing.

Interviewee: Not like I was ever a son to him anyway.

Interviewee: I know.

Interviewee: The only family that really matters is the one you pick for yourself.

Interviewee: Well, at least I got someone to go through this horseshit with me. That’s something, I guess.

…

Interviewee: Is there anything else we need to talk about?

Interviewee: Oh yeah, the other stuff.

Interviewee: I’m just glad you’re not pointing out how ‘self-aware’ I am. I hate it when therapists do that.

Interviewee: Yeah, it only grants me the ability to watch myself self-destruct from the VIP section of the stage. I can’t stop the problems just because I’m aware of them.

Interviewee: I am trying, this time. I am.

Interviewee: I know.

Interviewee: I’m just tired.

Interviewee: I’m sure we will, since I’m going to be stuck in a cell for the rest of my life.

Interviewee: At least it’s not home. But I’ll make my own home.

Interviewee: Thank you, doc. I’m glad to be here, at least. Who knows what would’ve happened if I was still at 17.

Interviewee: Or killed.

Interviewee: I could’ve sworn the Foundation did more than lock people up. That’s what the others are telling me.

Interviewee: You’re still a part of it. You have to at least acknowledge that.

Interviewee: Circles and circles.

Interviewee: Same time next week?

Interviewee: You know I’ll be there. It’s not like there’s a lot to do around here.

Interviewee: I’ll see you around. And thanks. I’m glad you’re trying.

When I was a kid, my dad decided to take me hunting for the first time.

We didn’t live out in the boonies or anything, but there was a patch of forest a few miles east of our place. We didn't do it because of food or anything, he just thought it was a fun hobby, something the two of us could bond over. And I guess with the deer population being so out of control back then, it didn’t feel weird. Just… a weekend thing.

It was just me and him, we got to the woods around dusk. I do know how to use a gun, of course, he always trained me to defend myself, although a hunting rifle is way clunkier than any handgun.

Honestly, the whole trip wasn’t all that exciting at first. We spotted maybe two or three deer, and I missed every shot. My dad kept cheering me on, trying to keep my spirits up, but I could tell he knew I was getting frustrated.

Well, I did manage to shoot a deer. It was standing still, looked a bit weird from a distance, just kind of… there. I raised my rifle, held my breath for what felt like forever, and pulled the trigger. One clean shot. The thing dropped like a sack of bricks, and my dad started clapping me on the back, proud as hell.

When we walked up to the deer, he suddenly grew dead silent. I looked down at the deer.

Pouring out of its mouth was a cascade of saliva, like a broken faucet. Its eyes weren’t looking at me- they were locked just over my shoulder, like it was watching something behind me. Its ears were all limp, and its body… Jesus. It looked starved. You could see the ribs pushing against its skin like they were trying to break free. It couldn't have weighed more than three hundred pounds, maybe less.

I reached out, almost instinctively, and my dad yanked my hand away. He just said, real firm, “We should go.”

I don't remember what we did next, all I can recall was me seating in the backseat while he made a few calls. I don’t know who. I just stared out the window, watching the trees roll by.

And then traffic hit. We came to a stop. I looked out the window and… I swear to God I saw that deer. Or something shaped like it. It was just standing there by the sidewalk. Same hunched posture. Same drooping ears. Same saliva dripping onto the concrete. I blinked, and it was gone.

We sat in silence for a while, until finally my dad asked, “You okay?”

I didn’t answer.

He laughed, a bit awkwardly, and told me, “Sorry you had to see that. Nature’s weird sometimes. In a few days, we'll just forget about this entire incident.”

Then he cleared his throat and said, “So, uh… you want to grab a snack? I’ve got a few bucks with your name on it.”

He smiled at me. I think I managed to nod.
We pulled into a gas station a few minutes later. He handed me a five and gave me this quick pat on the head.

“Go get yourself something nice.”

I grabbed a bag of chips, might've been Lays or Doritos, and waited at the counter while the cashier rang me up. As I stood there, I looked out the window, and I swear I saw that deer.

Standing behind some guy’s truck, slouched like before. Drool still spilling out like it had no control over it. I knew it was the same one. I felt it. My stomach dropped. The cashier snapped me out of it, asking if I wanted my receipt or something, and when I looked back outside, the truck was pulling away. No deer. Nothing. Just a red stain.

My dad kept trying to make small talk, but I didn't say a word back, just sitting in the backseat, looking out the window and eating my chips.

We got home around ten. Luckily, it was summer break or something, so I didn’t have to worry about school the next day. I remember waking up late that night, real groggy. I had to pee, so I left my room and stepped into the hallway.

And it was there.

Standing right in the middle of the hallway, just a few feet from me. That god damn deer was right there, two feet in front of me. I swear, I could hear it breathing. I couldn’t even scream. My heart just dropped into my gut and I froze.

I squeezed my eyes shut. Stayed like that for a few seconds. When I opened them again… it was gone. But you know what was there?

A god damn puddle of saliva.

Before I get any flack for posting this kind of stuff, I need you to stay with me for a bit.

The next thing I remember is bolting into my parents’ room, shaking my dad awake, crying, yelling about some monster in the house. He sat up, put a hand on my shoulder, and told me not to worry.

He said, “You’ll forget about it.”

Exactly like that.

Not “It was just a dream.” Not “It’s okay, you’re safe.” Just that I'll forget.

Now, you’re probably wondering why the hell I’m even talking about this now.

I still live in this place, my dad's in a retirement home, and my mom has been gone for awhile, so I ended up taking the house.

I was cleaning through the attic and I found a box. It had a bunch of junk inside of it, although one thing caught my eye. A photo.

In that image was me, and my dad, and that same fucking deer.

And the deer isn't the worst part, either. I was hand feeding it, I was feeding that thing. Saliva oozing on my hand, grains barely getting into it's malformed mouth, lapping food out of my hand like a childhood pet.

And there were more photos, so many fucking photos.

Me grinning next to it. Hugging it. Riding on its back with my mom holding my hand. In one of them, it looked like we were at a damn picnic.

Some of these images are in my own backyard, there's at least four of them near a sign that has "ANIMAL HOSPITAL" carved in. I tried to google it, but I can't find anything apart from local vet clinics.

And I don’t remember ANY of it. Not a second. These weren’t baby pictures, the oldest I was in these photos is no younger than fourteen.

For more context, I went on that hunting trip when I was SIXTEEN.

It's not right.

I’m going to see my dad tomorrow. I'll try to stay in touch.

SCP-480

ANIMAL HOSPITAL HUB

SCP-8368
open-season.raw_source: [[include :scp-wiki:theme:creepypasta]] [[include :scp-wiki:theme:anon]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:toggle-sidebar]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:info-ayers |lang=en |page=component:info-ayers |authorPage= https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/trouts-authorpage |comments= > The children asked him if to kill was not a sin > "Not when he looked so fierce", his mummy butted in > "If looks could kill, it would have been us instead of him" = (The Continuing Story of Bungalow Bill - The Beatles) Open Season ]] [[=]] [[module rate]] [[/=]] [[div class="blockquote"]] ##orange|**ThrowawayDeerGuy**## 8/2/2025 (Sat) 6:22:11 #78155243 ---- When I was a kid, my dad decided to take me hunting for the first time. We didn’t live out in the boonies or anything, but there was a patch of forest a few miles east of our place.  We didn't do it because of food or anything, he just thought it was a fun hobby, something the two of us could bond over.  And I guess with the deer population being so out of control back then, it didn’t feel weird. Just… a weekend thing. It was just me and him, we got to the woods around dusk. I do know how to use a gun, of course, he always trained me to defend myself, although a hunting rifle is way clunkier than any handgun. Honestly, the whole trip wasn’t all that exciting at first. We spotted maybe two or three deer, and I missed every shot. My dad kept cheering me on, trying to keep my spirits up, but I could tell he knew I was getting frustrated. Well, I //did// manage to shoot a deer. It was standing still, looked a bit weird from a distance, just kind of... there. I raised my rifle, held my breath for what felt like forever, and pulled the trigger. One clean shot. The thing dropped like a sack of bricks, and my dad started clapping me on the back, proud as hell. When we walked up to the deer, he suddenly grew dead silent. I looked down at the deer. Pouring out of its mouth was a cascade of saliva, like a broken faucet. Its eyes weren’t looking at me- they were locked just over my shoulder, like it was watching something behind me. Its ears were all limp, and its body... Jesus. It looked starved. You could see the ribs pushing against its skin like they were trying to break free. It couldn't have weighed more than three hundred pounds, maybe less. I reached out, almost instinctively, and my dad yanked my hand away. He just said, real firm, “We should go.” I don't remember what we did next, all I can recall was me seating in the backseat while he made a few calls. I don’t know who. I just stared out the window, watching the trees roll by. And then traffic hit. We came to a stop. I looked out the window and… I swear to God I saw that deer. Or something shaped like it. It was just standing there by the sidewalk. Same hunched posture. Same drooping ears. Same saliva dripping onto the concrete. I blinked, and it was gone. We sat in silence for a while, until finally my dad asked, “You okay?” I didn’t answer. He laughed, a bit awkwardly, and told me, “Sorry you had to see that. Nature’s weird sometimes. In a few days, we'll just forget about this entire incident.” Then he cleared his throat and said, “So, uh… you want to grab a snack? I’ve got a few bucks with your name on it.” He smiled at me. I think I managed to nod. We pulled into a gas station a few minutes later. He handed me a five and gave me this quick pat on the head. “Go get yourself something nice.” I grabbed a bag of chips, might've been Lays or Doritos, and waited at the counter while the cashier rang me up. As I stood there, I looked out the window, and I //swear// I saw that deer. Standing behind some guy’s truck, slouched like before. Drool still spilling out like it had no control over it. I knew it was the same one. I felt it. My stomach dropped. The cashier snapped me out of it, asking if I wanted my receipt or something, and when I looked back outside, the truck was pulling away. No deer. Nothing. Just a red stain. My dad kept trying to make small talk, but I didn't say a word back, just sitting in the backseat, looking out the window and eating my chips. We got home around ten. Luckily, it was summer break or something, so I didn’t have to worry about school the next day. I remember waking up late that night, real groggy. I had to pee, so I left my room and stepped into the hallway. And it was there. Standing right in the middle of the hallway, just a few feet from me. That god damn deer was right there, two feet in front of me. I swear, I could hear it breathing. I couldn’t even scream. My heart just dropped into my gut and I froze. I squeezed my eyes shut. Stayed like that for a few seconds. When I opened them again… it was gone. But you know what was there? A god damn puddle of saliva. Before I get any flack for posting this kind of stuff, I need you to stay with me for a bit. The next thing I remember is bolting into my parents’ room, shaking my dad awake, crying, yelling about some monster in the house. He sat up, put a hand on my shoulder, and told me not to worry. He said, “You’ll forget about it.” Exactly like that. Not “It was just a dream.” Not “It’s okay, you’re safe.” Just that I'll forget. Now, you’re probably wondering why the hell I’m even talking about this now. I still live in this place, my dad's in a retirement home, and my mom has been gone for awhile, so I ended up taking the house. I was cleaning through the attic and I found a box. It had a bunch of junk inside of it, although one thing caught my eye. A photo. In that image was me, and my dad, and that same fucking deer. And the deer isn't the worst part, either. I was hand feeding it, I was feeding that //thing//. Saliva oozing on my hand, grains barely getting into it's malformed mouth, lapping food out of my hand like a childhood pet. And there were more photos, so many fucking photos. Me grinning next to it. Hugging it. Riding on its back with my mom holding my hand. In one of them, it looked like we were at a damn picnic. Some of these images are in my own backyard, there's at least four of them near a sign that has "ANIMAL HOSPITAL" carved in. I tried to google it, but I can't find anything apart from local vet clinics. And I don’t remember ANY of it. Not a second. These weren’t baby pictures, the oldest I was in these photos is no younger than fourteen. For more context, I went on that hunting trip when I was SIXTEEN. It's not right. I’m going to see my dad tomorrow. I'll try to stay in touch.
