stuck-song-syndrome.raw_source: ===== [[include :scp-wiki:component:preview |text=//Hello listeners, and welcome to ✱✱.✱ FM -- The Halfway House.//]] ===== [[include :scp-wiki:theme:blankstyle]] [[include :scp-wiki:theme:queerstyle]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:text-style]] [[module css]] div#extra-div-1 {     background-image: url('https://scp-wiki.wdfiles.com/local--files/theme%3Aqueerstyle/SiteLogo_1.png');     filter: opacity(0.6); } [[/module]] [[>]] [[module rate]] [[/>]] [[=]] + Stuck Song Syndrome [[/=]] ----- Sitting on the soft carpet of her room, Billie Forsythe relished in the quiet of her new abode, delighted in the solitude. Billie, for the first time in a very long time, was not being watched. Back at Site-43, Billie had known little peace; days in the clinic were long, and while she wasn't handling some of the more basic day-to-day tasks, or consulting with staff on their medication, she wouldn't be able to leave the sight of her mother. To her credit, few could say that Helena didn't care about her daughter, but few denied the fact that she cared //too// much, though none would ever say it directly to her. The Medical Officer always had one eye trained on Billie; it didn't matter whether she was brushing up on her studies, letting heavy metal drown out the constant //whirs// and //beeps// of the pumps and vital machines, or if she was resting on one of the spare beds on a slow day. Billie was always being observed. Nights weren't much better either. A sliver of white fluorescents beamed into her room from the hallway, and she would be woken up to have her vitals taken. She had offered once to check her own when she learned how to do so, but Helena wanted to be certain. Needed to be certain. Certain that her daughter was stable, certain that she was doing everything in her power to take care of Billie. The only thing Billie was certain of was that she would never escape. She was happy to be proven wrong. SITE certainly took a moment to get used to, but for once, Billie felt the closest to normal she thought she would ever get. She could wander the seemingly endless expanse of halls or stay in her room, she could eat whenever and whatever she wanted, and now, with Heather's blessing, she could gaze longingly into the cold, conceptual abyss. It was wonderful. But, for all of the new experiences, there was one thing that gave Billie some comfort, no matter the situation. As she began to unpack the collection of scuffed cardboard boxes that held her treasured collection, throwing the packing material to the side, Billie's mind began to meander. //It's funny,// she thought, as she held a small digital recorder, shotgun mic attached via connected XLR, //I have all of the freedom in the world, and yet, I still come back to this.// The record player was unpacked with practiced reverence, and the tape recorder found a place alongside it on the table. Music, and by extension, audio recording, were one of the few 'Helena-approved' hobbies; those were exclusively the activities she had deemed safe enough for Billie. Back at 43, whenever Billie would ask to play with other kids her age, her mother would smile, gently, and hand her the recorder. Billie could remember walking the empty, grey tunnels of Site-43, hearing each footstep reverberate through the unused hallways. She saw herself, sitting at the end of a tunnel, headphones that were too big for her head, shotgun mic shakily pointed out in front of her, just listening to the natural noises 43 made. The drips, the creaks, the slight shifts and the cracking; on some days, they were her only companion. Naturally, she had used her preferred hobby to rebel against her mother's control. Helena used to say that 'music never hurt anybody' -- that was, until, Billie played deathcore for her mother. Helena never gave her speakers again, from that point on. Only headsets. //Enough moping,// Billie thought, standing and setting down her collection of records, to grab her next box. //What about having some fun... I wonder if Hana would like a mixtape?// ----- "Hello? Anyone home?" a muffled voice asked accompanied by a knock at the door. Billie could recognize it almost immediately: Hana. The warmth Billie felt rushed to her cheeks, and she just caught a glimpse of herself in her mirror; her usually pale face was flush, pink with both heat and affection. Billie remembered fondly their last encounter under the blanket; Hana's fingers interlaced with hers, her words, the shape of her face and her brown eyes. It snuck up on Billie during the day sometimes, only for her to be pulled out of the reverie by a query or falling object. The feeling was almost entirely new to Billie, and she wasn't sure what to make of it, nor how much of herself to give to it. "Y-yeah, I'm in here. Door's open." Billie watched as Hana slowly opened the door, sure to kick off her shoes by the entrance, before entering the room further. She looked comfortable; the heat from the summer didn't necessarily seem to pierce all the way through to SITE, though Billie was always cold regardless. Hana wore her usual baby blue jacket, with a set of athletic clothes underneath. She gave Billie a look of both awe and worry. "Are you alright? It looks like you've seen a ghost." Before Billie could answer, Hana traversed across the room, placing one of her hands on Billie's forehead. "God, you're almost burning. Do you have water?" Billie laughed. "May have pushed myself a little too hard." She motioned to the remaining half-completed music recorders on the floor. "Should almost be finished setting everything up, though." "A little?" Hana said, teasing Billie, one hand on her hip, the other still resting against Billie's forehead. "You're flush, are you running a fever?" "Oh, yeah, that," Billie replied, concealing her blush. "But it's no big deal, I always have a fever. Come on, let me show you around!" Billie took a few steps forward, and froze. "Wait," she said, stammering. "Sorry, I just realized, it's not... big enough to need a tour?" "Are you sure?" Hana snarked, "I might get lost on my way to the far side of the room." "See," Billie teased in return, "//this// is why they needed me to be your handler. Somebody has to take care of you, otherwise you'd have no clue what to do." "You're so right, I'm unbelievably lucky that you're there for me to depend on." Hana, in a fashion that Billie would quickly realize was a bad habit, had accidentally been incredibly genuine, with something that had started as a joke. Billie watched in real time, as Hana made the same realization -- Hana looked cute, blushing and staring down at her feet, hands pulling at her sleeves. "Let m-- Uh", Billie blustered, trying to fight the girls collected awkwardness. "Do you want to listen to some music?" "Yeah," Hana replied in a more reserved tone than Billie had expected. "I'd love to." Billie nodded. "Well, make yourself at home. I'm just going to grab another glass of water from the kitchenette, can I get you anything?" "I'm okay," Hana replied, as she drifted towards a comfortable-looking beanbag in the corner. "Thank you, though." //Come on Billie,// she thought to herself as she turned to enter her kitchenette. //You have to stop making this weird.// ----- //Stop it,// Hana thought to herself, as she walked further into Billie's bedroom area. //You have to stop making this weird.// When it came to crushes, Hana once thought of herself to be an expert. Once. She had enough experience, after all; well, as much experience that can be afforded to someone whose recollections of high school were cloudy and had to make do from movies from the 80s and 90s. Movies made everything look so easy: life was certainly not ideal, however, and there would be no actress for Hana to project herself onto this time. At school, Hana swore to keep things casual; there was no telling where she would be tomorrow, so there was no point in pursuing anything that lasted past the night. //But Billie... She's different.// A shiver ran down her spine. Part of Hana's mind had imagined what it would be like to transfer here forever. She would be subject to Heather's antics more often, sure, and she would have to endure Lillian's remarks, yeah, but-- maybe there was a future here for Hana. Maybe that future's name was-- Hana caught herself in the midst of taking a seat on Billie's bed, stopping herself mere centimeters from the surface. She stood up in the speed of a blink, as if sitting on the comforter would have caused her to fall forever. //Are you stupid, Hana? You can't sit on the bed of a girl you just met like that. It gives off the wrong idea.// Hana's cheeks pinkened slightly; she couldn't help herself. Though Hana tried to control her thoughts, in the way the psychologists at Site-19 directed her to, there were times where Billie was almost inescapable to her-- not that she minded that, of course. She just expected Billie to appear as a fleeting but familiar face she passed in the hallway, or from the muffled melody from a pair of headphones. No, Hana would not have that luxury, and she could hardly hear the word "handler" now without blushing. //'...they **needed** me to be your handler'-- does she know what she's saying? Am I that obviously into her?// Hana placed a hand on her forehead. //My handler. How gay is that? Heather **definitely** had something to do with this.// Just as she let out a deep breath, she turned her head and, with still blushing cheeks, welcomed Billie back into the room. ----- "So, what kind of music do you listen to?" Hana asked, as she stood awkwardly in the middle of Billie's room, hovering by the bed. "Taylor Swift?" she asked smarmily. "She's a good lyricist, but no," Billie replied, throwing herself down onto a wide beanbag, and patting the part beside her for Hana to join her on. "I... I'm a bit more hardcore than that?" "So, like, Metallica?" Hana asked, plopping down beside Billie, the beanbag sagging and dragging the two ever-so-slightly closer. "God, Hana," Billie asked, rolling her eyes. "Do I look like a middle aged man?" "I mean..." "Shut up," Billie said, pushing Hana playfully. Her hand lingered, an inadvertent desire to maintain physical contact for as long as possible; the second she realized what she was doing, she pulled her hand away, jumping up from the beanbag. //Shit. Stop this.// "Why don't you play a song for me?" Hana suggested, gazing at Billie's vinyl collection. Billie began to leaf through the sleeves, but she knew exactly what she was looking for. With a practiced ease, she slid the record out of the protective slip, gently placed it atop the turntable, and moved the needle over. A split-second later, the intense, but melodic sounds of Alesana's //The Emptiness// album filled Billie's bedroom. Billie let herself fall into the music, the drumline beating in tandem with her pulse, eyes closed, swaying and mouthing along to the words. It was a comfort for her, listening to the same albums -- she knew every note, every transition, and knew just what was coming next. Of course, she really didn't know what was coming next -- certainly not for a rogue hip to bump her. Billie opened her eyes, and saw Hana standing, hips cocked, hand outstretched. "What--" Billie was flustered, her musical reverie broken. "What's that?" "It's my hand, Billie." "Yeah. I know. What's it doing?" "Well," Hana said, head tilting, "I was going to ask you if you wanted to dance." "Do you even know how to dance?" Billie asked, smirking. //What's Hana doing? Fuck, she knows and is teasing me, isn't she?// "I mean, I know how to slow dance?" Hana offered with a shrug. "Wow," Billie said, in mock astonishment. "You //really// were the stereotypical high schooler, weren't you?" "I mean," Hana laughed morosely, "that's definitely one way to put it. But what about you, you've never done the awkward arms-length holding and sway before?" Billie shook her head, frowning. "I didn't go to high school, Hana. Seeing anybody else my own age was a major event for me, let alone dancing?" "Oh, right," Hana said awkwardly. "Sorry." The girls stood around, awkwardly, as the heavy guitar continued to reverberate in the background. Billie took the opportunity to beat herself up. //Why can't you just be normal?// she screamed at herself, internal frustration bubbling over. //Why do I have to be different? Can't I just pretend? No, apparently not! I just lash out, like an assho--// Hana's hand pulled her out of her mind, literally. Billie stumbled as Hana grabbed onto her hand, pulling the two closer together. When Billie reached out to stop herself from falling, her hand landed on Hana's upper shoulder, dangerously close to her chest. //Oh god you almost touched her boob.// Billie tried to prevent herself from hyperventilating, and managed to muster a few words. "What... what are you doing?" "Teaching you to sway," Hana said, grinning, taking Billie's hand from her shoulder, and placing it on the small of her back. "It's really easy, you just keep your hands there and... you just sway." Hana began to move her shoulders back and forth, gently wavering like a blade of grass in the wind, and Billie found herself mirroring Hana. Billie was immensely aware of her hands, but didn't want to pull away. She could feel how warm Hana was, through her shirt, and the slight callouses on Hana's hand felt rough around her neck in a way that Billie couldn't quite place, but undeniably gave her butterflies. The music was, undoubtedly, dissonant with their swaying; neither girl noticed, as they stared into each other's eyes. "See?" Hana said, smiling. "Not that bad, right?" "Yeah," Billie responded. "This is... nice." For a second, the two swayed in silence, an unspoken feeling unaddressed. //She's going to know,// Billie worried, biting her lip. Thankfully, Hana once again came to her rescue. "Do you feel like you missed something?" Hana asked, swaying gently with her. "By not going to high school, I mean." "Yeah, I guess? I mean, I've watched the movies, right? So I feel like I think I know what high school was, but also -- I think I just envied people who could go places, and do things, you know?" "Trust me," Hana shook her head. "High school is nothing like the movies, no matter how much I tried to make that fantasy fit." "Did something happen?" Billie asked, innocuously. "You could say that," Hana snorted, before scanning Billie's face. "Come on, you don't have to pretend for me." Billie tilted her head, causing Hana's expression to drop in response. "You read my file, right?" "No," Billie replied in confusion. "Was... was I supposed to?" "No, I just..." Hana said, slipping in a stunned silence. "I'm so used to being treated as a 'thing' by the Foundation, an object, an anomaly -- so I guess it's just nice to be seen as a girl first?" "I get it," Billie commiserated. "I'm not a formal anomaly, but... my condition is anomalous, at least, according to my mom. She's been trying to solve it as long as I can remember, and if you knew the number of people she has paraded through my exams, to 'study the mysterious anomaly'... Yeah, I definitely know what you mean." "Do you wish... do you ever wish that you could just be normal?" "Who wouldn't?" Billie paused, once again aware of how close she was to her crush. "But, I mean... It meant we got to meet, right? And I think that's pretty cool." "Yeah," Hana nodded, grinning. "I'm glad we met too." Before Billie inadvertently released a squeal in response, she let go of Hana, turning to change the record. "Let me put something else on, one second." "No worries," Hana said, relaxing back onto the beanbag chair. "I'm surprised, I didn't think I would like anything this hardcore, but--" Billie laughed, interrupting Hana. "//This// isn't hardcore, Hana. Trust me." "Okay, well," Hana replied, embarrassed. "I didn't think I could like music like this. You've got good taste. Did you ever think about like... being a DJ or something?" "You know," Billie said, focused on the task at hand. "I did, but -- can you imagine that conversation? There was something horrible about dredging up pieces of the past, just to put them back into another box. //Yes, this one may slide,// he thought, closing the drawer in front of him, //but a box is still a box.// His office was shaping up nicely, if he did say so himself; though there was still some work to do, some dusting, light rearranging, and generally setting in, it was as close to comfortable as a job was meant to be. Just before he could call it for the day-- there was a knock at his door. "Come in." Orville didn't bother to turn, watching the door open from the reflection in a glass cabinet. He plucked an ornate chess piece from one of the shelves, allowing a crystalline knight to rest in his hand. The door opened gingerly, revealing Hana, a member of his CTF. They hadn't spoken yet, but he recognized her from her dossier. //An anomaly, and an unstable one at that.// He didn't quite mind, rather, it was a fact, and he needed to consider the potential conflicts that may arise. Her profile had detailed her past missions, and the notes on her profile from Adams were mostly positive. //I can work with her, make her better than she is.// Just as he had, many times before. Another figure trailed in after her; another member of his team, but on the support end, Hana's handler, Forsythe. Those were ones he paid less attention to; he was better on the ground, getting his boots dirty, rather than watching from far above. Orville turned around, watching as Billie flinched, and Hana moved in front of her, ever so slightly. //Just enough to be intentional.// "Yes?" "Hello, sir. I'm Agent Thompson, I don't think we've spoken yet." "Agent Thompson, is this important? I was about to leave for the day, and given your lack of assignment, I cannot imagine this is time-sensiti--" "It is." Forsythe nearly gasped out, exhaling. //Forsythe is bold.// Pennrose looked between the two, and saw just enough hints of anxiety that, for the moment, he elected to humor them, and set the chess piece down on his desk. "What is so critical it must be handled //now//?" Hana passed a paper printout, turning it to face him. "We were monitoring the Noosphere--" "How?" "We have a radio station." "I'm sorry? Forsythe, run that by me again." Billie stepped forward, looking to Hana for support, who extended a hand and squeezed. Orville grinned, though not nearly enough for it to be visible. //Well, at least they trust each other.// "Hana and-- Agent Thompson and I started a 'radio station' that operates by broadcasting on Noospheric signals. We were testing it today, when we overheard a signal collision, from a group that we found in the Noosphere." "What were they doing? Do you know who they are?" Hana shook her head. "No idea. They talked about some sort of trial, and a payload, but..." Hana had trailed off, seeing the look on his face. //They came to me, so let's push them.// Orville set the paper down, and crossed his arms. //What kind of person is Agent Thompson?// "Why did you bring this to me? Congratulations, you two, you heard some radio chatter. Where I come from, people talk on radios all the time, and this is no more meaningful than a set of emails talking about a 'weapon'. What is the point in all of this?" Hana stepped forward without hesitation, staring him down. "Sir, with all due respect -- I think you are dismissing this too quickly. The way they were talking... I think they're trying to destroy an idea." "How?" The two were both silent, looking between each other. Hana had dropped her gaze, while Billie fidgeted with her sleeves. //Perhaps, a bit too far. After all, they are still so youn--// "I don't know," Hana said, looking back up, fire burning within. "And that scares me, sir." Orville snorted, uncrossing his arms. "Okay, fine. Your first mission is to track down and investigate this... 'rogue group' in the Noosphere. Congratulations, was that all?" "Yes sir, thank you, sir." Hana and Billie retreated from his office, and before they were out of his earshot, he heard Hana squeal in excitement, as Billie let out a sigh of relief. //She's going to be a pain in my ass, I can tell. Interesting, but a fucking pain.// ----- "Did you manage to get any more information?" Hana walked through the Noospheric abyss, having grown more comfortable in her exploration of the void. She trailed her hand through a field of conceptual debris, watching as it shifted and reacted to her extended fingers. "Yeah, I've tracked their signal further. Keep going straight for the next while, and you'll come to a T-junction. Take the path to the right." "Got it." Hana continued walking, with renewed vigor. "So, what did you think about Pennrose?" "Is... is this a secure channel?" The girls laughed, and Hana welcomed the companionship. "I liked him, but... I mean, I don't really have a lot to compare him to. He's certainly no Adams" "He was..." Billie was quiet, as if digging for the right words. "I think he's a talented asshole." "Oh? Those are pretty bold words for you, Billie, didn't think you had it in you!" "Shut up. I just... look, I've been around people just like him my entire life. I'm not trying to say that he's not talented, or that he's a dick for no reason, but, I can't say he's not one. Yes, he probably backs that up with skill, experience, something, but, don't we already have a Lillian?" Hana snorted, watching the signal blinking on a heads-up monitor. She wasn't far away from her estimation -- of course, in the Noosphere, estimation was about as good as anything else. "I don't know," Hana replied, thinking about Adams. "I think he's putting on an act, you know? There was something he wasn't saying, and I want to believe he has good intentions." "Sure." Billie snorted. "just like Lillian is going to apologize for being a raging c--" "I'm at the junction," Hana said, saving Billie from her own words. "How far away is the signal from here?" "You should..." "I should what?" "You should be able to see it." Hana stared out into the Noospheric plane, trying to see any level of detail. On the way over, the ground had slowly shifted to a concrete-like appearance, and she saw the occasional pillar, column or cubicle decorated with office supplies and tchotchkes, but where she was looking now? There was nothing. "I... I don't see anything Billie. Are you sure this is the right place?" Hana began to advance trying to get a lay of the land. "You should be almost on top of the signal now, that was where I detected their last pulse. Can you see anything? There should be a concept, //right there//." "And I'm telling you, there's //nothing.//" "Nothing nothing, or Noosphere nothing?" It took Hana a second to wrap her mind around that one, and she kept pacing as she did. She was about to reply when-- "Hana!" Billie's voice pierced through her headset. "Do not fucking move." "What?" "I'm getting a reading that... it doesn't make any sense, this..." "What is it? Should I be worried?" Hana was bouncing in anticipation, sweating. She looked around, trying to see what could be causing a reaction like that but... "It says that there is no concept there. But there was one, back when we started tracking them!" And then, Hana saw it. When you spend a long time going at a high speed in a car, your ability to judge how fast you are moving is twisted, something called velocitization. When you are wandering the Noospheric abyss for a long time, the nothing blends together, and you start to have trouble distinguishing between what is the Noospheric nothing, and what is actually nothing. Looking down, just inches in front of her feet, she didn't see the expected shimmering of the Noospheric plane that she walked here on. She didn't see the subtle shift of a conceptual material, or the blinking of a concept that was changing before her eyes. She saw the abyss, the //true// abyss, for the first time in a very long time. The Noosphere before her bent and contorted itself, bloating and collapsing, lensing as though eating the very combination of light and ideas around her. And suddenly, it was Prom Night, and Hana Thompson was the queen, standing on stage before the multitude of faces she could no longer recognize. It was Prom Night, and she was sinking impossibly deeper and deeper into the school's pool, being drawn towards a darkness that she would never be able to swim back from, if she had wanted to at all.   It was Prom Night, and it was the present, and once more the abyss called her name.   "I-I figured out what happened." Her mind screamed at her to run as fast and far away as she could get, and she felt every urge to pull her jacket closer to assure herself that she was real. "What is it?" Billie sounded anxious, scared even. //Is she worried about... me?// "Whatever they did? It worked. There's //nothing// here, literally. There is a giant hole in the Noosphere, down into the abyss. It's..." //It's so cold.// "You should come back, and we can figure out what to do next." Hana gazed into nothingness, and she felt the Noosphere begin to peel away around her. From within nothingness, Hana began to hear voices, calling to her, began to hear laughing and the slightly off-beat mixing of Billboard's Top-25 songs played from a DJ. And then, she once more found herself floating in the water, as a collection of figures swam around her. From within nothingness, a mass of grasping hands and fingers slowly extended upwards, grabbing at Hana's feet and legs and pulling her closer and closer before-- "Hana, you still with me?" And everything became clearer around her. "Ye-- yeah, okay..." She slowly took a step back, and then another, and again, and again, and again, until she was back at the junction, far away from the hole into the abyss. She was still frozen, as if submerged in icy water, unable to claw herself above the surface. The abyss that Hana had worked so hard to expel from her memory, the wound she had worked so hard to try to mend, finally set its gaze upon her. And all she could do was stare back. ----- Hana stumbled through the door that led to the safe haven that was meant to be SITE. There wasn't a definite point where she could tell when the Noosphere ended and the movie theater-like carpeting of floor began, but the change of scenery did very little to ease the railroad spike migraine that burrowed itself deep into her head. Even when she dropped to all fours, coughing as she tried to drink in the air around her, there was little relief; the air smelled of lacquer and moldy foam soaked with spray deodorant. SITE seemed to respond to these thoughts in kind. From across the room, Hana saw Billie, quite concerned, quickly move from behind her control panel to meet her at the door. "Please help me," was all Hana could mutter as she reached a hand out. Right before she could feel Billie take it, a moment before the girl's touch could help ground her, she drew her hand back, a rush of bile raising in her throat. //She can't know what happened.// Mustering what little focus she could, Hana quickly shot up and bolted, ducking into a nearby maintenance closet and closing the door behind her. She closed her eyes as she pressed her back against the metal door with as much of her weight as she could. The surface provided a sturdy return, but did very little to ease her malaise. "It's not real, Hana. It's not real. They fixed you, remember? You're just seeing things." Hana brought her knees to her chest, hoping that the compactness would return her to euthymia. "It's not real and it can't hurt you anymore." There was a soft //tap, tap, tap// on the door behind her. "Hana? Are you alright? Talk to me." //She can't know what happened.// ----- Billie looked at her wrist, uncomfortable shifting her watch. It wasn't like Hana to act like... this. The entire time they'd known each other, not once had Billie seen that confident demeanor waver. Whatever Hana had seen out there had definitely spooked her, bad, and that scared Billie. She tried knocking softly on the metal door again. "Hana? Hey, you've been in there for a while now. Are you still with me?" Only silence answered. //Hana this isn't like you. Say something. Please.// "I'm sorry... I'm so so sorry..." a voice weakly murmured from the other side of the door. Billie pushed herself closer to it, trying to get a better listen. "Hana?" "I can't escape it. It just keeps finding me." Hana retched and began coughing. "I can't even close my eyes without seeing them." Billie carefully tried the handle, finding it unlocked. //She's never going to let me in if she's leaning against the door. Unless...// Billie thought back to her training, and the many //many// lectures her mother had given her about interacting with patients in distress. "Hana, you've been in there for half an hour. I'm worried about you." "You can't see me like this, Billie. I-I'm... just not ready yet. I'm sorry." "Do you trust me?" Silence. Billie could hear Hana shuffle. "I do." "I'm going to close my eyes and come sit with you, alright? We can figure this out together." Another pause. "Do you promise?" "I promise, Hana. I would never do anything to hurt you." Billie heard more shuffling, and the sound of metallic reverberation as a weight removed itself from behind the door. //I really hope this works.// She wrapped her hand around the handle, shut her eyes, and entered the closet. Although she expected to trip over all matter of tool or loose wire, the path forward was clear, as if the tools had put themselves away and the wires slithered under the nearest shelving unit. But still, Billie walked forward, her arms extended, prodding at the walls as she walked forward, before finally touching something soft. She opened her eyes just a sliver, and was met with a field of baby blue caught on a protruding piece of metal. On the floor right beside her, curled in the fetal position, was Hana, quietly sobbing. "You know, when we first started talking this summer, you told me that you would help me be brave." She grabbed Hana's jacket and held it outwards. With a measured scoop, she wrapped Hana in her jacket and held the girl close to her chest, leaning into her, praying that whatever she was doing would work. "Please, let me help by returning the favor." She watched Hana's expression soften as the weight of her body leaned into Billie, tangling them together on the ground. Billie let out a sigh of relief, and with the arm that wasn't pinned underneath Hana, moved patch of hair out from in front of the girl's eyes. "Billie?" Hana said, weakly. "I'm here, Hana. I'm not going anywhere." ----- Heather Garrison was once again, in her office, staring down her computer terminal. This time, instead of the dull monotony that plagued her, she was working on something far more fun. A schematic turned around on her screen, digital callouts leading to memetic arrays. //Nonsense unless you know exactly what they mean.// Heather was, in fact, one of two people who understood them. //But I think this should work.// She leaned back in her desk chair, cracking her neck, straining at her latent soreness. A constant parade of projects danced through her mind of what to start working on next, a cavalcade of chaos that she called her font of inspiration beckoning, a feast for her mind. Her door opening decided that for her. "Heather!" Billie burst in, in an uncharacteristically Hana-esque display of recklessness. "There's an emergency." //Sure there is.// Watching Hana follow her in, winded, face red, looking away from her; Heather gave it slightly more weight than she normally would have. "Pennrose told me about your little excursion. Have fun chasing ghosts?" "Heath," Hana said, meekly. "This is... this is serious." Amusement dropped and concern raised, Heather stood from her desk, guiding the girls to a pair of loveseats, arranged around a table. She showed them to their seats and turned away, pausing. //Okay, let's review. Pennrose said they heard a transmission about some group with a weapon on the radio. Like him, I figured it was nothing. But, if they're...// "What did you find? How many combatants were there?" Heather sat, crossing one leg over the other, leaning forward. "Are you hurt?" Hana sat, silent, shell-shocked it seemed, while Billie burst out, gripping Hana's hand, knuckles white. "We didn't find any combatants, that's just the thing." Billie looked to Hana, and then continued. "When Hana went to the source of the signal, there was..." "A monster?" Heather scoffed. "No." Hana looked at her, directly, pleading for the Heather who had once [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/deadgirlwalking|snuck]]] her out of her containment cell. "Heather, there was nothing there." //Nothing? This isn't... why the hell are they so worked up about...// Heather stopped herself, considering the terror she still saw in Hana's gaze. //Okay, say that they are rightly worried about--// "As in, a hole in the Noosphere?" Hana nodded. //Fuck.// Heather tried not to let that show. "Right, well... yeah, I can see why you two were concerned. A hole in the Noosphere that shouldn't be there is... worrisome. Thank you two for letting me know. Was there anything else?" "What?" Billie stared at her, dumbfounded. "It's 'worrisome'? That's it?" "What do we do next?" Hana was bolder now, incensed. "Are we going to track them down, do we--" "We?" Heather held out her hands. "Slow down there girls. You don't have to do anything. So, I'd say, the answer is 'don't worry about it'!" //I need to talk to Lillian and Omnia, this shouldn't b--// "Don't worry about it?" Hana was yelling, on the verge of tears. "Are you fucking kidding me? I'm... I faced down the fucking abyss and you're telling me to just relax? Are you seriou--" "Hana, that's enough." Hana shut up, Heather having used her Director voice. "Yes. That is correct, I am telling you to //calm the fuck down//, and go do nothing." "But--" "But nothing." Heather glared at the two girls, frowning. "Don't you get it, Hana? Billie? You just told me that there is a group out there with the ability to erase things from the Noosphere, at will. Not erase a memory, not abstract an idea, they are //obliterating// the very concepts where they are. This is above your paygrade. Way above." //It's not absence, I would know. I don't think there's a pattern screamer that close so who could it be? Fuck, I just need to get them out of here so I can figure out what's happening.// "But Heather, Hana discovered it, shouldn't she--" "Absolutely not." Heather stood up, shaking her head. "Billie, you might not know this, but Hana? She has a pretty fucking awful track record when it comes to dealing with memories and concepts. Just ask her about prom. That will tell you //exactly// why you two shouldn't be fucking dealing with this." The room was silent. Hana's eyes met Heather, as the pained look of betrayal flashed over her face. "Am I clear?" "Yes, ma'am," the girls said in partial unison, rising from their seats, slamming the door behind them as they left the office. //Finally.// Heather massaged her temples, idly pinging Lillian to come to her office ASAP. //What the fuck did these two stumble into?// If Heather knew anything, and she often did: it was going to be a fucking mess. //Was... was I too harsh?// Heather frowned, shaking her head. //No, not when the stakes are this high. This is what being a Director is, sometimes, you just need to be a bit of an asshole.// She could dwell on how she could have handled that better another time, there were far more pressing matters at hand. ----- [[div class="text-container-wrap"]] +++ Hana <3 [[div class="text-container"]] [[div class="sent"]] [[span class="text"]]hey[[/span]] [[span class="text"]]you up[[/span]] [[/div]] [[div class="recv"]] [[span class="text"]]Yeah[[/span]] [[span class="text"]]I can't sleep[[/span]] [[/div]] [[div class="sent"]] [[span class="text"]]Heather was a dick.[[/span]] [[/div]] [[div class="recv"]] [[span class="text"]]It's[[/span]] [[span class="text"]]It's fine.[[/span]] [[/div]] [[div class="sent"]] [[span class="text"]]it's not fucking okay[[/span]] [[span class="text"]]sorry i just[[/span]] [[span class="text"]]she shouldn't have said that[[/span]] [[/div]] [[div class="recv"]] [[span class="text"]]Heather can be a dick sometimes.[[/span]] [[span class="text"]]Just the first time I've been on the receiving end, I guess.[[/span]] [[/div]] [[div class="sent"]] [[span class="text"]]you know what?[[/span]] [[span class="text"]]meet me at the door to the noosphere[[/span]] [[/div]] [[div class="recv"]] [[span class="text"]]Why?[[/span]] [[/div]] [[div class="sent"]] [[span class="text"]]i... i think i need to see what you saw[[/span]] [[/div]] [[/div]] [[/div]] ----- Billie Forsythe wasn't sure that her plan was a good one. To be fair, she hadn't been given many opportunities in life to formulate ones, nor to execute them. She was, however, pretty sure that this plan was questionable, at best. "Are we almost there?" Billie asked, pulling Hana with her through the Noosphere. "If... if you don't want to go there, I... it's okay to bail, you know that, right?" "You wanted to see the abyss, right?" Billie nodded. She had once, in another time, suspended herself before the emptiness and felt as if she could soar. She was besotted with the nothingness of the Noospheric abyss. //I need to see it again.// "Then I want to take you there." "Will you be okay?" "Yeah." Hana gave her a soft smile. "You're with me, I think... I think I'll be alright." The pair walked hand in hand, turning rocky, yet blank passages carved through thoughtspace, until Billie was a cavernous bowl open before there. "We're here." Hana nodded to the empty expanse. "This is the nothing." Billie kneeled down, staring at the surface of the Noosphere. There was a slight shimmer, a ripple of color, like heat rising from hot concrete on a summer's day, barely perceptible. It extended for ten, maybe twenty feet, and then... //The abyss.// "Can..." Billie bit her lip. "Do you think we can get closer?" "How close do you want to get?" //She's going to think I'm insane.// Billie steeled her courage. "I want to... I want to sit on the edge with you." Billie began to spiral, mind racing, thinking of all the things Hana could say. Hana stood there, transfixed, deep in thought, her neutral face turning more and more conflicted. //Fuck, I shouldn't have push--// "Okay." Hana nodded. "For-- For you." //She's incredible.// Billie stared at her crush in awe, as Hana bravely stepped towards the abyss, inching closer and closer to the edge with her, their fingers interlaced. Billie felt her hand warming up, Hana's heat offsetting her natural cold, mixing between the two girls to a stasis, somewhere in between. //Body temperature,// her nurse-brain reminded her. Hana stopped, beginning to sit down. Billie joined her, as they both scooted towards the edge of the Noosphere, inch by inch, until when she stuck her foot out, she felt nothing. Like a flat edge, there was a straight line, cut through the Noosphere, rounded, plummeting like a cliff-face. Billie carefully leaned forward looking down. There was nothing below them. Complete and utter emptiness. A sight that she had longed to return to, longed to revisit. There was a temptation, as there always was for her, to plunge within. To embrace the forever abyss, to disappear forever, falling eternal, alone until the end. This time, she felt Hana squeeze her hand. //I... I can't. Not when there is something more to my life. Not... not now.// Billie, resolute, leaned back, reclining, legs dangling over the edge, as she stared up at the flickering lights overhead. "It's gorgeous here." "You think?" Hana was lying back too, propped up on an elbow. "I... I just see the end. My--" "Hey, you don't..." Billie looked at Hana, letting go of her hand to touch her shoulder. "You don't owe me anything. Heather shouldn't have said anything, I'm not going to think about it. You tell me when you're ready." "I..." Hana's eyes began to water. "I want to tell you. I trust you, Billie." Billie gulped, pit in her stomach, anxiety welling to the forefront. Her heart quickened, as Hana leaned into her touch. They both lay down, side by side, Billie's arm across Hana's shoulders, holding her close. As they looked up at the thoughts dancing overhead, Hana continued. "Heather was talking about the reason I'm in containment. I... it was high school, and I was stupid. I just... I needed to be what I was meant to be, you know?" "I think so." "Right, homeschooled." Hana smiled, snickering. "I... I started to erase things. People. I... I wanted to be them, to be what they were, to be what I thought I deserved. I didn't care about who they were, I cared about who I could be." Billie pulled Hana closer, as she quietly began to cry. "I nearly drowned. I was in the pool, and they were pulling me in, deeper and deeper, into the nothingness, into the abyss, into..." "Into somewhere just like this." "Ye-- Yeah." Hana took some breaths to steady herself. "Somehow, I survived. But..." "It's okay, Hana." Billie let go of her shoulders, so she could turn and look at Hana. Hana looked at her, tears falling down, smiling in a grimace. "You must think I'm a monster." "I could never think that." Billie reached out, brushing the tears off of Hana's silken face. //Even when crying, she's so beautiful.// "Then what are you thinking?" Hana swallowed, blinking, fighting her emotions, the tears slowing. "I think that you are the bravest person I know." Billie brushed Hana's cheek, playing with her hair. "I think that you were young, and stupid, and I know that I've made mistakes that were just as bad. I just had a helicopter mom and an entire Foundation site to keep me from the same place you ended up." "Really?" "Yeah." Billie's heart soared as she saw Hana smile, a brilliant and magical sight. "Hana, you are so strong. You have been beaten down by the world, by being locked in containment, and yet... you still try, so fucking hard, all for other people. You're incredible, you know that?" "No, I'm not." Hana sniffled, wiping at her face. She looked at Billie, blinking slowly. "Yo-- You're so nice." It was Billie's turn to snort. "Not really. I just..." Billie froze, terrified about what she might say if she kept talking. Hana was gorgeous, painted by the flickering lights overhead, and Billie knew that if she didn't stop now, she might admit exactly what she felt. "You... you just what?" Hana had reached out, first teasing Billie's hair out, before her hand settled on the nape of her neck, playing with the fuzz of her fade. "You can... you can say anything to me." "I..." Billie stammered, face heating, unconsciously, reaching out with her hand, brushing an errant tear from Hana's face, coming to rest in Hana's mess of hair. "I don't want to say something wrong." She felt Hana's hand crawl up the back of her neck, pressing more firmly against her head, as Hana looked at her, eyes full of want. "You..." Billie couldn't take it any longer. "I think that I really like you." Billie tightened her hand, feeling Hana's heartbeat increase with her touch. "You are so beautiful, and I just..." "You..." Hana was pulling towards her as she did the same, her cherry lips parted just a hair. "You just what?" "I just..." Billie was nearly whispering, as they looked into each other's eyes, inches apart now. "I... I want to kiss you." "Okay." They each pulled the other in, gently kissing at first as Billie's mind soared, metaphorical fireworks made real, expanding in the Noosphere overhead. She fell into the embrace, tasting Hana for the first time, reveling in the sweetness. Hana grabbed at her, pulling her closer, as the two rolled around, hungrily devouring each other. After a minute, they separated. Billie felt like she was weightless. She stared at Hana's lips, saliva clinging between them, her tongue dancing on the edge. An invitation to resume. Billie leaned back over her, with pleasure, and their lips met again. Lying there, on the edge of the abyss, Hana and Billie spent the next hour finally letting their true feelings show. Their problems were forgotten. They were together, and that was what mattered. ----- [[include :scp-wiki:component:earthworm | first=false | last=false | hub=yes | previous-url=https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/preordained-diagnosis| previous-title=Preordained Diagnosis | next-url=/| next-title=Retrograde Amnesia | hub-url=https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forgotten-memories-hub| hub-title=Comorbidities — A Forgotten Memories Series ]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box |author=Queerious & Astersquill]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box-end]]

Ali Khan Hotel & Casino

Card Game Parlor 3 | Camera 8

A poker table sits at the centre of the view, 6 people are sat around it, each holding a hand of 5 cards. At the head of the table, PoI-7777 "The Dealer", dressed in a neon coloured crystalline suit, stands with his face obscured to the camera by the brim of his hat.

PoI-7777: Firstly, I'd like to thank you all for coming to test our new game on such short notice.

Dr. Yule: Get on with it, Bucko! We ain't got all day.

Dr. Queen: I hate to agree with the scum, but please, we get the gist. I have to pick up my kids in 3 hours so I unfortunately don't have the time to dilly dally.

PoI-7777: Alright then.

The Dealer places a card in front of each player and snaps his fingers. Suddenly all of the green on the table morphs into water, the cards transforming into pirate ships.

PoI-7777: We'll be playing "Sailship Royale". Each and every card in your 80 card decks represents an action you can take. The aim, to be the last ship standing. This is turn based of course, but at any time, you can spin the wheel of god. Whatever effect it lands on, is immediately applied to the board. You each can only spin the wheel a total of three times per game. You lose if your ship is destroyed or you run out available actions. Any questions?

Dr. Langstrum raises her hand.

PoI-7777: Yes?

Dr. Langstrum: What about drinks?

PoI-7777: Ah yes, as our esteemed play testers, you can request any drink of your choice at any time. Don't worry about causing a mess, everything in this room is waterproof.

Dr. Langstrum: Hell yeah, I'll have one Ocean Water cocktail then.

PoI-7777: Fabulous, that will be with you in a moment. Anyhow, the turn order will start with Dr. Yule here and continue clockwise, ending with Dr. Langstrum. Are you all ready?

Sir Williams: I don't know about these simpletons, but I'm ready to prove my greatness!

Dr. Swirl: Re—

Dr. Yule: LET'S JUST GET STARTED ALREADY!

PoI-7777: Alright, three, two, one…

An airhorn sound effect rings throughout the room. Dr. Yule smiles devilishly as he stares at his cards. After a few seconds, he tosses a card at the ship in front of him.

Dr. Yule: Lets see what this does.

Upon impact with the ship, the card transforms into a pirate dressed in wine red and right gold. With a loud roar, the pirate takes control of the ship, driving it towards the edge of the table where the Dealer stands.

Dr. Yule: Oh, hell yeah.

Dr. Queen: Guess it's my turn.

Dr. Queen stares at her hand for 2 seconds before placing 3 cards on top of the ship. After a second of delay, the cards transform into a fleet, guarding the ship on both sides. Dr. Queen smirks and gestures for Sir Williams to take his turn.

Sir Williams: Since these fools are too cowardly, I shall be the first to spin the wheel!

PoI-7777: Alright!

The Dealer snaps his fingers and a group of figures, clad entirely in black, push a massive lottery wheel into the room, although it is not legible from the angle of the camera.

PoI-7777: Well then, let's spin that wheel!!!!!!!!!!!!!

The Dealer tips his hat and presses a concealed button, causing the wheel to start spinning. It remains in motion for 2 minutes before landing on a green tile.

PoI-7777: Lucky you! Draw 2 cards!

Sir Williams does as told, now holding 7 cards.

Sir Williams: I'd like to spin again.

PoI-7777: Well, we've got a daredevil over here alright! Let us, once again, spin that wheel!!!

The Dealer presses the button again and the wheel spins for another 2 minutes before landing on another green tile. Sir Williams celebrates and draws 2 more cards.

Sir Williams: Now, does spinning the wheel count as taking my turn?

PoI-7777: Of course not! That would be absurd.

Sir Williams laughs.

Sir Williams: Excellent then I am going to spin the entire wheel and…! Play my entire hand to boot!

Sir. Williams flashes all 9 cards, each of which displaying the text "Spin the wheel and multiply the result by 2X (X being the number of these cards played at once. If this card is played solo, X=2)".

PoI-7777: Oh really?! Are you sure you want to multiply this result of this final spinning of the wheel by 521?

Sir Williams: Ha! I am the grand finance guru! My luck and skill is unmatched! Spin the darn wheel already, you serf!

PoI-7777: Welp, I warned ya.

The Dealer presses the button and the wheel starts spinning yet again. After 3 minutes of spinning, it lands on a black tile.

PoI-7777: Unfortunate!

PoI-7777 chuckles.

Sir Williams: What does that mean?!

PoI-7777: You landed on a disaster tile! That means we must now pull a card from the disaster deck!

The Dealer produces a deck of dark purple playing cards from his sleeve, placing them on the edge of the table.

PoI-7777: Your disaster is…

Multiple lights on the ceiling flash orange.

PoI-7777: Meteor Shower!

Sir Williams: Huh?

Tiny meteors begin to rain down from the ceiling and into Sir Williams' ship. After 5 minutes, the final meteor silently lands in the water, nothing of the ship remaining. Sir Williams stares at the empty space where his ship stood for another minute before slamming his fist against the table edge.

Sir Williams: Fuck you!

PoI-7777: You lost fair and square my friend.

Sir Williams: I won't stand for this!

Sir Williams snaps his fingers and vanishes in a puff of smoke. The Dealer laughs.

PoI-7777: Well, that guy's a sore loser.

Dr. Langstrum: Oh, he is. Massive sore loser loser, that guy.

Dr. Langstrum finishes her second Ocean Water and orders a third as Dr. Swirl stares at her cards.

Dr. Swirl: I guess I'll… play this.

Dr. Swirl tosses a card towards the board. As it makes contact with the water, Dr. Swirl's ship moves to where Sir Williams' ship once stood and opened fire on Dr. Queen's fleet, taking down one ship and damaging 2 others. Dr. Swirl nods to Dr. Langstrum who downs her third ocean water in one gulp and tosses her hand onto her ship. One by one, the card's vanish and the ship increases in grandeur, eventually becoming reinforced by a metal outer layer.

PoI-7777: And so, round one concludes. How are yall feeling?

Dr. Queen: I think this game will make you a lot of mo—

Dr. Yule: Shut up!

Dr. Yule draws a card and places it on top of his ship. Upon impact, the ship duplicates and begins to move towards Dr. Langstrum's ship.

Dr. Yule: I'm going to take you down!

Dr. Langstrum: WOO! I'd like to spin the wheel!

PoI-7777: Good choice!

The Dealer presses the button and the wheel spins, landing on a yellow tile after a minute and a half.

PoI-7777: Oh, that means you get to take your turn early! Play away!

Another ocean water cocktail is presented to Dr. Langstrum, who downs it one gulp and orders another before drawing a card and tossing it into play. Upon impact, her ship turns to face Dr. Yule's fleet, moves in-between the two and opens fire, quickly sinking both ships.

Dr. Yule: Fuck! That's not fair!

Dr. Yule attempts to punch the Dealer, who catches his fist with ease.

PoI-7777: HA!

The footage turns to golden static for 2 seconds before returning to normal. Dr. Yule can be seen being dragged out of the room, unconscious and without his labcoat. The Dealer uses a towel to wipe the blood off his hands.

PoI-7777: I never said this would be fair, did I?

Dr. Queen: Thank the lords, that guy was quite annoying.

Dr. Queen draws a card and laughs.

Dr. Queen: Oh, whoever designed this game needs a raise!

Dr. Queen places three card atop her fleet in a triangle formation. Suddenly, her fleet combines into an aircraft carrier, holding a missile launcher.

Dr. Queen: Full throttle!

With a loud bang, the missiles launch from the carrier and swiftly land in sinking Dr. Swirl's vessel.

Dr. Swirl: Dammit.

Dr. Queen: Sorry girly, but you aren't as hot as your girlfriend.

Dr. Swirl sighs.

Dr. Swirl: Whatever. Good game.

PoI-7777: Since you've been much calmer than those men, I'll let you stay and watch.

Dr. Swirl: Alright.

Dr. Langstrum: Yippeessssssssssshhhhhhhh?!

<Extraneous data removed>

After 2 total hours of gameplay, the board is now unrecognisable, now resembling trenches, no naval vessels can be seen. Dr. Langstrum is visibly inebriated.

Dr. Langstrum: I'm gunna bet yu-you

Dr. Swirl: Babe, I think you've had too much to drink.

Dr. Langstrum: You swound like swodo and the beeg fuckoff dragoon that struck me with ferts an hour agoo.

Dr. Langstrum burps as she tosses a card on the field, which transforms into 5 wounded soldiers.

Dr. Queen: I would like to spin the wheel.

Dr. Langstrum: Me too!

PoI-7777: I'm sorry Miss Langstrum, but you've already spun three times.

Dr. Langstrum: Bullfrog! I did… I didn't… I can't rememb.

PoI-7777: Well, Mrs Queen, this will be your last spin of the wheel. Are you sure?

Dr. Queen: Of course.

PoI-7777: Well then, lets spin! That! Wheel!

The Dealer presses the button and the wheel whirs to life. After 3 minutes, it dramatically lands on a black tile.

PoI-7777: Disaster time!

Dr. Queen: I'd like to play this.

Dr. Queen places a card with the text "Disaster Shield" in front of the dealer.

PoI-7777: Great decision.

Dr. Langstrum: Bring it on, swayby!

PoI-7777: Alright, your disaster is…!

The Dealer draws a card from the disaster deck and smirks.

PoI-7777: LANDMINE!

The group of soldiers take a step forward, immediately steeping on a land mine, which explodes, killing the entire group instantly. Dr. Langstrum makes incoherent noises of frustration as Dr. Queen silently celebrates. Dr. Swirl sighs, picks up Dr. Langstrum in her arms and leaves the room.

Dr. Queen: What's my prize?

Dr. Queen stands as the board returns to a normal poker table. The Dealer chuckles.

PoI-7777: Nothing!

Dr. Queen: …Excuse me?

PoI-7777: The fun of playing is reward enough.

Dr. Queen: You're saying I could've spent this time fucking my wife but instead I played this stupid as shit card game?!

PoI-7777: Well, you had fu—

Dr. Queen screeches, causing the room to erupt in pink light for 10 seconds. Once the feed returns, the room can be seen in rubble. The Dealer can be seen in the same position, unharmed. After a few seconds, he turns and leaves.

PoI-7777: (muttering) I think that went well.

sunsetter.raw_content:
• 

    close

    Info

    X

    A tale about the Apostate is on its way "soon."

    The epigraph is Supertramp's Goodbye Stranger

7eventy7evenfold

Goodbye, stranger. It's been nice,
Hope you find your paradise,
Tried to see your point of view,
Hope your dreams will all come true

Goodbye Mary, goodbye Jane,
Will we ever meet again?
Feel no sorrow; feel no shame—
Come tomorrow, feel no pain

If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold...

It seems we're at an impasse.

It is the year of our LORD, 2200. My heart, my mind and my soul all bear an excruciating weight. Those in the same vein as me are beginning to meet their end, no matter what effort they make to survive, and for no reason at all. My loved ones pass, just the same as those I resent. All that I love, just as soon be goodbyes.

I am a Nobody. Centuries have passed since I was first cursed the right to utter those words and mean them, from the chasm of my heart. I have not been able to feel, to befriend, even to love, for a being beyond my power has drawn out my soul and murdered it in cold blood. It is on my hands, now, staining my fingers a deep red as I grasp at what is left and find an absence in its place.

I remember it clearly now. 1775 is the number engraved into my mind that reminds me of the year I lost it all. An angel had come unto me — a form composed of millions of quills and feathers, alight with a brilliant radiance — saying "Be not afraid," and granting me with a task. Then he, in his holiness, asked me if I wanted to give it all to preserve the Earth, the promise of Paradise following. I answered "Yes."

A parasite of my making, to torture my soul to no end. And yet I know that he was right, that without me, this world would not be able to stand on its own two feet, rather it would burn and wither away into the wind. I contain the knowledge of one million scholars, and the weight of one million stars, all amassed together into a cacophony of nothing that eats away at my being, a faceless husk to leech off of those around me until they, too, are nobodies.

To be blessed by Him in such a sardonic way leaves me beyond hollow.

A cosmic trip to ease the mind is required. As a first in a series of episodes, I am overtaken by a horrible, bright static, and when it ceases, I find myself sitting on a railing, far above ground. I allow my cane to fall to the hard pavement, before unlatching my fingers and leaping into the darkest night, only for my curse to rescue me, allowing me to drift freely. I yearn for an adventure through space and through time, and I allow it to happen, letting my matrix guide me. With another brief flash of static, I arrive at a water planet. I am in a galaxy not too dissimilar to my own. I plummet into the water, before letting myself float in its purplish hue, my hands splashing about and making a mess. It is beautiful. The clouds in the sky appear as mountains in the wind, certainly denser than those I am familiar with. There is life brewing on this planet, slow-burning in such a fashion as to hatch in many years. But I haven't the time.

Letting that deep white static overtake me once more, I come to, and find my feet failing to meet solid ground as an immense force violently draws me towards a gas giant. I stop myself in the mustard yellow air, simply allowing myself to float. Taking a breath, I jet into the planet, letting its air, but not its force, overtake me. Though I am not hurt, it still pains me. This is much, much less pleasant than the cool purple of the water. I grow tired of holding myself together and leave that wretched sight.

At once, a deep shadow is cast onto me. Confused and frightened, I turn around and face my gaze towards a multicolored show of galaxies dancing, before realizing I find myself on a planet long forsaken by its sun. It holds no value. It is just like me; never to be thought of again, as it is damned away into the vastness of eternity, only being lit by the late image of distant galaxies, one day to die out just as well. I love you. But this is not enough. Static. Black out.

Wake up. I'm not sure where I am. I see nothing but dull flames, and I begin feeling the urge to party 'til my legs give out— What the fuck? Get out of my head, you're not invited— OUT. I dig my fingers deep into the delicious Party Pie my "eyes" and rip them out. I can still see, but whatever was in my head ceased. Thank God. Take me away from there.

I black out again, and this time I awake somewhere on the outskirts of the observable universe. My vision slowly grows distorted as I feel myself being pulled across space and time. No, this cannot happen. That is invalid. I am a cosmic criminal. Let me out. I resist the pull of the wormhole and nearly escape, but it collapses in on me. I feel its claws attempting to pull me apart, but I am deeply disconnected from reality to such a degree that I slip out, as if its hands are wet. I see a bright, red light, near a mangled amalgamation of entrails, in the distance. It doesn't notice me, yet grows fearful. Fuck this, you can't contain me in a void. I am the void.

I rip apart the hole in unreality with my bare hands, unleashing my vocals to SCREAM my way out, barraged by a violent sensory overload of color, before I fall to the floor on a balcony. It has a beautiful view of the night sky, with a boreal feeling overtaking me, and I can sense that I have been returned to the one place I could make an argument for "belonging to." I turn and am met with curtains veiling a window. I lift it open, and can see… myself. I am struggling against a gunman. A memory assaults me, and I can recall this very moment, just over two centuries ago. How time flies when nobody cares. I do not care. Take me somewhere nice, perhaps… let me see the future.

I am assaulted by static as it seeps over every inch of my body and takes control of me. I watch as my body tries and fails to maintain itself. I cannot think properly. Who did this… let me out, please. My head is bleeding. I am curtained in darkness. I ask the static for forgiveness. I beg the static to take me to the present. I cry for the static. I weep for the static. The static fails me.

It is the year of our LORD, 2200. I land on my feet after falling from a skyscraper, and decide that it is not fit for me to die today. I walk down a dingy sidewalk. My cane is back, resting in my hands. Its clacking against the concrete leaves an annoying noise in my ears that ticks me off. Nobody seems to notice.

I am a violator of logic. My history is outlined by white chalk. I cannot exist. But here I am. I enter a diner. Cue man asking questions. I answer. He leaves. Minutes pass in a blur. He returns. Hands me objects. I begin a feast. A man not dissimilar to me manifests in my booth, just across from me. He sits and waits and the eyes of the poor old sap he's using to talk are dead, the skin yellowish and rotten. He babbles, in an ugly tan jacket and a shitty matching flat cap. He used to have a normal trilby, you know.

"7. We need to talk," he speaks in a way that demands I inquire more. I look at him. Into his face, if you can call it that.

"Not today, E—"

"Yes today. Today marks forty years since the Expurgation began, and it's catching up to us. Everything's unstable, damnit. Even Heaven." He keeps moving his stupid mouth. "Someone as ontologically insecure as you doesn't need to be screwing with spacetime right now. Until the suits and haloes find a cause and stop the death of all things weird, can you not?"

I look at him. Let's break it down for him.

"Hey, Emissary. Ambassador. Whatever you call yourself. Can I ask you something?"

"What?"

"Can you not give me shit today? Every year for God knows how long, you just keep going on and on about these fucking guidelines and the 'fate of the narrative' and all that jazz. Well you know what? The author isn't just gonna let their fucking narrative die." He takes a sip from a coffee mug that honest to You just appeared in his hands. "It doesn't matter that you're the New God, that things are dying, or anything else. They need this. They need me and you and that stupid angel cunt you sicked on me and that isn't going anywhere, okay?"

He just kept fucking staring at me. I hate that face he always has. He has a face?

"The universe is fine. We're both not going anywhere, okay?" I think it's getting to him. "So don't. I want to just have one more roadtrip before Death shoots me in the face and I die 'til I'm needed again." My items are cold. Unappetizing. I slide the plate to him. "You can have the food if you'd like. I wasn't hungry anyways." He stares at me like I shot his dog.

"Alright, 7. Just…" His mouth hangs open. "…just promise not to fuck anything up, alright?"

"Promise. And when I'm back, call me Pluto." At this point, I'm at least half-confident my fingers cross themselves. But I can't feel them. He leaves — disappears. The employees disappear. The diner disappears. Everything is consumed by static. Not again. Please. Just take me home.

Suddenly, I am made to kneel, as absence subsumes the structure of the building, replacing it with a realm devoid of thought. Despite its foundation, it reeks of hatred and malice. What is this place? Is this truly my home? I notice a castle in the distance and through the molecular gaps, I notice someone not at all unlike me sitting atop a throne built on lies and curiosity. He similarly dons a coat and trilby, and his eyes gleam crimson… the Devil. Antipathy fuels the dimensions of this place. I want not to be here. A maniacal episode almost overtakes me, but I refuse. Take me somewhere familiar, comfort me.

I let the static take me, covering my body and seeping inside of me once more. It is a solace. I feel my feet touch the ground, and—

I am standing at a helipad. A calendar at a security booth places me in 2000. I gaze off into the deep desert, and — staring intently — I can see this building. And myself. I face back around and walk towards the entrance of the building, but a guard asks me for an I.D. I shake his hand and he presents a biometric scanner. I access it and he lets me go. He doesn't seem to notice that it presents his information afterward. I walk through the door and see a giant room with several pathways. I notice one labelled "Administrative Quarters." Walking through, I am greeted with mahogany hallways that lead towards nowhere in particular. I want to see someone. I approach a door labeled "Site Director." I peer through the window. The weary Dolloran Light sits at an office desk, biting her nails. She's worried she'll lose her job because of an accident. She is always so stressed. She passed along less than two centuries ago. A poor dream loser. I close my eyes and let the static kill my presence. Right before I fully leave, she looks up at the window. She almost saw me.

I open my eyes to my very own "dreamland." Ceiling stars hang from a deep blue ceiling — or painted into the walls — with four doors prompting me to go anywhere. I politely reject the offer, sitting on a floor that resembles the Earth's lunar partner. Such a lovely place. A classical piece presents itself as ambience. A dramatic andante of beautiful proportions. I rest for a few moments, calming my head. For just a second, I could swear I saw the Devil, with all of his six wings, standing in the dim-lit corner.

Not the end.

I neglect to leave, but I must. A voice behind me beckons.

One last time.

It is the year of our LORD, 2200. I am on a Hawaiian beach. The sun assaults me, and I am powerless to its advances. I lift myself, limping over to a nearby hanger. I try to place my trilby atop, but it falls through as if it weren't there. I catch it and return to my seat, letting it droop over my head. My cane lies across my body. An intense light begins to shimmer in the sea — violet death. A skeletal figure approaches me, and a gong sounds, the incessant ringing failing to disturb my lovely little laydown.

Despite being a freak of nature, the thing that has been pursuing me for four centuries isn't affected by whatever is killing us off. In fact, despite what would be popular belief, he is absolutely thriving, in an odd way. Whether it be by my powers leaving me, or his simply overpowering me, I cannot remember his name. Not a fault of my own, but of reality. That's okay, though, as most simply title him O5-4.

I blink, and now he stands over me, blotting out that sweltering sun. The stench of gunpowder trails him. I have no need for the hat that is drooping over my head, so I drop it to the floor. It fizzles into obscurity, as all things surely will.

I look downwards at my feet; my legs are gone, too. No need for a cane anymore. I let it drift away into the wind, in some sort of pathetic anticlimax.

"Hello again, N," he speaks. He doesn't move his mouth— he wills it into the air. His sudden conversation catches me off guard.

"Hi, John. I take it it's about time? I'm down with a bad case of the cosmic cold."

"Mhm. It was a good run. Almost sad to see you go after such time," he assures. "But also, I'm more than certain you'll be back soon enough. Different iteration, different time."

"Yeah. I'm not going anywhere for long. I will be back. But I think it's time to rest for…" I trail off.

He shuffles. "I know what you mean. Take care."

"Thank you," I weakly mutter. "And goodnight."

Night falls, and a deep slumber awaits me. He draws a revolver and hammers it, I don't so much as flinch when he squeezes the trigger, setting a bullet on the path straight to my forehead, sure to kill me. My curse attempts to rescue me from certain death again, causing my systems to overclock and my perception of time to slow to a screeching halt. I can see it clear, now; the violet glow from his ribcage, the bullet peeking from his gun, the expressionless sorrow in his face, the stars that seem to form a pair of wings just behind him. An apostate soul to guide me to my creator, that I may return to Them and face Them again in a way They cannot recognize.

The stars are beautiful in their clarity. I can see Little Dipper from here. Strange.

My gaze falls back down and I know what I have to do. I must die tonight. Someone above me wills it.

I draw a pocket watch from my sleeve and press it. Before my curse can even react to my action, I am rendered dead by a loud— BOOM!
