With Quinn stabilized for now, Theo rushes to the aid of his Conclave. He liberates the healthiest of them first, counting on them to free and treat the stags who are in dire straits from blood loss. Even with his ice magic, the process of freeing his allies is unbearably slow. Each stag freed releases the Sidereal Stag from one of its red bindings, but with their ever-tightening grip on its legs and neck, there's no telling how much longer it or the Conclave has left. It is then that a long, slender tendril of roots and thorns whips out from behind Theo, freeing two stags in one fell swoop before receding back to its source: the deathly pale Quinn, who has propped themselves up from the altar and joined the fray in spite of the abdominal wound that is simply itching to tear itself open again at the slightest jostle.

"Quinn, you shouldn't be moving right n—"

"Theo," Quinn says hoarsely, "I love you dearly, but please, let me do this for you."

Theo's eyes water; he nods once in agreement.

Using the cloud of dust to mask their footsteps, Sylas carves into Zaryus from all sides with their knife. They target the legs first, with the hope that the poison will interfere with Zaryus' mobility and make him an even easier target. Next is his arms, for Sylas suspects that he can't channel his magic nearly as effectively without the use of his hands. Finally, a few expertly placed cuts along Zaryus' abdomen prove effective at dosing his center of mass. They've trained for many years to rely on their hearing in survival situations—and even with the chaos of battle all around them, they've already etched Zaryus' cries of pain into their heart and cleared their mind of anything else that could cloud their judgement.

Of course, the safer option would be to launch arrows into the cloud from the outside—but beyond needing to prevent him from escaping the cloud, Sylas needs to hear the tearing of his robe and skin, to feel his flesh give way as their jagged knife proves itself to be his superior. Unfortunately, it takes only one omnidirectional burst of blood to disperse the cloud of dust, and only one hand to grab Sylas by the throat and pin them to the ground.

"This is the best you can do? Your desperation outpaces your rage, and both are dwarfed by my hatred towards your false god. Your ways of 'tolerance' and 'love' have no power here—at my hand, you will die all the same. Such is the Law of Blood."

Sylas spits in Zaryus' face, but only receives laughter in response.

With a free hand, they retrieves a small red pepper from their bag. They bite down on it and utter another incantation; at that, they inhale deeply through their nose, and their eyes water intensely. Zaryus releases Sylas and attempts to jump backwards, but the poison makes him sluggish—when a gout of vengeful fire bursts forth from their mouth, it burns away the rest of his hood and sets his mask ablaze. He screams in pain, and when he discards his mask, Sylas can't help but admire the deep red hue of the knife scars that have already left his face disfigured and marred.

Through the Conclave's combined efforts, fourteen of the twenty kidnapped members have been freed thus far. The bindings on the Sidereal Stag's legs dissipate into nothingness, allowing it to stand up unsteadily in spite of the red bindings that continue tightening around its neck. As Theo goes to free the fifteenth stag, a red robe bashes him on the side of his left knee, sending him tumbling to the ground. He stands up to counterattack, but he isn't fast enough to stop the cultist and one of their allies—the last of their allies, in fact—from rushing at Quinn. Fortunately, V's blades once more prove effective at thwarting their efforts.

"Do my eyes deceive me," Quinn exclaims, their eyes lighting up from sheer elation and surprise, "or is that you, V?"

"In the flesh," V says. She struggles to maintain her footing in the face of the attackers' superior strength, but blood from a wound on her thigh shoots out as bolas that bind the attacker's legs, allowing her to knock them back.

"You have tits now!" says the delighted Quinn, who follows up by coughing up a rather concerning quantity of blood.

"And you look like utter shit," she grins.

A gout of frost from Theo freezes the attackers' legs in place, giving V the opportunity to needs to cut them down.

Sylas and Zaryus' back and forth continues. Using the embers of flame that linger in their mouth, Sylas unleashes arrows of fire on the all-too-flammable robes of the slain cultists, effectively boxing Zaryus between them. Four more arrows embed themselves in his rended, charred flesh, but while Sylas' maneuvers slow more and more from sheer exhaustion, Zaryus' wounds only serve to provide him with more blood for his foul magic. On all counts, the amount of poison Zaryus has received should have fully paralyzed him by now—but between his thaumaturgical enhancements and the continued expulsion of this blood, Sylas' dwindling rate of doses simply can't keep up.

"Tired already, Warden?"

"I'm just getting started."

"You're all bark and no bite. Why do you waste your time?"

"I've been buying time, you filthy, disgusting creature. Look around you, Zaryus. Your lackeys are all dead, and my stags are nearly freed. It's over for you—we've won."

Before Zaryus can let loose a retort, he is forced to block a flurry of blows from a shifting crimson tendril, which snakes out from the carcass of the nearest red robe and relentlessly harasses him at V's behest. Theo then unleashes a cone of cold at Zaryus' feet, but when this magical frost snuffs out the burning corpses, he seizes his opportunity for a counterattack. Using sheer force of will, Zaryus exerts his command over not only V's tendril of blood, but also the blood still present within the corpses of his fallen allies. With his supreme hemomancy, he uses the tendril to slam V into the wall, followed by a barrage of burnt corpses to pin Theo against the opposite wall. He then brandishes his lance and sets his sights on Quinn.

"Your efforts are futile. I will end this here and now."

Zaryus charges at Quinn, hoping to complete the ritual by lancing them through the heart. With the last of their strength, Sylas intercepts the charge and takes the blow instead. It bores a large hole in their shoulder; Sylas' vision doubles from the pain, but the tingling sense of elation that follows courses out from their spine all the way to the tips of their fingers, keeping every inch of their squirming body fully awake and fully alert.

With their face mere inches away from Zaryus', Sylas sees the Sidereal Stag in the reflection of his dark red irises. With the last of its bindings released, the astral eminence stands tall and proud. Its starry form offers an impossibly beautiful, yet hopelessly brief glimpse into the infinite expanses of space and time. Its twinkling stars shine down on the teeming life of the countless planets that orbit them, with large nebulae and vastly larger galactic walls gracing the void with glory beyond belief, beyond reason, beyond life itself. The Sidereal Stag stares back at them through this reflection, nodding once at them before unleashing a brilliant flash of celestial light that blinds the unsuspecting Zaryus.

The moment Zaryus covers his eyes, Sylas swigs the rest of the poison and bites down on Zaryus' arm. They dig into his flesh with the full force of their jaw—extracting a tortured scream from him that exhilarates them beyond belief—and expel the venomous contents of their mouth into the deepest recesses of his muscle tissue. Zaryus' animated blood lashes out on instinct and wraps itself around Sylas' throat, but it is shunted back into his arm and forcibly circulated through his body by a final surge of V's blood magic. Five seconds later, the poison fully sets in, and both Zaryus and V collapse to their knees.

Sitting up slowly, the disoriented Sylas takes stock of the situation. All twelve of the red robes are dead, and with any luck, Zaryus will soon follow. Sylas, V, and Theo are fully depleted of adrenaline and spirit alike. Quinn and the other stags, in spite of their severe injuries, are hard at work taking care of their own. From what they can see, at least one stag has succumbed to the blood loss, with two more being unconscious and on the verge of passing along with them. This sight fills Sylas' vision with red, returning them to the terrible smell of blood and smoke at the Conclave all over again.

To Sylas' horror, Zaryus has other plans. Despite being fully paralyzed, tendrils of blood burst forth from his wounds, raising him into the air and dragging him towards them.

"This… changes nothing…"

With their legs depleted of energy, Sylas attempts to push themselves to their feet—but the excruciatingly large hole in their shoulder brings those plans to a short, fruitless end. The others try to drag themselves forward to intervene, but with their injuries, Sylas knows all too well that they can't make it in time.

"Do you feel it, Warden? The Howling… it tugs at us… compels us…. consumes us…—"

As Zaryus looms over them, Sylas grips their knife for dear life. They curse at themselves under their breath, for in spite of all of their determination, whether they survive comes down to the dice roll of who acts faster.

"In the end, He will break you… He will ruin you… HE WILL—"

A deafening crack rings out from behind Sylas, ricocheting off the walls and reverberating throughout the ritual chamber. As the bullet whizzes past, it takes them a full three seconds to realize that its true destination is the original arrow hole in Zaryus' shoulder, and that they have in fact not reached their gruesome end quite just yet. The bullet rips through the already-brutalized flesh and bone with ease, and when they push past the initial horror of a gun being fired in their vicinity, Sylas nearly finds themselves too mesmerized by the carnage left in its wake to turn around and discover who fired it.

Cassandra spins the barrel of her revolver, casually pulls the safety without a care in the world, and fires again.

This time, the bullet lands at the bottom of Zaryus' right eye socket, precisely where the maxilla meets the zygomatic bone. Fragments of these bones ripple out into his orbital cavity, shredding his eye in its entirety and spraying large, crimson-stained blobs of clear vitreous gel back onto Sylas. The rescued members of the Conclave yelp in horror, flinching backwards and clutching onto their loved ones out of weary, adrenaline-depleted instinct. Only being partially desensitized to skull-bullet collisions, Theo averts his gaze, but not before covering Quinn's eyes. V smiles in relief and joy. As Zaryus rolls onto the floor and cries out, Sylas drinks in every millisecond of the brutal, agonizing pain he experiences with their hungry green eyes, although a dim concern that these bullets might prove fatal creeps into the back of their still-pounding skull.

"Relax, Sylas," reassures Cassandra. "It takes a lot more than that to kill someone of his caliber."

At that, the mostly-paralyzed Zaryus chuckles to himself. It devolves into a restrained giggle, and then into unhinged, maniacal laughter. "So these are your lackies, Cassandra? Once more, you prove too cowardly to face me one on one."

"Wait," Sylas says. "You know her?"

Zaryus continues laughing. "I understand now. She's kept you in the dark, hasn't she? Such ignorant, usable fools."

Cassandra maintains a neutral expression that gives nothing away. From up close, however, Sylas detects a slight, disdainful crease in her brow.

"What are you talking about?" Theo asks urgently.

"Cassandra was one of us," sneers Zaryus. "She was a proud bearer of the Red Cloak, led our profane congregations in sin and iniquity, slaughtered hundreds in the name of our Lord—Just. Like. Me."

All eyes are on Cassandra, who remains unmoving and unflinching.

"Then she ran off to worship some bastardized version of the Red God like the filthy heretic she is," says Zaryus as he spits at her feet. "The scars on my face are from my attempts to put an end to her madness."

At that, Cassandra finally breaks into laughter. "She Who Weeps Crimson is already far greater than The Scarlet King has ever been. The war's over, Zaryus—the Crimson Weavers have won. History simply… hasn't caught up yet. Isn't that right, V?"

Theo looks to V, who immediately spouts off rhetoric as though she had rehearsed it. "You're correct. The Scarlet Fool destroys, but the Great Weaver reshapes. The Slumbering Idiot defiles his subjects and enemies alike, while the Mistress of Chains wishes to see us all ascend to greater heights. The Red Pretender is cold, cruel apathy, but the Red Dancer loves all who earn Her warm, radiant favor. The masses will learn of Her supremacy soon enough."

Theo clutches his head. "I knew it—you're in a fucking cult. Kool-Aid and everything, huh? Gods, V, I should have never let you leave, I… what happened to you? Are you okay?!"

V finally breaks from Theo's gaze and looks to the ground with downcast eyes. She opens her mouth to reply, but when Cassandra answers for her, she swallows it all and returns to the cold comfort of her indoctrination. "She's never been better, darling. So much blood spilled in Her name… I truly couldn't ask for a better apprentice."

"What have you done to her?!"

The ceaseless arguing that disgraces Sylas' still-ringing ears fades into the background of their mind. Their senses are bombarded by the smell of blood that permeates the room, their clothes, their skin, their soul. In the face of the overwhelming metallic odor of death and destruction, how could anything else matter?

An enraged Quinn limps forward and summons a wood-carved staff into their hand. "If you think for one second that you can come in here and backstab my Conclave—"

"'Backstab'? Me?" says Cassandra, who does little to hide her insincerity. "Of course not. I'm here to help, Quinn. It's what I do."

Blood from the holes in Sylas' shoulder, in Quinn's stomach, in Zaryus' eye and shoulder, in the stags' hands and feet. The sweet crimson that leaks from the minced carcasses of the red robes, and the expelled lifeblood of at least one stag who succumbed to their injuries. Their murderous, red-stained hands, their harmonious hunting knife turned insatiable executioner's blade, their carnivorous mouth still filled with the taste of iron and large chunks of scarlet flesh. The rage, the fear, the hatred. The smell of blood swirls through the room, filling Sylas' vision with burning red hatred, howling into their mind the terrible bloodshed they know in their heart to be the only path forward.

"You're full of shit, Cassandra," yells Theo.

"Think what you'd like, but this has never been about me, has it? No, the only person in this room that truly matters is right here in front of me."

The blood-drunk Sylas looks up at Cassandra, who stares back down at them with a warm, gleeful smile.

"It's time, dear Sylas."

Sylas drops their knife and eagerly pounces on Zaryus as though they were a child tearing apart a Christmas present. They use their nails to cut his flesh to ribbons, starting with the forearm he futilely blocks with and working all the way up to his terror-stricken face. There, Sylas takes their sweet time adding their own artistic vision atop the canvas of scars that Cassandra has prepared for them—first ripping his lower lip down to the tip of his jaw, then tearing large holes in the beautiful web of muscles that constitute the left side of his cheek, and after that enjoying the terrible shredding of the cartilage that makes up his nose.

The onlookers freeze in place, their mouths agape at the gruesome picture before them. Theo's hand hovers over his quivering mouth, but before long, he is the first to break from his fearful inaction and rush forward to intervene. A perplexed, beyond-terrified Quinn soon follows. Even V joins in, her delighted smile quickly fading into a grimace of disgust and concern.

"Sylas, stop—"

In an instant, Theo's left arm contorts at strange, unnatural angles against his will. His legs follow soon after, bringing him to his knees, and then to the cold, blood-soaked floor. Theo watches in horror as Cassandra commands the internal blood of every other onlooker in the room—Quinn, the stags, even V herself are sent tumbling to the ground in response to her hand gestures. Only Sylas remains free—free to maul, to rip, to tear, to kill the source of all their troubles and woes.

Sylas jams his thumb into Zaryus' left eye, plunging him into darkness forevermore. They enjoy the terrible squish yielded from their bodily dismantling, their fine-tuned control over an enemy they once held such fearful reverence towards, the bloodcurling scream of fear and grief it extracts from his helpless body. Never again would Zaryus gaze upon the vile destruction he brings forth in the name of his supposed 'god'. Never again would Zaryus take and defile that which Sylas holds so near and dear to their heart. Never again would Zaryus know peace, know safety, know joy, know power. The only certainty afforded to him is that Sylas, and Sylas alone, would be his undoing.

"Sylas," strains Theo, "don't let her do this. Don't let her make you—"

Sylas reaches both hands into the hole in Zaryus' shoulder and pulls it apart with all their might. With every tendon and muscle and ligament they snap, a memory flashes through their horrid mind. Their initiation as a young, timid fawn, barely cognizant of the occult and their identity, who had finally worked up the courage to run away from home and join a community who actually cares about them. The first time they shot a bow—three bullseyes in a row!—and the bright red blush it yielded from the onlooking Quinn. Their first kiss with Theo underneath the dangling mistletoe that spun their world off its axes. The momentous occasion of their top surgery, and the excitement of their induction to the Horned Wardens barely two months afterwards. How could Sylas spit in the face of these memories with their cruelty?

Quinn fights the urge to cry. "Sylas, no… this isn't you, this—"

"This is who you have always been—your rage, your hatred, your victory. Don't let them take this from you."

Sylas' bloodlust returns with a vengeance. With much exertion, Zaryus' arm finally comes off with a loud crunch of bone. Zaryus screams, but Sylas screams louder, bringing the severed arm down upon his face over and over and over and over and over and over and over again as tears stream down their face in full force, every collision conjuring a different emotion into the forefront of their mind. The fear of their violent compulsions, of manifesting them into reality at the mere thought of opening up to the others about them, of being exiled from the Order for their incurable severity. Their bitter self-loathing, of how far they've strayed from the life they once had, of their inability to do anything to save the ones they love from vile monsters like Zaryus, of being alone with nothing but the smell of blood and smoke and blood and smoke and—

"You'll never be safe while his heart still beats. He is a kidnapper, a murderer, an irredeemable cultist of a mad god the world would be better off forgetting. Slaughtering him is the only way forward."

Sylas drops Zaryus' arm and looks to their Conclave, their friends, their family. Without Sylas, it all falls apart—their peaceful ways simply can't save them. They need Sylas' protection, Sylas' destructiveness, Sylas' mur—

"Wait," Sylas says, looking frantically to Cassandra, then to their people, then back to Cassandra, "what are you doing to them?!"

"This choice is yours and yours alone, Sylas. I won't let them take it away from you."

"I…"

What kind of family would try to stop Sylas here, at the crescendo of their work, their duty? Prevent them from seizing the one opportunity they have to enact the justice they lack the means, will, and stomach to carry out themselves? To deny Sylas this terrible, glorious, stomach-churning, beautiful part of themselves in the name of 'peace' and 'tranquility'?

Sylas releases Zaryus and crawls over to grab their blood-soaked knife. With another flick of her wrist, Cassandra forces Zaryus onto his knees, his head held low, his arm pinned behind his back, his mauled face dripping copious amounts of blood onto the cold stone floor. The perfect position for judgement, for punishment, for execution.

"So tell me, little fawn: will you do what needs to be done?"

Sylas raises their knife to Zaryus' throat, but when they gaze upon the face of their blood-soaked knife, they flinch backwards—for the briefest moment, they do not recognize their own reflection within it. Hyperventilation soon follows, with the nerves in their hand crying out in fear one last time before the pins and needles drown them in total numbness.

Sylas then looks to their people, their horrified, sickened people, who have been made to watch the spectacle in its entirety by Cassandra's blood magic. Their disgust threatens to drown Sylas in resentful rage all over again, but in Quinn and Theo's anguished faces, they find something curious: guilt. Guilt over not anticipating this breakdown ahead of time, over not being there for them when they needed it most, for not cradling this desperate, wounded side of them and telling them that yes, everything will be okay, love.

When Sylas blinks, they are returned to the majestic visage of the Sidereal Stag. When It nodded at them, It harbored no disapproval or disgust for them—only acceptance in its purest, most divine form. And all at once, they finally understand.

"…I won't do it."

"Oh?"

Drained of all energy and spirit, Sylas turns back to Cassandra and allows their knife to clatter to the floor.

"I'm sorry, but this is as far as I go."

The others exhale in relief, but their hearts drop into their stomachs merely two seconds later when Cassandra raises her revolver.

"Consider your options carefully, child."

"Kill me if you must, but I won't bloody my hands anymore. It ends here, Cassandra."

Through their tears, Sylas stares Cassandra down. Her narrowed crimson eyes are filled with barely-restrained anger and genuine disappointment, and her bony finger hovers over the trigger, ready to blow a hole in their head at the slightest twitch. Her gaze remains utterly affixed to Sylas. No one else in the room even registers in her mind—the others strain against Cassandra's magic to no avail, and Zaryus is balanced on the thin edge of consciousness, with only the gurgling of blood escaping the confines of his ruined mouth.

Cassandra inhales slowly. Behind her other emotions, Sylas senses something else filling her mind. They narrow their eyes, gazing deeper into her soul in search of answers, and at long last they find… admiration.

Click.

No bullet exits the chamber. Cassandra chuckles knowingly, holstering her unloaded revolver with a quick, effortless twirl.

"Well done, Sylas. You win."

With a flick of her wrist, the onlookers are freed from their magical binding. Theo and Quinn stand up unsteadily, rushing over to grab onto the tearful Sylas and dote over them as best they can. The other stags interpose themselves between her and the reunited throuple, ready to fight in defense of their Warden in spite of their injuries.

Sylas looks down at their shaking, bloodied hands. "I'm sorry, I… I shouldn't have—"

Quinn shushes them with a smile. "It's okay, love, we're here. We've got you."

Sylas nuzzles into Quinn, basking deeply in the comforting presence of their lost love. They then look to Theo, who stares back at them with a smile of pride and joy that makes their very soul ache to the core.

At this display of affection, Cassandra sighs deeply. "You really are a wonderful stag, Sylas. You'll make an excellent ally in the battles to come."

"Like hell I will."

"I doubt you'll have much say in the matter," she muses. "These are desperate times, after all. I'm sure our paths will cross again soon enough."

Sylas furrows their brow; Cassandra simply smiles. With another quick hand motion, the battered Zaryus rises into the air, levitating past the stags and towards her.

"Come along now, V. I have what we came here for—now the real work begins."

V stands up unsteadily and attempts to regain her balance following Cassandra's blood binding. She slowly walks over to her master, but is stopped by Theo, who grabs her wrist with a firm hand.

"V, you… don't go with her," he pleas. "Stay with us. Please."

V looks back tearfully; her face is stricken with grief and fear in equal measure.

"I'm sorry, Theo," she says solemnly before hardening her heart, "but this is the only path forward. I… don't look for me. It won't end well."

Theo's grip loosens, and V continues walking. She joins Cassandra, who strolls towards the exit with the incapacitated Zaryus in tow.

"…What next, boss?"

As she reaches the exit, Cassandra retrieves the relic from her cloak and brandishes it proudly. It appears to be a collection of papers, each handwritten in blood red ink, that had seemingly been torn out of a book.

"We're off to make history."

Cassandra and V slink into the shadows, leaving only the reunited Conclave of Reeds in the bloodied barrens of the ritual chamber.

Back at the Conclave of Reeds, a lengthy funeral of poetic words, songs, and keening is held for the fallen stags. Each of the seven deceased—five slain during the initial attack, plus two more who succumbed to blood loss from the ritual—are fully cleaned up, dressed in their favorite clothes, adorned with white gladiolus flowers, and gently lowered into the creek. Quinn takes it upon themselves to tend to Hershel's body, planting a mournful kiss upon his forehead before letting their beloved sidereal flow towards the starry horizon alongside the rest of his kin. The Conclave watches solemnly as the stars themselves claim the gentle dead, transforming them into scatterings of celestial motes that each disperse in brilliant flashes of white starlight.

The rebuilding process in the days that follow is certainly not without its challenges, but before long, the Conclave of Reeds is repaired to a reasonably functional state. Even in the absence of their dearly departed friends, life goes on—the best the stags can do, they reason, is live a good life in their stead.

…

After a quick knock, Theo enters Quinn's quarters, smiling warmly at the sight of Sylas lying on the bed and resting their head on Quinn's lap.

"How's the sidereal life treating you today, love?" he asks gently.

"Pretty good, I think," says Quinn. "Haven't gotten too much sleep, but beyond that, I scarcely have any complaints. It's everything I had hoped for and more."

"I'm glad," Theo grins. When he sits down next to the two of them, Quinn wastes no time diving in for a kiss on the cheek. He then teases: "Enjoying the view, I see."

"Indeed I am. This one just woke up a few minutes ago."

"I'm very awake," mumbles the sleepy Sylas, who struggles to keep their eyes open.

"I'm sure you are," giggles Theo. "Still adjusting to being on break?"

"Yup. I can hardly believe I volunteered for this. A whole year of not being a Horned Warden…"

Sylas clenches their fist involuntarily; Quinn helps them relax by offering their hand to hold onto, and then reassures: "The others are hard at work making sure we're well protected even without you on duty, so don't you worry a thing. Just focus on yourself, alright?"

"I suppose so," they say begrudgingly. The thought of the Conclave being defenseless without them, the fear that any day now something terrible could happen to their people again, brings back the horrid smell of blood all over again. But when Theo's hand reaches their hair, they can't help but nuzzle into the comforting safety it provides.

"You'll be back in shape in no time," says Theo, "especially once you get some counseling. After all that, you'll be ready for your Mirror Hunt."

"I hope so," sighs Sylas. "I hate to imagine what sort of inner demons it'll make me fight as external ones."

"You have a whole year at minimum to prepare," reassures Quinn. "Nobody's doing the ritual until we know you can handle it. And once you do… well, you'll be free of everything that's been holding you back!"

"I can't pretend I haven't been looking forward to that," Sylas sighs, "but I'll need to find some hobbies to hold me over. The boredom is killing me."

"I have a few ideas," teases Theo. "But first thing's first—Quinn, did you read my latest text?"

"I did—everything's been passed along to the other sidereals. If their scouts find anything hinting to her location, we'll be the first to know."

The ever-curious Sylas looks to the other two in confusion. "What's all this about?"

"It's simple," Quinn declares, confident as ever. "We're going to bring V home."

    The smell of the rain
    Author: Onigura
    ⚠️ Content warning: Mentions of suicide, minor gore

    Told in reverse chronological order, this story is my attempt at trying out several writing styles while maintaining the eerie familiarity of something that's very important to me. It's also my first tale, so I hope you like it.

⚠️ content warning

Joel

Joel awakens abruptly to an alarm, covered in semi-dried sweat. His quarters are too hot at night, but so cold in the morning.

His time at the Foundation hasn't been particularly harrowing or intensive on him, but sometimes he feels they wake him up far too early. What could they possibly need a run-of-the-mill agent for at 4:30 in the morning, after all?

Whatever. It's fine. At least they pay somewhat well. On top of that, his vacation is coming up soon: he's going to see his little sister again tomorrow.

Joel lays in bed a little longer as the alarm blares in his ears. His eyes can barely stay open, as if they're glued shut. Just a bit longer, c'mon…

…

Alright, this alarm's getting annoying. Time to get out of bed.

Joel lethargically walks to the bathroom located in his quarters. He must have kicked his shirt off in his sleep. His right arm was exposed for the majority of the time he was out, so it's freezing while the rest of his body is at a regular temperature.

Joel peels his eyes open to find the light switch, only to shut them again rapidly. It's far too bright. A groan escapes as he feels around, looking for his toothbrush.

Joel brushes his teeth while trying to open his eyes. He turns the water on, rinses, and washes his face, which brings him a newfound energy. It wakes him up, so to speak.

Joel, having freshened up, slips out of his pajamas and into his uniform. He turns on the lights in his quarters, stopping the alarm. He rubs some deodorant on, sprays a single spritz of company-issued cologne on his chest, and pops in a stick of gum. He can't stand not being fresh.

He works at his hair for a bit, combing out the bedhead before he grabs his keycard and slings his rifle over his shoulder. He's an exceptionally skilled marksman, but there's nothing special about that when you deal with otherworldly threats like he's expected to.

He holsters his handgun and taser, and leaves his quarters. He's been assigned to the same anomaly for almost two weeks now. Some dude who won't wake up. Can they let this go already?

Joel makes his way to the lounge, where he can make himself a brilliant cup of coffee for him and his buddy. The coffee they serve here is the best he's ever had. He prepares a triple-shot espresso for his friend and a mocha latte (hot chocolate and black coffee, with creamer and Splenda) for himself.

He grabs a bagel on the way out and stuffs it into his pocket as he shambles to Orison's office.

…

As Joel approaches the door, he notices but fails to acknowledge a sign hanging on the doorknob that reads "TRANSCRIPTION IN PROGRESS - DO NOT DISTURB," a mundane error he's proven prone to.

…

Agent Rabanaque pushes the door open with his foot.

"Mike! Got you a little something. Your favorite."

"Joel, don't you know how to read the sign on the door?"

Joel collapses, dropping the coffees he was carrying. Orison grumbles about having to clean it up.

"Oh, great. He's in for it tomorrow."

…

…

…

The sound of leaves rustling fills the air. It smells like hot dogs and burgers on the grill. It's a balmy summer night with a soft, warm breeze blowing through. Intermittent chatter can be heard in the background as Joel makes another lap around his community pool. He can see stars in the sky, accompanying a beautiful nebula. He has to share this with someone.

"Lisa! Can you see that?" Joel exclaims, pointing to the sky.

Lisa opens her mouth to respond, but doesn't say anything. She appears awestruck by the beauty of the night sky.

An explosion is heard in the distance. Joel and his sister turn their heads, as well as several others in the pool.

It's followed by a second, then a third. The night sky fills with newfound light in a stunning blaze. Younger children with sparklers scurry around the pool in excitement.

It's the fourth of July again.

A few adults can be heard cheering. It's boisterous, but instills joy in the others. A few children join in, including Joel and his sister.

They've never been more excited than now.

Now.

This is now, right?

Of course it is. What else would it be?

Why does Joel feel so uneasy?

Joel submerges himself underwater, holding his nose. He sticks his hand above water in an attempt to get his sister to notice and join him. He wants to know what the fireworks look like from under the surface.

There's a man at the bottom of the pool.

Of course there is. He's always been there. Nothing to worry about. This is just how he remembers it.

His clothes aren't wet. His hair isn't wet. He seems completely dry.

He's wearing a brown trench coat, with his hands in his pockets.

His face is pretty round. His eyes, large. His eyebrows are exceptionally bushy.

He has a very prominent lower lip.

He looks terribly uncanny to Joel.

He incites a gross feeling of unease in Joel. He couldn't possibly have been there.

Joel notices that he can breathe underwater. That definitely didn't happen before.

Who is this man?

"Hello?"

…

No response from the man. Can he hear him under the water?

What water?

Joel isn't in the pool anymore. Was he always out?

This doesn't make any sense. Joel was never in the pool.

Joel stands in his backyard. Birds are heard chirping outside as the scent of clean soil fills the air. It's humid and brisk.

Lisa is on the trampoline in the backyard, waving at Joel.

"It's all wet! It's super bouncy right now!"

"Woah! That's so cool!"

Joel rushes over to the trampoline in excitement, his sandals flipping and flopping loudly as he stomps on the wet grass. He slips, but regains his balance as he slides over a patch of mud.

He scrambles onto the trampoline, kicking off his sandals as he jumps as high as he can. Lisa was right: the trampoline is exceptionally bouncy right now. The water must be making the net heavier, giving an extraordinarily wobbly and rubbery feeling.

Joel and Lisa laugh as they play on the trampoline. They spin and do flips and bounce significantly higher than usual.

As Joel spins, he notices a man watching from the porch. It's the same man that was under the pool. The same man that was always there.

He goes into the air once more as a rebound from his last jump.

He does not hit the trampoline again.

…

Joel is sitting in an old-timey diner with Lisa and their babysitter.

What is happening to him?

He thinks to himself as he takes a bite out of his apple pie. He definitely remembers the trampoline, at least a little bit. It feels like it was years ago. Was it years ago?

A bouncy tune is playing on the old-fashioned jukebox. Lisa hums along to it, apparently familiar with the song that's playing. Joel attempts to join his sister, but doesn't know the tune to hum to. He resorts to rhythmically drumming on the table with his hands, exciting Lisa. She hums louder, and Joel drums harder. Their babysitter urges them to quiet down.

The babysitter sighs and takes a sip of his coffee. Joel doesn't quite remember this occurring. Did he ever have a babysitter?

How old is he?

Joel isn't supposed to be here. A brief moment of clarity finds him, and he knows that what's happening is not real. This is some sort of dream, some sort of hallucination.

Joel hasn't seen his sister in months. She's still in the hospital.

…

The hospital.

Joel finds himself in the hospital where his sister is located. He remembers his dreams. The pool, the trampoline, the diner.

Is this really all he remembers his sister by? Impossible.

Joel can no longer feel himself breathing. He's suffocating in this hospital. It's painful, not nearly as pleasant as the last three dreams. What's making this happen? He can't breathe in or out. His face rapidly changes color.

Nobody walking by seems to notice. Isn't this a hospital? Can't anyone help him?

Joel feels like collapsing. He tries to, but his body won't let him. He continues walking down the corridor as it seems to expand infinitely beyond his vision. It's so long, but he knows what awaits him in his sister's room. He knows what he did.

Joel can only keep walking down this endless hallway. He can't breathe. His body won't respond to anything his brain tells it to do. He's locked here with naught but his mind.

That man watches from several of the windows that Joel walks past. His face is sickening.

Joel keeps walking by, and that man keeps staring. He won't show himself from beyond those windows. He's a coward. Joel is filled with rage, but can't help but continue walking to his bedridden sister.

Joel needs to awaken.

He focuses as hard as he can, attempting to close his eyes. He knows how to forcefully awaken himself from a nightmare. He used to do it all the time as a kid. What's stopping him now? Some creepy man who's too chicken to face him?

Joel shuts his eyes against his own will. His body is forcing against it, but if Joel can keep like this for just a little longer…

He can move his hand. His real hand.

He can move his leg. His real leg.

He can move his eyes…

But that man appears in front of them. His sickeningly dead face. His lifeless eyes glare into Joel's. A chill goes down Joel's spine unlike any before. His body is completely immobilized as a lifetime of fear seeps into his veins. And yet, he continues walking.

He wants to yell. He wants to kick and scream. He wants out of this nightmare.

How is he supposed to make it out of this hospital? Away from these blinding lights, away from this cold air? Away from the unpleasant buzzing and indistinct chatter? Away from the sound of his own footsteps and the smell of rubbing alcohol?

Away from this man?

Orison

Senior Researcher Orison sits in his office when his assistant, an agent named Gloria, walks in while holding a tablet.

Orison looks up from his desk, then continues writing on a document in front of him.

"How are you, Gloria? Got something to report?"

"Yes."

"Do tell, please."

"We're getting word that there's some more sightings of your guy. You know, the one you can't seem to prove exists?"

Orison grumbles to himself.

"You know, we've had dream-based entities before. A series of mass reportings of the same man is good enough evidence to classify him as his own anomaly. We just don't seem to have enough information to write up containment procedures, but this is why we do research on the subject."

Gloria sighs.

"You're right. I just think you're putting too much effort into something that's very likely a bust."

"Gloria, if everything we did was successful, we wouldn't have any problems."

Gloria rolls her eyes.

"Sure. Whatever you say."

"Fill me in on the details."

"Alright. It was just a few days ago, and we're getting this description from a lot of different people. A lot of people from a town in Pennsylvania began calling the number on your flyers, claiming they saw your guy in their sleep."

"Well, send a small task force to whatever town it is for basic investigation. It'll probably show up blank again."

"Do you have any recommendations?"

"None. We don't need that many people; just get a group of maybe three or four field agents together."

"Roger."

Gloria begins tapping on her tablet. Orison looks back down and continues writing.

A few minutes of silence pass.

"Gloria, why are you still here? Is there something else you came here to tell me?"

"How did you discover this… dream guy in the first place? Did you dream of him?"

"I've only ever seen him once. It was at the same time a few hundred other people saw him in the site and surrounding area. My personal theory is that he's got a radius surrounding him that makes people see him in their sleep. He's exceptionally elusive, on top of that."

"So, what, you're saying he was near this site?"

"I'm not saying anything for sure. It's an analyzation based off patterns that we see involving him. He could be some kind of sorcerer… or just a superpowered creep. We've found zero logs, IDs, fingerprints, DNA, anything involving him. At least, not yet. Facial recognition is still inconclusive, so we have to go through people individually for a solid answer."

"Well… who's to say that he isn't real in the first place?"

"He is real, Gloria. This kind of thing doesn't just happen! I've dealt with far worse in my time and far less believable."

"Geez, okay. What was your dream like?"

"I don't remember many dreams, you know."

"Oh… Then-"

"But this one remains particularly vivid in my memory. It wasn't as much of a dream as it was a… Sleep paralysis may be the word.

"I wasn't in my quarters, but rather, my childhood home. I was in a child's body, can you believe it? Hah. It felt like my body when I was far younger. The pain in my lower spine had gone, and it was quite pleasant. That is, until I heard a burning ringing in my ears. Oh, it was deafening. It felt as if my ears were being plugged with nails.

"I couldn't move my hands to cover my ears, but I doubt that that'd have helped anyways. I could sense my state of helplessness in this room, and I pondered why I was there. My entire body was numb, and I could see him in the corner. That… man.

"He was horrifying to look at. I couldn't tell you why. He looked human, but my instincts were yelling at me to escape. His eyes were dead and blank. His face, absolutely lifeless. I can assure you that I have never felt more fear than in that single moment, and I can't even put a name to it. All I could comprehend was that this man, this man that was in front of me was not human. I know how insane that sounds. I've seen horrors beyond our comprehension; demons that appear to be ripped straight from the deepest layers of the earth. But this man was something else.

"He didn't seem hostile. He seemed the opposite: calm and collected. Perhaps it was something about that that terrified me so. His specious humanity shook me to my core, and I couldn't do anything about it.

"Perhaps he smelled my fear, or sensed it. He began walking towards me in my dream, and an even stronger wave of horror washed over me once more: the strongest yet. His movement was so unnatural. It should never have happened! He was mortifying enough in the corner of my room, but seeing him move even the slightest bit confirmed to me that it was alive, and it petrified me. I felt myself forcing myself awake, and that is when this happened."

Orison violently points to his eyes. The left is missing, and both have a heavy manner of scarring surrounding them.

"I awoke, and ripped and clawed. I never wanted to see that again for as long as I lived, but the damage was done. The last thing I would ever see from that eye would be that man. It was then that I stopped and realized the horror of my actions. I was safe where I was, in my quarters."

Orison shivers.

"So I sketched him. It wasn't difficult, as his face was engraved into my mind. It was all I could think about. I needed to know that other people went through what I went through. I just needed the knowledge that I wasn't alone in my agony. I began placing flyers on the site bulletin boards, and thankfully, a few others had seen him in their sleep as well."

Gloria taps her chin.

"Why were you the only one to rip out your eyes? If this guy was as scary as you say he was, why didn't anyone else think that way?"

"I don't know, Gloria. When I drew him out on my paper, I realized that he wasn't nearly as scary as I thought he was. I imagine he must have done something to me during my sleep to incite such terror. His face is merely unsettling to me now. When I woke up, I wasn't myself. A cry escaped my body in terror, but it made no sound. This isn't something I would do to something that just looks odd to me now. He was in control there, not me.

"And now, whenever I lay down to sleep, all I can remember is my terror in that moment. I begin sweating, and a fraction of a fraction of that horror returns to my body. It's enough to keep me awake. I've since developed an uncanny aversion to sleeping."

"Ah… Sorry about that."

"Have you any more inquiries, or may I resume my work?"

"Uh, no. Sorry. Thanks for your time, Michael."

"Mmm. You're welcome."

Orison takes a sip of his triple-shot espresso as Gloria exits.

Brook

I

There are no winners in war. That's a fact. I'm so sick of this shit.

I miss my sister. I want to see her again. That's never going to happen. I'm so tired. What am I even fighting for?

I'm just a statistic here. Some name that gets crossed off at the end of the day. Whatever.

Shucks to this bullshit.
…

I can't handle this anymore. There's mothers out there, sobbing that their son never came back from war because of me. Because of my own doing. Because of my own fear.

All of these troops are just people. Scared and hopeful for this to end. The man on my right was struggling with a divorce for three years. The one on my left had just found the love of his life right before he was deployed.

Both of them have bullets in their heads. Well, had.

I thought I was going to die here.

I just want out of these damn trenches. I just want to see my sister again. She was all I had in this life. My first and only best friend.

I wish she wrote me. I miss her laugh. I miss her smile. I miss who I grew up with.

But I just had to go ahead and send her that first letter. I knew what she was struggling with. I knew why she was always drinking or smoking. But I just had to be rude. I just had to be too much of a pussy to talk to her in person, and not wait until I get fucking drafted to confront her. I could have avoided this.

This could have been entirely avoided by me.

I ruined it. I really hope it wasn't my fault. I didn't mean to send her over the edge.

Or maybe I did. Am I that horrible?

Bullets are flying by me. I half-hope that one of them connects. Is it possible to see her?

I'm done. I hate this.

I'm leaving.

II

I could never just walk out. They wouldn't let me, obviously. My life is clearly valuable, right? They must "need me out there on the front lines."

Well, they can't do anything to stop me. What are they gonna do, tie my gun to my hands? I will never take another life for as long as I live. They can torture me if they want, or fine me thousands for objecting. Nobody can make me hold another weapon.

So, I hotwired one of our ATVs and left. They aren't really hard to find around here, and they're all designed for endurance, so who's to stop me from just… leaving? It's really as stupid as it sounds. I could have just done this the whole time.

Driving out at the highest speed possible, my fear of cars escapes me. I used to be mortified of being in vehicles of any sort, but that's just a grain of sand compared to my fear of taking someone else from seeing their family again. I've stopped dozens of brothers and sisters from coming home. I don't deserve to live.

My old house shouldn't be too far from here. Since the entire area has been effectively sacked by war, it's mostly abandoned, meaning I can revisit easily. I'm actually excited for this. The place where I grew up? This beautiful home that holds so many memories for me?

I'm happy in this moment, for the first time in the longest time.

Geez, I'm horrible. I miss my sister.

I want to see her again.

III

It's raining outside.

I love the smell of the rain. It reminds me of the power outage so many years ago. I was only in elementary school when it happened, still living in that beautiful house.

It was such an ethereal time. Life without any electricity or stimulation. Using flashlights for a week.

I can catch glimpses of that time whenever it rains now. Smelling the rain is just another reminder of it. I can see why dad loved it so much.

Fuck, I miss it. I miss her.

I can feel the cool beads of rain hitting my face as I drive by. It's relaxing. My former neighborhood is just up ahead. I'm so excited. I can feel a smile creeping onto my face, which disgusts me. I shouldn't be allowed this kind of euphoria. I'm the reason I can't see my sister again.

…

I want to go back to that time. Despite all my fear in the moment, I can still remember the smell of the rain.

IV

There's the snack store! Man, I almost forgot about it. Went there every Saturday. Maybe they still have some food in the back…?

Nah. That'd be ridiculous. It's probably rotting.

There's the park where I learned to ride a bike with Ana. We would go there all the time with our bikes, roller skates, and skateboards. I forget how to do all of those things. Except for biking.

There's the bridge we'd always run up and down. We always asked to go swimming in the creek below, but dad never let us because "the water is dirty." That bridge was just the coolest thing to younger me; just being suspended above a body of water, but not being entirely on it was the most incredible feeling.

…

There's the school. My father's school.

Nice to see that he got to live out his dream. Finally. I'm happy for him. I'll visit him after this.

…

I know what's next. I'm almost excited.

My old house, still standing strong after all this time. It's been vacant since we moved out, and was set up for demolition before the war. I haven't been here since I was 17, revisiting for fun. Ana was there with me. But now she isn't.

And it's my fault.

V

Someone's in my house.

I thought it was vacant.

"Hey! Who are you?"

The stranger raises his hands calmly, and turns to look at Brook.

Fuck! This guy's scary as shit. What the hell?

"Hello."

Oh my goodness, what an unpleasant voice. He sounds like how biting into a towel feels.

He looks so familiar.

"Have we met?"

"Once."

Why is he talking so cryptically?

"When? Where?"

"Soon, here."

"That doesn't make any sense. Speak like a regular person."

The stranger lowers his arms to his sides, and puts them in the pockets of his trench coat.

"I see."

Huh?

"You see what? What are you seeing? Talk regularly, damn."

"Ana."

…

What…?

How does he…?

"How do you-"

The stranger points to a collection of papers held in Brook's left arm.

Huh?

Those weren't there before. What are these?

My letters. I thought I delivered these. How are they here?

"How did you do that? Are you messing with me?"

The stranger shakes his head.

"Don't you miss her?"

"How do you know about that? Don't fuck with me, guy. I swear I'll-"

The stranger holds up a hand.

"Don't you want a second chance?"

…

"…Yes."

The stranger points to the papers in Brook's hand once again.

"Read them again."

…

"What's going to happen?"

The stranger says nothing, and continues pointing.

…

I mean…

It's worth a shot, isn't it?

This feels anticlimactic.

If there's any way I can do it, and this creepy guy knows how to…

Whether or not I live or die, I'm definitely still going to read them. If something happens, it happens.

Will I really be able to see her again?








VI

It's one o'clock in the afternoon. It's grossly overcast with thick, dark clouds outside. The air is thick with humidity, and it's extraordinarily hot despite the lack of sunlight. Brook looks around, unable find the stranger. His house is in a far greater condition than just a few minutes ago.

He looks in his hand to find that he is holding a cheap flashlight. His letters are gone. He clicks it on.

"Am I asleep? Is this real?"

He gets no response. His father must be out.

"Ana? Are you here?"

He quickly speedwalks to the living room. Is it true?

His living room is empty. Maybe the basement? She would retreat down there when she was scared.

He hurries down the wooden stairs to his unfinished basement, illuminating it with his flashlight.

"Ana?"

He gets no response. It's stuffy and hot in here, so it's unlikely that she'd be hiding in the basement right now. He runs back upstairs and checks the yard to see if she's outside or in the parking lot.

He pushes open the backdoor, only to find disappointment. His sister isn't outside. It smells like rain.

He walks back inside, checking throughout the house. It only then dawns on him that he hadn't yet checked her room. Is this really true? Or just a fading memory?

He climbs up the stairs on all fours, and runs to her room. He might be building up a sweat, but it's too humid inside the house to tell. The door to her room is shut.

He walks over to the door, and knocks. This must be some sort of trick, some sort of-

"What?"

Brook shoves the door open.

On the bed sits his sister, reading a book under her flashlight. She waves to Brook as he walks in.

[[include :scp-wiki:info:end]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:info-cw]] @@ @@ = **__Joel__** Joel awakens abruptly to an alarm, covered in semi-dried sweat. His quarters are too hot at night, but so cold in the morning. His time at the Foundation hasn't been particularly harrowing or intensive on him, but sometimes he feels they wake him up far too early. What could they possibly need a run-of-the-mill agent for at 4:30 in the morning, after all? Whatever. It's fine. At least they pay somewhat well. On top of that, his vacation is coming up soon: he's going to see his little sister again tomorrow. Joel lays in bed a little longer as the alarm blares in his ears. His eyes can barely stay open, as if they're glued shut. Just a bit longer, c'mon... ... Alright, this alarm's getting annoying. Time to get out of bed. Joel lethargically walks to the bathroom located in his quarters. He must have kicked his shirt off in his sleep. His right arm was exposed for the majority of the time he was out, so it's freezing while the rest of his body is at a regular temperature. Joel peels his eyes open to find the light switch, only to shut them again rapidly. It's far too bright. A groan escapes as he feels around, looking for his toothbrush. Joel brushes his teeth while trying to open his eyes. He turns the water on, rinses, and washes his face, which brings him a newfound energy. It wakes him up, so to speak. Joel, having freshened up, slips out of his pajamas and into his uniform. He turns on the lights in his quarters, stopping the alarm. He rubs some deodorant on, sprays a single spritz of company-issued cologne on his chest, and pops in a stick of gum. He can't stand not being fresh. He works at his hair for a bit, combing out the bedhead before he grabs his keycard and slings his rifle over his shoulder. He's an exceptionally skilled marksman, but there's nothing special about that when you deal with otherworldly threats like he's expected to. He holsters his handgun and taser, and leaves his quarters. He's been assigned to the same anomaly for almost two weeks now. Some dude who won't wake up. Can they let this go already? Joel makes his way to the lounge, where he can make himself a brilliant cup of coffee for him and his buddy. The coffee they serve here is the best he's ever had. He prepares a triple-shot espresso for his friend and a mocha latte (hot chocolate and black coffee, with creamer and Splenda) for himself. He grabs a bagel on the way out and stuffs it into his pocket as he shambles to Orison's office. ... As Joel approaches the door, he notices but fails to acknowledge a sign hanging on the doorknob that reads "TRANSCRIPTION IN PROGRESS - DO NOT DISTURB," a mundane error he's proven prone to. ... Agent Rabanaque pushes the door open with his foot. "Mike! Got you a little something. Your favorite." "Joel, don't you know how to read the sign on the door?" Joel collapses, dropping the coffees he was carrying. Orison grumbles about having to clean it up. "Oh, great. He's in for it tomorrow." ... ... ... The sound of leaves rustling fills the air. It smells like hot dogs and burgers on the grill. It's a balmy summer night with a soft, warm breeze blowing through. Intermittent chatter can be heard in the background as Joel makes another lap around his community pool. He can see stars in the sky, accompanying a beautiful nebula. He has to share this with someone. "Lisa! Can you see that?" Joel exclaims, pointing to the sky. Lisa opens her mouth to respond, but doesn't say anything. She appears awestruck by the beauty of the night sky. An explosion is heard in the distance. Joel and his sister turn their heads, as well as several others in the pool. It's followed by a second, then a third. The night sky fills with newfound light in a stunning blaze. Younger children with sparklers scurry around the pool in excitement. It's the fourth of July again. A few adults can be heard cheering. It's boisterous, but instills joy in the others. A few children join in, including Joel and his sister. They've never been more excited than now. Now. This is now, right? Of course it is. What else would it be? Why does Joel feel so uneasy? Joel submerges himself underwater, holding his nose. He sticks his hand above water in an attempt to get his sister to notice and join him. He wants to know what the fireworks look like from under the surface. There's a man at the bottom of the pool. Of course there is. He's always been there. Nothing to worry about. This is just how he remembers it. His clothes aren't wet. His hair isn't wet. He seems completely dry. He's wearing a brown trench coat, with his hands in his pockets. His face is pretty round. His eyes, large. His eyebrows are exceptionally bushy. He has a very prominent lower lip. He looks terribly uncanny to Joel. He incites a gross feeling of unease in Joel. He couldn't possibly have been there. Joel notices that he can breathe underwater. That definitely didn't happen before. Who is this man? "Hello?" ... No response from the man. Can he hear him under the water? What water? Joel isn't in the pool anymore. Was he always out? This doesn't make any sense. Joel was never in the pool. Joel stands in his backyard. Birds are heard chirping outside as the scent of clean soil fills the air. It's humid and brisk. Lisa is on the trampoline in the backyard, waving at Joel. "It's all wet! It's super bouncy right now!" "Woah! That's so cool!" Joel rushes over to the trampoline in excitement, his sandals flipping and flopping loudly as he stomps on the wet grass. He slips, but regains his balance as he slides over a patch of mud. He scrambles onto the trampoline, kicking off his sandals as he jumps as high as he can. Lisa was right: the trampoline is exceptionally bouncy right now. The water must be making the net heavier, giving an extraordinarily wobbly and rubbery feeling. Joel and Lisa laugh as they play on the trampoline. They spin and do flips and bounce significantly higher than usual. As Joel spins, he notices a man watching from the porch. It's the same man that was under the pool. The same man that was always there. He goes into the air once more as a rebound from his last jump. He does not hit the trampoline again. ... Joel is sitting in an old-timey diner with Lisa and their babysitter. What is happening to him? He thinks to himself as he takes a bite out of his apple pie. He definitely remembers the trampoline, at least a little bit. It feels like it was years ago. Was it years ago? A bouncy tune is playing on the old-fashioned jukebox. Lisa hums along to it, apparently familiar with the song that's playing. Joel attempts to join his sister, but doesn't know the tune to hum to. He resorts to rhythmically drumming on the table with his hands, exciting Lisa. She hums louder, and Joel drums harder. Their babysitter urges them to quiet down. The babysitter sighs and takes a sip of his coffee. Joel doesn't quite remember this occurring. Did he ever have a babysitter? How old is he? Joel isn't supposed to be here. A brief moment of clarity finds him, and he knows that what's happening is not real. This is some sort of dream, some sort of hallucination. Joel hasn't seen his sister in months. She's still in the hospital. ... The hospital. Joel finds himself in the hospital where his sister is located. He remembers his dreams. The pool, the trampoline, the diner. Is this really all he remembers his sister by? Impossible. Joel can no longer feel himself breathing. He's suffocating in this hospital. It's painful, not nearly as pleasant as the last three dreams. What's making this happen? He can't breathe in or out. His face rapidly changes color. Nobody walking by seems to notice. Isn't this a hospital? Can't anyone help him? Joel feels like collapsing. He tries to, but his body won't let him. He continues walking down the corridor as it seems to expand infinitely beyond his vision. It's so long, but he knows what awaits him in his sister's room. He knows what he did. Joel can only keep walking down this endless hallway. He can't breathe. His body won't respond to anything his brain tells it to do. He's locked here with naught but his mind. That man watches from several of the windows that Joel walks past. His face is sickening. Joel keeps walking by, and that man keeps staring. He won't show himself from beyond those windows. He's a coward. Joel is filled with rage, but can't help but continue walking to his bedridden sister. Joel needs to awaken. He focuses as hard as he can, attempting to close his eyes. He knows how to forcefully awaken himself from a nightmare. He used to do it all the time as a kid. What's stopping him now? Some creepy man who's too chicken to face him? Joel shuts his eyes against his own will. His body is forcing against it, but if Joel can keep like this for just a little longer... He can move his hand. His real hand. He can move his leg. His real leg. He can move his eyes... But that man appears in front of them. His sickeningly dead face. His lifeless eyes glare into Joel's. A chill goes down Joel's spine unlike any before. His body is completely immobilized as a lifetime of fear seeps into his veins. And yet, he continues walking. He wants to yell. He wants to kick and scream. He wants out of this nightmare. How is he supposed to make it out of this hospital? Away from these blinding lights, away from this cold air? Away from the unpleasant buzzing and indistinct chatter? Away from the sound of his own footsteps and the smell of rubbing alcohol? Ana was there with me. But now she isn't. And it's my fault. = __**V**__ Someone's in my house. I thought it was vacant. "Hey! Who are you?" //The stranger raises his hands calmly, and turns to look at Brook.// Fuck! This guy's scary as shit. What the hell? "Hello." Oh my goodness, what an unpleasant voice. He sounds like how biting into a towel feels. He looks so familiar. "Have we met?" "Once." Why is he talking so cryptically? "When? Where?" "Soon, here." "That doesn't make any sense. Speak like a regular person." //The stranger lowers his arms to his sides, and puts them in the pockets of his trench coat.// "I see." Huh? "You see what? What are you seeing? Talk regularly, damn." "Ana." ... What...? How does he...? "How do you-" //The stranger points to a collection of papers held in Brook's left arm.// Huh? Those weren't there before. What are these? My letters. I thought I delivered these. How are they here? "How did you do that? Are you messing with me?" //The stranger shakes his head.// "Don't you miss her?" "How do you know about that? Don't fuck with me, guy. I swear I'll-" //The stranger holds up a hand.// "Don't you want a second chance?" ... "...Yes." //The stranger points to the papers in Brook's hand once again.// "Read them again." ... "What's going to happen?" //The stranger says nothing, and continues pointing.// ... I mean... It's worth a shot, isn't it? This feels anticlimactic. If there's any way I can do it, and this creepy guy knows how to... Whether or not I live or die, I'm definitely still going to read them. If something happens, it happens. Will I really be able to see her again? @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ = **__VI__** @@ @@ It's one o'clock in the afternoon. It's grossly overcast with thick, dark clouds outside. The air is thick with humidity, and it's extraordinarily hot despite the lack of sunlight. Brook looks around, unable find the stranger. His house is in a far greater condition than just a few minutes ago. He looks in his hand to find that he is holding a cheap flashlight. His letters are gone. He clicks it on. "Am I asleep? Is this real?" He gets no response. His father must be out. "Ana? Are you here?" He quickly speedwalks to the living room. Is it true? His living room is empty. Maybe the basement? She would retreat down there when she was scared. He hurries down the wooden stairs to his unfinished basement, illuminating it with his flashlight. "Ana?" He gets no response. It's stuffy and hot in here, so it's unlikely that she'd be hiding in the basement right now. He runs back upstairs and checks the yard to see if she's outside or in the parking lot. He pushes open the backdoor, only to find disappointment. His sister isn't outside. It smells like rain. He walks back inside, checking throughout the house. It only then dawns on him that he hadn't yet checked her room. Is this really true? Or just a fading memory? He climbs up the stairs on all fours, and runs to her room. He might be building up a sweat, but it's too humid inside the house to tell. The door to her room is shut. He walks over to the door, and knocks. This must be some sort of trick, some sort of- "What?" Brook shoves the door open. @@ @@ On the bed sits his sister, reading a book under her flashlight. She waves to Brook as he walks in. @@ @@ ----- [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box-end]]
