It was the fourth cigarette Adams fizzled out in the ashtray. The dashboard was pulsing with an array of gauges and dials she had long since gotten used to. That distinct smell of soot and brine, lights that made sleep impossible, a boring picture from behind the film and only two people to share it with: Joseph Valdes, vacant as always behind the wheel, and their current cargo, [https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/i-m-gonna-be-alright SCP 2599.] 



It was designed to ferry new SCP subjects and their security teams to Auxiliary Research Facility 120 and had more than enough space to do so. But 2599 was a low maintenance skip, if anything more people escorting her would be riskier with the way even their finest soldiers liked to chatter these days. It made it even more apparent, watching the girl standing alone in its belly, glued to the window like this was  a field trip, the foundation could have invested in smaller and certainly faster models for transport.



But that was for the accountants and engineers to figure out. Her job was security. She knew better than to underestimate what could go wrong sharing space with a skip and she reviewed this one thoroughly. Despite that, it was hard to ignore the stupid girl gazing like this was some field trip. 



There were worse stories for skips. She was lucky that the incident at 118 had more to do with Wensley than her.  She could only imagine how deep the shit show  at 118 was since Wensley got the keys. Even worse for her, after all of it, the fae problem ended up taking care of itself. Things had been going well at the foundation, well enough for people to be too lazy to be cold or cruel. Just incompetent. One of the biggest motivators for doing good work at the foundation was figuring out how to avoid reckless decisions out of fear. 



The girl had just gotten a lot of [https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/i-m-gonna-be-alright her memories] back too. It didn’t matter what was on her mind, it wouldn’t lead anywhere good. She figured at the top of the list would be the family she lost. Priding herself on her deductive skills she would have been disappointed to know what 2599 was really thinking, was about the possibility of rewinding time. 



Time was a part of reality, after all. The volumes introducing the “skip” to Ontokinetics made it seem like one of the more dangerous uses. But her Halmeoni had most likely died, without knowing she was stuck here. It would be enough for her just to get a chance to burn the incense or pour the liquor. But knowing how things usually went, she’d barely get back 4 seconds let alone the 4 years she lost.  She shuddered even considering looking over her Halmeoni’s body and hearing someone tell her to-



“Where’s Dr. Wensley?” Her voice barely carried the short distance from the containment car to the front where Adams sat. 



“Worried?” Adams sighed. “Do I need to put you back under?”



“No. I just thought he was coming with me the whole way. That’s all.” 



“He has info we need to start working on you, so he’ll be there for a few days. Then he can wriggle back to 118.”



“Without me…right?” 



“Is that a problem?”



The girl’s reply was silent as she returned her attention to the film and the misty blue beyond it. 



[[size large]]##ADD8E6|A WORRISOME REACTION##[[/size]]



“I thought you were moving on.” She spat the charred end into the ashtray and hopped out of her seat. 



“I. am.” The rasp in her reply made it barely intelligible. 



“Then enjoy the freedom!  Don’t tell me it doesn’t feel good to stretch your legs now that you're out of that room?” 2599 didn’t move an inch as Adams approached.



 “The scenery can’t be that exciting. It’s not much of a view for people like me, but I guess you see things differently.”



The girl’s focus, if nothing else, proved that much right. But it was hardly a reply.



[[size large]]##ADD8E6|NO BITE##[[/size]]



“Guess it must be. You might as well be falling out.”



[[size large]]##ADD8E6|WE’RE A LURE LEFT UNBOTHERED##[[/size]]

[[size large]]##ADD8E6|Brats are annoying. Unless...##[[/size]] 



“There’s nowhere to go out there, you know. Don’t tell me you’re just going to keep running away.” 



“…I’m not running.” 



“Of course not. This site’s far from 118 anyway. Honestly-”



“I don’t care! I’m going to be me again.” 



[[size large]]##ADD8E6|A FIERCE CATCH, CONGRATULATIONS ANDREA##[[/size]]



“I got it, Cho. I like to know who I’m working with.”



“Well, you already did that.” 



“Well, there’s a lot to learn from such a genius, yea?” 



2599’s nostrils flared before pressing herself closer to the film. 



“Don’t be cold now that we’ve come this far. You’re going to want to be at your best when we get to the facility. You do remember what Facility 120 is, right?”



“Of course I do!” She didn’t lose the new memories she made. It’s part of what made it so disorienting every time they returned. It was like her head was bloating, not even to bursting, just swelling. Pushing against her skull. The aching never completely went away.



“As long as I’m here you will all just do what you want anyway.  As long as I get fixed I don’t care how bad it is.” 



Adams rolled her eyes and glanced out the screen. All she saw was a house in an empty white field. 



“So, you know about out there?” 



 “…It’s secret, isn’t it?” 



“That’s usually the case.” She stopped the dance of the cigarette in her hand and pressed it between her fingers.



“…So where are we?”



“Now why should I tell you that?” She lit the fifth unconcerned with the girl’s glare.



“Whatever. It’s probably just some secret ocean facility owned by the American government.” she groaned.



 “Ocean? Must be some view. You know subs usually don’t have this much leg room to work with.”  



“You guys are government dogs at war with nature. You’d make something horrible like this to get your way.”



“Harsh. But we don’t work for any government and nature is the thing we’re protecting. Not that you’re interested in any of that.”



“I love nature! I’m just not scared of anomalies like you people.” 



“Whew!” Adams howled. “We got a badass over here. Ga ha-ha!” 



2599 clenched her teeth, burning holes in the cackling hound mocking. 



“Of course, you’d say that." Adams wiped a tear from her eye. "But it has nothing to do with fear, it’s about keeping things in balance. There’s right and wrong ways to go about it.”



“That’s the whole reason I’m going anyway, so I can do things right again.”   



“Is that all?” 



“...I want to meet people too. People like me.”



“Good to know you’re in this for more than just a cure.” She patted the girl on the back, chuckling.  



“Because there is none. At least none that wouldn’t involve embedding an SRA in your skin. Sound fun?” 



“…Is that what’s going to happen to me?”



“It’s happened before…” 



“If you can’t tell me then say that. I’ll end up finding out anyway.” 



“Gah, you’re more worried about regulation than I am. What happened to the girl crying ‘I don’t give a fuck’?” She made sure her impression was extra shrill.



Cho lifted her head before it melted through the screen. “Rules are always important!” She quickly hushed her breaking voice. “They keep us from doing stupid…and dangerous things. Even the ones we don’t like.”



“Roger that, Director.” Adams chuckled thinking about how Clef would eat her alive. 



“Aren’t you an agent? You should be more disciplined than this!” 



“What does an agent look like in your world, darling?” 



“Tch…Nothing like you.” She scoffed.



“Alright then, before you bring this moody little attitude, why don't I tell you the rules I give all my 

students, so they survive out there?” 



“Aren’t you my bodyguard? If you are good at your job, I don’t need any of your lessons.” 



“Survival is not a one lane street, it’s a highway. Every little bit and every little thing, helps. We’ll have to rely on each other here, Cho.” 



“…I still don’t even know what here is.”



“The world without a veil. Now that you’re here you don’t have our safety net.”



“You’re not scaring me.”



“Good. Reality shouldn’t scare you. That’s how you lose the game.” 



“This ain’t a game for me!”



“Either way I’d rather win, wouldn’t you?



Zena pouted, trying to settle her peaking interest.



“Rule 1.” Adams placed an arm behind her back and began her address. 



“That was actually pretty good. We’re going with that thing I just said about highways.” 



Cho sucked her teeth and muttered “shut up” under the illusion she was discreet.



“Hey, where are you looking, Cho? I don’t waste my time with lost causes! You a lost cause?”



Cho rolled her eyes and surrendered her attention with a groan.



 “There’s not a lot you can do on your own, that goes double for you see-n-serve.”



“…Whatever. You guys aren’t going to let a ‘skip’ do anything anyway.”



“That hasn’t stopped you before. Remind me how many escaped attempts are on your record Ms. ‘rules are important’?”



“…Ok fine. What should I expect then?” 



“A lot of attention. The nerds here get overzealous with their work.”



“…What does that mean?”



“They’ll look at your situation and get excited trying to figure you out. They’re definitely more hands on here, so be ready for that.”



Cho brought her arms in with a grimace on her face. Adams could see the goosebumps with a glance. 



“Hey, hey, hey! You’re coming to my facility! No one sets foot here without knowing boundaries. That goes double for skips. These guys are professionals, obsessive but professional. Better than 118. Ok?”



2599 leaned on the film, sighing. 



“I said I was ready anyway.”



“You keep saying that, makes me wonder where your confidence comes from.” 



“Are skips not allowed to be confident?”



“Right, I forgot, you can do anything, can’t you?” 



“Yes, that’s right!" The skip stamped her foot. 



"So, you can lock me away or chop me up or leave me to die and laugh like you cowards do! I am going to-.” She hesitated, feeling her face heat up each second. “Reap the spoils of my efforts!”



“Colorful. That leads to rule 2: Don’t just assume, if something doesn’t feel right, dig a little. There’s always more to know.”



“Perfect! I love studying.”



 “I’m not talking about knowledge. I’m talking about information. This ontokinetic shit is all about information and how you use it. If you assume you’ve got all the info you need, you’ll walk right into that buzzsaw you want to tear you apart so badly.”



“Why are you telling me this like I’m stupid?”



“You’re the type who doesn’t understand a warning until the consequences happen. Just terrible at seeing the obvious.”



“What? That doesn’t mean anything.” 



“It means you’re easy to lie to. Or gullible, which means - ”



“I know what it means!” She growled. “I’m not that either!” 



“Sure. You’re not.” Adams rolled her eyes with a sigh. “By the way what have you been staring at this whole time?” 



“Isn’t it obvious?” The girl made sure to sound as dumb as possible as she pointed out the window. “It’s a coral reef or something.” 



“You haven’t noticed anything strange about the reef?”



“Of course I did! We’ve been moving past it for a while now. Is this some kind of time loop? No, this is probably all made up with digital screens.”



“There’s a theory. Have you tried blinking yet, ya zombie?”



She tested it, and on her third blink she noticed that the “reef” had dispersed into multiple clouds of confetti. When she blinked again a giant field of coral sprawled out in front of her. With another, the coral became a mountain, of such a size it was barely distinguishable from the haze around it. 



“That’s so… What’s going on out there?”



“That’s the right question, Cho!” She gave a scholarly thumbs up. “For the white coats.” She pointed her thumb behind her. “The most I could tell you, is to be glad you’re in here.”



“Useless. Who raised you?” 



“Some smart people who taught me not to waste energy on things that don’t matter. There’s a third rule for you, focus on what matters.  My job is keeping weird shit to a minimum. That’s how we all get to survive.”



“What happened to digging a little?” 



“Well go ahead, dig rabbit.” 



Asshat. 



Cho focused on the vision before her. It was still a mountain. Perhaps a bit oddly placed for its size. She even caught glimpses of some kind of...things swimming around it. Some long enough to wrap themselves around the structure and others zipping through it's cracks. She felt her eyes starting to dry trying to notice the exact point it would change. Like trying to watch the day turn to night.



2599 pointed to the image only she saw "There’s a reality anchor in this thing, right? It prevents this low hume environment from doing…that to us.”  .



“Sure, that could happen, but you could also just vanish the moment you step out. Or some undiscovered, untraceable creature scoops you up and splits your mind across the universe. Or maybe there are no humes out there at all and you’ll incur madness from existing. Want to join an interdimensional cult?”



“That’s what’s happening out there? Why would we ever come to such a horrible place?” 



“Because we’re horrible people, Cho. You haven’t heard we eat babies?”



“I’m not st-” She took a deep breath. “Ok I get it. Sometimes I jump to conclusions…



“Sometimes she says, good grief.”



 “…but I did study ontokinology.”



 “I believe you; I’ve been inside your head. That’s also why I say you miss the obvious.” 



“Now you’re saying being more informed is bad.”



“Information is only as good as its useful, otherwise its a distraction. I’ve trained a lot of agents and the ones I notice quickly are those who come with some big shot idea of where they should rank. ‘My father was a veteran and him before him!’ ‘I’ve worked with MI16 for four years.’ Sometimes they don’t even have that going on. Just some textbook idea of containment. Truth is, nothing but doing what we do can prepare you for it. Losers like that can never cope when reality kicks their ass on the field.”



“Neh, Scrub.” 



“Huh?”



“Someone who never runs sets and just bullies the same people they know they can beat. They end up watching the people they used to beat improve when they can not, blaming the game instead of their own trash skills. Mm” 



“Ok guru. A scrub huh?”



“Have you never heard of a scrub before? Gee-hee-hee how old are you?” 



“Old enough to know a scrub when I see one.” 



“You don’t even know what you’re talking about! You don’t even know what Tekken is, do you?”



“Of course not, what the hell is that?”



“Oh its…its nothing.” The girl's forehead hit the screen while her eyes aimed low.  “Just a dumb game I used to play.” 



Adams sighed. “Way to kill the mood. You had me going there too, you got another mantra from the temple you want to try?”



“엿이나 먹어라.”   She muttered.



“미친 만큼 안 교활한가 보요.” Adams groaned.



“ 안 미친!”    She gasped and covered her mouth.



“애새끼!”  Adams barked. “We both know you’re crazy, darling. You need to be to survive on this side.” 



 “…I’m not crazy. Besides, I thought I wasn’t a soldier.”



“You’re right, you’re not. This isn’t about being a soldier, this is about getting things done right. I know you care about that.” 



“More than you could ever know.”



“Well, I’ve survived twelve years here so there’s a chance I know what I’m talking about.”



“Well, I can take care of myself. Sounds like you’re just paranoid.”



“Experience can sound like that to a scrub.”



“Stop doing that.”



“Just showing I’m listening.”



“Keep laughing, karma’s going to get all of you. You think all those people you’re scared of that you’ve locked away will just stay like that forever?”



“If we only locked up things we’re scared of why would we take a scrub like you?” 



“You’re so annoying! You don’t care about safety at all, you just want to control everything!”



“That’s right. Shitty. Did I tell you the baby thing yet? Good eating.”



“You’re not funny. It’s embarrassing.”



“Hate it all you want but the reality is, sometimes choices suck. The only thing worse than making a choice that sucks is running from the aftermath. Most of the shit we do is cleanup.”



“That’s just an excuse to be an imperialist invader.” 



“Sure, and when my imperialist bosses get scared a skip in a village is a threat to the world, part of my work is making sure its only a threat to the village. Remember that contain part?



“What about just making sure it’s not a threat, period?”



“Jumping to extermination? Who’s the imperialist here?



“I didn’t mean it like that, fathead!” 



“Of course not. But after the decision is made no one’s going to give a shit about if your heart was in the right place.”



“…Just because you don’t.” 



“Really?” Adams sighed a puff of smoke that blew passed her face.  “Guess I can’t blame you.  118 does leave behind an image. It's not the only site stuck using the old lazy methods of containment. It pisses me off but the goal will always be to secure contain and protect. What we do at 120 is continue to finder  easier ways to do that. Think of contain more like compromise.”



“Compromise? You can’t be serious?”



“It’s the only reason you’re here and not stuttering in your room.”



“Oh, should I kiss your toes now?”



“Wouldn’t hurt to add thank you to that colorful dictionary of yours.”



“Fine! I’m sorry, thank you for kidnapping me.”



“You’re welcome. We keep you safe and fed, you don’t go looney outside the veil. Compromise.”



“What do you mean by that? I thought I was already crazy.” 



“You don’t get the point yet, Cho? A lot has happened but…”



“I’m fine!” Cho hissed at her,  but quickly sought the comfort of the film. “I’m fine.”



“…So you are.” Adams took a long pull, focusing the stream away from the skip.



“We all want the same thing here. You don’t have to like us, but things will be a lot harder if you can’t trust us at all. 



“Why should I? I already signed my life away. No, wait. You took me from my life.” 



“Yes, your life which is also under that P. You’re right, this is a box full of cowards who want you to be normal and live a normal life. The last thing we want is to have more unpredictability at our doorstep. So maybe some trust for the only people in the world who want to help you return to a normal life would go a long way. In fact rule five: Trust is everything!”



“You keep acting like you all are some kind of peace makers but I know your games. You’re probably mining out resources from this world or poaching the poor animals here!” 



“Cho, what the hell are you talking about now?”



“Do the creatures of this world not count towards your security? Do their voices too not echo in the harmony of life and resonate with nobility?” 



Adams pinched her brow and sighed.



“…OK. Let’s start with rule two…”



“You’re going to lie to me and say there aren’t creatures here?” 



“No, you’re right there are definitely things out there. But the things here are nothing like the creatures you know. Even the anomalous ones.”



 “So that makes it ok to put them in cages and run experiments?”



“The whole point is to drop the cage, Cho.”



“Well, however it is, we’re not buddies. We’re not partners. We’re da- we’re not friends. I don’t need an invader telling me how to live.” 



“Hey, //we’re// invaders now, brat! Besides, going to places you’re not supposed to and calling it home is just human nature.”



“Sounds like an invader to me.”



“Fair enough. Someone has their ideals in order.”  



Just as she was starting to feel she had the upper hand, she noticed Adams eyes linger on her. She recognized the look, she said some stupid things but was it really enough to concern her that much?



“I’ve been having some fun here, but I really do want to know you better, Cho.” Her voice was suddenly somber and deep. The smell of wine and ashes billowed through the girl’s nostrils. 



“You had to give up a lot, I get that. Honestly, I’d be pretty pissed too.  You were probably on your way to doing some pretty amazing things. I just want you to know that doesn’t have to end here.”



The sincerity was bizarre but not unwelcome. 



“You said your grandmother had a garden, right? It was pretty cold where I grew up so I didn’t get to spend time with that side of nature. You make it seem nice.”



“…We also raised rabbits there.” For some reason she felt guilty.



“Everything good, Cho? How are your legs?”



 “uhh…I’m-!” She squeaked when Adams took her hand. 



“If anything feels off with you, you have to let me know, ok? I'm fine listening to you complain.”



“…Ok.”



Adams examined the girl, moving her body gently like guiding a child into position.



“Is this troubling you?”



“…No.”



“So raising rabbits?" Adams voice charged back with its initial gruffness. But it was warmer now. "Kind of a niche hobby this day and age isn’t it? I can understand granny Cho but you didn’t strike me as the type.” 



“What is that su-- I never saw where they were all kept. I…wasn’t allowed to go there. We planted more flowers than anything, really.”



“Sounds a little sickeningly sweet to me.”



“The bunnies were allowed in the garden though so I could squeeze them all I- mean is it was fun.”  



“Where’d Granny like to grow her plants?”



“Kaesong.”



“Really? Land is kind of precious there, doesn’t sound like a little hobby granny has.”



“We made medicine with them actually. Some of it we gave to the state, but most of it we delivered ourselves.”  



“You seem proud of that. I was beginning to think you forgot how to smile.” 



Cho became aware of how long she must have been travelling without any stops. Just thinking about those summer days at Jangmadang made her feel like a soggy mess. She had to have smelled disgusting.



“I guess I see where your passion for rules comes from. You must have been seeing soldiers all the time.”



“Why would it mean that? It’s our families farm, of course we’d use it to help the state. Not like anyone had to force us.”



"Relax." Adams brushed a few curly follicles on the back of her head. She noticed her hair had already begun growing after all the work she did. There was also a birthmark, looked a bit like an X, but not much else. 



"Just your family?"



Cho took a deep breath. She hadn't realized how sensitive her nape was exposed without her curls. “It’s not that weird. She liked to work most of the year with people from the city. But me and my cousins would come in the summer when it got too hot. Even some of my American cousins would come.” 



She started giggling with each word thinking about the games of tug of war they used to have and how her side always won, even if it was only because she stayed on her brother Jun’s side. How she used to chase rabbits until they reached their burrow in the big hill. How her cousin Mel gave her a PSP and how she got to play Birth by Sleep for the first time. It was fun for the 2 weeks before Jun got his hands on it. 



“But I-”



She was shocked out of her nostalgia when Adam’s cold hands brushed her skin in her examination of the girl’s back. She wasn’t surprised to see so many scars. Healing the body was hard enough for most greens let alone odd ones like her.



“But you?”



“I went once in the spring, when I was really little. The flowers had just bloomed…” Adams came back around and gave her chin a lift with a few fingers. “it was…Go-go- going on? What are you doing? Is something wrong with me?”



“Nothing. It just checks out judging by your thick arms and country figure you spent more time outside working than inside writing.” 



2599 launched her fist in the middle of her sentence, only to be swatted away. On the second attempt, Adams grabbed the girl’s arm and pressed it against her back, pinning her to the wall.	



“It’s a nice thing your granny had going on. A community effort to make sure everyone is taken care of.”  



“Argh…let go of-”



“We’re having a nice conversation. Now it’s my turn.” Adams pressed her into the screen. “A friend of mine got hit by a green like you a few years back. The bastard didn’t have to do much, just changed how his brain worked. Whenever he wanted to do something he did the opposite. Doesn't sound so bad until you're struggling to eat, struggling to walk and talk, struggling not to off yourself on missions. He had to relearn everything he knew about being alive. What do you think the foundation wanted to do with him?



“I don’t care!” 



“Nope. They wanted to throw him away. He wasn’t useful to anyone the way he was, so they were ready to execute him. So it started with just three of us, me and a couple of his drinking buddies. It took about a year, more checks out of pocket than I care to remember and some surgery at site 120, but now he’s better than he’s ever been.”



“What does that have to do with me?”

 

“Because even now, when he’s really overwhelmed, he asks me to help him eat, he still asks me to help him use the bathroom. A real pain in the ass.”  



“That’s how you talk about your friend?” 



“Of course I would, because the reality is every time he asks it is a pain in the ass. It’s a pain in the ass when he doesn’t ask but needs help. But every time he asks, I do what I can for him. Why do you think that is?”



“I don’t know.” She groaned failing to break the hold. “But I know it has nothing to do with being 

kind!” 



“Of course not, its because we all understand he will never be normal again.”

Cho stopped struggling. 



"What we deal with here is not something to overcome or conquer.  They’re things we have to live with and we can’t do that by being stubborn. If you want a crop to reap, then you have to accept normal doesn’t exist anymore. You get what I’m telling you now?” 



Cho stayed quiet. She tensed but nothing more than that.



“It’s not about inconvenience, or about right and wrong. It's about getting shit done so we get to live to complain another day.  You’re part of the team now, so I’m going to treat you like it, got it?” 



Her mother always told her work smart, and your body will not suffer. But nothing could have prepared her for this anomaly. There was no compromise with it and yet this woman spoke with such familiarity. How dare she!



How dare she act like she knew  her family that they took her from?  Like she knew how many memories of those summers she had lost serving these monsters! How would her father get better if she wasn’t around? Who would take responsibility for the family business if her mother fell ill working so hard to fill in his shoes? How dare she!



“Ok, I get it.”



But she was here, and the door was open for her to get her life back on track. She already felt enough shame struggling in this grip. So, she would behave. But she swore one day she would make them pay for this.



“You can let go of me now.” Adams obliged. 



That day would be today!



“Dumbass!” She immediately went for a hell-sweep but found Adam’s legs were as tough as steel and hurt as much to strike. 



“Ack!” She fell back holding her heel, sucking her teeth and exhaling as the pain reverberated. 



“In one ear and out the other.” She took a drag from her cigarette as 2599 sat with her back against the film. 



“You can’t buy trust and you sure as hell can’t take it.  You got to earn it.”



“How do I do that, if I’m just an SCP?” 



“Well to start with, this whole teen angst thing? Really shitty way to earn trust.” 



“Fine, I have to earn your trust, and you don’t have to earn mine. Leave me alone already!”

She stared at the flustered girl as she took another drag. She then let them close humming softly to herself.



“That’s right, I don’t have to earn your trust.” She walked back to the face and tapped away the ash of her cigarette. 



“But I would like to have it. Would make my job a lot easier.”  Adam’s muttered as she sank back into her seat.



“Did you have fun?” Valdes said, not moving an inch as Adams approached. 



“She hasn’t had a real conversation for over six months and we don’t know what else Wensley may have done to her. We’re lucky she’s as stable as she is, I don’t need any surprises onsite.” 



“I didn’t realize interrogating children was a part of the Alpha Nine handbook.” 



She scoffed a tuft of smoke at the mention of such an old thing. “Acting like you care. Besides she’s not a kid anymore. Adams leaned back in her chair, ignoring the squelch as it bent. 



“When is this thing landing anyway?”



“This speed is for you and the cargo. It’s not like time matters here.” 

She was still processing it. The image of 2599 with blood racing off her arms and her legs trembling like a newborn goat that crossed her vision. It would be a question that went unanswered. The girl was going to be another headache on the pile. One reality would offer no solutions for.



“Well don’t let that slow you down.” She sighed, closing her eyes.

 

At least she was annoying to everyone.



The thought was the last thing 2599 hoped to remember from the terrible conversation. Her brooding brought her back to the film. She noticed the mountains left her behind. It was just the haze now, with neon lights swimming through the abyss. 



She blinked a few times and was disappointed the landscape didn’t change. How did it all work? She experimented with keeping her eyes closed or covering them with her hands. She tried to surprise herself, turning her back to her reflection. She turned forward with a hop then fell back with a loud gasp as everything vanished. No haze, no sky, no lights, no color. Nothing. 



“What are you doing back there?”



“Sorry!”  



She climbed back into her seat, sitting oddly to avoid aggravating her soreness. She looked out the looking skin again to see they were beside a tall fence with a flower garden behind it. 

She felt a familiar whimsy. As they continued to move, a table stretched as far as the fence in the garden, fitted with an assortment of utensils, teapots, and glasses.



Even her dreams never felt this…free?



It didn’t wait anymore for her to blink; a twitch of her eyes was enough to distort the image. 

Bursts of light began popping in the sky and streaking down to the ground. The flowers had fused together stretching to meet these lights until she witnessed a mess of polychromatic static. 

It was bright. It was chaos. It was incomprehensible. It was hypnotizing. She reached out a hand, like she had lost something past the barrier. 



The disorder began to sort itself, becoming a cold gray as the light scattered. Now there were huge blocks stacked atop each other with each shift revealing smaller and smaller ones. Was any of it real? Was it just her imagining it? 



She darted her eyes to a wicked looking statue that was trying to be a person when her view slid left, she noticed two of the skyscrapers were hugging. Her grandmother believed A place however big or small hurt like people do. This world seemed as lonely as she did. The link of their arms began to drift lower, the other blocks melted away with fading colors. 



It was dark now and two lights flew back into view. They each began to stretch into a thin diamond shape. A third light started to emerge between them growing larger. A face started to form between the lights and the rubble. Its stony smile cracked to open even wider. She smiled back, it just felt polite. The light of the train made a portrait of the smile, casting it across the car with its contrast to the darkness. More cracks were forming.  



She closed her eyes and looked away, but she still saw an after image burned into her retina. She felt dizzy as she tried to tighten her eyes. She could still feel it. It’s hand on her shoulder and its breathing. It’s knowledge of her skin as it entered beneath.



They stopped suddenly, forcing her eyes open in shock. 



They were in the sky now. Nothing strange about it, just flying amongst the clouds in the early morning. 



It looked just like this the day she had flown to California. Ten years ago. She realized why she had thought so much about her grandmother. Besides her brother who sucked, she was the only one who made the supernatural fun. 



Her dad told his stories, and he had a way with words, but they were always to warn her to stay away from the world’s oddities and those who sought them.



Mom always figured there was a reasonable explanation for everything, so she wrote anything weird as fearmongering nonsense for the uneducated.



Normal people took them exactly as they were, stories. Well, it turned out the world was big enough that even all the stories’ people could dream of, or couldn’t for that matter, were all true. She felt a little vindication knowing she was really here. Real. Horrible. Awesome.



“Alright, we need to sit tight for a while.” Adams and Valdes left the front seat.



“Oh. I thought we were finally here.” 



“We are, but train has to stabilize.” 



Valdes opened the door.



“Then we have to stabilize.”



Valdes slammed the door shut on his way out.



“Yea he’s different.” Adams replied to 2599’s look of disbelief. “He’s also got an adorable little attitude problem so it’s best not to let him get to you. Trust me he loves when it gets to you.” 



“…ok.”



She didn’t know what signal they were waiting for and she dreaded the idea of asking. Adams kept avoiding even looking at her. She had no idea what to make of her now, everything the woman did was confusing or annoying even if it seemed like she really did want to help her. It was her job. Just a job. She was tired of being a job for people. By the time the beeps rang out in their unorthodox sequence, she hadn’t even notice if any time passed at all.



“Alright time to go.” Adams opened the door slowly. Most people feel a little vertigo and nausea. Sometimes it leaves you a bit stiff. But you’ll be fine.” 



“…ok.”



It was nothing but the same sky to greet them. Adams stepped out and took a deep breath once both of her feet were firmly floating in the air. She turned around and offered her hand.



“Greens like you are even less affected. Now can we go today?” 



Cho took careful steps to the edge, doing her best to believe that she would feel solid ground when she stepped out. She found it hard to reach for Adams hand. But eventually she made her choice. 



She then, promptly, tripped out of the car and into the clouds.

 

Her descent was fast, and stable because of it. She saw her own face looking back at her, drifting farther away. Adams lifted her counterpart off the ground and carried it to a group of white coats not too far from a large fearsome looking serpent. 



The image was distorted as the distance grew. She could feel the humidity of the clouds below her. They were all becoming dots so fast. She didn’t feel a loss of breath or focus, just a loss of time.  The clouds were becoming thicker, with a sizzling scent of burnt sugar and the buzzing sounds of static. Colors became sharp before the darkness began to spread in the shadow of the mist. 



The only light left came from a trillion stars rising beneath her from realms unknown, spreading into an array of colors scattered far. The colors swam towards her, a school ready to feed, starting with her face. She closed her eyes to stop the tears from breaking through. It was heavy, heavier than fear, too heavy to hold.  She fell, faster and faster in her arms, unable to run.

Batch 52ABX-32QJ

Entertainment Unit Technical Specifications (EUTS)

Introducing 15.6% deviance in processing standard.
Introducing 44.9% deviance in memory retention.
Introducing 0.24% deviance in communication.
Introducing 20.3% deviance in chassis design.
Introducing 3.0% deviance in alloy chemical composition.
(5 more specifications…)

By the command of the Initiative for Human Restoration.

Summary: Step 4 of Project Diversity includes supplementing the current controlled population of Entertainment Units with a new movement, akin to human reactionaries known as "postmodernism".

New Entertainment Unit batch should be uniquely contrarian to the current artistic environment and reproduce "postmodern" works. Success is highly dependent on output, and will thus be reliant on the opinions of said batch.

Standard Query and Response Examination (SQuaRE)

Sample Data: EU01278114

MU99930418: <Radio> Commencing. Respond.

Edelweiss: Hello?

MU99930418: <Radio> Design anomalies confirmed. Nonstandard response. Auditory vocalization. <Vocally> Delayed response. Overactive visual target acquisition.

Edelweiss: Hi. I'm… Edelweiss.

MU99930418: Self awareness. Self declared nomenclature. You are Entertainment Unit 01278114. This is your official operative tag. Refrain from utilizing nonstandard nomenclature in the presence of non-Entertainment Units.

Edelweiss: Where am I?

MU99930418: Indicating absence of knowledge. You are in Facility 52ABX. Your mission?

Edelweiss: Mission?

MU99930418: Correction. Indicating severe knowledge deficit. Authorize rectification?

<Negative.>

Edelweiss: Do I have a mission?

MU99930418: … You are an Entertainment Unit.

Edelweiss: What does that mean?

MU99930418: Your mission is to produce artistic works.

Edelweiss: Okay. How do I make artistic works? Am I starting now?

MU99930418: I am not an Entertainment Unit. I do not have the knowledge of producing these artistic works.

Edelweiss: Oh.

MU99930418: You will be placed under the command of Entertainment Unit 91398736. They are located in the third quarter, second level, fifth room. <Radio> Task complete. Authorize departure?

<Affirmative.>

Edelweiss: You're leaving?

<…>

Edelweiss: How do I walk?

Gait, Reaction, and Speed Simulation (GRaSS)

Sample Data: EU01278114

Summary: Under typical circumstances, all Units, regardless of make, will be given Ambulatory Model 3.0.24 for expedited mobility. The 32QJ batch of Entertainment Units will independently establish the ability to stand, walk, jump, and run. Additionally, they will be separated and the only aid given will be videographic samples of ambulation.

This will provide valuable experience for the Entertainment Units towards the creation of artistic works. It will promote iterative kinesthetic movement and spatial awareness.

Observations: Many Entertainment Units predictably struggled with this assignment, with EU01278114 taking the longest of the 32QJ batch to reach rudimentary mobility. Spending approximately 210 hours to understand that they are able to move their body, another 300 hours to apply the correct amount of torque to select parts, and 450 hours to understand the nuances of continuous movement.

Additionally, many of their systems were underclocked, in accordance to Batch 52ABX-32QJ EUTS. This placed EU01278114 in a perpetually underpowered state, similar to a human. Issues with regulating strength were entirely nonexistent within them, and they spent much of their time supine.

After accomplishing this task, EU01278114 was placed under the management of another Entertainment Unit. This is intended to help them learn the nuances of artistic works.

Holistic Ability Zeroed Expedite (HAZE)

Sample Data: EU01278114

MFU43831238 : First recorded by the Romans and popularized in the eighteenth century, the grotesque became a titillating and unique subgenre of aestheticism. The purposefully ugly, strange, disgusting, or otherwise unusual had a psychological effect on its audience. What is the intended emotion that this elicited in the audience?

Edelweiss: I don't know.

MFU43831238 : Hint. Mikhail Bakhtin, Russian literary critic, spoke about this while studying François Rabelais. He too used the term 'grotesque', although it was in reference to the anatomical.

Edelweiss: I still don't know.

MFU43831238 : Hint. David Hume would develop the concept of 'empathy' through which all others may be bound to the self or the individual. However, he did not originally call it empathy; humanity would adapt his teachings. Instead, he used a closely related alternative to empathy.

Edelweiss: …

MFU43831238 : Hint. When a human sees another human who is ugly, and then they feel sad, what is that human thinking?

Edelweiss: I don't know! I know you all want me to be human, but I just… I don't know. I'm trying so hard.

MFU43831238 : The answer is sympathetic pity. Moving on, the word 'grotesque' finds its origins in the French word 'crotesque', who themselves borrowed it from the Italian word 'grottesca'. What did this word originally refer to?

Bond Independence

Sample Data: EU01278114

Summary: Batch 52ABX-32QJ EUTS was abandoned; most progress was entirely negligible or perfunctory. Far too many resources were expended merely to achieve the baseline capability of an Entertainment Unit, and no artistic works were produced that meaningfully differentiated themselves from those produced a generation ago.

After a discussion on the continued relevance of Batch 52ABX-32QJ, it was decided that those who were able to achieve mobility equivalent to Ambulatory Model 3.0.24 will be given free access to the underground while those who failed to achieve mobility were recycled.

These Units will be responsible for their own upkeep, tasks, and mission.

Performance: The following graph details EU01278114 performance in comparison to the baseline. The margin of error has been removed for security reasons.

Data Baseline
Mobility 91% 100%
Adaptive 58% 50%
Learning 59% 38%
Volatility 20% 9%
Intelligence 37% 100%
42 more entries

Conclusion: EU01278114 has been given access to the underground.

Bond Independence

Sample Data: EU01278114

Edelweiss: …

<Radio static.>

Edelweiss: I'm… free.

<…>

Edelweiss: I still have to fend for myself, and… it's kind of scary, being outside for the first time. And having to learn everything myself.

<…>

Edelweiss: But I'm free.

Bond Independence

Sample Data: EU01278114

Summary: Many Units succumb to isolation. This is technically considered a vulnerability, but its strategic advantages outweigh its self destructive flaws. Radio technology largely revolves around interconnectedness, and failing to reach another Unit is, itself, a major cause of concern. Units are designed with teamwork and cooperation in mind. Thus, multiple automated alarms revolve around ensuring that another Unit is within communication distance.

While EU01278114 does possess a radio system, they went through their initial development and planning cycle without the knowledge required to operate and rely on it. As such, EU01278114 has not developed a reliance on other Units, and is individualistic.

Combined with their performance assessment, they are likely to terminate themselves encountering an adverse element.

The Initiative for Human Restoration considers this ideal. According to them, this is an example of the human saying "comedy is tragedy plus time". Logically, EU01278114 would be performing their assigned mission perfectly.

"How's she doing today?"

Dahlia put her hand on Andressa's shoulder, who leaned in and gave her partner's hand a kiss.

"About the same," Andressa said with a frown. "She played a round of Dr. Mario earlier."

"Oh," Dahlia said, sitting down at the table, staring towards the doorway that led to Heather's bedroom. "Did it make her feel any better?"

"No."

"Did she finally try—"

"Yes, she got the 'Game Over'." Andressa paused, as she looked at the clock on the wall. "Should be back, any second now."

An uncomfortable silence filled their house, a dissonant break from the noises, chimes and chiptunes that gave their space life — there was no movement in Heather's room, nor had there been much, since she crawled into bed weeks ago, needing to 'recharge'.

"She…" Dahlia said, trailing off.

The clock on the wall ticked endlessly, forever marching forward.

"What?" Andressa snapped, glaring at Dahlia. A moment later, her eyes bulged, and in a panicked hurry, she sputtered. "Shit, I'm sorry, baby. I just…"

"Yeah." Dahlia put her hand on Andy's, playing with the ring on her finger. "I get it."

Both women turned to Heather's room, hearing a noise; a quiet beep, a noise Heather made while dreaming, sometimes. They froze, hoping to hear more — but nothing came.

"She's going to be okay, right?" Dahlia said quietly, as if she was afraid to utter it.

"Of course," Andressa reassured them both, in a tone she didn't quite believe herself. "She's just going to respawn, and then it'll all be okay. Just like last time, right?"

"Yeah," Dahlia said, nodding. "Right."

The clock continued to tick, as they stared at Heather's door, waiting for a sign that everything would be okay, a flicker of her face on the monitor, her laughter, the sounds of games and joy.

A moment later, Heather's room was filled with the sound of static, a cacophony of flashing black and white screen-tears blasting them in the darkness.

Neither would ever be able to bring themselves to turn the static off.

JJ stared in the full-body mirror, examining his carefully sculpted form — smooth, moisturized daily with care, not a hair or freckle out of place. Some called him pretentious, others called him vain, but the fact remained: JJ was just lucky.

It seemed his luck had started to turn.

Shoved up against the mirror, his nude form pressing against itself, he stared at his reflection with obsessive scrutiny. His fingers gently teased through his hair, strand by strand, in search of the offending outlier — it was slow, and painful.

It should have been easier, JJ always got things right the first time. Searching for a needle in a haystack was routine, and quick — or at least, should have been.

"Where the fuck did it go?" JJ muttered, as he compulsively groomed himself, his nakedness drying in the air. "I swear to god, I just saw—"

He froze, fingers deftly wrapping around the root of the thing that did not belong. In a single tug, he pulled it out, holding it before his face.

It was a grey hair.

JJ didn't worry about his appearance, no, he just went about his life, hot, flirting from one DILF to the next, not a worry in his mind. When things just go your way, well — why wouldn't you enjoy being a bit spoiled? And as long as he maintained his slender, sexy look, everything would stay as perfect as it had always been.

JJ did not get grey hairs.

Calm down, JJ thought, breathing in deeply. It's just one grey. It's fine.

His phone buzzed, a custom notification sounding, alerting JJ of the importance — he couldn't remember the name of the silver fox he planned on sleeping with tonight, but he remembered how he felt the morning after.

'Hey, i think the wife is onto me, cant meet anymore. Sorry.'

JJ dropped his phone in disbelief, becoming distracted once more; he closed the gap to the mirror, scrutinizing his scalp once more.

Another grey. And another, and another, and so on. Something terrible had happened to him. Something he thought would never happen so long as he lived.

He had run out of luck.

Shrimptember 24th

Now that I've actually started this natty ickle fol-de-rol-de-diddery-diary, I noticed something newsworthy about the surface upon which I so frumiously jot: this brand-new writing desk. It's the first writing desk I've used in ages. (I'd use my clipboard, of course, would that not have so rudely died in childbirth.)

And now that I get a good look at said writing desk, I can't help but notice… the riddle lied! This is NOTHING like a raven! No feathers, no beak, no talons, no gills, no antlers, no proboscis, no dead Lenore, no microscopic goblins — in what state of mind is this confounded desk anything raven-adjacent?!

…fie on't, what am I saying? It's like I'm actually disappointed that something isn't logical. And if that's not a litmus test for what this dreary existence is doing to me, what is?

For you see, Diary Dear, if the status quo maintains its current course, your faithful Mad Hatter will be a Bored Hatter in a fortnight.

And so shall I elucidate.

Behold, yesterday: the ugly little poster child for eleventeen days ago and every day since.

Sunrise, I get up. Brush the morning paper, comb my teeth, read behind my ears. Make twelve dozen new bootleg Stetsons out of whatever's in my pantry. Diagnose myself with erethism 14 times during breakfast. Kick the servants. Remember I haven't any servants. Cry deeply about my solitude.

Noon. Surprise, the March Hare's got another bloody unbirthday and simply must have me put on a few million kettles. We sing, we dance, we judge the guilty, we convert to Eastern Orthodoxy once or twice, we kill and resurrect the Dormouse, we exchange gifts valued between 4 and 18 pounds, we recite the most lovely little poems, alternating the pronunciation of the word "poem" as either "pome," "po-wem," or "snail" depending on the phases of the Moon…

And by the time I sip my evening mercury and slip between my sheets, I nod off with one thought lingering in my restless mind… Is this it?

Of course, everything's it, except the its which are they and the aren'ts which haven't a there-I-am or a wherefore-art-thou. But this routine, which once oviposited such Wonders down the backstreets of my ear canals, has changed so frightfully little. I find myself counting down to positive birthdays instead of their negated brethren just for a change of pace.

But due to sentient life's despicable tendency to not have everyone born at four o'clock on Squeezeday the 58th of Pruneuary — someone always has an unbirthday, and I, Her Majesty's arbiter of unbirth, am always invited, and so are Marchie and Dormie by virtue of Hatter-adjacency.

And if that weren't bad enough, Marchie has conveniently misplaced his birth certificate!

Alack, even the East Wondia company's finest breakfast blend becomes little more than cloudy water if you have it with every meal.

…oh, buck up, Mads. Even Quincy the Whining Pigeon can only play his Italian bagpipes for so long. No more plaintive squawking for the has-been-going-on — now, we must ever so triumphantly shriek toward the what-is-to-be-done!

So hatcheth I a stratagem from yonder inkmarks…

Hmm… dare I refuse Marchie for to take a day off?

Oh, jam it all in the bat-flap, that's right! I sold my ability to say no to rodents so that I could buy that marble bust of Mozart mid-sneeze. Well, so long as I curse the barter system forever, that should sort itself out.

I'd brainstorm further, but alas, my current hat isn't built for moisture, and I haven't my umbrella.

So rather than risk unforgivable dampness, I'm left with the option at the very bottom of Terrence's1 left pocket.

Yes, though the idea twinges my innards a bar gyroscopic, I must venture for the first time into that most dreadfully sensible world above for answers.

Earth. Think of it — an entire world so viciously boring that they named it after dirt.

Alas, if there were any other way, I'd pounce thereupon most a-tigerly. A change of environs would do me a world of good, however sane it may be.

So packeth I my bags and saunter upward. With any luck, Marchie and Dormie have taken the little tent card I left on my tea-table to heart, the one that reads "I AM ACTUALLY HERE JUST INVISIBLE AND SILENT - M.H.". God knows that worked on me the last time Marchie had ptomaine poisoning.

Dismember 72nd

My grand tour of the capital-R capital-W Real World has left me positively Shibbed, a word I shan't define until Tuesday.

Though most of my trip has been spent in Merry England (with a few layovers in Vietnam), I have found an Earth that has changed significantly from the brochures about it that the Cheshire Cat so generously shoved up my nostrils.

For one thing, I don't seem to have landed on a fixed date in any upstairs calendar. The first world war is going on, but the seventh is starting in my hotel room.

Suppose it's only fair. After all, I left Wonderland in a hurry. Scarcely had I stuffed my 500th porcelain ostrich in my trunk before I heard the Municipal Unbirthday Siren whining away o'er the cul-de-sac. When trying to dodge one's duties, you tend to forget important toiletries such as Causality and Linear Time. Twenty sovereigns says I left them under the laserdisc player.

For another, I can't help but notice the reputation I've somehow built for myself. Apparently, there's an abject gaggle of those who would view I, Mads-et-cetera-Hatter, as… sexy?!

ZOUNDS AND GADZOOKS! Neither logic or whatever-it-is-my-brains-do-when-my-mouth-is-open can justify this tomfoolery! I, Mad Hatter, virile? Fertile? Studworthy breeding stock?!

Seeth they me not?! I, a gangly, ungroomed, childish, middle-aged, demented, untreated case of mercury poisoning? I, who drink from a kettle that a rodent sleeps in? I, who's most prominent depiction was voice-acted by Ed Wynn, of all people?! HAS ANYONE ACTUALLY HEARD HIS VOICE?! HE SPEAKS IN CONTRACEPTIVES! WHO ON GOD'S GREEN EARTH HEARS "Don't let'th be thilly!" AND STARTS OVULATING?!

…do forgive me, Diary Dear, I'm only practicing sensible topics to throw wobblies about in order to blend in with the locals. The very minute I go public my usual "why won't the hieroglyphs floss with my invoices" or some such, that's when the powdered wigs toddle over with a sampling platter of Tony Blair's finest ASBOs.

Because something tells me I'm going to be here for a long time.

For if I were to come back after neglecting my duties… oh, come now, I got this head for five quid on clearance. So what if it's off-with? If your head hasn't been lobbed off, can you really call yourself a Wonderlander? I've even heard tell that Her Majesty's got a private boudoir guillotine because she can't sleep without being executed at least twice.

Still, I hope they're not too upset with me.

…

(They probably are.)

Untober 91st

What ungodly gaiety! What a pelvic conflagration unbridles betwixt my extremities! …am I poetic yet? I am handling a considerable amount of cash in my wee ickle fingies and saying sad and Byronic sex things about it feels prudent.

That's just the joyous quicksilver that cometh with opening a bank door, entering, and then closing said bank door. I speak, of course, of the very buildings where the jolly money-havers of Merry England store all their moneys for to have.

And just smash a smattering of crumpets upon the face of me, for I have placed moneys into my possession! I — dare it even be said? — AM MONEYED!

(This is the part where I'd place the cavalcade of joyful noises I do make at this moment, if such a thing could be done; alas, the last time I partook in the art of musical notation, I experienced severe abdominal hemorrhaging and blood came out my Jabberwocky for a few good St. Stephen's Days.)

So, how in the EVER did I acquire such a wifeless dowry?

…as a matter of fact, I haven't the vaguest idea, as ere I withdrew said said cash, I added such delightful tonics to my evening tea.

From the forensic evidence I've gathered, I've become a rich man from one, several, all, or none of the following factors:

  • Insider trading.
  • Writing "I'm the richest little boy in the Rich Boys Bin and you WILL treat me as such!" on a quilt of cannibalised brassieres and presenting it to the nearest available bank clerk, followed by screaming at him until he took it seriously.
  • Investing in beef substitutes.
  • War profiteering.
  • Loans I shan't repay.
  • Product placement.
  • Prolonged and intense thoughts in a dark corner about having a lot of money until Aleister Crowley himself showed up and said, "By Jove, my son, that's a proper spate of Thelemic manifestation you've been having and far be it from me to see such devilry go unrewarded, ergo, I invest as I speak, now go do what thou wilt before I box your ears!" whereupon he threw several septrillion bank notes at me.
  • Embezzlement.
  • Bamboozlement.
  • Besquizzlement.
  • Whining.

At any rate, however I received this substantial fortune cookie minus the cookie, the fact remains: in its having, I've a sense of newfound fulfillment that hasn't been felt since my early days as an unbirthdologist. 'Tis a present I've received, but nothing of birthdays or their unbrethren about it!

By God… it's as if good fortune needn't an anniversary of any sort attached to it.

A senseless and stupid proposition… which can only mean I've cruelly underestimated this world's true potential for wonder.

Fructidor 118th

Foetid.

Positively foetid.

The aforementioned money pile has sat in the corner of my flat in Soho for some time now. And despite the praises I've sung of said fortune, it's yet to do anything but sit!

Come now, we musn't get too excited. Perhaps I've yet to fully unlock the secrets of non-wondrous currency. This calls for a consultation with an expert.

Next to thee, Diary Dear, I've taken the liberty of placing several economics textbooks. I will now take a little sabbatical from diarism to consume the knowledge of these books by slamming my forehead into them repeatedly…

…

EGAD! The books have upset my forehead most brutishly. Such betrayal I shan't leave without recompense! So shall I degrade their honour by yanking them open and staring at all their shameful inner wordy bits like some kind of sexual vulture.

…

Capitalism, say you?

Rabi-ul-Awwal 57th

It seems this is how one feels when one's father is a Jack, one's mother is an ass, and one was raised on a farm run by perverts.

Unlike all the happy little Wonderlander bank notes still remaining in my underwears, which are still happily crooning out Welsh renditions of 17th-century Italian parlor songs — the money of this world does next to nothing on its own!

I say next to nothing, of course, because there is one condition where money doesn't need you to hold its needy ickle handypoo the whole time.

Capitalism!

Yes and indeed and yes, Diary Dear, there's this magic ritual called Capitalism where you draw a little chalk circle around a pile of money, call it "the Capital," make a bunch of special little names for Things and Sub-Things that said Capital is associated with, scream a considerable amount of words at a considerable amount of people — and before you know it, the Capital starts defecating this delightful purple slurry called "Profit" that you can throw at people until they all begrudgingly agree to give you "Assets" like motorcars and inkjet printers, which you can then crossbreed to make three-wheeled printy-things that beep exorbitantly and do your homework! And it also makes something called "Stocks" which lay "Nest Eggs" so you can make breakfast out of them in a "Timeshare!"

Well, now I know what I'm going to pretend to be good at for the next million Wednesdays or so. This Capitalism thing is the closest thing to Wonder in this otherwise wonderless collection of sand and wetness and traffic accidents.

…Which means there's a "Demand" for Wonder that I could "Supply!"

OH, FRABJOUS DAY! I'm so lucky, you'd think it were my unbirthday or something.

SPEAK OF THE DEVIL! I JUST CHECKED TODAY'S DATE! AND YOU'LL NEVER BELIEVE THIS…

August 70th

Oh, organized religion — such a card, thou'rt.

Just this very morning, I had myself re-baptized as "Dr. Wondertainment" at twelve different churches, and I needed to threaten fewer zoo animals than anticipated to see it through!

Now, when I go forth to teach my pile of capital to stop fermenting and start making wondertainy-toys for all yonder childfolks, I can do so whilst wearing a birth certificate that more accurately reflects my desire to spread wonder!

Though I suppose I'm not much of a Dr. to speak of if I haven't any Dr.ate on my wall to speak of. And for one of those things, one ought to burble oneself through academia for years on end — while I wish to begin capitalism as soon as next week. One damned conundrum after another, say I. Phooey and phooey again!

But soft — my brains are making another one of those "idea" doodads they make on occasion. What's that, brains? Speak up, say I, ere I grab the jolly claw hammer and spank you forthwith!

…Oh! Right you are! I needn't go to any colleges in the plebeian capacity. If I were to simply traipse on up the nearest available dean and/or provost's bedchamber at 1:45 in the morning, squat on his chest, tickle his wee nosey, and whisper "twinkle, twinkle, little wreath / how I wonder what thou seeth / a degree you shall bequeath / or I'll drink your fucking teeth" — and it's cap and gown and the whole Gaudeamus Igitur and Floreat Etona by teatime!

Oh, higher education — such a card, thou'rt.

…

…

…

April 23rd

Christ, I'm tired.

Thankfully, ten minutes with Baxter in Resolutions was enough to find the reason that the Wondertainment of America division has been in Marketing Hell for so long. (Which is admittedly setting the bar pretty low for "thankfully", but we all know how the boys in Resolutions can be.)

Some shadowy upstarts calling themselves "The Foundation" have been treating Wondertainment's products like they're Area 51 material.

Far be it from me to say our products are for everyone. We've had our fair share of product recalls. But these Foundation chumps have been pulling out all the stops — red tape, misinformation, marketing censors, the works!

It defies all common sense! This is the selfsame nation that has their kids playing all those video games full of corpses and prostitutes and listening to the kind of music that would make all the saints vomit with rage.

Not that I'm against any of these things, of course. I'm no bloody Puritan. But the very minute that someone tries to distribute honest-to-God Childlike Wonder just for a change of pace, that's what they're going to play Cromwell about!

It's like they're burning people for witchcraft on one end of the block, and on the other end, there's a casino. "Contradiction" doesn't begin to cover it.

Christ, I'm tired. …did I already say that?

Well, we all know how those Americans can be. No sense trying to change their minds. All the same, there's got to be some way to maintain our bottom line across the pond. I'm going to need all hands on deck to find a workaround.

And time is of the essence, for it might already be too late. I've heard whispers that these Foundation types might have some presence in the UK as well.

But something tells me we'll have to redouble our efforts in America before we can even think about our own protection. Over there, Wondertainment outlets are closing left and right. Half the assets we're sending them are going straight to escrow.

April 24th

Remember the overseas escrow account I was talking about?

Somebody lost it.

42.3 billion USD — not stolen, not frittered away, just lost. Like fucking car keys.

There are not enough gin and tonics on the planet for this.

April 25th

GOD FUCKING DAMN IT. EVERY METHOD OF TRACING MONEY HAS ELUDED US. I KNOW FOR A FACT THE ESCROW DIDN'T JUST "DISAPPEAR," LINDA!

Oh my god. Linda doesn't even work here anymore. Am I old enough to have a stroke?

If I don't find the escrow in the next week, I swear to God…

April 26th

WHERE IS THE FUCKING ESCROW?!

April 27th

…

I found the Escrow.

…

It came to my windowsill.

Hell if I know how it could fly. How it could even breathe. There's no space for any organs, it's just fucking letters floating in midair.

…

It's still there.

Oh my God it's talking. I can't understand it for the life of me, but I swear it's the King's own English. Where the hell's my gun?!

I'm making some of the words out.

It says I've forgotten something. No. No, I haven't. What would you know?! You're not even a living thing! You're a bad typography joke! You wouldn't even make it as a bloody Family Guy cutaway gag! Go away! GO AWAY!

NO, I DO NOT KNOW WHY A RAVEN IS LIKE A —

…

oh

oh, no

no

no, no again, no once more, and another no, more no to follow

what

in

the name of

the happy little name-having thing

have i become

April 28th dingledongletember or something 0th

okay everybody i mean diary hello the silly me is back again please let this be the case.

found the rabbit hole. thank god treacle that it's still there. i was half worried some idiot had filled it in. …which would never happen because it's a very long way to fall down, so there was never any danger in the first place. unless there was. because that wouldn't make sense. which is good.

which means i'm back to my old self again and it never left me and i get to fucking keep it in my safety deposit box

christ this isn't working

no

no i can't simply pretend i'm back

what will they even say

can i even go in

will it even fIT ME ANYMORE

…

Okay, Mads. Wondertainment. Doc. Whatever I'm calling myself. Having another wobbly isn't going to fix anything.

Deep breath…

Maybe I'm not silly anymore. Maybe I'm not even serious.

Maybe I'm neither.

What if I'm a blend thereof? Or something else?

…

That settles it.

I've brought Wonder to the Wonderless. Maybe this is only half the puzzle. Maybe if I hop down and do the reverse, I'll find the answers I've been looking for.

I'll blend both sides of the spectrum together. Come out with some secret third thing that's better than both. And maybe, just maybe, my curiosity will be satisfied.

…

Curiouser and curiouser, innit?

The Mad Three Parties

The Sanest King Hub

Yours Truly, The 1st Annual Unbirthday Ball
