you-sleep-when-they-sleep.raw_content:
Sleeping for a snowy dream

🕰️ Word Count: 3.6k Words 🕰️

…

I turned my head around disoriented by the world around me. It was dark with an absence of color every way. The temperature was not exactly cold or hot although I felt the warmth drain out of me. There was no gravity to match the nothingness to see and I only floated around in the air.


"Matty?"


I called out knowing he had to be somewhere. No matter how hard I tried to turn, I couldn't shift my body. I was forced to just float around in nothingness in hopes that he heard me.


"Daddy!"


He ran up to me and pounced on my chest. We both began to spin backward in the air in circles. I felt warmth come from his body and heat me right back up.


"Hey Matty. What's up?"


"I had… I tried to go to bed, but that guy with all the scales and the teeth came out of my closet! Bleh."


I made sure to hug him tight.


"What did he do?"


"He just watched me and got closer to my bed. But I threw my pillow at him and was able to jump out of the window!"


I opened my eyes wide and made sure to check his body to make sure he wasn't hurt.


"Ah. That's… Smart."


"Yeah! And I think he's still in my room!"


The world around us shifted. Matty dropped to the ground and I regained my footing. We found ourselves standing on the pavement just outside of home. The yard quickly filled with snow and the sky with a thousand stars. Our clothes shifted to winter outfits — myself in a puffy blue jacket, him in a puffy blue vest, coats under both of our waterproof layers, with warm gloves and thick shoes to boot.


"We should go to the park!"


I looked back inside the house. His bedroom curtains were closed, so I couldn't see inside. I trusted him that a monster awaited — at least for the moment. If spending time at the park didn't get the monster to go away, then at least it would let Matty calm down.


"Lead the way."


He took my hand and began to drag me down the pavement to the edge of the road. Every other light in our neighborhood was on although we couldn't see anybody on the street. Matty paused and looked back at me.


"Did I take you from anything? I'm sorry if I did."


"Bah. It's way past my bedtime, anyway. I oughta go to sleep soon."


He kept going and once again dragged me down the street. We both laughed as we made it to the park. Leaned against a bench sat two sleds and Matty ran away from me to grab one. I trailed behind as he mounted the top of a steep hill and sat down on his sled. By the time I barely made it up the hill, he was already midway down.


"Wheeeee!"


I heard him cry out as he descended. I sat down and made chase and the small hill transformed into a mountain slope.

Matty let me speed up to him and just barely trail behind.

We saw a ramp in the distance. Matty turned toward it and leaned ahead — speeding up way faster than I could go no matter how hard I tried to. I saw him rocket toward the ramp getting closer and closer and closer until striking the ramp and shooting at least a hundred feet in the air. I had a perfect view of him being launched into space where I was on the slope.

I smiled staring up at him. Well, at least until he fell off the sled.


"Matty!"


I leaned forward as hard as I could to hit the ramp. Matty let out a scream just as I flew up into the air. We got closer and closer until he seemed like he would fall within reach of my sled.

But as he fell, I didn't rise. I would undershoot him just barely.

Without hesitation, I put both feet on the sled and lunged ahead. This time, I caught him. I turned around and put Matty in front of me while the cold air stabbed needles against my neck.

Our fall was broken by a deep pile of snow that buried the two of us deep underground. Before I had a second to recover, Matty shot out of the pile and out of the snow. As soon as I dragged myself upright I saw that we were back in the park and the mountain was gone. Matty bounced up and down in the air.


"Again! Again!"


I laughed.


"Maybe let's not go sledding tonight."


"Aww."


"I know, I know. I'm old and can't keep up."


"Well you caught me! You're not that old!"


"How about we make snow angels for a second? I promise we can play tag after."


"Okayyy… But only if you promise!"


Matty dropped down to the snow and moved his limbs out and in to create snow angels.

As I stood I wiped snow off of my clothes acting like I wasn't immediately about to lie back down in it. A minute later, Matty had already finished his angel when I finally started mine.


"Are we ever going to have a winter with actual snow?"


I grabbed a fistful of snow and crumpled it in my hand.


"This seems actual enough."


"But it's just dream snow! Not real snow!"


"Trust me, snow ain't all it's cracked up to be. When I lived in Spokane, every winter would be cold and frozen and miserable."


"Did you make snowmen and snow angels?"


"Sometimes. Not so much when I graduated high school."


"See! You don't remember it being good because you weren't doing anything fun in it!"


"Well you know how we're going up to Gran's house over the summer?"


"Yeah?"


"While we're there, you should try and convince her to let us come over for Christmas next year."


"Really?"


"I'll also try to convince her. She's a tough cookie to crack, but I think we can do it."


"Deal!"


The sky grew brighter as thousands more stars popped up covering every inch. There were hardly any splotches of black we could see.


"Is the monster still going to be there when we get back?"

"Hmm. I don't think so."


"Why?"


"It's close to Christmas. They probably want to go on vacation."


"Monsters have vacations?"


"Oh yeah."


…


"But what if it's still there?"


"Well, then I'll have to head in first and beat the snot out of it!"


I flexed my muscles and Matty laughed.


"Okay!"


Matty and I turned quiet as we stared up at the stars. I heard the snow around him no longer shift as we took a second to breathe.


"Did you know that chickens are dinosaurs?"


"Wuh?"


"Yeah. Birds are just some type of weird reptile that evolved to get feathers and fly."


"You're making that up."


"No, I'm not. It's true!"


"That's weird…"


"The funny thing is; whenever you talk about the guy with the scales and the teeth in a trench coat — all I can think about is that he's just made of fifty chickens."


"Fifty chickens wouldn't fit in a coat!"


"Of course they would!"


"That's way too many! The most you could fit is like… Ten!"


"Ten? You think they could only fit ten chickens in a coat?"


"Yeah! Well… Maybe a few more. But not fifty!"


"Well I imagine they're all kind of squeezed together in there. One in each glove, two in each shoe — and at least three in the head."


"Where are the rest of them?"


"Uhhh. Well, you've got to fit at least thirty in the main body. Then a few more on the arms and legs. You've got around fifty spread throughout."


"No way!"


"Don't forget the hat, too. There's got to be a few under the hat."


"Hrmph. I still don't buy it! It's like only thirty."


He shot up and left his snow angel, I joined him.


"It's kind of cold… We should go inside and get hot cocoa!"


"That sounds amazing right now."


We slowly made our way back up the hill. The ascent was much faster than it was when we went down, and a few minutes later we stood in front of our house. Matty hesitated to enter it and only stared at his bedroom window.

I grabbed his hand and walked toward the door at a steady pace. It was unlocked when I arrived and opened with ease. I flicked on a few lights within the house before heading to the kitchen.

Matty broke away from my hand to go to our couch and read some comics. Meanwhile, I put two mugs of milk in the microwave and got out all the toppings I could think of — even some we didn't have.

I mixed in real fresh dark chocolate and unwhipped cream before I sprayed a swirl of actually whipped cream atop it.

I sprinkled chocolate chips and mini marshmallows atop which seemed to melt and brown as I left them there. I even put on some nutmeg and crushed graham crackers.

He awaited patiently at the couch as I brought both mugs over.


"Oo! Thank you!"


Matty snatched up his mug and quickly began to down it.


"Yeah? You like it?"


He paused from his mug to regain his breath for a second. Chocolate was melted all over his lips.


"Yeah!"


I laughed as he finished his hot cocoa and I started to drink my own. It was the best mug I ever had; creamy and deep. The chocolate had a nutty flavor I don't think I'd ever tasted in hot cocoa before. Meanwhile the nutmeg added a great touch to it, as well.

As I saw Matty finish his hot chocolate, I grabbed a tissue.


"Come here."


I wiped his face clean of everything that spilled onto his face. After a second, he was good as new.


"It's getting pretty late, isn't it?"


Matty looked at his room's door. I could feel the dread come off of him manifest in the air. The beats of his heart grew louder and louder to a point where I could hear them feet away.


"Actually, I guess I did promise you that game of tag."


"Oh yeah!"


The chair I was seated on faded out of existence and I fell backward. Our kitchen disappeared as I fell until my descent was broken by a pile of snow. I was back in my winter clothing from the park. I looked around the woods, seeing snow-covered trees only broken by a small gravel path.

I turned my head around, looking for him.


"Matty?"


I felt his hand come out of nowhere and push against my chest to make me fall back into the snow.


"Tag! You're it!"


I dragged myself up and saw him running away from me, giggling.


"Why I oughta!"


I laughed and brushed snow off of my coat before giving chase.

We ran through the paths, snowy gravel shifting with every step. I was just barely behind him but not able to catch up.

He made a turn away from the main path down one marked by pine needles and stones. The trees closed in as we made chase — branches getting in my face and obscuring my vision.

When we finally made it out of the narrow trail, we looked down on a small little Christmas town. Red and white poles with LEDs littering every street. Every single hut and cabin had a humungous chimney with smoke billowing up to the moon. Bright yellow lights left every window with only black silhouettes of whatever was inside each house being visible.

He punched ahead past the clear snowy ground we stood on so I couldn't catch him. A set of wooden stairs presented themself to him, leading him down a hillside I couldn't see over.

As I finally crossed over the hill, and began practically tripping down the wooden stairs, I saw a giant lodge ahead. Its lights were yellow and fully-well lit, smoke came from a dozen chimneys much akin to the town.

Matty somehow was already at the door. He turned around and stopped to taunt me, only letting me close enough to see him stick out his tongue before he ran inside.

The front door was a revolving door. I stepped into it and began to spin — but I wasn't given entry. Instead I only sped up as the doors revolved faster and faster.

Speed threw me back against one of the rotating doors. I couldn't see anything outside as the speed got faster and faster.

When the doors spat me out, I flew across the room. I landed on a couch, seated upright, and with my clothes shifted to a fancy tuxedo. Smooth jazz echoed through the lodge as I got to my two feet. I only walked, for now, while I looked at the fancy winter hotel. Where I had been thrown from laid a giant glass window. I couldn't see the revolving door anywhere.

Outside the window was a giant slope that undercut the lodge. At the very bottom, despite fog and snowfall, I saw the same park by our house, albeit a couple-thousand feet down.


"Hey! Slowpoke! Catch up!"


The second I snapped around I saw Matty at the entrance to a hallway. I ran toward him and he grinned. Just when I was within pinching distance, he began to bolt.


"Why you! Get back here!"


He laughed. And I laughed. The hallways of the lodge went on infinitely only with the occasional turn and hundreds of rooms.

Matty turned and zigged and zagged every other entrance in an effort to slow me down. We found ourselves deep in the lodge by the time I was close to tagging him. He turned one last corner, and I foolishly followed.

I found myself seated in a saddle on the back of a t-Rex. Reigns to control it were in my hands.

We were back outside and I once again adorned my given winter outfit. No trees were anywhere near us, now, and instead had been pushed minutes away on either side. Ahead of me and my t-rex was Matty as he rode a triceratops that was running at full speed.

Quickly the both of us made chase to Matty, although my ride wasn't nearly as fast as his. He slowed down to knock over a giant redwood tree that appeared just out of the darkness, and thankfully we were able to walk on over it. It took a bit for Matty to regain his speed and I pulled up right beside him. He looked up at me. A megaphone manifested in my hand and I raised it to my mouth.


"Pull over!"


He grinned and started to make a sharp turn to the left. Before a second thought crossed my head, I made a leap.

I glided through the air attempting to jump on his triceratops. Time even slowed down as I fell. I was close — able to swipe my hands at its tail — but I wasn't quite going to make it.

Then, I felt a large, scaly tail lift me up from my chest and launch me in the air. The t-rex I rode launched me ahead in the air. This time, at a now normally-speeded pace, I fell on the back of the triceratops. I tried to get up to get Matty, but we started going faster than I could stay upright. I clung on to some leather straps of the saddle Matty sat on.

The trees narrowed around us, but I couldn't make out any details because of the speed we went. They all seemed to pass in nothing but blurs.

Suddenly the triceratops froze in its tracks and dug its feet in the ground. Me and Matty went flying ahead down a steep slope of snow.

I rolled around and around as gravity pulled me ahead. Matty, meanwhile, found another sled and rode that so he didn't get covered in cold. Snow collected around me and soon I was surrounded by a giant snowball rolling downhill. My head still peaked out, which gave me just enough sight to keep following Matty.

He looked back and tried to speed up as best as he can to avoid getting absorbed into the snowball. Try as he did, he was not fast enough and was squashed somewhere inside of it. I didn't even have a minute after to react when the snowball crashed against the bottom of the slope and shattered into a million sparkles every which way.

I laid down on the ground, half-covered in snow. I stayed motionless for a bit, regaining myself. I heard snow crunch leading up to me.


"Daddy? Are you okay?"


I stayed silent and waited for him to come closer to check on his old man. He crept ahead, cautious. When he stood over me, I shot my hand up against his arm.


"Tag. Gotchya."


"Awwww-"


Matty kicked the snow while I got up laughing. I was covered head-to-toe in the stuff while I looked around. Right there, in front of where we landed, was our house by itself. No neighbors, no road, no park.


"Alright. We both need to go to bed now."


I scooped him up and put him on my shoulders. We slowly made our way back to the house although neither of us were in a rush.


"You wouldn't have got me if I didn't check on you…"


"Sure I would've."


"You were nowhere near me!"


"I got close a few times. You've got to admit, jumping on that triceratops was at least a little bit awesome, right?"


"… I guess…"


"Hah!"


"You know next time I'm not going to be so nice! If you're stuck in the snow, I'm not going to help you!"


"Well I guess I'll have to catch up sooner next time."


We entered the house. On the table still sat our mugs, both refilled with steaming-hot cocoa. I took a detour to get our mugs before we went to his room.

The door had a sign on it which read, "MATTY'S CAVE. NO ENTRY ALLOWED." I cautiously wrapped my fingers around the handle. Matty dropped down from my shoulders and hid behind my legs. I gently opened the door and walked through.

A large bed took up most of the room — while a desk fitted out with lamps and pencils and papers and drawings sat right next to it. The floor of his room had a city-themed carpet with half-built Lego sets littered throughout every other step. A few shelfs were on the wall with completed sets. Right next to the door was a bookshelf filled to the brim, although the only books that really got any use were Percy Jackson novels.

I checked the closet, and the only stuff inside was a dresser and some clothes hanging around.


"Nobody's here."


"You're sure?"


"Mhm. No monsters in sight."


Matty ran inside and jumped onto his bed, hot cocoa still in-hand. I turned a lamp on and then shut off the room light.


"Alright. After you finish that, you need to brush your teeth."


"But we're sleeping. Why do I need to brush my teeth?"


"Oh. Uh. Good point."


He shot into crisscross-applesauce position and sipped down on his drink.


"What if the monster with the scales comes back?"


"Do you think they will?"


"Yeah! What if he's just hiding really well?"


Matty pointed to his closet.


"Tell you what-"


I grabbed handfuls of unused Lego bricks and scattered them both in the carpet and just in front of it.


"If they somehow sneak their way into it, whenever they try to come out they're going to step on Legos and start running away in pain.


Matty giggled.


"That's not going to work!"


"It will! Then after they start running around, I think they're going to trip and their trench coat will come off. When that happens, I need you to count how many chickens they were made of."


"What if I can't catch all of the chickens?"


"Then we can just say I'm right about their being fifty chickens crammed into them."


Matty grumbled.


"There's only like forty chickens in it at most…"


He finished his hot chocolate and I took the mug from him. I set the mug down on his desk while he tucked under the sheets.


"Goodnight Matty."


"Goodnight."


I shut of the lamp and the room briefly turned to darkness. Glow-in-the-dark stickers of stars were strewn across the ceiling of his room and shone through the darkness. I stood against the dark and walked through the door.


"You're sure the scaly guy isn't coming back?"

"I'm sure. And, if he does — I'll come right back here and slug him straight in the eye! Sound like a deal?"


"Hrm. Deal."

"Goodnight."

I stepped through the door to wake up back in the living room. It was late, about 1 A.M. The TV was still on and playing some weird late-night documentaries. I shut off the TV and began walking to my room. Before I finished the journey, I quietly peeked inside Matty's room to check that he was still asleep. His blankets were thrown on the ground and he was laid flat. I walked inside quietly and lifted his sheets back on him so he wouldn't be cold. After that, I left the room for my own.

My teeth still needed to be brushed and my face needed to be cleaned. It took a few minutes for me to get finished, and after that point I sat down in bed. The alarm specifically read, "1:23 A.M." when I checked it. A sigh left my mouth as I tucked myself into the sheets and fell back.

The weight around my eyes grew and I let them close. Should Matty need me, I'll already be visiting right there in dreamland.

[[/>]] [[=]] He finished his hot chocolate and I took the mug from him. I set the mug down on his desk while he tucked under the sheets. [[/=]] [[<]] "Goodnight Matty." [[/<]] [[>]] "Goodnight." [[/>]] [[=]] I shut of the lamp and the room briefly turned to darkness. Glow-in-the-dark stickers of stars were strewn across the ceiling of his room and shone through the darkness. I stood against the dark and walked through the door. [[/=]] "You're sure the scaly guy isn't coming back?" [[/>]] [[<]] "I'm sure. And, if he does -- I'll come right back here and slug him straight in the eye! Sound like a deal?" [[/<]] "Hrm. Deal." [[/>]] [[<]] "Goodnight." [[/<]] I stepped through the door to wake up back in the living room. It was late, about 1 A.M. The TV was still on and playing some weird late-night documentaries. I shut off the TV and began walking to my room. Before I finished the journey, I quietly peeked inside Matty's room to check that he was still asleep. His blankets were thrown on the ground and he was laid flat. I walked inside quietly and lifted his sheets back on him so he wouldn't be cold. After that, I left the room for my own. My teeth still needed to be brushed and my face needed to be cleaned. It took a few minutes for me to get finished, and after that point I sat down in bed. The alarm specifically read, "1:23 A.M." when I checked it. A sigh left my mouth as I tucked myself into the sheets and fell back. The weight around my eyes grew and I let them close. Should Matty need me, I'll already be visiting right there in dreamland. [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box-end]]

you-want-takeout.raw_content:
4:56
Another beautiful evening in the city. Well cities to be exact.

New York City. NYC. The Big Apple. The city that never sleeps.

Even now he could hear the honking, the screams, the laughs, the joy. Of course it had its problems but its magnificence drowned them out.

"Well look who it is. Looks like Mr. Hotshot here is too busy for us poor lonely security guards!"

He grinned. Ryker was always a masterful joker. Probably the reason why he was assigned as chief of site security.

"Cool it. I've only been Level 3 for a week, surprised I'm not dead yet."

He was poached by the Foundation three weeks after graduating from Purdue. Not top of his class but high enough to get their interest. Where he came short in his academic career, he more than made up for his creativity. Turns out when you're dealing with anart, being creative is a huge upside. Big Shocker.

"Well if you do I'll make sure to tell the misses."

"See you in the morning Ryker!"

"Only if I'm not dead!"

5:11

The sunset gleamed and bounced across the skyscrapers to where he stood.

It was fortunate he was placed here right in the dead center of the city, Manhattan. From the outside it looked like a vacant apartment building, old grimy windows, crumbling walls, and lots of scaffolding right by the entrance. Site-28 was a masterpiece of deception, not even the UIU knew where it was, only that it existed.

He walked south toward Spring Street, the closest place where he could catch the subway. For all the millions that were poured into the MTA, the place still looked like a shithole. In the corner of his eye he spotted some police officers harassing what looked to be a homeless teen. The poor girl looked terrified. Probably a new one, just kicked to the curb. Rent was getting higher and higher, thank god the Foundation paid its people well.

He looked away from the girl. He couldn't help even if he wanted to; the UIU might trace him back to Site-28, and he preferred to keep his job. He hopped aboard the E train. It was one of the nicer trains that the city kept. Hope that girl caught a break.

6:01

He got off by Roosevelt. Queens was one of quieter areas of the city, only by comparison though. His wife worked nearby in one of the big hotels in the city. He couldn't remember the brand but was still immensely proud of her. She was manager and with her ambition he knew he would see her soar one day.

He strolled right into the lobby and sat on the green couch by the corner. It was a habit they made. He would take the Sub and walk to her place before they both drove home together.

"Excuse me stranger but you're gonna have to pay for looking that handsome."

He looked up from his phone. She had this flirtatious smile glued to her face. She was teasing him and she knew it. God, she was stunning.

He replied just as smugly, "Really? Then you should really see my wife. Have you seen her? She’s blond, stunning, weirdly into ‘How to Train Your Dragon.’ "

"How could you not?!"

"You want takeout? I'm thinking Chinese."

"No! Japanese!"

"Come on! We've had Japanese three times this week!"

"Nope! I need comfort food."

He chuckled. His wife looked too lovable when she was stubborn and he always gave in.

"Fine, but no sushi!"

"Deal!"

He looked back and the flashing sign stared back.

"Hilton - Splendor Impassivity"

7:19

He pressed the dial button. It rings for a few seconds. Someone picks up.

"Hello?"

An overly cheery voice answered. Figures.

"Hello. You have reached Smart City Properties! How can we help?"

"I'm looking for a location."

"Okay, where are you looking?"

"Manhattan, NYC."

"I'm sorry we don't have any properties in Manhattan. I can give you names of other companies that might, would you like that?"

"Omega Charlie 334 Hecate 37"

He waits for a few seconds. Did they hang up?

"Standby."

Her cheery voice is gone. It seems clinical, almost hateful now.

"Does the Black Moon howl?"

"Only when eternal night begins."

"Confirmed. What do you need, agent McKay?"

"Sending over some info now. Give it to the Site Director, I will be awaiting her response."

Click.

8:24

"Japanese followed by ice cream. Not the greatest decision-maker are you?"

"Shut up. It's my life, and I'll live it the way I want."

"Not when I'll be paying for it."

She looked back at him. Even now he loved her for all her little quirks. Did she even deserve this? After all she's done? All the blood on her hands, the families she'd broken, the betrayal and heartbreak she's caused. And here she was eating a tub of mint ice cream with a man that would do whatever it took to make her happy.

It was never really a choice though. It was her family legacy stretching back to her great-grandparents who were part of the original defectors. She was told from birth of what she would become, what she could do, what she had to stomach. It was better to leave all those thoughts at work, right now she was content.

8:43

"Splendor Impassivity?"

"It seems so. One of our agents in the UIU relayed this information to us. He requests orders on how to approach it."

"So what do we know about whatever the hell it is?"

"As you know, Backdoor SoHo is one of the few places the UIU has a large presence."

Director ███████ only nods along.

"After a few raids, they've discovered remnants of machinery standard for the Chaos Insurgency."

"This isn't exactly news Ryker. We've known the Chaos Insurgency to be operating here for the last few decades. They're trouble but they never really posed a threat here."

"Until now. This intel suggests this 'Splendor Impassivity' program is responsible for the huge increase in the Insurgency's budget and it's only growing. My gut tells me there’s something larger at play here."

"And we don't have any leads?"

"No. We don't have a single name to go off of."

Director ███████ leans back in her chair.

"Okay. Let the UIU handle this. I'm guessing it's some kind of human tracking program. Give them a tip to point them in the right direction. With enough time they may find the facility on their own. Notify our agents in MC&D, hopefully they can grab something."

"Understood. Good night."

Director ███████ suddenly stands up.

"Ryker! Where's Dr. Price? He's supposed to hand over those reports to me today."

Ryker stops and looks backward.

"Oh Keith? He's at home with his wife. I think he left those reports on his desk."

Director ███████ glares at Ryker for a minute before softening.

"Thank you. Have a good night Ryker."

How to Lie To Your Family

your-ashes-under-my-skin.raw_content:
An ancient Scottish warrior-maiden grapples with her closest friend and greatest rival. Her every action is haunted by the absence of her other half, and by her presence.

Anorrack & DrGrimoire

(1479 words)

Dedicated to our wives, Anorrack's of two years and Grim's soon-to-be. Happy International Lesbians Day!
— Anorrack & DrGrimoire

I remember how we play.

The salted wind rips down the bare coast and tousles your hair as we joust and spar, with lengths of ash cut from the only tree in leagues of the broken and forlorn castle upon the island of Skye. Scáthach judges as we play, from her seat in the courtyard, her tattoos glimmering in the noonday sun, shimmering and enchanted and suffused with the magick of her own soul. Tattoos made to mimic the ancient secrets whispered by Cú Chulainn as payment for her teachings. She wears them proudly, the marks of the Warrior Maiden.

She stands and calls out my stance, kicks at my feet so out of form, slaps my face as I mouth off against her teaching, and praises you in equal measure, lauding your perfect form, your graceful stance, caressing your cheek as you bask in the radiance of her approval.

I feel a hole in my gut, a knot of anger and rage and spite. She favors you more, you with your flaxen hair, you with your unblemished skin and your long, graceful limbs. You who have never been scarred by the claws of famine or the teeth of plague. You…

You, with your comely, even face, your smiling eyes of emerald and growing grass. You, with your toned arms and legs, padded thick with fat even in the leanest nights when even the moon is starved and thin.

You, who are so, so beautiful.

I find you, later that night, in your room, pretending to be asleep in the dark. I find you there.

You find me there.

We find each other, we find our fingers roaming over each others’ bare skin, yours tracing lines down the scars lacing across my body like the tight knit of a crone’s craft. Marks of lessons I never seem to learn. Pocks of childhood scabs, kisses of the red plague and the pale raised ridges of skin stretched too tight by hunger, snapped back after famine’s end.

Your lips find my ear in the consuming dark, your uneven breath as loud as a summer storm, blanketing out any other sound. You call me beautiful, that night.

I will never forget it.

I remember how we fight.

We are like fire, like lightning. We are weapons sculpted of muscle and flesh, every curve, every line perfected by years of harsh training, measured only against each other. The others never intervene, never compete, for how can they? How can anyone compete with you but me?

We clash with the sound of armies against each other, spear on spear and flesh on flesh, close as lovers, closer even, close enough to taste. Blood and sweat and spit on coy lips. A little ending at your hands, a little ending at mine. Blunted weapons, leaving cuts just deep enough to be a lesson. Songs written on our skin, of growing, of hating, of wanting. How often do we dance this dance? How often have we pressed ourselves against each other, bare-chested or in mail or furs, you striking at me, me at you. How many times have you won, and how many have I?

Who can say?

I can. Even as I rage at Scáthach, for choosing you over me, her eldest student, first of her spear-maidens, I understand it. You have always been the better part of us. You have always been her favorite, and mine too. I admit that to myself a year after I leave, carrying nothing but my spear and a blanket that still smells like you and me making war on each other, heavy with the scent of iron and smoke. I roam the world, aimless, seeing the legions at march and the midnight sun, the white cliffs of chalk and the deep green forests. Anything to fill the hole left by the absence of you.

Before I go, you call out to me. You call me selfish, that night. It’s a blow that hurts more than any you landed on me before.

I will never forget it.

I remember how I cry.

I return with my spear, battered yet strong from battles hard fought and won, with my blanket which no longer smells of you, carrying my pride like a banner held high, like I had made a name for myself, like I had marked the world bloody with my spear, dealing it a blow it would never forget. Like my leaving you had been an adventure to be immortalized in song and passed on, mother to daughter, for generation on generation on generation. I tell myself, on the long walk back, over and over like a mantra, that those are the reasons I come back to the lonely castle on that lonely isle, that I come to boast, to brag, to sing.

But that’s not why I return.

I can never stay away from you.

I will always come back to you.

I will always be too late.

Your lips, blue as the sky above Skye, your skin as gray as the slate and sea. I remember how you lay there, so fragile when you were strong, so pale when you were vibrant, Scáthach’s tattoos still fresh upon your flesh, the mantle barely worn. Your students, now, with Scáthach long gone, your students tell of how you fell. You, struck down by a coward’s blow.

How I hunt them down and avenge you, stalking them through field and fen, tracking their lumbering steps fleet of foot, ceaselessly, tirelessly. How I break them, with the arms that held you, with the spear that clashed against yours, how I weep as I take my pound of flesh for what they did to you, you who were always the better half of us. You who were the better half of me.

I feel your spirit, in the space between spaces, in the void where no void should be, staring out at me with your eyes of coin and your hair so sparse and brittle. I feel your voice like an autumn breeze, whispering in my ear, so low I can scarcely hear it. You call me by my name, my true name. The name I have told no one but you. You call me Warrior Maiden. You name me heir.

I will never forget it.

I remember how we touch.

Your skin, burnt to ashes and rubbed into open wounds that trace the curves you once caressed, with fingers now sharpened by knapped flint, driving the ink that was you into my flesh.

You pierce me, over and over, and I feel you, stronger and stronger, with each stick, with each stab of your sharpened bones, etching all that is left of you on every inch of me, all that remains from the funeral pyre, your charred flesh mixed with that of ash boughs, from the same tree our sparring sticks were hewn.

I don the mantle of Scáthach, and I don you through it.

Over and over, the last bits of you drive into me. Over and over, we get closer and closer, together, total and inexorable and burning in a way beyond the animal heat of sex or the soft warmth of love or even the cold sear of death. All of you, burned forever into all of me, a brand I will carry until my own passing, one I wear proudly. Shamefully.

You haunt my steps. You haunt the spaces I do not go, the corners where no mortal trods. I can feel you, staring at me, judging me for the things that I do not do, loving me for the few things I do. You are so close yet so far, separated by the skein of our worlds. A wall of ash and salt and blood. I feel you in my sleep, in the witching hour where monsters dwell and spells are cast, you are there with me while I sleep, brushing your fingers across my tattoos of you, across my scars of blade and pox, touching my auburn hair, making me ache with absence and pleasure and pain all at once. I wake to your whisper, at the edge of my hearing, and I fall asleep again dreaming of your coming.

Your spirit haunts me. I wear it as you wear my body, channeled into me through the tattoos of Scáthach, granting me your speed, your grace, your strength.

Granting me your memory.

Sometimes I think I can hear your voice once more, as clear as the day I lost you, when I am alone on that forsaken isle, when my students that dance in your footsteps have departed, when the wind howls through the empty windows and empty rooms, when it is the deepest night of Samhain, I hear you call out to me, I hear you call me lover.

I will never forget you.

Your skin, burnt to ashes and rubbed into open wounds that trace the curves you once caressed, with fingers now sharpened by knapped flint, driving the ink that was you into my flesh. You pierce me, over and over, and I feel you, stronger and stronger, with each stick, with each stab of your sharpened bones, etching all that is left of you on every inch of me, all that remains from the funeral pyre, your charred flesh mixed with that of ash boughs, from the same tree our sparring sticks were hewn. I don the mantle of Scáthach, and I don you through it. Over and over, the last bits of you drive into me. Over and over, we get closer and closer, together, total and inexorable and burning in a way beyond the animal heat of sex or the soft warmth of love or even the cold sear of death. All of you, burned forever into all of me, a brand I will carry until my own passing, one I wear proudly. Shamefully. You haunt my steps. You haunt the spaces I do not go, the corners where no mortal trods. I can feel you, staring at me, judging me for the things that I do not do, loving me for the few things I do. You are so close yet so far, separated by the skein of our worlds. A wall of ash and salt and blood. I feel you in my sleep, in the witching hour where monsters dwell and spells are cast, you are there with me while I sleep, brushing your fingers across my tattoos of you, across my scars of blade and pox, touching my auburn hair, making me ache with absence and pleasure and pain all at once. I wake to your whisper, at the edge of my hearing, and I fall asleep again dreaming of your coming. Your spirit haunts me. I wear it as you wear my body, channeled into me through the tattoos of Scáthach, granting me your speed, your grace, your strength. Granting me your memory. Sometimes I think I can hear your voice once more, as clear as the day I lost you, when I am alone on that forsaken isle, when my students that dance in your footsteps have departed, when the wind howls through the empty windows and empty rooms, when it is the deepest night of Samhain, I hear you call out to me, I hear you call me lover. I will never forget you.

“Think you could lend me some of those?” Ash looked at the red cup filled with rattling change.

Katie gripped her quarters tightly to her chest. “What happened to all yours from yesterday?"

“Spent it all trying to beat my high score,” Ash said with a grin, sticking her hands in her flannel jacket pockets as they walked.

“All of it?! On Tron?! It’s not even that hard!”

“The games keep changing!” Ash waved her off. “Just when I get the hang of one—” A soft breeze blew her long blond hair into her face, and she swept it back over her ear.

Katie sighed, “Fine, you can borrow some of mine when we get there.”

“Sorry, know I usually pay for everythin', but my dad figured out I was using his card and cut me off.”

“That’s what you get for stealing,” Katie huffed.

“Nah, fuck him! He’s always off on his ‘business trips’, spending God knows how much, least he could do is toss some change my way from time to time,” Ash grumbled, kicking a rock down the sidewalk.

“Stealing is always wrong, though, Ash. That’s what my mom says.”

“Get off your high horse Kate, you don't know what you're talkin' about. Your mom’s always there when you need her.”

Katie rubbed at her arm awkwardly, her pace slowing down. “Yeah… guess so…”

Ash just snorted back. She was usually right about these things. “C'mon, race you there!” she yelled with a tap on Katie’s shoulder and took off sprinting. Katie struggled to keep up, putting a hand on the cup to keep all her money from spilling out.

The sun beat down on the sleepy small town of Sitka. This summer was unusually hot; the air felt thick and stuck to their clothes. Katie wiped sweat off her forehead, squinting and struggling to see the neon sign of the arcade up ahead. She couldn’t wait to get into the air-conditioned indoors.

The duo sprinted past scattered adults and dark storefronts. The town had been through a rough patch since the logging business died out, but the arcade was hanging on, fueled by all the kids out of school.

Ash got there first and ducked inside. Katie followed after, and a blast of cool air hit her face. She leaned against her knees, out of breath, her eyes adjusting to the darker interior. Beeps and boops assaulted her ears, and the pop music playing loudly on the speakers didn’t help either.

Ash chuckled, “You're super out of shape, Kate.”

A boy shoved Katie from behind, almost sending her tumbling to the floor; she just barely kept a grip on her cup.

“Hey, watch it, bitch!” he hissed at her.

Ash stormed right up to the skinny boy and grabbed him by the throat, “Call her that again, and you’ll be eatin' out a plastic tube the rest of summer, got it?” dripped from her voice like venom.

The kid struggled to shake his blond head, holding his hands up in defense, “Y-yeah sure, whatever man!” She tossed him back, and he stumbled off clutching his throat, “Fucking psycho…”

Ash sighed. She set her hands on Katie’s shoulders, inspecting her, “You okay?”

“Yeah…”

“Hey, if anybody ever gives you trouble, you let me know, huh? I’ll hack ‘em up and hide the bodies,” Ash grinned.

“No, don’t get in any fights for me, Ash,” Katie mumbled, rubbing at her arm.

Ash let out a soft sigh, “M’kay sure, whatever you want, dude. C'mon, let’s get out of the walkway here.” Ash quickly reached her hand into Katie’s cup and grabbed a fistful of change before disappearing into the rows of cabinets and crowds of kids.

Katie stood herself back up, ready to follow, before a raspy voice rang out from just behind her.

“Hey, can I play with you?”

She turned to see a teenage girl about her age wearing a torn, stained hoodie. Her tangled black hair fell to her shoulders. Her greyish-black eyes were sunken into her pale face, and her pupils were extremely dilated . She looked like she didn’t know what to do with her limbs, standing like a puppet with its strings cut. Katie felt a chill run up her spine looking at her.

“Oh! Uh, you need to borrow some quarters, too?” Katie offered.

The girl cocked her head to the side, “Um… I guess? I don't think I've ever been to one of these places before.”

Katie shuffled around awkwardly. The girl’s bloodshot eyes bored into her soul, and she slouched and held her right arm close to her body. She was actually rather cute in a sort of creepy way. Katie decided to take a chance on her and took a deep breath to shove her fight-or-flight response down. “Here, lemme show you then,” she said with a forced smile. She guided the girl over to a machine; Space Invaders, and put a coin in. The game started with its 8-bit jingle. “See? You use this stick to move and press this button to fire.” The girl hesitantly stepped up to the machine and started playing. She was quite bad, but she had a smile on her face.

“So… you new in town? What’s your name?” Katie asked, leaning against the machine. The girl glanced to the side, eyes flicking between Katie and the screen.

“Oh right… I… I’m Riley. Just… got here, yeah.”

“Well, it's nice to meet you, Riley. I’m Katie. My friend Ash should be somewhere 'round here too…” she trailed off and glanced around, but couldn’t spot her at the moment. “Anyway, you stayin' here in town long?"

Riley sucked in a breath, then sighed as her character died on screen. She let go of the controls, rubbing at her arm, and returned her attention to Katie. “I… hope so?"

Katie frowned, "Like… you aren't sure if you're gonna move here or… what?"

Riley just shuffled around under Katie’s gaze, not answering. She looked dirty and underweight. An idea came to Katie and she gestured over her shoulder, “Come on, why don't we grab some pizza? I’m starvin'.”

Riley perked up at that, "Okay."

Katie led her new friend over to the red booths along the side of the building and sat her down along with her cup of change. “Wait here a moment," she said, and then went to the front desk to get some slices.

When she came back, Riley was fiddling with the strings on her hoodie. Katie slid into the seat across from her and set the steaming plates down.

"Here you go, hot 'n fresh!"

Riley inspected her slice before grabbing it and shoving half of it in her mouth. She spat it back out a moment later, sticking her tongue out into the cool air with a wince.

Katie snorted a laugh, “You are so weird, dude.”

A soft blush filled Riley’s face.

Ash appeared and slammed her hands down on the table, making both of them jump. “Hey, I’m out.”

“Already? You serious?”

Ash didn’t answer, instead turning her attention quickly to Riley, who looked ready to bolt out of the arcade at the sight of the intimidating girl towering over her, “Who’s this?”

“Oh, this is Riley! She’s new in town, I was just showin' her around the place.”

Ash glanced between the two. “Not lookin’ to replace me, are you, Kate?” she said it like she was joking, but a slight frown was on her face.

“No?”

“You starting at the high school here?” Ash stared at the new girl, squinting slightly.

“Uh… s-school?” Riley stammered.

“Yeah? What are you, homeschooled or somethin'?”

“No… I just…” Riley looked down at the table and squirmed in her seat.

“Hey, lay off her for a moment, Ash,” Katie glared at her friend.

“What? Just askin’ her some questions.”

Katie stood up a little in her seat. “Well, I don’t think she needs you interrogating her right now.”

“She probably doesn’t need you speaking for her either,” Ash snapped back.

“Well, she’s just—”

“I’m sorry!” Riley suddenly spoke up, “I’ll just— I’ll just leave…” She slid out of the booth, not making eye contact.

“No, Riley, don’t!” Katie stood up fast and moved to stop her, “I’m sorry, okay?” Riley held her arms close to her body, eyes darting between Katie and Ash like a cornered animal. “D'you have somewhere to stay tonight?”

“What do you mean?” Riley tilted her head a little.

“I mean, are you here with your parents?”

“Kate, what are you doin'?” Ash mumbled to herself, barely audible under the music.

Riley kicked at the colored spotted carpet, “I-I don’t…”

“You don’t… have parents?” Katie tried.

Riley was quiet for a moment, then nodded, “Yeah… sure… that.”

Ash let out a loud sigh. Katie ignored her, “D'you want to stay at my place for a bit? No offense… you smell like you need a shower.”

“Kate,” Ash barked.

“What?” Katie answered in a tired voice.

“We’re going— right now.” She grabbed Katie’s hand, but Katie just ripped it away. “Kate, this is a bad idea.”

“How? I just want to help her out.”

“I don’t… want to cause any trouble…” Riley whimpered.

“You’re not, I promise. I’m not tryin' to force you into anything, I just— You look super lost,” Katie admitted, offering her hand. After a moment, Riley slowly reached out and took it. Her skin was hot, hotter than the summer weather could explain. Katie almost pulled her hand away, but stopped herself. Riley couldn’t seem to keep eye contact, her grip was light and shaky.

Ash rubbed at her eyes. “Fine. Let’s go,” she grumbled before storming off towards the front entrance. Katie grabbed her money and followed with Riley in tow.

As they stepped out into the harsh sunlight, Riley squeezed her eyes shut and covered them with her free hand. She kept close right behind Katie, never letting go of her hand. As they walked down the hot sidewalk out of downtown and into the surrounding suburbs, the shade of the trees lining the sidewalk provided some relief from the sun's assault. Riley brought her hand back down, though she still seemed to struggle keeping her eyes open.

Soon, they made it to a small house painted a faded pale blue. The lawn was overgrown, and a rock path led up to the screen door. Ash walked right in, and Katie followed. Nobody ever locked their doors in this town. Ash made for the fridge in the kitchen off to the right and grabbed a can of Coke, cracking it open as she kept an eye on their visitor. Katie left her coins on a cabinet next to the door and led Riley down a short hallway past the stairs to a bathroom on the left.

“You can wash up here, I’ll get you some fresh clothes,” Katie explained. Riley peeked into the room before slowly heading inside. Katie gently closed the door behind her and returned to the front door to kick her shoes off. As she turned around, she jumped back with a gasp as Ash stood right behind her. “Damn it Ash, what now?”

“You tryin' to adopt her?” Ash spoke sternly.

“No, Jesus, Ash! She’s just homeless, okay? I know we don’t have anybody like that around here, and I wanted to help her out.”

“She’s probably a runaway, or a criminal, or somethin'.”

“Or maybe she was kidnapped? D'you ever think of that?” Katie pushed Ash out of the way and moved towards the stairs.

“Then we should turn her in to the cops or somethin', Kate!” Ash raised her voice. “Not invite her into your house while your mom’s at work, what a great fuckin' plan, what if she robs us or murders us?!”

Katie spun around with clenched fists, “What’s your problem?! She’s just a scared girl!”

“She freaks me out! Didn’t you see her eyes? She looks like she’s on drugs! Something’s really wrong with her, and we shouldn’t make it our problem too.”

“You know, you’re always like this! What if it were me? What if I was scared and hurt and just needed a place to stay?!”

Ash rolled her eyes, "Sure, like I'm not already taking care of you every moment of every day."

Katie’s hands shook; she was clenching her fists so tightly her nails dug into her palms, “What's that supposed to mean?! I can take care of myself just fine!”

"No you can't Kate, anytime something happens at school you come running to me. When you want something I'm always the one buying. I'm always the one taking the heat when you get in trouble. You can barely function without me! I always have to be there every fuckin' second whenever you do something stupid."

Katie struggled to come up with a rebuttal. "Y'know what? Fuck you Ash." She spun back around and stormed up the stairs.

"Kate, wait— Come on!" Ash yelled out.

Katie just went straight into her room and slammed the door. She fell onto the end of her bed, taking a few deep breaths. Just this once, Ash didn’t need to have her way.

Sitting back up and resting her elbows on her knees, she ran her fingers through her short auburn hair. She massaged her scalp and felt her heartbeat slow back down. With a final deep breath, she stood back up and slid her closet door open and grabbed some clothes off the floor that she hadn’t yet found the energy to fold. With a cautious peek outside, she inched back down the stairs, clothes in hand. Ash was nowhere to be seen, so she turned and moved down the hall to the bathroom. The water was running, but it was otherwise rather quiet.

“Everythin' alright in there?” Katie asked with a light rap of her knuckles against the door. There was a bit of a rustle inside, and a bottle hit the floor.

“Yeah?” Riley’s voice echoed quietly.

“Got some fresh clothes here when you need them, so… just let me know, okay?”

“H-hold on!” There was another clatter, and the door opened a crack. Riley’s face peeked out. “Um… how does the shower… work?”

“Just turn the nozzles? What, is it not warm enough?”

To her surprise, Riley shook her head. “No, I want it colder…”

“What? But—” Katie just sighed, “I’ll just leave these here then.” She set the clothes down just by the door. “Come find me in the kitchen when you’re done, okay? I’ll get you something to eat, sandwiches maybe. We never finished our pizza, remember?” she chuckled.

Riley just stared blankly for a moment before an awkward smile suddenly broke out across her pale skin. “Thanks… Thank you, Katie.”

Katie smiled back just as awkwardly. Riley's face was very symmetrical and slightly angular, but when she smiled her cheeks puffed up a little. Katie thought it was cute. Riley broke eye contact and slipped back inside, shutting the door a little forcefully.

Katie headed down the hall and took a peek out the front window. Ash sat on the front steps with a lit cigarette between her fingers, her can of Coke next to her. Katie appreciated that Ash never smoked in her house at least, even though Katie's mother did occasionally. Ash's blond hair shone in the sunlight like a halo surrounded her. She was so tall and lean and gorgeous, Katie felt so short and soft and a little pudgy in comparison. She sighed and tried to shove the thoughts from her mind as she walked into the kitchen.

Katie stood on her toes to grab a bag of bread off the top of the fridge. She pulled out two pairs of slices; then hesitated a moment before pulling out a third for Ash. After some peanut butter and grape jelly from the fridge, and she had three PB&J’s ready to go on paper towels. She sat down and tapped her fingers on her leg. Around five minutes later she heard a door open and Riley came around the corner trying to squeeze water out of her hair.

She was barefoot, wearing the grey Atari tee and black shorts Katie gave her. Water steamed off her skin, strange given how cold she had claimed her shower was. She peered at the round kitchen table with squinting eyes, “What’s that?”

“Pee-Bee-Jay,” Katie grinned at her. Riley looked a lot better now, her skin had a little color in it again. Her pupils were still unnaturally wide open though, her eyes looked like two tiny black holes.

“Oh, right…” Riley sat down beside her and took a hesitant bite. She closed her eyes as a subtle smile spread across her face. Katie watched her for a bit before venturing a question.

“So… don’t mean to pry if there’s uncomfortable stuff you don’t wanna get into right now, but would you wanna tell me a little more about yourself? Where you come from, for example?”

“Um… south,” she mumbled before taking another messy bite.

“Okay, how far south? Like, the Cities? Or Wisconsin? Iowa?”

Riley stared up at the ceiling as she chewed, “I uhh…” she went quiet for a moment, then swallowed, “I don’t… know…”

“How do you not know?!”

Riley squirmed in her seat, “I just— I can’t—” she sighed, “It's… hard to explain…”

Katie let out a deep sigh of her own, “Fine… I’ll leave it be.” She took a bite of her sandwich and turned away from Riley.

Something was up with this girl, but once again Katie took that unsettling feeling and crammed it back down. She wasn’t gonna deny somebody help just cause they acted a little weird and had some issues, everybody had their quirks.

To her surprise, though, Riley set her sandwich down and turned to face her, “Wait… Katie?” She rubbed at the underside of her arm with a thumb, right along her veins. Her arms shook slightly and her fingers twitched randomly.

“Yeah?” Katie tried to return eye contact; Riley kept glancing away.

“I guess… you've been real nice to me. I mean, I think I can trust you,” she sucked in a deep breath, “I ran away from home. I lied, I do have parents. Or… I did?"

"What d'you mean? What happened to them?"

"I… can't remember. I don't even know how I got here."

"How's that even— I'm sorry I'm just havin' some trouble wrapping my head around this," Katie admitted with a sigh.

"I woke up laying on some rocks in the woods a few hours ago. All I've managed to remember so far is my name and the image of an apartment in a city somewhere. I think I lived there. But the memory feels… sad. Melancholic. And… there's fear too. Something bad happened there. I think I ran away because of that, but I don't know how I ended up here. I just feel… weird. Sick." Riley scratched at the table while she explained, her fingernails cracked and broken.

"How can you just forget your entire life?" Katie wondered out loud. Riley simply shrugged. "Is there anything I can even do? I want to help you, but I don't know how."

Riley looked up into her eyes. "Why do you care so much?"

"Because you're really—" Katie stopped herself. "I mean… it's just the right thing to do."

"Your friend seems to disagree. I heard what she was saying."

Katie felt her face drop. "Oh, you caught all of that? Shit, I'm sorry. Ash is— Well, she usually looks after me. Or… tries to. I don't know why she won't do the same for you."

"Probably because I'm so wrong and freaky looking." Riley mumbled, echoing Ash's words.

"No, you're not! I mean, you were definitely a little… disheveled when you approached me, but that's not your fault. Now that you've cleaned up you're actually really pretty." That seemed to send a heated blush through Riley's face and she broke eye contact.

"You're just saying that."

"No, I mean it!" Katie said, leaning in closer. "I really… like…" Her words seemed to get tangled up in her throat as Riley glanced back up and the both of them found themselves face to face. "Um…" was all she managed to mumble out before she felt Riley's warm lips meet her own. Katie's heart seemed to skip a beat and all her muscles tensed up. Her mind raced with incoherent thoughts and she didn't know what to do with herself. A ticklish sensation filled her throat and she gagged slightly and coughed. Riley jerked her head away.

"I'm so sorry! I shouldn't have done that, I shouldn't have— I don't know what I was thinking!"

"No, you're fine! I just… wasn't expecting that." Katie felt all warm and her insides were swimming around, making her a little nauseous. Riley buried her face in her hands. Katie wasn't sure what to say to her for a moment. Riley wasn't like any girl she had ever met before. She didn't even realize there were other girls that felt the same way she did. Katie felt… guilty. Conflicted. It felt wrong but… exciting somehow. "Now I feel a little sick." She finally admitted.

"Me too…" Riley mumbled out, not looking up from her palms.

"I kinda liked it though. I've never kissed another girl before." Katie started running her fingers through her hair reflexively. Riley didn't respond. "I'm gonna… get us somethin' to drink,” Katie slid out of her seat and grabbed two cans from her super old fridge. She sat them down on the table and slid one in front of Riley. Riley finally pulled her hands away and picked it up, inspecting it.

“Uh, how do I—”

“Heh, just pull the tab at the top,” Katie chuckled.

“Right, yeah, of course that makes sense…”

Katie gave her a warm smile, Riley's confusion at simple everyday things was so adorable to her.

Riley popped the can with a crack and gulped it down, then paused and coughed a bit of the bubbling liquid back up. Katie rolled her eyes and took a small bite of her food. Riley set her drink down and did the same, smearing jelly onto the corners of her mouth. "I feel a little better." She spoke up, mouth still full of food.

"Yeah? You mentioned feeling bad."

"Yeah my head's been throbbing like… like a fever since I woke up and I've been so hungry and thirsty… but this has helped a little bit though. Oh… um… and I still feel a little bad about… what just… happened."

"It was… sudden," Katie admitted. "But… nice. If that's not wrong of me to say."

"I… guess. You've just been so kind, and I got a little caught in the moment…" Riley rubbed at the back of her neck.

Katie gave her a soft smile. "Well, I'm glad to hear getting some food in your system has helped. I wonder what could have made you just… forget everything though. Could you have… hit your head really hard? Thought that was just a movie thing."

Riley shrugged and sighed before taking another large bite of her sandwich. The front door suddenly cracked open, and Ash came in, a halo of cigarette smoke following her. Katie felt a twinge of guilt looking at her. She used to have… certain kinds of feelings towards Ash too, but she didn't think Ash felt exactly the same way back. She sighed, her mind awash with such confusing emotions and just tried to force a small smile.

“Hey, I made some sandwiches for everyone.”

Ash just glared at her, then at Riley.

“You gonna leave soon?” She spoke flatly to the dark-haired girl.

“I hope not. At least if Katie doesn’t want me to.”

“I think it would be best if you did.”

“Well, this is kinda my house, Ash. So it’s not your decision,” Katie piped up.

“No, it's your mom’s house. I wonder how she’ll feel seeing a strange, dirty homeless girl in it,” Ash growled.

“But, I’m not dirty, I just showered?” Riley mumbled.

“Look, how about you let me worry about that for once, huh, Ash?!” Katie raised her voice.

Ash gave her one final glare before storming off down the hall, grumbling to herself, “This is so fucking stupid…”

Riley turned to Katie, her eyebrows raised.

“It’ll be fine, I’ll hide you from my mom if I have to, promise,” Katie said, setting a hand on her shoulder.

Riley just wrinkled her nose, "I hate the smell of cigarettes."

"Yeah, yeah me too."

Riley finished off the last bite of her sandwich and licked her fingers and lips clean. A thought came to Katie, “Hey, come on, lemme show you my room!” Katie dropped her sandwich and hopped out of her seat to hurry towards the stairs. Riley grabbed her drink and followed.

Katie’s room was pretty tiny, her bed took up most of the space. Random knick-knacks filled her shelves, comic books, bird feathers, action figures… cool stuff Katie liked to collect. Well, she thought they were cool anyway.

“Wasn’t expecting it to be so messy,” Riley mumbled.

“Heh, yeah, I've been meaning to like organize and stuff but… yeah.” Katie rubbed the back of her head, a slight smile on her face.

Several large movie posters were hung up covering the walls. Riley peered at one in particular; Two figures were standing on some rings. One of them looked up at the other who had his arms outstretched to a beam of light coming from behind him. “Wait, that… looks familiar.” Riley moved over to it, setting her drink down on the bedside table.

“Oh, Tron? Yeah, it was pretty cool, those effects were so rad. Didn’t really understand the plot much though, but I got the poster for free from a friend at the movies.”

Riley reached out a hand and tilted her head at the image.

“I think I saw this one. With somebody, my… mom, I think.” She smiled. "Hey, I think I can remember my mom!” Her smile suddenly dropped off. “Why does that make me sad?”

“Maybe you miss her. D'you think you might want to go back home? It’s okay if you don’t, I mean…”

Riley turned back around slowly, arms crossed, “No… I left for a reason. A very good reason. I can’t remember why, but home didn’t feel like home anymore.”

“Do you regret leaving? With everything that’s happened 'n all…” Katie rubbed at her arm.

“I don’t regret meeting you.”

Katie felt a smile force its way across her face, and she suddenly couldn’t keep eye contact. Riley smiled back, looking just as flustered.

The sound of a car pulling up came from outside, and a door downstairs creaked open, then banged closed.

“Oh no,” Katie breathed and moved to look out her window, pulling the blinds open. “Oh fuck no…”

“What? What’s going on?”

“Just… stay here. I’ll be right back, I promise!” Katie rushed to leave the room.

“Wait! Katie!” Riley yelled from behind her, but she didn’t stop, storming down the stairs.
Throwing the door open, she saw Ash standing on the front steps in mid-conversation with a dark-skinned deputy with a thick mustache.

“—didn’t get a last name, no… ah shit.” She dropped a cigarette and stamped it out with her foot as she turned around. “Katie, hold on now—”

“What did you do?!” Katie shouted.

“I did the right thing, Kate. That girl was reported missing in Minneapolis a week ago. Deputy here just told me they got her picture at the station.”

“That’s not—” Katie huffed. “Ash, you don’t understand!”

Ash held out her hand like it was some kind of magic gesture that would miraculously make everything okay. “Kate, calm down and just bring her out here.”

As it happened, there was no need for that as Riley poked her head out from behind Katie. “What’s happening?” she asked. The deputy came forward, taking his hat off.

“You Riley Dunne, kid?”

“Um… maybe,” Riley mumbled out. The deputy's eyebrows raised from behind his shaded aviators.

“Huh, well, you should come to the station with me. Your father’s been lookin' for you,” he didn’t say it like she had a choice.

Something lit up behind Riley’s eyes, “Wait, my father?”

“He’s been askin’ all over about you.”

Riley seemed to shrink down even smaller.

“Kate, get your shoes. We all gotta go, come on,” Ash ordered.

Katie’s fists balled once again, but she didn’t see a way out of this. She didn’t know how to run from the cops. Much to the dismay of every bone in her body, she went back inside to grab shoes for herself and Riley. Just the way the girl shrank and shivered at the mention of her dad made Katie scared, too. She was putting some pieces together in her head, and she didn’t like the picture they were forming.

The drive to the sheriff’s station back downtown had so much tension Katie could cut it with a knife. Riley squirmed around, knees curled up into her chest as she held her legs up on the seat. She was shaking, and Katie didn’t know how she could help her. Ash just leaned against the door, face in her hand. She didn’t look at either of them the whole ride. Katie wanted to push her out of the car.

Three or four long, uncomfortable hours passed at the station. The place felt boiling and the air was stuffy. The creaking old fans meandered in circles overhead and didn’t help one bit. Katie tapped her fingers against the bench the whole time, never taking her eyes off Riley. She was sat at a desk a short distance away from Katie and Ash. Katie watched her trying to flick a long strand of hair out of her face, but it always fell right back down against her nose. The officers talked with Riley occasionally, trying to get her to say what she had been doing for the past week. They weren’t very nice about it. She could feel the condescending disgust in their voices. They did not like Riley. Riley didn’t like them. But she couldn't tell them anything they wanted to hear, so they eventually gave up. Katie thought cops were supposed to be kind and comforting to missing kids.

Then he finally arrived.

He had short black hair and unshaven stubble and a bit of a beer gut, too. He wasn’t in uniform, just wearing a worn windbreaker that half hung off his shoulders, but Katie caught a glimpse of a badge on his belt. He was a cop too, great. Something flashed across his face when he saw his daughter but it wasn’t joy, not exactly.

“Here we go,” Ash finally spoke up. “See? Now she goes home with her dad, and everything goes back to normal for us.”

“Ash, you don’t— You don’t get it. I was talking to Riley, and she—" Katie sighed. "Well, this… doesn't feel right,” Katie spoke in a hushed voice. “We can’t let him take her, we have to get her out of here somehow.”

“What the fuck for, Kate? This is it. The happy end to the story. We did what we were supposed to, let's just go back to the arcade after this, please?”

Katie just grumbled and leaned her arms against her knees. She tried thinking up some crazy scheme to get them out of there somehow, but nothing sprang to mind. This wasn’t an action movie. She couldn’t fight three grown adults. Maybe Ash could, but she didn’t seem interested. Katie didn’t get it. Ash had no love for the rule of law, so why was she so stubborn about getting Riley gone?

The father walked over to the local officers and spoke with them out of earshot. The station was pretty empty at the moment, there seemed to be only the two deputies there. One of them pointed out Katie and Ash sitting on a bench across the room, and he looked their way. Katie squirmed under his gaze. He turned his attention back to his daughter, who looked just as tense as Katie felt. He spoke a little louder with her, and Katie could catch his words better over the humming of the ceiling fans.

“You are so selfish, you know that?” His voice came out like sandpaper. Riley just scowled at him. “I know after… after your mother—” Riley tilted her head to the side at that, her frown softening.

“Wait, Mom? What happened to Mom?”

He snorted, “You know exactly what happened! God, this just so fucking typical. I try to give you everything I can, and you just spit in my face. It’s not easy for me either, you know?!”

“I’m… sorry?” Riley whimpered out.

“You ungrateful little shit. You know, I was half hoping they would never find you,” he growled out under his breath.

Katie barely caught his words, they formed a pit in her stomach. She couldn’t watch Riley leave with this man.

“We’re going home, and you are never pulling a stunt like this again, you understand?”

“No…” Riley whispered. The deputies didn’t seem to even be paying attention, they were sipping at coffee and mumbling to each other. Ash was watching, though. Her eyes were wide, and she covered her mouth with her hands.

“Riley, get up. We’re leaving now,” he ordered.

“No… no… no… no… no…” she pleaded louder, panicking. She tried to hide her face in her hands. He leaned over the desk and grabbed her wrist, twisting it away from her. She yelped in pain.

“Get up!”

“NO!” Riley screamed, and the air around his arm shimmered. In a moment a loud crack reverberated through the room, and now he was the one screaming. His skin shifted with the air, bubbling like boiling water before it ripped and crimson gushed out in every direction. The arm fell to the floor in several pieces, burning the wooden floors around it. He held his bleeding stump; his screams made Katie cover her ears.

The air shimmered for a second, a terrible ripping sound rang out, and then Riley’s father was gone. He was just a mess of flesh and bone slumping over onto the metal desk now, a red mist shifting and bubbling sickly in the air above him. Riley just stared at the gore, her eyes wide open. Then a hissing sound came from her throat as a smile broke out across her face, a wide unnatural smile forcing her mouth open into a toothy grin. Her teeth opened and the hiss turned into a shrill laugh. Laughing. She was laughing. The deputies were frozen in shock and horror for a moment before one quickly drew his sidearm. Katie squeezed her eyes shut and fell into a ball on the floor. She heard three loud bangs and more screams, and cracks, and above it all, Riley's sharp hissing laughter cutting through the air.

When it finally went quiet, she blinked her eyes open and somehow found the strength to stand on her shaking legs. Her heart was threatening to rip itself out of her chest. The sight before her almost made her vomit. One body was missing his head, his gun still gripped tightly in his lifeless hand as he lay limp against a desk. The other was split down the middle, part of him on the floor, and part of him had stained the far wall in a streak of scarlet. Shards of bone were stuck within the walls and floor all over the place, jutting out like broken teeth. All the desks surrounding the viscera had been melted too, and the wooden floors simmered, adding to the thick mist in the air. In the middle of it all stood Riley, the sharp grin still on her face. Her t-shirt was coated in steaming blood. Her head turned slowly to look at Katie. She still let out a few giggles.

Katie couldn’t move. She couldn’t understand what she was looking at. Riley’s eyes were black, blank, inhuman. This… thing wasn’t human. She felt a whimper of pure fear escape her throat. Riley cocked her head, then something came back to her eyes. Some undefinable spark of consciousness. Her eyes flicked between the various piles of steaming flesh around her. The sick smile finally fell away from her face. She looked down at her hands. They were covered in boiling blood, her skin sizzling from the heat. Her breathing picked up, her chest rising and falling quicker and quicker. She let out another giggle. Then it turned into loud hiccups. "What did I— " She whimpered out. Her hiccups turned into a heavy cry. She screamed and collapsed to the floor, clawing at her eyes with shaking fingers. “D-Dad?” she choked out. “Dad, I’m s-sorry… don’t… d-don’t leave me alone… I don’t want to be alone anymore… I want to go h-home…”

A hand fell on her shoulder and nearly made Katie jump; Ash was looking at her with wide eyes. She wanted to leave, Katie could tell. It would be the smart thing to do. Run and run and run back home. But Katie found herself moving forward, towards the sobs and the screams.

“Kate… don’t…” Ash’s whimper came from behind. But Katie didn’t listen. She stopped just in front of Riley and kneeled down slowly. Her Atari shirt wasn’t just soaked in blood, it had three little holes in it, one on the left shoulder, the upper chest, and in the gut.

“You’re hurt—you've been shot,” Katie mumbled out. She reached out without thinking.

“N-no… no don’t touch me!” Riley fell back suddenly and tried crawling away backwards from her, leaving a steaming streak of blood across the floor.

“Please… let me help you… I just wanted to help… I… I just…” Katie found that now she was crying too, the reality of the situation sinking in. Once again, she tried crawling towards Riley on all fours.

“No! I-I don’t want to hurt you too!”

“Riley, please, I—”

“JUST GET AWAY!” Riley shrieked, and a swirling heat engulfed Katie. She was flung backwards into a half-melted desk. Her head smacked against the metal, and her skin lit up with pain, all across her sides and back. Somebody started screaming.

It took her brain a moment to realize it was her own voice.

Katie's vision turned dark and blurry, but she could see Riley’s face still, peeking out from under her cowl of dark hair. Blood streamed from her eyes and nose. She seemed to be hyperventilating. “N-No K-Katie, I’m sorry I— Please get up, I didn’t— Please, I’m sorry!” she sobbed. Suddenly, she gagged, vomiting scarlet onto the floor. With one final heavy gasp, her bloodshot eyes rolled back into her skull, and she dropped to the floor, twitching for a few final moments before going still. Her skin was so white it looked almost translucent. She seemed dead, and Katie feared she was going to die next. Slowly, she was pulled away into an enveloping darkness as, mercifully, all feeling finally left her body.

Katie ran into the cool air of the arcade and let out a sigh of relief. This summer’s heatwave was starting to get too much to bear.

“Hey, you beat me for once!” Katie spun around to see Ash’s grinning face. Her expression softened as Katie started clutching her sides. “Hey, how're you doin'?”

Katie took in some deep breaths as she once again felt a sharp stabbing pain rush up her back. “I-I’m fine, don’t worry.”

“I always worry about you, Kate,” Ash mused. Katie just let out a groan at that. Ash scratched at the back of her head. "Yeah, uh… come to think of it, maybe you really shouldn't be runnin' around after just getting out of the hospital."

"I'm okay, just a little hungry maybe," That was an understatement. Katie was starving all the time. Ever since she woke up at the hospital, she felt like she had a throbbing fever, and nothing ever satisfied her hunger.

"M'kay, we could get some pizza, I guess?"

"Yeah, pizza sounds good."

Katie slid into an empty booth while Ash went to get them both some slices. Katie started absentmindedly picking at the burn scars on her arms. As Ash came back with some plates, she let out a chastising tsk.

"Kate…"

Katie moved her arm under the table. "Right… sorry." Ash set the food down and sat across from her.

"Hey, um… weird question. How much d'you remember about what happened last week?"

Katie nibbled at her steaming slice. "Hm? I don't know… not really anything. The doctor said I hit my head pretty hard."

"Yeah, said the same to me, but… I wasn't hurt nearly as much as you. I just… I don't know, some things aren't lining up in my head, what were we doin' at the station at all?"

"We walk by it every day on the way to here, so I probably just ran in trying to save people from the fire, and you ran in after me."

"I… guess… I just figured I would at least remember some of it, but that whole day is just—" She rubbed at her eyes. "Never mind."

"I would rather put all of this behind us anyway…" Katie mumbled as she started to pick at her arm again. "I just know schools gonna suck when I show up with these scars."

"Well, I think they look pretty metal," Ash grinned. "You should really stop picking at them, though." Katie huffed and took her hand away, returning to her pizza.

"I'm just dreading this school year 'cause Cynthia and her friends can be so mean…" She could picture their sneering, haughty faces and imagined ripping their heads off and cutting them to pieces. She blinked, shocked by the sudden violent thoughts. She knew she shouldn't allow these thoughts into her mind, just like her mom said. She took another bite of her pizza and tried to think of happy things. But the sauce just made her think of blood and gore and she didn't know why.

"They should be leaving you alone outta fear of me," Ash huffed, her voice interrupting Katie's thoughts.

"Yeah, I don't think that's how that works Ash," Katie smirked.

"No seriously, if anybody's giving you trouble just tell me so I can kick the shit outta them, then they'll leave you be." Ash leaned forward onto the table.

"No, Ash… you really don't—"

"Come on, I'll just scare 'em a little and they'll see it's not worth it, promise not to break any bones."

"Ash, no. I really, really don't want you getting into stupid fights for me. I don't like seeing you get hurt."

Ash took a deep breath and leaned back into her seat.

"Yeah… sure of course. You're right…" Ash tapped her fingers against the table for a moment. "Hey, Kate, y'know… you mean a lot to me too."

"Huh?"

"I just mean— ‘cause you said—" She sighed. "Forget it."

Katie finished off her slice, stuffing the last few bites into her mouth. "Mhm… Cool… Hey, are you gonna eat that?" Katie gestured to Ash's still untouched slice. She slid it across the table.

"All yours."

Katie dug in as Ash picked at the skin around her nails, staring off into the distance. Katie scarfed down the slice in half a minute and pulled a napkin out of the holder on the table to wipe her mouth. The pain had subsided but still she was hungry. She hated that. She already felt fat enough as is. She glanced back up at Ash and felt a little bad about blowing her off.

"Hey, Ash, let's go play Tron, huh? I'll help you out with the Light Cycles game."

Ash glanced back at her friend and smiled softly. "Thanks, Kate." She slowly slid out her seat and stood up.

Katie scooted out and joined her, the both of them walking off and disappearing into the crowd of kids.
