your-burning-kindness.raw_source: [[include :scp-wiki:theme:black-highlighter-theme]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:toggle-sidebar-bhl]] [[include :scp-wiki:info:start]] **Content Warning:** Gore [[include :scp-wiki:info:end]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:info-cw]] “Think you could lend me some of those?” Ash looked at the red cup filled with rattling change. Katie gripped her quarters tightly to her chest. “What happened to all yours from yesterday?" “Spent it all trying to beat my high score,” Ash said with a grin, sticking her hands in her flannel jacket pockets as they walked. “All of it?! On Tron?! It’s not even that hard!” “The games keep changing!” Ash waved her off. “Just when I get the hang of one—” A soft breeze blew her long blond hair into her face, and she swept it back over her ear. Katie sighed, “Fine, you can borrow some of mine when we get there.” “Sorry, know I usually pay for everythin', but my dad figured out I was using his card and cut me off.” “That’s what you get for stealing,” Katie huffed. “Nah, fuck him! He’s always off on his ‘business trips’, spending God knows how much, least he could do is toss some change my way from time to time,” Ash grumbled, kicking a rock down the sidewalk. “Stealing is always wrong, though, Ash. That’s what my mom says.” “Get off your high horse Kate, you don't know what you're talkin' about. //Your// mom’s always there when you need her.” Katie rubbed at her arm awkwardly, her pace slowing down. “Yeah… guess so…” Ash just snorted back. She was usually right about these things. “C'mon, race you there!” she yelled with a tap on Katie’s shoulder and took off sprinting. Katie struggled to keep up, putting a hand on the cup to keep all her money from spilling out. The sun beat down on the sleepy small town of Sitka. This summer was unusually hot; the air felt thick and stuck to their clothes. Katie wiped sweat off her forehead, squinting and struggling to see the neon sign of the arcade up ahead. She couldn’t wait to get into the air-conditioned indoors. The duo sprinted past scattered adults and dark storefronts. The town had been through a rough patch since the logging business died out, but the arcade was hanging on, fueled by all the kids out of school. Ash got there first and ducked inside. Katie followed after, and a blast of cool air hit her face. She leaned against her knees, out of breath, her eyes adjusting to the darker interior. Beeps and boops assaulted her ears, and the pop music playing loudly on the speakers didn’t help either. Ash chuckled, “You're super out of shape, Kate.” A boy shoved Katie from behind, almost sending her tumbling to the floor; she just barely kept a grip on her cup. “Hey, watch it, bitch!” he hissed at her. Ash stormed right up to the skinny boy and grabbed him by the throat, “Call her that again, and you’ll be eatin' out a plastic tube the rest of summer, got it?” dripped from her voice like venom. The kid struggled to shake his blond head, holding his hands up in defense, “Y-yeah sure, whatever man!” She tossed him back, and he stumbled off clutching his throat, “Fucking psycho…” Ash sighed. She set her hands on Katie’s shoulders, inspecting her, “You okay?” “Yeah…” “Hey, if anybody ever gives you trouble, you let me know, huh? I’ll hack ‘em up and hide the bodies,” Ash grinned. “No, don’t get in any fights for me, Ash,” Katie mumbled, rubbing at her arm. Ash let out a soft sigh, “M’kay sure, whatever you want, dude. C'mon, let’s get out of the walkway here.” Ash quickly reached her hand into Katie’s cup and grabbed a fistful of change before disappearing into the rows of cabinets and crowds of kids. Katie stood herself back up, ready to follow, before a raspy voice rang out from just behind her. “Hey, can I play with you?” She turned to see a teenage girl about her age wearing a torn, stained hoodie. Her tangled black hair fell to her shoulders. Her greyish-black eyes were sunken into her pale face, and her pupils were extremely dilated . She looked like she didn’t know what to do with her limbs, standing like a puppet with its strings cut. Katie felt a chill run up her spine looking at her. “Oh! Uh, you need to borrow some quarters, too?” Katie offered. The girl cocked her head to the side, “Um... I guess? I don't think I've ever been to one of these places before.” Katie shuffled around awkwardly. The girl’s bloodshot eyes bored into her soul, and she slouched and held her right arm close to her body. She was actually rather cute in a sort of creepy way. Katie decided to take a chance on her and took a deep breath to shove her fight-or-flight response down. “Here, lemme show you then,” she said with a forced smile. She guided the girl over to a machine; Space Invaders, and put a coin in. The game started with its 8-bit jingle. “See? You use this stick to move and press this button to fire.” The girl hesitantly stepped up to the machine and started playing. She was quite bad, but she had a smile on her face. “So… you new in town? What’s your name?” Katie asked, leaning against the machine. The girl glanced to the side, eyes flicking between Katie and the screen. “Oh right… I… I’m Riley. Just… got here, yeah.” “Well, it's nice to meet you, Riley. I’m Katie. My friend Ash should be somewhere 'round here too…” she trailed off and glanced around, but couldn’t spot her at the moment. “Anyway, you stayin' here in town long?" Riley sucked in a breath, then sighed as her character died on screen. She let go of the controls, rubbing at her arm, and returned her attention to Katie. “I... hope so?" Katie frowned, "Like... you aren't sure if you're gonna move here or... what?" Riley just shuffled around under Katie’s gaze, not answering. She looked dirty and underweight. An idea came to Katie and she gestured over her shoulder, “Come on, why don't we grab some pizza? I’m starvin'.” Riley perked up at that, "Okay." Katie led her new friend over to the red booths along the side of the building and sat her down along with her cup of change. “Wait here a moment," she said, and then went to the front desk to get some slices. When she came back, Riley was fiddling with the strings on her hoodie. Katie slid into the seat across from her and set the steaming plates down. "Here you go, hot 'n fresh!" Riley inspected her slice before grabbing it and shoving half of it in her mouth. She spat it back out a moment later, sticking her tongue out into the cool air with a wince. Katie snorted a laugh, “You are so weird, dude.” A soft blush filled Riley’s face. Ash appeared and slammed her hands down on the table, making both of them jump. “Hey, I’m out.” “Already? You serious?” Ash didn’t answer, instead turning her attention quickly to Riley, who looked ready to bolt out of the arcade at the sight of the intimidating girl towering over her, “Who’s this?” “Oh, this is Riley! She’s new in town, I was just showin' her around the place.” Ash glanced between the two. “Not lookin’ to replace me, are you, Kate?” she said it like she was joking, but a slight frown was on her face. “No?” “You starting at the high school here?” Ash stared at the new girl, squinting slightly. “Uh… s-school?” Riley stammered. “Yeah? What are you, homeschooled or somethin'?” “No… I just…” Riley looked down at the table and squirmed in her seat. “Hey, lay off her for a moment, Ash,” Katie glared at her friend. “What? Just askin’ her some questions.” Katie stood up a little in her seat. “Well, I don’t think she needs you interrogating her right now.” “She probably doesn’t need you speaking for her either,” Ash snapped back. “Well, she’s just—” “I’m sorry!” Riley suddenly spoke up, “I’ll just— I’ll just leave…” She slid out of the booth, not making eye contact. “No, Riley, don’t!” Katie stood up fast and moved to stop her, “I’m sorry, okay?” Riley held her arms close to her body, eyes darting between Katie and Ash like a cornered animal. “D'you have somewhere to stay tonight?” “What do you mean?” Riley tilted her head a little. “I mean, are you here with your parents?” “Kate, what are you doin'?” Ash mumbled to herself, barely audible under the music. Riley kicked at the colored spotted carpet, “I-I don’t…” “You don’t… have parents?” Katie tried. Riley was quiet for a moment, then nodded, “Yeah... sure... that.” Ash let out a loud sigh. Katie ignored her, “D'you want to stay at my place for a bit? No offense... you smell like you need a shower.” “Kate,” Ash barked. “What?” Katie answered in a tired voice. “We’re going— //right now//.” She grabbed Katie’s hand, but Katie just ripped it away. “Kate, this is a //bad// idea.” “How? I just want to help her out.” “I don’t… want to cause any trouble…” Riley whimpered. “You’re not, I promise. I’m not tryin' to force you into anything, I just— You look super lost,” Katie admitted, offering her hand. After a moment, Riley slowly reached out and took it. Her skin was hot, hotter than the summer weather could explain. Katie almost pulled her hand away, but stopped herself. Riley couldn’t seem to keep eye contact, her grip was light and shaky. Ash rubbed at her eyes. “//Fine.// Let’s go,” she grumbled before storming off towards the front entrance. Katie grabbed her money and followed with Riley in tow. As they stepped out into the harsh sunlight, Riley squeezed her eyes shut and covered them with her free hand. She kept close right behind Katie, never letting go of her hand. As they walked down the hot sidewalk out of downtown and into the surrounding suburbs, the shade of the trees lining the sidewalk provided some relief from the sun's assault. Riley brought her hand back down, though she still seemed to struggle keeping her eyes open. Soon, they made it to a small house painted a faded pale blue. The lawn was overgrown, and a rock path led up to the screen door. Ash walked right in, and Katie followed. Nobody ever locked their doors in this town. Ash made for the fridge in the kitchen off to the right and grabbed a can of Coke, cracking it open as she kept an eye on their visitor. Katie left her coins on a cabinet next to the door and led Riley down a short hallway past the stairs to a bathroom on the left. “You can wash up here, I’ll get you some fresh clothes,” Katie explained. Riley peeked into the room before slowly heading inside. Katie gently closed the door behind her and returned to the front door to kick her shoes off. As she turned around, she jumped back with a gasp as Ash stood right behind her. “Damn it Ash, what now?” “You tryin' to adopt her?” Ash spoke sternly. “No, Jesus, Ash! She’s just homeless, okay? I know we don’t have anybody like that around here, and I wanted to help her out.” “She’s probably a runaway, or a criminal, or somethin'.” “Or maybe she was kidnapped? D'you ever think of that?” Katie pushed Ash out of the way and moved towards the stairs. “Then we should turn her in to the cops or somethin', Kate!” Ash raised her voice. “Not invite her into your house while your mom’s at work, what a great fuckin' plan, what if she robs us or murders us?!” Katie spun around with clenched fists, “What’s your problem?! She’s just a scared girl!” “She freaks me out! Didn’t you see her eyes? She looks like she’s on drugs! Something’s really wrong with her, and we shouldn’t make it our problem too.” “You know, you’re always like this! What if it were me? What if I was scared and hurt and just needed a place to stay?!” Ash rolled her eyes, "Sure, like I'm not already taking care of you every moment of every day." Katie’s hands shook; she was clenching her fists so tightly her nails dug into her palms, “What's that supposed to mean?! I can take care of myself just fine!” "No you can't Kate, anytime something happens at school you come running to me. When you want something I'm always the one buying. I'm always the one taking the heat when you get in trouble. You can barely function without me! I always have to be there every fuckin' second whenever you do something stupid." Katie struggled to come up with a rebuttal. "Y'know what? Fuck you Ash." She spun back around and stormed up the stairs. "Kate, wait— Come on!" Ash yelled out. Katie just went straight into her room and slammed the door. She fell onto the end of her bed, taking a few deep breaths. Just this once, Ash didn’t need to have her way. Sitting back up and resting her elbows on her knees, she ran her fingers through her short auburn hair. She massaged her scalp and felt her heartbeat slow back down. With a final deep breath, she stood back up and slid her closet door open and grabbed some clothes off the floor that she hadn’t yet found the energy to fold. With a cautious peek outside, she inched back down the stairs, clothes in hand. Ash was nowhere to be seen, so she turned and moved down the hall to the bathroom. The water was running, but it was otherwise rather quiet. “Everythin' alright in there?” Katie asked with a light rap of her knuckles against the door. There was a bit of a rustle inside, and a bottle hit the floor. “Yeah?” Riley’s voice echoed quietly. “Got some fresh clothes here when you need them, so… just let me know, okay?” “H-hold on!” There was another clatter, and the door opened a crack. Riley’s face peeked out. “Um… how does the shower… work?” “Just turn the nozzles? What, is it not warm enough?” To her surprise, Riley shook her head. “No, I want it colder…” “What? But—” Katie just sighed, “I’ll just leave these here then.” She set the clothes down just by the door. “Come find me in the kitchen when you’re done, okay? I’ll get you something to eat, sandwiches maybe. We never finished our pizza, remember?” she chuckled. Riley just stared blankly for a moment before an awkward smile suddenly broke out across her pale skin. “Thanks... Thank you, Katie.” Katie smiled back just as awkwardly. Riley's face was very symmetrical and slightly angular, but when she smiled her cheeks puffed up a little. Katie thought it was cute. Riley broke eye contact and slipped back inside, shutting the door a little forcefully. Katie headed down the hall and took a peek out the front window. Ash sat on the front steps with a lit cigarette between her fingers, her can of Coke next to her. Katie appreciated that Ash never smoked in her house at least, even though Katie's mother did occasionally. Ash's blond hair shone in the sunlight like a halo surrounded her. She was so tall and lean and gorgeous, Katie felt so short and soft and a little pudgy in comparison. She sighed and tried to shove the thoughts from her mind as she walked into the kitchen. Katie stood on her toes to grab a bag of bread off the top of the fridge. She pulled out two pairs of slices; then hesitated a moment before pulling out a third for Ash. After some peanut butter and grape jelly from the fridge, and she had three PB&J’s ready to go on paper towels. She sat down and tapped her fingers on her leg. Around five minutes later she heard a door open and Riley came around the corner trying to squeeze water out of her hair. She was barefoot, wearing the grey Atari tee and black shorts Katie gave her. Water steamed off her skin, strange given how cold she had claimed her shower was. She peered at the round kitchen table with squinting eyes, “What’s that?” “Pee-Bee-Jay,” Katie grinned at her. Riley looked a lot better now, her skin had a little color in it again. Her pupils were still unnaturally wide open though, her eyes looked like two tiny black holes. “Oh, right…” Riley sat down beside her and took a hesitant bite. She closed her eyes as a subtle smile spread across her face. Katie watched her for a bit before venturing a question. “So… don’t mean to pry if there’s uncomfortable stuff you don’t wanna get into right now, but would you wanna tell me a little more about yourself? Where you come from, for example?” “Um… south,” she mumbled before taking another messy bite. “Okay, how far south? Like, the Cities? Or Wisconsin? Iowa?” Riley stared up at the ceiling as she chewed, “I uhh…” she went quiet for a moment, then swallowed, “I don’t… know…” “How do you //not know//?!” Riley squirmed in her seat, “I just— I can’t—” she sighed, “It's… hard to explain…” Katie let out a deep sigh of her own, “Fine… I’ll leave it be.” She took a bite of her sandwich and turned away from Riley. Something was up with this girl, but once again Katie took that unsettling feeling and crammed it back down. She wasn’t gonna deny somebody help just cause they acted a little weird and had some issues, everybody had their quirks. To her surprise, though, Riley set her sandwich down and turned to face her, “Wait… Katie?” She rubbed at the underside of her arm with a thumb, right along her veins. Her arms shook slightly and her fingers twitched randomly. “Yeah?” Katie tried to return eye contact; Riley kept glancing away. “I guess… you've been real nice to me. I mean, I think I can trust you,” she sucked in a deep breath, “I ran away from home. I lied, I do have parents. Or... I did?" "What d'you mean? What happened to them?" "I... can't remember. I don't even know how I got here." "How's that even— I'm sorry I'm just havin' some trouble wrapping my head around this," Katie admitted with a sigh. "I woke up laying on some rocks in the woods a few hours ago. All I've managed to remember so far is my name and the image of an apartment in a city somewhere. I think I lived there. But the memory feels... sad. Melancholic. And... there's fear too. Something bad happened there. I think I ran away because of that, but I don't know how I ended up here. I just feel... weird. Sick." Riley scratched at the table while she explained, her fingernails cracked and broken. "How can you just forget your entire life?" Katie wondered out loud. Riley simply shrugged. "Is there anything I can even do? I want to help you, but I don't know how." Riley looked up into her eyes. "Why do you care so much?" "Because you're really—" Katie stopped herself. "I mean... it's just the right thing to do." "Your friend seems to disagree. I heard what she was saying." Katie felt her face drop. "Oh, you caught all of that? Shit, I'm sorry. Ash is— Well, she usually looks after me. Or... tries to. I don't know why she won't do the same for you." "Probably because I'm so wrong and freaky looking." Riley mumbled, echoing Ash's words. "No, you're not! I mean, you were definitely a little... disheveled when you approached me, but that's not your fault. Now that you've cleaned up you're actually really pretty." That seemed to send a heated blush through Riley's face and she broke eye contact. "You're just saying that." "No, I mean it!" Katie said, leaning in closer. "I really... like..." Her words seemed to get tangled up in her throat as Riley glanced back up and the both of them found themselves face to face. "Um..." was all she managed to mumble out before she felt Riley's warm lips meet her own. Katie's heart seemed to skip a beat and all her muscles tensed up. Her mind raced with incoherent thoughts and she didn't know what to do with herself. A ticklish sensation filled her throat and she gagged slightly and coughed. Riley jerked her head away. "I'm so sorry! I shouldn't have done that, I shouldn't have— I don't know what I was thinking!" "No, you're fine! I just... wasn't expecting that." Katie felt all warm and her insides were swimming around, making her a little nauseous. Riley buried her face in her hands. Katie wasn't sure what to say to her for a moment. Riley wasn't like any girl she had ever met before. She didn't even realize there were other girls that felt the same way she did. Katie felt... guilty. Conflicted. It felt wrong but... exciting somehow. "Now I feel a little sick." She finally admitted. "Me too..." Riley mumbled out, not looking up from her palms. "I kinda liked it though. I've never kissed another girl before." Katie started running her fingers through her hair reflexively. Riley didn't respond. "I'm gonna... get us somethin' to drink,” Katie slid out of her seat and grabbed two cans from her super old fridge. She sat them down on the table and slid one in front of Riley. Riley finally pulled her hands away and picked it up, inspecting it. “Uh, how do I—” “Heh, just pull the tab at the top,” Katie chuckled. “Right, yeah, of course that makes sense…” Katie gave her a warm smile, Riley's confusion at simple everyday things was so adorable to her. Riley popped the can with a crack and gulped it down, then paused and coughed a bit of the bubbling liquid back up. Katie rolled her eyes and took a small bite of her food. Riley set her drink down and did the same, smearing jelly onto the corners of her mouth. "I feel a little better." She spoke up, mouth still full of food. "Yeah? You mentioned feeling bad." "Yeah my head's been throbbing like... like a fever since I woke up and I've been so hungry and thirsty... but this has helped a little bit though. Oh... um... and I still feel a little bad about... what just... happened." "It was... sudden," Katie admitted. "But... nice. If that's not wrong of me to say." "I... guess. You've just been so kind, and I got a little caught in the moment..." Riley rubbed at the back of her neck. Katie gave her a soft smile. "Well, I'm glad to hear getting some food in your system has helped. I wonder what could have made you just... forget everything though. Could you have... hit your head really hard? Thought that was just a movie thing." Riley shrugged and sighed before taking another large bite of her sandwich. The front door suddenly cracked open, and Ash came in, a halo of cigarette smoke following her. Katie felt a twinge of guilt looking at her. She used to have... certain kinds of feelings towards Ash too, but she didn't think Ash felt exactly the same way back. She sighed, her mind awash with such confusing emotions and just tried to force a small smile. “Hey, I made some sandwiches for everyone.” Ash just glared at her, then at Riley. “You gonna leave soon?” She spoke flatly to the dark-haired girl. “I hope not. At least if Katie doesn’t want me to.” “I think it would be best if you did.” “Well, this is kinda my house, Ash. So it’s not your decision,” Katie piped up. “No, it's your //mom’s// house. I wonder how she’ll feel seeing a strange, dirty homeless girl in it,” Ash growled. “But, I’m not dirty, I just showered?” Riley mumbled. “Look, how about you let me worry about that for once, huh, Ash?!” Katie raised her voice. Ash gave her one final glare before storming off down the hall, grumbling to herself, “This is so fucking stupid…” Riley turned to Katie, her eyebrows raised. “It’ll be fine, I’ll hide you from my mom if I have to, promise,” Katie said, setting a hand on her shoulder. Riley just wrinkled her nose, "I hate the smell of cigarettes." "Yeah, yeah me too." Riley finished off the last bite of her sandwich and licked her fingers and lips clean. A thought came to Katie, “Hey, come on, lemme show you my room!” Katie dropped her sandwich and hopped out of her seat to hurry towards the stairs. Riley grabbed her drink and followed. Katie’s room was pretty tiny, her bed took up most of the space. Random knick-knacks filled her shelves, comic books, bird feathers, action figures... cool stuff Katie liked to collect. Well, she thought they were cool anyway. “Wasn’t expecting it to be so messy,” Riley mumbled. “Heh, yeah, I've been meaning to like organize and stuff but... yeah.” Katie rubbed the back of her head, a slight smile on her face. Several large movie posters were hung up covering the walls. Riley peered at one in particular; Two figures were standing on some rings. One of them looked up at the other who had his arms outstretched to a beam of light coming from behind him. “Wait, that… looks familiar.” Riley moved over to it, setting her drink down on the bedside table. “Oh, Tron? Yeah, it was pretty cool, those effects were //so// rad. Didn’t really understand the plot much though, but I got the poster for free from a friend at the movies.” Riley reached out a hand and tilted her head at the image. “I think I saw this one. With somebody, my… mom, I think.” She smiled. "Hey, I think I can remember my mom!” Her smile suddenly dropped off. “Why does that make me sad?” “Maybe you miss her. D'you think you might want to go back home? It’s okay if you don’t, I mean…” Riley turned back around slowly, arms crossed, “No… I left for a reason. A very good reason. I can’t remember why, but home didn’t feel like home anymore.” “Do you regret leaving? With everything that’s happened 'n all…” Katie rubbed at her arm. “I don’t regret meeting you.” Katie felt a smile force its way across her face, and she suddenly couldn’t keep eye contact. Riley smiled back, looking just as flustered. The sound of a car pulling up came from outside, and a door downstairs creaked open, then banged closed. “Oh no,” Katie breathed and moved to look out her window, pulling the blinds open. “Oh fuck no…” “What? What’s going on?” “Just… stay here. I’ll be right back, I promise!” Katie rushed to leave the room. “Wait! Katie!” Riley yelled from behind her, but she didn’t stop, storming down the stairs. Throwing the door open, she saw Ash standing on the front steps in mid-conversation with a dark-skinned deputy with a thick mustache. “—didn’t get a last name, no… ah shit.” She dropped a cigarette and stamped it out with her foot as she turned around. “Katie, hold on now—” “What did you do?!” Katie shouted. “I did the right thing, Kate. That girl was reported missing in Minneapolis a week ago. Deputy here just told me they got her picture at the station.” “That’s not—” Katie huffed. “Ash, you don’t understand!” Ash held out her hand like it was some kind of magic gesture that would miraculously make everything okay. “Kate, calm down and just bring her out here.” As it happened, there was no need for that as Riley poked her head out from behind Katie. “What’s happening?” she asked. The deputy came forward, taking his hat off. “You Riley Dunne, kid?” “Um… maybe,” Riley mumbled out. The deputy's eyebrows raised from behind his shaded aviators. “Huh, well, you should come to the station with me. Your father’s been lookin' for you,” he didn’t say it like she had a choice. Something lit up behind Riley’s eyes, “Wait, my father?” “He’s been askin’ all over about you.” Riley seemed to shrink down even smaller. “Kate, get your shoes. We all gotta go, come on,” Ash ordered. Katie’s fists balled once again, but she didn’t see a way out of this. She didn’t know how to run from the cops. Much to the dismay of every bone in her body, she went back inside to grab shoes for herself and Riley. Just the way the girl shrank and shivered at the mention of her dad made Katie scared, too. She was putting some pieces together in her head, and she didn’t like the picture they were forming. The drive to the sheriff’s station back downtown had so much tension Katie could cut it with a knife. Riley squirmed around, knees curled up into her chest as she held her legs up on the seat. She was shaking, and Katie didn’t know how she could help her. Ash just leaned against the door, face in her hand. She didn’t look at either of them the whole ride. Katie wanted to push her out of the car. Three or four long, uncomfortable hours passed at the station. The place felt boiling and the air was stuffy. The creaking old fans meandered in circles overhead and didn’t help one bit. Katie tapped her fingers against the bench the whole time, never taking her eyes off Riley. She was sat at a desk a short distance away from Katie and Ash. Katie watched her trying to flick a long strand of hair out of her face, but it always fell right back down against her nose. The officers talked with Riley occasionally, trying to get her to say what she had been doing for the past week. They weren’t very nice about it. She could feel the condescending disgust in their voices. They did not like Riley. Riley didn’t like them. But she couldn't tell them anything they wanted to hear, so they eventually gave up. Katie thought cops were supposed to be kind and comforting to missing kids. Then //he// finally arrived. He had short black hair and unshaven stubble and a bit of a beer gut, too. He wasn’t in uniform, just wearing a worn windbreaker that half hung off his shoulders, but Katie caught a glimpse of a badge on his belt. He was a cop too, great. Something flashed across his face when he saw his daughter but it wasn’t joy, not exactly. “Here we go,” Ash finally spoke up. “See? Now she goes home with her dad, and everything goes back to normal for us.” “Ash, you don’t— You don’t get it. I was talking to Riley, and she—" Katie sighed. "Well, this... doesn't feel right,” Katie spoke in a hushed voice. “We can’t let him take her, we have to get her out of here somehow.” “What the fuck for, Kate? This is it. The happy end to the story. We did what we were supposed to, let's just go back to the arcade after this, please?” Katie just grumbled and leaned her arms against her knees. She tried thinking up some crazy scheme to get them out of there somehow, but nothing sprang to mind. This wasn’t an action movie. She couldn’t fight three grown adults. Maybe Ash could, but she didn’t seem interested. Katie didn’t get it. Ash had no love for the rule of law, so why was she so stubborn about getting Riley gone? The father walked over to the local officers and spoke with them out of earshot. The station was pretty empty at the moment, there seemed to be only the two deputies there. One of them pointed out Katie and Ash sitting on a bench across the room, and he looked their way. Katie squirmed under his gaze. He turned his attention back to his daughter, who looked just as tense as Katie felt. He spoke a little louder with her, and Katie could catch his words better over the humming of the ceiling fans. “You are so selfish, you know that?” His voice came out like sandpaper. Riley just scowled at him. “I know after… after your mother—” Riley tilted her head to the side at that, her frown softening. “Wait, Mom? What happened to Mom?” He snorted, “You know exactly what happened! God, this just so fucking typical. I try to give you everything I can, and you just spit in my face. It’s not easy for me either, you know?!” “I’m… sorry?” Riley whimpered out. “You ungrateful little shit. You know, I was half hoping they would never find you,” he growled out under his breath. Katie barely caught his words, they formed a pit in her stomach. She couldn’t watch Riley leave with this man. “We’re going home, and you are never pulling a stunt like this again, you understand?” “No…” Riley whispered. The deputies didn’t seem to even be paying attention, they were sipping at coffee and mumbling to each other. Ash was watching, though. Her eyes were wide, and she covered her mouth with her hands. “Riley, get up. We’re leaving now,” he ordered. “No… no... no... no... no…” she pleaded louder, panicking. She tried to hide her face in her hands. He leaned over the desk and grabbed her wrist, twisting it away from her. She yelped in pain. “Get //up//!” “NO!” Riley screamed, and the air around his arm shimmered. In a moment a loud crack reverberated through the room, and now he was the one screaming. His skin shifted with the air, bubbling like boiling water before it ripped and crimson gushed out in every direction. The arm fell to the floor in several pieces, burning the wooden floors around it. He held his bleeding stump; his screams made Katie cover her ears. The air shimmered for a second, a terrible ripping sound rang out, and then Riley’s father was gone. He was just a mess of flesh and bone slumping over onto the metal desk now, a red mist shifting and bubbling sickly in the air above him. Riley just stared at the gore, her eyes wide open. Then a hissing sound came from her throat as a smile broke out across her face, a wide unnatural smile forcing her mouth open into a toothy grin. Her teeth opened and the hiss turned into a shrill laugh. Laughing. She was //laughing//. The deputies were frozen in shock and horror for a moment before one quickly drew his sidearm. Katie squeezed her eyes shut and fell into a ball on the floor. She heard three loud bangs and more screams, and cracks, and above it all, Riley's sharp hissing laughter cutting through the air. When it finally went quiet, she blinked her eyes open and somehow found the strength to stand on her shaking legs. Her heart was threatening to rip itself out of her chest. The sight before her almost made her vomit. One body was missing his head, his gun still gripped tightly in his lifeless hand as he lay limp against a desk. The other was split down the middle, part of him on the floor, and part of him had stained the far wall in a streak of scarlet. Shards of bone were stuck within the walls and floor all over the place, jutting out like broken teeth. All the desks surrounding the viscera had been melted too, and the wooden floors simmered, adding to the thick mist in the air. In the middle of it all stood Riley, the sharp grin still on her face. Her t-shirt was coated in steaming blood. Her head turned slowly to look at Katie. She still let out a few giggles. Katie couldn’t move. She couldn’t understand what she was looking at. Riley’s eyes were black, blank, inhuman. This... //thing// wasn’t human. She felt a whimper of pure fear escape her throat. Riley cocked her head, then something came back to her eyes. Some undefinable spark of consciousness. Her eyes flicked between the various piles of steaming flesh around her. The sick smile finally fell away from her face. She looked down at her hands. They were covered in boiling blood, her skin sizzling from the heat. Her breathing picked up, her chest rising and falling quicker and quicker. She let out another giggle. Then it turned into loud hiccups. "What did I— " She whimpered out. Her hiccups turned into a heavy cry. She screamed and collapsed to the floor, clawing at her eyes with shaking fingers. “D-Dad?” she choked out. “Dad, I’m s-sorry… don’t… d-don’t leave me alone… I don’t want to be alone anymore… I want to go h-home…” A hand fell on her shoulder and nearly made Katie jump; Ash was looking at her with wide eyes. She wanted to leave, Katie could tell. It would be the smart thing to do. Run and run and run back home. But Katie found herself moving forward, towards the sobs and the screams. “Kate… don’t...” Ash’s whimper came from behind. But Katie didn’t listen. She stopped just in front of Riley and kneeled down slowly. Her Atari shirt wasn’t just soaked in blood, it had three little holes in it, one on the left shoulder, the upper chest, and in the gut. “You’re hurt—you've been shot,” Katie mumbled out. She reached out without thinking. “N-no… no don’t touch me!” Riley fell back suddenly and tried crawling away backwards from her, leaving a steaming streak of blood across the floor. “Please… let me help you… I just wanted to help… I… I just…” Katie found that now she was crying too, the reality of the situation sinking in. Once again, she tried crawling towards Riley on all fours. “No! I-I don’t want to hurt you too!” “Riley, please, I—” “JUST GET AWAY!” Riley shrieked, and a swirling heat engulfed Katie. She was flung backwards into a half-melted desk. Her head smacked against the metal, and her skin lit up with pain, all across her sides and back. Somebody started screaming. It took her brain a moment to realize it was her own voice. Katie's vision turned dark and blurry, but she could see Riley’s face still, peeking out from under her cowl of dark hair. Blood streamed from her eyes and nose. She seemed to be hyperventilating. “N-No K-Katie, I’m sorry I— Please get up, I didn’t— Please, I’m sorry!” she sobbed. Suddenly, she gagged, vomiting scarlet onto the floor. With one final heavy gasp, her bloodshot eyes rolled back into her skull, and she dropped to the floor, twitching for a few final moments before going still. Her skin was so white it looked almost translucent. [https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-8786 She seemed dead], and Katie feared she was going to die next. Slowly, she was pulled away into an enveloping darkness as, mercifully, all feeling finally left her body. ---- Katie ran into the cool air of the arcade and let out a sigh of relief. This summer’s heatwave was starting to get too much to bear. “Hey, you beat me for once!” Katie spun around to see Ash’s grinning face. Her expression softened as Katie started clutching her sides. “Hey, how're you doin'?” Katie took in some deep breaths as she once again felt a sharp stabbing pain rush up her back. “I-I’m fine, don’t worry.” “I always worry about you, Kate,” Ash mused. Katie just let out a groan at that. Ash scratched at the back of her head. "Yeah, uh... come to think of it, maybe you really shouldn't be runnin' around after just getting out of the hospital." "I'm okay, just a little hungry maybe," That was an understatement. Katie was starving all the time. Ever since she woke up at the hospital, she felt like she had a throbbing fever, and nothing ever satisfied her hunger. "M'kay, we could get some pizza, I guess?" "Yeah, pizza sounds good." Katie slid into an empty booth while Ash went to get them both some slices. Katie started absentmindedly picking at the burn scars on her arms. As Ash came back with some plates, she let out a chastising tsk. "Kate..." Katie moved her arm under the table. "Right... sorry." Ash set the food down and sat across from her. "Hey, um... weird question. How much d'you remember about what happened last week?" Katie nibbled at her steaming slice. "Hm? I don't know... not really anything. The doctor said I hit my head pretty hard." "Yeah, said the same to me, but... I wasn't hurt //nearly// as much as you. I just... I don't know, some things aren't lining up in my head, what were we doin' at the station at all?" "We walk by it every day on the way to here, so I probably just ran in trying to save people from the fire, and you ran in after me." "I... guess... I just figured I would at least remember //some// of it, but that whole day is just—" She rubbed at her eyes. "Never mind." "I would rather put all of this behind us anyway..." Katie mumbled as she started to pick at her arm again. "I just know schools gonna suck when I show up with these scars." "Well, I think they look pretty metal," Ash grinned. "You should really stop picking at them, though." Katie huffed and took her hand away, returning to her pizza. "I'm just dreading this school year 'cause Cynthia and her friends can be so mean..." She could picture their sneering, haughty faces and imagined ripping their heads off and cutting them to pieces. She blinked, shocked by the sudden violent thoughts. She knew she shouldn't allow these thoughts into her mind, just like her mom said. She took another bite of her pizza and tried to think of happy things. But the sauce just made her think of blood and gore and she didn't know why. "They should be leaving you alone outta fear of me," Ash huffed, her voice interrupting Katie's thoughts. "Yeah, I don't think that's how that works Ash," Katie smirked. "No seriously, if anybody's giving you trouble just tell me so I can kick the shit outta them, then they'll leave you be." Ash leaned forward onto the table. "No, Ash... you really don't—" "Come on, I'll just scare 'em a little and they'll see it's not worth it, promise not to break any bones." "Ash, //no//. I really, //really// don't want you getting into stupid fights for me. I don't like seeing you get hurt." Ash took a deep breath and leaned back into her seat. "Yeah... sure of course. You're right..." Ash tapped her fingers against the table for a moment. "Hey, Kate, y'know... you mean a lot to me too." "Huh?" "I just mean— ‘cause you said—" She sighed. "Forget it." Katie finished off her slice, stuffing the last few bites into her mouth. "Mhm... Cool... Hey, are you gonna eat that?" Katie gestured to Ash's still untouched slice. She slid it across the table. "All yours." Katie dug in as Ash picked at the skin around her nails, staring off into the distance. Katie scarfed down the slice in half a minute and pulled a napkin out of the holder on the table to wipe her mouth. The pain had subsided but still she was hungry. She hated that. She already felt fat enough as is. She glanced back up at Ash and felt a little bad about blowing her off. "Hey, Ash, let's go play Tron, huh? I'll help you out with the Light Cycles game." Ash glanced back at her friend and smiled softly. "Thanks, Kate." She slowly slid out her seat and stood up. Katie scooted out and joined her, the both of them walking off and disappearing into the crowd of kids. [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box-end]]

your-glow-lights-my-way.raw_content:
stay there, i'll catch up
i like to imagine the things we'll discuss
don't wait for me, you'll grow bored
you'll see me in a bit

the noise

i can pull myself from the static more and more
i can think of me and see myself clearly in my minds eye
i can feel shape
are you excited?

the noise

i'll be there soon, i just need to catch my breath
i ache but i move
are you that feeling up my spine?
i can't get you off of my mind either

the noise

can you hear me now?
it hurts to speak
but you'll see me soon
your glow lights my way



the silence

your-memory-will-carry-on.raw_content:
I love you, Dad. And I will always love you.

by MasterTman2

Dr. Maslov T. Manferd was awoken by a phone call. What he was doing earlier in the day was unimportant, and what he was going to do later in the day was equally unimportant.

He rolled over and picked up the phone. "Maslov," his mother began. "You need to call out of work tonight."

"Huh? Why?" he asked in his groggy state.

"Something happened to your father." She sounded as though she was sobbing.

"What?" Maslov sat up in his bed. He was no longer tired. "What happened? Is he okay?"

"Your aunt is coming to pick you up." She hung up the phone.

Maslov sat for a few moments, trying to comprehend what just happened, before he got out of bed and raced to put his shoes on.

His aunt arrived at his house some time later.

When he got in the car, he realized that the car had none of his immediate family. He asked what was going on.

"Something happened to your father," his aunt replied. "We needed to come pick you up."

Maslov took a moment to process that. "To go where?"

"The hospital."

He didn't pry further.

On the way, his aunt stopped by her house. While there, she picked up two additional family members and they all crammed themselves into her car.

He glanced at her phone which had the GPS turned on. It read 60 minutes until they reached the hospital. If he was that far away, he must have gotten injured while he was driving his semi truck for work.

Nobody would tell him what exactly happened. Maslov was getting more worried by the second.

Midway through the car ride, his uncle got a phone call.

The man on the phone asked a few questions. His uncle gave a few answers.

"Make it quick," his uncle added without thinking. "I just lost my—"

His aunt quickly shushed his uncle.

Maslov heard what he said, however. He stared at his uncle for a few moments as tears welled in his eyes.

He didn't want to believe it, but there's only so many things that that phrase can mean.

They arrived at the hospital. Another one of his uncles took him away from the group. Him and a doctor explained what happened.

Once he was ready, his uncle brought him to the family waiting room, and they all went to go see Maslov's father.

His mother was already there. She was lying on his chest. He was unmoving.

Maslov sat for a few moments in a chair next to his father. He sat in silence for a bit to process what had happened. After some time, he began to cry.

He cried harder than he ever cried before.

Maslov sat in his office. Maslov normally sat in silence in his office quite often, but this was a different kind of silence.

He was thinking about what had happened. He wasn't trying to think too hard about what happened, because if he thought too hard about it he would start crying again.

He read over some text conversations he had had with his friends about it. It was comforting to talk about it, but at the same time he didn't want to annoy them by talking about it too much.

Maslov was snapped out of his trance by a knock on his office door.

"Hey." Cheg Hill was standing in the door.

Maslov smiled. "How'd you get in here?"

Cheg pulled up a chair and sat next to Maslov. "I have my ways. Apparently, I've been around you enough that they either don't care or just don't know that I'm Hand."

"Just don't steal anything on your way out and you should be fine," Maslov chuckled before falling into silence, staring at the ground.

"I just— I miss him."

"I know." Cheg pulled Maslov into a hug. "Try to remember all the good times you had with him."

"I just wish I could speak with him again. I miss his— " Maslov sat up. "Wait. Wait wait wait. The— the Bone Batallion. I just— I just need to change what they write on his tombstone. I've seen their recruitment ads.

"Maslov." Cheg tries to get his attention.

"Nono, wait. Then he'd be a skeleton. Okay, I just have to wait until I shift again. I can spend a year with him wherever I end up, the Right Phase or the Third Empire or something, hell I'd take that universe where humans are livestock. I'll be fine with being a dog-person if I got to see him again."

"Maslov. You know he won't be there. That's not how your powers work."

Maslov paused. "Yeah, you're right," He sighed before quickly looking up again. "Wait, I've heard about some portals, they sent people to other dimensions, right? I just— I just need to go to a universe that has him. I can deal with getting used to shifting into that universe's local universe cluster. I'll be able to be with him again."

"What about the Maslov that's already there? What are you going to do with him? Replace him? Your dad there will notice that you're different."

"But— but I— I—"

Cheg reached over to Maslov and engulfed him in a hug. Maslov began sobbing.

"I know, I know. Let it out. It's gonna be okay."

"I just— " Maslov said between sobs. "I need him back."

"I know you do. But unfortunately, that's not a feasible option. But you will work through this. You will persevere.

"You will be okay."

And I will always love you. ]] ===== [[>]] [[module Rate]] [[/>]] [[div style="text-align: right; margin-right: 2em; margin-top: -20px;"]] by [[[mastertman2-s-menagerie| MasterTman2]]] [[/div]] [[[scp-8086|Dr. Maslov T. Manferd]]] was awoken by a phone call. What he was doing earlier in the day was unimportant, and what he was going to do later in the day was equally unimportant. He rolled over and picked up the phone. "Maslov," his mother began. "You need to call out of work tonight." "Huh? Why?" he asked in his groggy state. "Something happened to your father." She sounded as though she was sobbing. "What?" Maslov sat up in his bed. He was no longer tired. "What happened? Is he okay?" "Your aunt is coming to pick you up." She hung up the phone. Maslov sat for a few moments, trying to comprehend what just happened, before he got out of bed and raced to put his shoes on. ----- His aunt arrived at his house some time later. When he got in the car, he realized that the car had none of his immediate family. He asked what was going on. "Something happened to your father," his aunt replied. "We needed to come pick you up." Maslov took a moment to process that. "To go where?" "The hospital." He didn't pry further. ----- On the way, his aunt stopped by her house. While there, she picked up two additional family members and they all crammed themselves into her car. He glanced at her phone which had the GPS turned on. It read 60 minutes until they reached the hospital. If he was that far away, he must have gotten injured while he was driving his semi truck for work. Nobody would tell him what exactly happened. Maslov was getting more worried by the second. ----- Midway through the car ride, his uncle got a phone call. The man on the phone asked a few questions. His uncle gave a few answers. "Make it quick," his uncle added without thinking. "I just lost my--" His aunt quickly shushed his uncle. Maslov heard what he said, however. He stared at his uncle for a few moments as tears welled in his eyes. He didn't want to believe it, but there's only so many things that that phrase can mean. ---- They arrived at the hospital. Another one of his uncles took him away from the group. Him and a doctor explained what happened. Once he was ready, his uncle brought him to the family waiting room, and they all went to go see Maslov's father. His mother was already there. She was lying on his chest. He was unmoving. Maslov sat for a few moments in a chair next to his father. He sat in silence for a bit to process what had happened. After some time, he began to cry. He cried harder than he ever cried before. ----- Maslov sat in his office. Maslov normally sat in silence in his office quite often, but this was a different kind of silence. He was thinking about what had happened. He wasn't trying to think too hard about what happened, because if he thought too hard about it he would start crying again. He read over some text conversations he had had with his friends about it. It was comforting to talk about it, but at the same time he didn't want to annoy them by talking about it too much. Maslov was snapped out of his trance by a knock on his office door. "Hey." [[[the-standstill|Cheg Hill]]] was standing in the door. Maslov smiled. "How'd you get in here?" Cheg pulled up a chair and sat next to Maslov. "I have my ways. Apparently, I've been around you enough that they either don't care or just don't know that I'm Hand." "Just don't steal anything on your way out and you should be fine," Maslov chuckled before falling into silence, staring at the ground. "I just-- I miss him." "I know." Cheg pulled Maslov into a hug. "Try to remember all the good times you had with him." "I just wish I could speak with him again. I miss his-- " Maslov sat up. "Wait. Wait wait wait. The-- the [[[scp-5572|Bone Batallion]]]. I just-- I just need to change what they write on his tombstone. I've seen their [[[the-first-occult-flame-war|recruitment ads]]]. "Maslov." Cheg tries to get his attention. "Nono, wait. Then he'd be a skeleton. Okay, I just have to wait until I shift again. I can spend a year with him wherever I end up, the [[[scp-cn-1997|Right Phase]]] or the [[[scp-1483|Third Empire]]] or something, hell I'd take that universe where [[[http://scp-int.wikidot.com/scp-280-fr|humans are livestock]]]. I'll be fine with being a dog-person if I got to see him again." "Maslov. You know he won't be there. That's not how your powers work." Maslov paused. "Yeah, you're right," He sighed before quickly looking up again. "Wait, I've heard about some portals, they sent people to other dimensions, right? I just-- I just need to go to a universe that has him. I can deal with getting used to shifting into that universe's local universe cluster. I'll be able to be with him again." "What about the Maslov that's already there? What are you going to do with him? Replace him? Your dad there will notice that you're different." "But-- but I-- I--" Cheg reached over to Maslov and engulfed him in a hug. Maslov began sobbing. "I know, I know. Let it out. It's gonna be okay." "I just-- " Maslov said between sobs. "I //need// him back." "I know you do. But unfortunately, that's not a feasible option. But you will work through this. You will persevere. "You will be okay." PoufyPoufson

Yours Truly, The 1st Annual Unbirthday Ball - by PoufyPoufson

More by this author

The Well, Well,

"WELL, IT'S A HOLE AFTER ALL,"

"It's just, well, I remembered it being more… grandiose? When did we build a factory around it? Taxes, please? Do you remember?"

"I do recall it being around the time we tried to reissue Mr. Brass…" Taxes scoffed, "What a waste that was!"

"I shouldn't have listened to the Brothers… they ruined my vision," the Hatter shuddered, "I mean really, who plays with a toy that teaches arithmetic, that teaches subtraction and addition…"

"THE COPPER WAS JUST TOO EXPENSIVE…"

The Hatter looked at DEATH and furrowed his brow.

"I don't terribly want to think of margins right now," the Hatter hopped twice, "Not now or forever."

The three figures stood in a factory of brick, a castle of cogs and a portal of pearl: a well, a torn seam, a gate to a dream… the world from which Dr. Wondertainment first unfurled. It had been many years ago when he laid down his hat, he hadn't returned since his wallet grew fat.

"IS THIS REALLY WHAT YOU WANT?" said DEATH gazing off.

"I cannot stay here a moment longer. I cannot stomach anymore meetings and conferences and focus groups and lines going up, up, up. I'm sorry Taxes, you must understand." the Hatter tilted his head down to offer condolences.

"I understand." said Taxes.

"SO TIME WILL NOT COME?"

The Hatter's face soured.

"Time is the illness! Time is ill! It's Time, always Time, he is the robber elite, the thief, thief, thief! I have to be rid of him, I have to stay still, forever. I am so tired of moving. Do you understand?"

"WE ARE ALWAYS MOVING."

"Of course I am always moving! I do a little jig, I hold hands merrily, merrily, I fall down, yes I move, I move, but Time! Time moves too quickly, dances too fast, not a good party mate! Not at all!"

"So, home is better?" Taxes asked.

"Everything was better back then," the Hatter assured.

"NOW IS NOT THE SAME AS BACK THEN." replied DEATH.

"It will be the same. It will be safe. It will be fun. It has to be."

The three stepped towards the sightless pit ahead. Centrally located within the room, it whispered impolitely to the group: COME TO ME, FEED ME NOW, COME TO ME, FEED ME NOW.

"THERE IS NEVER A RETURNING."

"Why would I want to return to all of this? To fluorescent lights and spreadsheets?" the Hatter scoffed, stepping forward.

DEATH followed in step, floating forward.

"REMEMBER WHAT YOU WANTED WHEN YOU GAVE ME THE HAT."

The Hatter falls forward, down into the dark. DEATH follows kindly, as does Taxes.

The dark flurries around, with frightening speed, images of stuffed bears, folded paper planes, men in shackles and men in paint, of impossible candies and cavernous brains. Twisted and thorny vines crawled the walls of the pit, they reached out with teas and candies and toys, numerous small things, useless things, to peddle and whet.

These animate plants were keen to sell, to convince the Hatter all they need is right there, with papers and buttons and widgets and bells, everything he owned should be theirs, and theirs only. These are the vines he so longed to escape from, a final temptation as he falls down and down. Leave it all behind, he thinks, I will be free

Cards of hearts and spades and diamonds flutter past. A child's dress and a studded hat. A fluttering newspaper hovers in front of the three.

"The Queen is dead…" Taxes reads from the headline.

"The Queen is dead?" asks the Hatter.

"THE QUEEN IS DEAD." affirms DEATH.

The Hatter gulps as he falls and falls.

"Am I to believe that there's no set of laws?"

"NO SET OF LAWS?"

"No set of laws." Taxes mourns.

"IS THIS SO?"

"I think so." the Hatter said, "Can't be worse than being Incorporate!"

"I HOPE YOU ARE RIGHT, HATLESS HATTER. LET YOUR FUN BEGIN."

DEATH, Taxes, and the Hatter land suddenly in a pile of leaves and petals and mud with a heavy thud. The Hatter looks around, and sees great rigs and towers of splintered steel, each of them with a worn out sign: "PROPERTY OF WONDER BROS INC." These were the machinations of his former company, the fingers that stretched deep into the the glistening loam of Wonderland and scraped up chunks of congealed Dilly-Dally Oil.

"The rigs are still running?" Taxes asked.

"Yes, yes the Brothers remain intent on sucking the joy out like fat mosquitoes… I hate mosquitoes, they always spoil the tea… terrible company. Terrible company…" the Hatter shook off some dust from his coat. "I could do something so much better with all those gears and steel and- Bah! No, no, I have to stay on topic, yes… I need a smoke, probably… where are the alliums? Puff, Puff?"

"THEY EXPERIENCED POPULATION DECLINE DUE TO INDUSTRIAL ACTIVITY…"

"Tch." the Hatter kicked a pebble. "Do you think I'd mooch some oil off one of those?"

"Why not just dig some of your own out?" Taxes offered. "It's much more economical!"

"IT IS DRY HERE."

The brush surrounding the clearing where the three landed was wiry and dusty, tufts of purple, dead grasses and sticks and shoots. A well-trodden path lay ahead, seeming to venture into the taller fields of gregarious grasses, further towards the hills where the rigs shot out of the ground like indignant teenagers. DEATH seemed to be staring at the sky while Taxes and the Hatter deign go further into the grasses.

"Come on, friend! It's not a smoke without DEATH around the corner! Aren't you coming?" Taxes plead.

"No, no, surely he's thinking about abandoning me, just like Time did, and Mr. Burgundy… well, he'd be in bad company." The Hatter chucked a pebble at DEATH in protest.

"I'M NOT ABANDONING YOU, YOU COD! DEATH NEVER LEAVES." The pebble missed DEATH narrowly.

"So you're coming to smoke, then?" the Hatter asked.

"NO. I WILL CATCH UP LATER."



The Royal Roach

The grasses were dull, having suffered the drought of oil in the area, but still, they lived up to their name. The Hatter frolicked along the path through the grasses, eavesdropping on the conversations that flowed from the flowers of the gregarious grasses:

"I think I heard someone fall from the sky?" one of them chattered, hushed and suspicious.

"Is it more of the suited men? I don't like them, they're loud and they put up those ugly gray ladders!" another replied.

"Will you two grow a grain? Nobody fell from the sky, that does't happen anymore…" A grumpier grass protested.

"Some things never change!" The Hatter mused.

"Some things never change…" Taxes glumly echoed.

Though their purple and blue had faded, once candy-pink and teal, their propensity for gossip was still very much real. The Hatter, however, had a one track mind. Eavesdropping was fine enough, he needed to find something to puff. And despite his fixation, he noticed a vine reach out to try and trip him-

"Hey, mister, I don't recognize you? Are you the man they say fell from the sky, the great blue?" One of the grasses yawned. It grabbed the Hatter gently, intent on an answer.

"Has it been so long, so terribly long? I'm the Tea Party Hatter, I'm sure you must know of me!"

"No, that can't be right, you haven't got a hat. And nobody drinks tea anymore, that's for geezers!" the Grass teased.

"I haven't got a hat anymore, but it's me in the flesh-"

"Shouldn't we be finding some oil to smoke?" Taxes interrupted.

"Right, right, yes. I am terribly peckish, say, gumptious grass, do you know where I can find something inhalable, a hookah, some oil, something to smoke, kindly?" The Hatter asked, fidgeting against the vines wrapped around him.

"Something to smoke? I don't smoke-" The grass deadpanned. It unwound a wind to point up above, "-But they do."

It was pointing to one of the rigs nearest to the field. Within walking distance, to boot.

"Mads, they said the-"

"I heard, I heard. I don't want to go near those things, they're ugly, they're boring and they-"

"They have oil…" Taxes reminded.

"Fine," The Hatter waved his hands about. "We climb the rig. But I don't want to be caught by the suits! We better not be! Thank you, Señor Grassio, we will be off to smoke. I would invite you, but you're a bit, err- flammable?"

"Fine, fine! Leave! I never needed you anyways! I'm not into people-definitely-did-not-fall-from-the-sky anyways!" The grass pouted, and let go of the Hatter.

They clanked up the steps, wary of any signs of workers or surveillance, but this rig seemed to almost have been abandoned. It was dusty and draped in disrepair- very little signs of present activity, and it certainly wasn't actively drilling. It was a few minutes of spiraling up the scaffolding before they reached the top of the rig, a large set of platforms wrapped around the extractor, the terminus for the pipes that permeated the wondrous soil below.

Taxes immediately rummaged around the spare barrels and tins designed to store the oil, but the Hatter simply rested against the rusted rails and looked out at the stretched of wooded expanse ahead of the rig. Clusters of colossal flowers and mushrooms dwarfed by the towering rigs, distant fields of dull gray death from where his fingers had touched, and further off, no doubt, his old stomping yard.

"Here we are, then! I found a tin, filled with oil. Have you got a pipe already?" Taxes asked, producing a crumpled metal tin, tarnished and browned.

The Hatter pulled out a plain glass pipe and lighter. He absent-mindedly handed the pipe to Taxes, who filled it with the pearlescent fluid. It took a few attempts to get it to catch, but eventually it did start smoking, producing dark purple fumes with dazzling glimmers of light speckled throughout.

"Why did I have to leave this place?" The Hatter coughed, sputtering out smoke.

"No clue. But it looks like things have happened in your absence."

"What do you mean?"

Taxes turned the Hatter to the other direction, pointing off in the distance where a faint city lay. The Hatter squinted, forcing his eyes to comb the horizon: A castle town, crumbled and abandoned, but most importantly, stamped with regal emblems that had ruled over his world so long ago.

"The queen is dead…" The Hatter mumbled to himself.

"I believe so, yes!" Taxes replied, blowing circles.

"I could be King…" Hatter muses, playing with a gear that had flung from a clock. "Kings get the best croquet mallets."

"You could be King!" Taxes agreed.

There is much to be done.


The Proper Politics

The Cupmaster is not typically a nervous man. Sixty years of service, sixty years of furnishing and stylizing all manner of nobility, of barons and dukes and even princes of hearts, and yet this, this was a time to sweat. The Cupmaster had never heard of the Hatter before the coup. Who wears hats anymore, anyways? In the aptly aforementioned sixty years, the Cupmaster had never done a hat.

Though, he hadn't done many cups, either.

Interpreting the purchase orders written by the Hatter and his council had proven to be a conundrum. At one point, he had been tasked with turning the luminous chandelier into a fully edible cake, perhaps to be dropped on the guests to celebrate the crowning. However, the Cupmaster managed to convince him of this impossibility, the ceilings had been lifted from 40 meters to infinity, and the Cupmaster was not very good at climbing.

Still, he had laid out a regal cloth upon the central banquet table, and ordered the finest of leaded glass instruments and utensils for eating. The drapes, he felt, we meant to match the cloths upon the table, for everything to be this harmonious tasteful, and subtly lavish production. It had to be made worth the attendees' time, what with the ordeal of navigating all of the labyrinthian halls installed at the whim of the would-be-king. The bears were constantly shuffling about, adding embroideries and buttons wherever a naked surface was found.

The Cupmaster was not fond of the bears. They were constantly frollicking and mucking about, the ones who laid the tile and grout, who toiled endlessly at construction projects, whose origins the Cupmaster did not know much about. They walked and danced and drew like children, with bodies of cloth and eyes of coal. But they labored away dutifully, efficiently, and loyally to the Hatter-King's goal. The Cupmaster himself was not nearly as certain. From generations of servants upon servants upon servants, he knew a cummerbund from lapel, a bergamot from mandarin, but he did not much care for the pastimes of infants.

Best bite his tongue-

"No, No, No- Lilac! Lilac, lilac, lilac!" the Hatter huffed. "What is wrong with you? Does this look like lilac? I want it lilac, not purple! My friends- Hate! Purple… but they like lilac, and I need lilac. No, happy, happy, happy- I'll do it myself!"

He shook his frock coat as if trying to rid it of something before producing a blade from one of his seemingly endless pockets. Gently folding the table cloth up and off of the table in front, he laid his hand on the table.

"I can assure you, your grace, we can find-" the Cupmaster panicked.

"Quiet! I am counting! Mathing! Shhh-" the Hatter mumbled to himself: "One, Two, Three, and-!"

In quick, quiet fury, the blade falls, briskly severing one, two, three fingers from the Hatter's right hand. A brief wince and sharp inhale is all he produces before the fingers are plucked and plopped into his mouth agape. The Cupmaster shrieked, fraught with horror and confusion.

"Not as good," the Hatter says between chews, "As ladyfingers-"

He spits out the chewed mass he had collected against his cheek onto the floor. Once flesh, now a sticky clump of sparkles.

"Chop-chop! Our friends will be here any day now!" He says, before kicking the clump down the hall a bit. The Hatter curtsies and looks expectantly at the clump on the ground- "Aha!"

It twitches and grows, and somewhat glows- creases become valleys and valleys become curves, and as it increases in size, it contorts until a silhouette springs forth, garnished neatly- with two little eyes. From the speck of sticky Wondergunk, comes another one- complete with an elegant frock and hat, much like the Hatter's own.

"Dr. Styletainment- No, we'll work on the name later… you must work quickly, dress the hall, please, please, and!" the Hatter looks at the Cupmaster with boredom, "Get this thing something to wear."

"What's wrong with my suit?" the Cupmaster frowns.

"It's dated." The Hatter and his new yes-man say in unison.

"New, new, new, everything must be new! Shiny, buttons! Joy, Joy, Joy! Out with the old, out with the hearts and clubs and spades and diamonds- well, I'm okay with diamonds. But everything else, new, better, funner! Do you understand?" The Hatter points at the tablecloth. "This must go."

"It's too dark for the room, reminds me of elephant tongue. That's not what you want, is it?" the yes-man asks.

"Yes, yes, exactly! It's too, elephant-y! That's exactly it. You understand it! Flawless! Great work! Take care of that while I go do very important things!" the Hatter scatters off, up the stairs, suspended in a flurry of scurrying builder bears, each carrying out the various agendas set by the yes-court, the whims of the soon to be king. The tallest order of all, fixing the dullness, the drabness, the not-at-all-wondrousness, that had to be carried out before the crowning.

The Hatter cared not for the architecture of buildings, and so the avatars severed from his being were tasked with draping the halls and corridors and buttresses with towering mountains of cloth, fabric, plaid, with gears that turned large clocks and springs, with rooms that popped like jacks in boxes, with a crown at the top of this citadel designed to mirror that which would soon rest on the head of the Hatter, one that waived away Wondertainment, and instead, promised nothing but autocratic wonder.

"Oh good, you're back!" said a man much like him, save dressed and colored flat. "There are matters to discuss," said Bureautainment, anointed Wondercrat. The Hatter, the King, waves his hands:

"It is slow, it is slow, it is far too slow. Who is leading the bears? Look at my fingers! I said lilac, and he brought me purple. Not even tyrian purple! It's too atomic, too atomic. All of the friends, all of the friends-"

"Well, I wanted to convene, there are matters at hand," Bureautainment decried. If the Hatter must reign, so too must the king meddle in matters of land. "What of the brothers?"

"Let them eat cake! But the macarons are for VIPs, only. Very Imaginative People! That they are not," The Hatter yawned. "What a boring idea."

"Do we send an invitation?" the Wondercrat asked, troubled trenches forming on his face.

"No," said the Hatter, "It'd be a waste!"

"Well, then, I guess we should make do." the yes-man resigned. "The builder-bears have made steady progress on the changes to the castle, which should be done in time for the coronation-"

"Unbirthday Ball." The Hatter corrected.

"Unbirthday Ball, right, yes. My apologies."

"You are humbly forgiven. Please hurry, though. I need to rest. It's such hard work today!"

"Well, there are some troubles, the head helper of the builders asked, is it so necessary to have the clock tower built of clocks? His brigade talks of bricks, since clocks have less stock… The tower that rests on a jack in a box, well, that was no task, but the builder bear barracks grow weary of clocks."

"It's non-negotiable, I fear. They will have to make do. Clocks clog time…" The Hatter frowns. "Everything will be perfect, everything will work perfectly. This is perfect."

"Of course, my liege." The Yes Man recuses himself.

The Hatter paces in figures of eight.

"WHAT'S THE FUSS? AREN'T YOU HAVING FUN?" DEATH looms over his shoulder.

"They're all a bunch of idiots. I-D-I-O-T-S! Capital S! What did they all do without me, without their King! The sanest of them all, me, yes, me. Why don't they get it?"

"YOU'RE NOT QUITE THE MAN WHO SAT IN THE SAND…"

"No, not quite, but I will be, soon. Soon." The Hatter sighed. "Tell me, dearly departed, what color must a banquet hall be draped?"

"SUBURBAN BEIGE."

"Lilac, of course- No! Beige? Are you some sort of calvinist now, then?" The Hatter scoffed, pacing in circles.

"TIME ASKS OF YOU."

"Time-" The Hatter squints, "Is on holiday. What matter of it to me? The King!"

"SHOULD I TELL TIME YOU'RE HAVING FUN WITHOUT HIM, THEN?"

"I suppose. But do not invite him to the ball. He will spoil the madeleines."

DEATH leaves, floating through the window and off the sill, having suffered the gloating past his fill- the Hatter waves goodbye, pacing again in his room. That DEATH still hung around, even now in this world, that Time still asked for him, it loomed in his mind. Through feverish whimsy, the thoughts linger, forming…

"What of my subjects?" The Hatter mutters. He wanders again where DEATH did us part, surveying the land unfurled from his fort: the pastures, the parishes, the mercantile carriages- the land of which his finances had greedily disparaged. What of the people who knew not of toys, the labor that supplied him with oil? Should we all not be partiers?

Time is not here now. Time does not reach here.

He laughs.

"Let there not be a single article of boredom, here in Wonderland, from this day on! Taxes can rot! Time can rot!"

Once was a queen, once was a king, now only lies the ruler- the King of all the Tarts. And everyone loves tarts.


The Coronation

It had been a splendidly lurid affair, with attendees from all corners of Wonderland in attendance. The Blue Catterfly had even traveled to the ball, despite his advanced age and infirm, and was happily huffing away at the all-you-can-smoke Dilly Dally & Hashish bar, stocked with the finest inebriating agents from the flipside- exotic earthly substances that could kill the sludgiest of Wonderlandian hookah den denigrates.

The decorations, rightfully amended to suit the fine tastes of the soon-to-be King, were the embodiment of peace and joy- especially the balloons, provided in-kind by all those found guilty of First Degree Sternness in the recent weeks, sentenced to gleeful inflation! The idea had been suggested by Taxes as a more budget-friendly alternative to importing Swiss Clouds from the skies of Basel. The Hatter protested at first, but eventually turned around on the basis of combining opposition suppression with decoration- he quite liked the look of the balloons.

Monsieur Jacquisine Smythingfarfarawelli had been hired as caterer, providing the most exquisite pastries and desserts. There was to be- per order of the King- only sweets and desserts, with the exception of pea and lamb aspic, an old favorite of DEATH's. There had been sword-swallowers, fire-eaters, and the builder-bears had graciously provided many sets of jacks-in-boxes and cloth-mime bussers, complete with human leather (source unsourced!)

"You know, I knew him before he was famous," Taxes said to the Haberdasher and his wife.

"Really? What was he like? I must confess I hadn't heard of him before he announced he was taking the throne!" The wife replied. She was dressed in a beautiful satin gown, studded with star-shaped sequins and tailored to effortlessly accommodate her visage above the bust- the neck and head of a yellowtail snapper.

"Well, you see, he has always been industrious and social, yes, a hedon indeed!" Taxes gloated.

"It will be good for business. The textiles here are immaculate!" The Haberdasher marveled, taking a swig of the Braggadocious Brandy he had been rather keen of the entire party.

"Immaculate!" His wife parroted.

"Immaculate," Taxes embellished, "And very luxurious. It was not cheap setting up this ball, not cheap at all, but I helped put it all together, yes!"

"Very impressive." The Haberdasher agreed, as did his wife.

Taxes had been running around entertaining all of the guests and visitors. Though there was a vast array of knick-knacks and treats and pleasantries, he still felt it prudent to fraternize with all of the future citizenry. However, the main event, the coronation proceedings, were due to begin any moment now, and he was hesitant to delve terribly deep into any one conversation, lest he miss the start of the ceremony. This was, of course, his trusted responsibility, as one of the Hatter's longest and most trusted friends- a seat in the Yes Court was not nearly as fitting, nor a coveted ministership- yes, this was the most important place Taxes could be.

"Attention all partiers, revelers, and future subjects of his majesty: please welcome, to kick off this Unbirthday Ball: the Unbirthday Ballet, presented by Misters Tumble and Twirl!:" The Yes-man of the Ministry of Petty Complaints had been tasked with leading the ceremony and attention-seeking. The opening act, a dance performed by two Little Misters, never released, was to be watched by all attendees before the king was to be crowned.

Mr. Tumble, a fragile, crystalline man, performed his acrobatics with grace and anxiety. Mr. Twirl performed his contortionist act with freakish delight, and the crowds ooh'd and ahh'd at the mystical balance between the two's movements.

Taxes paid acute attention to every reaction, scanning the faces for signs of boredom and sternness- signs of future dissent. Instead, the two misters carried along, wowing the crowd and finally climaxing with Mr. Tumble cascading from atop the chandelier and shattering on the ground- with the onlookers gasping aloud.

Mr. Twirl then produced a bejeweled dustbin and broom, sweeping Mr. Tumble's shards up, and gathering them into a tumbler. He shook the tumbler back and forth, gently spinning and twisting upward. At last he release and flung the contents to the floor, revealing a tiny Mr. Tumble, perfectly intact.

The audience applauded and marveled and gasped. But Mr. Twirl waved his hands, a flourish to silence, and proceeded to slowly twist inwardly outward with bombast and violence. His arms intertwined, rubbery like jello, he turned into knots, ties, and then a giant birthday bow. Mr. Twirl continued stretching in all different manners, before exerting himself for the final act: he tied and tied, and knotted and knotted, and tangled and twirled into a great big rubber ball at least three ceilings tall.

The crowd erupted into hysterical applause.

"Thank you, ladies and gentlemen, those were our astoundingly talented Little Misters Tumble and Twirl: can you believe that they used to work a boring corporate job?" The Yes-Man of Petty Complaints commended, drawing attention back to the ceremony. "But now: the moment we are all here for…"

Up above, a Yes Man gulped.

"Is this really what we want?" whispered the Minister of Bouncy Fortifications to the Hatter.

This Yes Man, like all others, was concocted from a severed finger of the Hatter, a spitting image of the magnanimous soon-to-be-king.

"Of course it is, of course of course! The King gets the best biscuits, the best horses, the best games, yes, this is how it has to be. No more of the inane parties with the hares and mice and clocks and inanities, yes, this is where my life truly begins…" The Hatter glimmered, "Now, quiet, you, it's starting any moment now!"

A hollow, tinny drumroll began, and the chandelier above began to creak and croak, before suddenly free falling towards the banquet table below. The crowds shrieked and panicked and froze before the chandelier stopped with just inches to go. The lights went from a dull flicker to bright fluorescent blue, purple, and green.

"Ladies and Gentleman," The Yes Man Below continued escalating intensity,"Your new king, the best king, the Sanest King!"

The Chandelier had now revealed itself to be a platform with a golden studded throne, a throne where the Hatter was eagerly seated. He was surrounded by the rest of the Yes Court, who waited in place.

DEATH lurked just behind the Hatter, with a crown fashioned of pink and green plaid in hand. He lifted the crown, just above the Hatter's head, as the crowd's rapturous applause reached a feverish pitch.

"ARE YOU SURE YOU WANT THIS?" whispered DEATH.

"Yes, yes, the people are raving! Let's give them the show that I want! Hurry, hurry, hurry!" The Hatter anxiously fiddled with the armrests.

DEATH shrugged, and unceremoniously plopped the crown on the Hatter's matted hair. The crowd roared.

"Yes, yes, my adoring new subjects, young and old, pink and not-so-pink: It is I, your king, your most bestest belovedest, it is time now, for me to take the helm, the heaviest hat of all, the crown, the crown of all of Wonderland, yes, yes, please keep clapping, keep clapping from the tackiest chateau to the dingiest town!"

The Hatter, now the king, stepped off the chandelier and onto the ballroom floor. He waltzed towards the curtain that concealed the Great Unbirther.

"And now for my final act as a simple man, now, great subjects, I take the throne, I take the titled: I will be unborn, yes, turned anew, I will be unborn from a simple Hatter into what I always knew, your most excellent, wisest, handsomest, fairest, justest, humblest, and most importantly: your Sanest King!"

The Hatter pulled down the curtain with a theatrical flourish.

"ARE YOU HAVING FUN YET?" asked DEATH, poking from behind.

The Hatter simply ignored, and let himself be baptized by the candy-pink flesh.

However, the Cupmaster managed to convince him of this impossibility, the ceilings had been lifted from 40 meters to infinity, and the Cupmaster was not very good at climbing. Still, he had laid out a regal cloth upon the central banquet table, and ordered the finest of leaded glass instruments and utensils for eating. The drapes, he felt, we meant to match the cloths upon the table, for everything to be this harmonious tasteful, and subtly lavish production.
